author: lukacf
body:
A delivery whose caller left while it was parked behind a member's in-flight admission could still execute: a ghost turn. `actor_isolation::abandoned_delivery_behind_a_parked_lane_is_never_executed` caught it under load. 3/30 runs failed at 10 copies on two pinned cores, and each failure actually executed the abandoned prompt (`["first", "abandoned"]`).

## Root cause

The actor's per-member admission lane skips a parked delivery whose caller is gone. It checks `caller_is_closed()` on the delivery's reply channel when it pops the entry, and again when admission starts.

`MobHandle::execute_machine_command` ran every command, `SubmitWork` included, through `meerkat_runtime::stack_relief::relieve_caller_stack`. The reply receiver therefore lived on the relieved task, not in the caller's future. When the caller dropped, `AbortOnDrop` aborted that task, but abort is asynchronous: the task, and the receiver with it, is dropped only at its next poll, possibly later on another worker. `relieve_caller_stack`'s own doc comment warns about this ("cancellation is WEAKER than inline drop").

So the caller could be gone (its `JoinHandle` resolved) while the receiver was still alive. A lane pop in that window saw a live caller and ran the turn.

## Fix

- `execute_machine_command` routes `SubmitWork` inline (`MobHandle::submit_work_command`). The reply receiver now lives in the caller's own future and closes the moment the caller drops. The `SubmitWork` arm is a thin forward (build the payload, send the actor command), not the large routing frame the relief exists for. Every other command keeps the relief. Comments at both sites explain why.
- Test: the timer polls and sleeps are replaced with typed events.
  - The two `wait_until` polls (10 ms sleeps, 2 s deadlines) become typed waits:
    - a `Notify`-backed `FaultInjectingRuntimeStore::wait_parked_admission_arrivals`;
    - the existing `MemberAdmissionBacklogGauge::wait_for_snapshot` for the lane depth.
  - The 100 ms pre-abort sleep is gone.
  - The 300 ms "give a ghost turn every chance" quiet period is replaced by a positive event: a test-only `skipped_abandoned` counter on the backlog gauge, bumped when the lane skips the entry. The test waits for exactly that skip, so a regression now fails (the wait never resolves) instead of passing on timing.

## Evidence

Recipe: `taskset -c 180-181`, 10 concurrent copies, `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608`.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before | 27/30 (3 executed the abandoned prompt) |
| After | 60/60 (6 rounds), all logs `1 passed` |

## Stack

`SubmitWork` now polls on the caller's stack instead of a fresh relief task:

Debug frame sizes (`-Zemit-stack-sizes`, decoded with `llvm-readobj --stack-sizes`):

| Frame on the caller's stack | Bytes (debug) |
|---|---|
| `MobHandle::execute_machine_command::{closure#0}` (SubmitWork arm) | 5,864 |
| `MobHandle::submit_work_command::{closure#0}` | 7,496 |
| `send_actor_command::{closure#0}` for SubmitWork | 7,032 |
| `submit_work_payload` (synchronous; not live with the send) | 9,192 |

The deepest chain is about 22.5 KB. Before, the caller held the `relieve_caller_stack::<MobMachineCommandResult, ..>` frame, 28,232 B, so the caller's debug stack gets about 5.7 KB smaller.

`router::tests::rpc_dispatch_path_fits_debug_worker_stack_budget` passes at its 4 MiB bound, as do the two `mob_member_send` router tests that drive SubmitWork. The release budget (`make stack-budget-release`, 1 MiB) is deferred to the batch's final full gate. Release frames are far smaller than debug ones.

Gates: `clippy -p meerkat-mob --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `nextest -p meerkat-mob --lib` 2456 passed; `make wasm-check` green. Pushed with `SKIP=machine-codegen-verify,cargo-test,cargo-clippy` after running those gates myself; the other pre-push hooks ran.

author: petedillo
body:
## Summary

This PR adds `codex-review`, a runner that serializes Codex reviews on `codex-248`. Every review spends the same ChatGPT Plus allowance, so two parallel runs would each read the quota before the other spent it.

- **Lock.** The runner takes `flock` on `~/work/.codex-review.lock`. A second caller waits up to `codex_review_lock_wait_s` (3600 s), then exits 3.
- **Quota after the lock.** `codex-quota` runs once the lock is held, so each review sees what the previous one left.
- **Separate files.** Each run writes its prompt, log and final message under `~/work/reviews/runs/` with a UTC timestamp.
- **Footer metadata.** The prompt names the model and effort. The first review, on [petedio-iac#406](https://github.com/PeteDio-Labs/petedio-iac/pull/406), had to write `unavailable` for both.
- **Input checks.** The repo, PR number and effort are validated; a bad argument exits 2.

The README's "Run a review" section now points to `codex-review <repo> <n> [high]` instead of the hand-typed chain from [petedio-iac#409](https://github.com/PeteDio-Labs/petedio-iac/pull/409).

## Verification

- `ansible-lint roles/codex`: 0 failures, production profile.
- `scripts/deploy-codex-248.sh --check`: `failed=0 changed=1`; the one change is **Install the review runner**.
- On the host, with the lock wait set to 5 s: no arguments, a bad repo, PR `0` and effort `xhigh` each exit 2. With the lock held, a second call waited 5 s and exited 3.

body:
## 背景

本番のひな形の項目（license_master・service_master・purchase_order）を見ると、基本契約書と個別利用許諾条件書は同じものを違う名前で持っていた。名前だけで共通の欄を決めると、同じ相手先の担当者などを 2 回入れることになる。

## 変更

`server/documents/field-synonyms.ts` に同じ意味の欄の組を持つ。共通の欄は組ごとに 1 つにし、入れた値は組のすべての名前に入れる（`expandShared`）。

| 組 | 基本契約書 | 個別利用許諾条件書 | 発注書 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 相手方 名称・住所・代表者 | VENDOR_NAME・VENDOR_ADDRESS・VENDOR_REP | Licensor_氏名会社名・Licensor_住所・Licensor_代表者名 | VENDOR_* |
| 相手方の担当者 | NOTICE_CONTACT_NAME・PHONE・EMAIL | Licensor_担当者・電話・メール | VENDOR_CONTACT_NAME・PHONE・EMAIL |
| 当社 名称・住所・代表者 | PARTY_A_* | Licensee_氏名会社名・住所・代表者名 | PARTY_A_* |

業務委託の基本契約書と発注書は VENDOR_*・PARTY_A_* が同じ名前なので、組にしなくても共通になる（違うのは相手方の担当者だけ）。

## 確認
- typecheck / build / `npm test`（1687 pass。組の判定と、値の展開のテストを追加）
- ローカルで基本契約書のひな形を本番の項目に差し替え、Chromium で確認。共通の欄に「ライセンサー名称・住所」「ライセンシー名称・住所・代表者」「通知先 担当者・電話・メール」がまとまって出た

author: jeremi
body:
The container pilot previously installed Registry Stack 0.27 while the adaptors targeted newer clients. Upgrade the fresh synthetic deployment and all four adaptor dependency graphs to published 0.38.0, with pinned release checksums and OCI digests.

The pilot now uses stock ThunderID, Casework review followed by explicit BREG application, and Evidence with a persistent non-exportable Transit key. Its runtime, Compose project, host ports and volumes are separate from retained 0.27 data. Explicit client bindings include the private CA, OAuth audience/resource/scopes and governed Evidence verification policy.

The bridge validates canonical 0.38 HookEnvelope deliveries and returns the native notification acknowledgement after OpenFn acceptance. Existing jobs retain their normalized input shape; the legacy bridge body mode remains available. Recovery uses current runtime configuration and retains identities, delivery generations and credential associations.

The supervised local signer policy requires a numeric key version without an ACL version allowlist; the released signer pins and verifies version 1, and startup refuses rotated keys. The operator limitation is documented in deployment/README.md.

Validation:
- 124 Node and 28 Python tests; all four adaptor package dry runs.
- Fresh preparation with published Linux tools and eight Evidence fixtures.
- Released native BREG OAuth/metadata and Evidence send/verify, including missing-source unavailability.
- Native source authorization, intake approval refusal, Casework review and explicit BREG application.
- Complete OpenFn registration, exact/conflicting retries, correction submission, separate approval/application, and verified destination effects.
- Retained service restart and exact replay; native replay of three retained dead letters with generation advancement and payload erasure.
- All three live failure/recovery scenarios: exhausted delivery replay, retry of the failed destination step, and queued work retained across restart.

author: articialroamer
body:
Closes #96.

Fixes a crash where turns played from a saved physics snapshot (held Space, auto travel) threw a null 'handle' error near props. Each restored drive now owns its records, and bad records fail with a named error.

How to try: In the loaded game, hold Space or turn on auto travel and drive past rocks, fences and other props for 20 or more turns. Turns should keep playing with no crash screen, and the game should keep saving.

The factory merges it when the committee approves.

## Summary

Settles the two things a DHF with change requests from before MedHarness's closure criteria has to settle once (MedHarness `docs/adopting.md`, "Change requests you already have").

**A status that is no state of the type.**
- `CR-004` and `CR-009` were `implementing`, which is not a CR state. Both have merged PRs (#44, #62), so they are `completed`.
- `CR-013` was still `new`, but its feature shipped (#112, #113): the toolbar shows the formatted patient name (`Toolbar.tsx` uses `formatPatientName`) and has tests. It is `completed`.

**Completed CRs that never recorded their closure.** `build release` re-runs `verify completion` for every completed CR it includes, by default every completed CR not yet in a release. CR-003 to CR-013 closed before `implementation_notes`, `affected_items` and `triage_result` existed, so they fail it. `REL-001` lists them in `included_items`, which takes them out of the default, so the next release checks only CRs closed with their records (CR-014 onwards). They are deliberately not backfilled: a triage approval written afterwards would not be a record of anything.

Records were written with `medharness item update` / `item create`; `CR-004`, `CR-009` and `CR-013` each changed in one line (`status`), checked with a semantic diff.

- `DHF/items/08_rel/REL-001.yaml`: new, version `baseline`, lists CR-003 to CR-013

author: 9uile
body:
## Summary

Adds the human-on-the-loop orchestration milestone: an explicit, persisted **Cycle** that runs implement → verify → review for a Work Item, fixes routine problems automatically, and stops for a human only when a decision is needed. Automation ends at `HUMAN_REVIEW_READY`; nothing creates, reviews, or merges PRs.

- **Domain**: `Cycle`, `Review`, `Finding`, run `purpose`. States, reasons, and every allowed transition are defined in one table (`src/domain/cycle.ts`). The review policy (`src/domain/review.ts`) is deterministic code: routine categories with a file path → `AUTO_FIX`; design/scope/API/schema/security/dependency/architecture/decision/ambiguity/`unknown` → `NEEDS_HUMAN`.
- **Structured results**: Codex `--output-schema`, Claude Code `--output-format json --json-schema`. Orvia validates strictly with the approved limits (20 findings, title 200, detail 2,000, …). Anything invalid or oversized → `BLOCKED / REVIEW_PROTOCOL_INVALID` (other stages `RESULT_PROTOCOL_INVALID`). No free-text fallback, no truncation.
- **Loop**: failed checks and `AUTO_FIX` findings go to the fix agent (it sees only those findings), then verify → review again. `orchestration.max_review_fix_cycles` (default 3) → `NEEDS_HUMAN / LOOP_LIMIT`; the count restarts when a human resumes.
- **Human**: `NEEDS_HUMAN` carries a reason, and `get_cycle` lists the finding ids that need a decision. Answer with the existing `record_decision` / `add_context`, then `resume_cycle`; every prompt is rebuilt from the latest Plan, decisions, and context after the worktree identity is checked again.
- **Safety**: no transaction is held while an agent runs. `pause_cycle` and `cancel_cycle` use the Foundation's process-group termination and stop a stage that started meanwhile before recording the new state. A restart → `BLOCKED / RUN_INTERRUPTED` with no relaunch. Reviews run read-only. Prompts state the instruction precedence (Orvia rules > decisions > cycle instructions/context > AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md > defaults), and the rest of the repository is data.
- **Storage**: migration 0002 adds `cycles`, `reviews`, `review_findings`, and run `cycle_id`/`purpose`/`result`. A partial unique index allows one active cycle per Work Item. Stage results are written with ordinary write capacity (not the control reserve); if they do not fit → `BLOCKED / STORAGE_HARD_LIMIT`. Raw output stays in the bounded cache, and all cache files of a running run are protected from cleanup.
- **Operations** (CLI, IPC, and MCP from the registry): `start_cycle`, `get_cycle`, `get_current_review`, `get_review`, `pause_cycle`, `resume_cycle`, `cancel_cycle`. `get_status` shows each open Work Item's active cycle.
- **Docs**: README (Orchestration cycles section), CHANGELOG, ADR 0010.

No new runtime dependencies.

### Finalization: provider-neutral agents and dogfooding readiness

- **Agent Profiles and capabilities.** Cycles and runs refer to Agent Profiles (`agents.profiles` in `config.json`: a user-chosen id → adapter, command, optional narrower capabilities), not to agent CLIs. Capabilities are `workspaceRead`, `workspaceWrite`, `commandExecution`, `structuredResult`; effective = adapter ∩ profile. Each stage requires a fixed set (`requiredCapabilitiesFor`), checked before any agent starts (`AGENT_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH` with profile, stage, required, available, missing), and each run is granted only its stage's set. Profiles resolve from explicit request → configured default → error; there is no fallback. They resolve again at every launch, so a profile removed or narrowed since the cycle started blocks the resume. `list_agent_profiles` and `doctor` show availability, capabilities, and runnable stages. `src/domain` and `src/application` no longer name any provider.
- **Review evidence (option B).** Orvia collects `git status` and the diff from the cycle's base commit and puts them in the review prompt, so reviewers need only `workspaceRead` + `structuredResult`. Changes above `orchestration.max_review_diff_kb` (256 KiB, maintainer's choice) stop at `NEEDS_HUMAN / CHANGES_TOO_LARGE` instead of a partial review. ADR 0011 compares option A.
- **Cache hard bound.** Open writers' accepted bytes are counted instead of their lagging file size, so measurements and cleanup during a run can no longer push the cache past `cache_max_mb`. A concurrency test samples the disk; it fails against the previous implementation and its observed peak reaches but does not exceed the cap.
- **Structured result storage.** A stage's result space is reserved before the agent starts. No room is `RESULT_STORAGE_EXHAUSTED`, and only malformed or oversized agent output is a protocol error.
- **Fixes found in local validation with real CLIs.** Verification now lists only checks: a failing exploratory command had caused two needless fix rounds. Post-run cleanup no longer logs an error during daemon shutdown.
- **ENOENT cleanup race** (`ab86b5f`) now has a regression test (fails 3/3 on the previous code).
- **Pause launch race** (`pause_work_item` while a stage starts → `BLOCKED / START_FAILED` instead of `PAUSED`, no agent runs): deferred; README and ADR 0010 state the behaviour.
- **Real agent validation** (local; CI runs fake adapters only): codex-cli 0.159.0 and Claude Code 2.1.287. Results are in README → Compatibility.
- **Docs:** README (profiles, compatibility, MCP-client-centred integration, local dogfooding), ADR 0011, ADR 0010 updated, `docs/dogfooding-log.md`.

**Breaking for anyone who ran an earlier build of this PR:**
- Migration 0002 was edited within this unreleased PR (profile columns, base commit, new reasons). A database created by an earlier build of this branch fails at startup with `MIGRATION_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH`; delete that development `state.db` and its backups. Databases from `master` upgrade normally.
- `agents.codex` / `agents.claude` config keys are rejected (`CONFIG_INVALID`); use `agents.profiles`. `start_run` takes `profileId`; `start_cycle` takes `implementationProfileId` / `reviewProfileId` (optional with defaults) and `baseRef`.

## Related issue

None.

## Type of change

- [x] feat
- [x] fix
- [x] docs
- [ ] refactor
- [x] test
- [ ] chore / ci

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run check` passes in `nix develop` (216 tests)
- [x] Tests added or updated (state machine, policy, result validation, adapters, migration 0001→0002, end-to-end fake-agent cycles: happy path, auto fix, escalation + decision + resume, unknown, invalid reviewer output, loop limit, pause, restart and crash recovery, two Work Items, cache and database limits)
- [x] Docs updated (README Implemented/Planned sections stay accurate)
- [x] ADR added in `docs/adr/` if the change is architectural (ADR 0010, ADR 0011)
- [x] Migration added if the schema changed (never edit an applied migration) — 0002 was edited before release; see above
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or private source in the diff

Known limitation: real agent CLIs are not run in CI. Adapters' command lines and result extraction are unit-tested, the loop is tested with scripted fake adapters, and the real CLIs were run locally (README → Compatibility).

author: ncimino
body:
> **Tip history:** `aca73ec` (OGRE reviewed: REQUEST_CHANGES) → `75a547a` (`--no-ff` merge of #291 @ `fca598a`, so `validation.yml` runs on this PR into `merge/nik-mac`) → **`7a99946`** (OGRE fixes). **OGRE approved at `7a99946`.** The diff also includes #291's workflow changes (`validation.yml`, `branch-name-check.yml`, `auto-pr-to-main.yml`, `.github/scripts/auto-pr.sh`). They drop out once #291 is folded into `merge/nik-mac`.

---

## What
Billing's Keycloak login links a sign-in to an existing billing user only when that is safe. `WeOwnOIDCBackend` is in `billing-docker/{template,sites/billing}/app/core/auth.py`; both copies are identical.

1. **By `sub`.** The login matches the user whose `Customer.kc_user_id == sub`. If that user is **staff or superuser, the login fails**: admin access is local login only.
2. **Else by e-mail**, and only when all of these hold:
   - `email_verified` is the JSON value `true`;
   - the target is **not** staff/superuser;
   - the target is **not yet bound** to a Keycloak sub (no Customer, or `kc_user_id == ""`).
3. **Else a new user** (the library default).
4. `_sync` **refuses to replace a non-empty, different `kc_user_id`**. This is defence in depth for (2). It no longer copies an unverified e-mail onto the user.
5. `ensure_break_glass` **refuses to create or promote `weown-admin` when that user is bound to a Keycloak identity**. It writes `REFUSED: …` to stderr and promotes nothing. It returns 0, because `start.sh` is `set -e` and billing must still boot (the same pattern as its missing-password branch). An unbound `weown-admin` is adopted as before.

A refused login raises `SuspiciousOperation`; mozilla-django-oidc 4.0.1 catches it and fails the login (`authenticate` → `None`). The log line is `oidc login refused: <event> (user_id=<pk>)`. It never contains the e-mail or the sub (weown-fleet#107).

Fixes WeOwnDev/weown-fleet#96

## Changes in response to OGRE (REQUEST_CHANGES at `aca73ec`)
- **Blocking #1, takeover of a bound account by a verified e-mail:** fixed by (2) and (4). The paid entitlement follows `kc_user_id` (`views.py:299`, `set_subscription_active`), so it can no longer move to another Keycloak user.
- **#2, sub path onto superuser, and break-glass promoting an OIDC user:** fixed by (1) and (5). As orc directed, the sub path also excludes `is_staff`, the same as the e-mail path. A manually flagged staff user must use local login.

## Test evidence (fails before, passes after)
`core.tests.OIDCAccountLinkTests`, now 8 cases (Django 5.2.17, mozilla-django-oidc 4.0.1).

New in `7a99946`, run against the `75a547a` auth/break-glass code:

| test | before (`75a547a`) | after (`7a99946`) |
|---|---|---|
| `test_verified_email_cannot_take_over_an_account_bound_to_another_sub` | **FAIL** (`1 == 1`: the login lands on the victim) | ok |
| `test_sync_refuses_to_rebind_a_different_sub` | **FAIL** (SuspiciousOperation not raised) | ok |
| `test_sub_bound_to_staff_or_superuser_fails_the_login` | **FAIL** (SuspiciousOperation not raised) | ok |
| `test_break_glass_refuses_to_promote_a_keycloak_bound_user` | **FAIL** (`True is not false`: promoted) | ok |

The 4 earlier cases (unverified takeover, break-glass e-mail, verified link, returning user by sub) still pass.

Full `core` suite at `7a99946`, for both `template/app` and `sites/billing/app`:
- SQLite: 91/91 OK.
- **PostgreSQL 16.11** (throwaway `postgres:16` docker container, local only): 91/91 OK.
- `makemigrations --check`: no changes.

**Size:**
- This commit: +35/−6 code and +45 tests per copy.
- Cumulative fix vs base `3c6644a`: **+58/−4 code (auth.py +50/−4, ensure_break_glass.py +8) and +87 tests per copy, about 149 lines**.
- Both copies together are twice that (template and live render are identical).

## Operator step: one-off prod audit (read-only; not run by the agent)
This finds links made under the old e-mail-only logic onto staff/superuser accounts. It prints ids and flags only, no e-mail. Run it in the billing compose directory on the billing host. Either form works.

```sh
# SQL via the db container (official postgres image: local socket auth)
docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml exec db psql -U billing -d billing -c \
  "SELECT c.id AS customer_id, u.id AS user_id, u.username, u.is_staff, u.is_superuser
     FROM core_customer c JOIN auth_user u ON u.id = c.user_id
    WHERE c.kc_user_id <> '' AND (u.is_staff OR u.is_superuser);"

# or Django ORM via the web container's secrets entrypoint
docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml exec web /opt/weown_billing/entrypoint-infisical.sh \
  python manage.py shell -c "from django.db.models import Q; from core.models import Customer; \
  qs = Customer.objects.exclude(kc_user_id='').filter(Q(user__is_superuser=True) | Q(user__is_staff=True)); \
  print(qs.count()); [print(c.pk, c.user_id, c.user.username, c.user.is_staff, c.user.is_superuser) for c in qs]"
```
Expected: 0 rows. Any row is a Keycloak identity bound to an elevated account. After this PR, that identity can no longer log in through SSO. Decide per row whether to unbind it (`kc_user_id=''`) or drop the flag.

## Not covered
- `sub` is stored without `iss` (OGRE non-blocking). There is a single realm today. A realm migration would push every login onto the e-mail fallback, which now refuses bound accounts.
- No unique DB constraint on non-empty `kc_user_id` or on `User.email`. Duplicates still fail closed ("Multiple users returned").
- A `preferred_username` collision on create still fails with IntegrityError (500, fail-closed; pre-existing).
- No CHANGELOG entry, to avoid conflicts between the parallel fix PRs.

## Unverified
- **The live realm's `verifyEmail` and any IdP-broker "Trust Email" setting are still unverified.** Together they decide what `email_verified=true` means. If `verifyEmail` is off, new users have `email_verified=false` and are linked by `sub` only. A pre-existing e-mail-only user then gets a new account on first SSO login instead of being linked.
- The prod audit above has not been run (it needs prod access).
- Postgres was tested on `postgres:16`, not the prod image.

## Review status
Touches **authentication**. **OGRE APPROVE @ `7a99946`** (https://github.com/WeOwnNetwork/ai/pull/286#issuecomment-5943892942): OGRE-cleared. Marked ready for review. **Waiting for Nik to fold** (agent merges are off). #291's workflow changes ride along. #291 itself is waiting on Nik's fold (fold it first or together). OGRE's non-blocking items are ticketed; see the PR comments.

author: ugexe
body:
Previously `$a ** 2` and `$a²` were much slower than `$a * $a` under RakuAST, where before the RakuAST release they were about the same speed (this came up on IRC). The legacy optimizer rewrites `$var ** 2` to `$var * $var`. The RakuAST port of that rewrite (a636ef36c8) only fired for typed lexicals, never for `$a²`, and the multiply it built compiled to a plain `call`. The power routine itself was also slow for a square. An Int went through `nqp::pow_I`, which builds a libtommath bignum even for a small base, and a Num with an Int exponent went through `Real ** Real`, which bridges both operands and dispatches again.

The first commit puts the fast path in the power routines instead. `Int ** Int` and `Rational ** Int` multiply when the exponent is 2, the Num candidates multiply for `2e0`, and a new `Num:D ** Int:D` candidate skips the `Bridge` detour. That speeds up every shape and not just a plain variable, e.g. `@a[$i] ** 2` or `f() ** 2`, on both frontends. A Num square is now the correctly rounded product, so `$x ** 2` agrees with `$x * $x` where libm `pow` can be off in the last place.

The second commit gives a literal postfix like `$x²`, and the vulgar fraction postfix, a static callee lookup like the other operators get. The legacy frontend already does this for the superscript.

The third commit removes the RakuAST square rewrite. It had to reproduce what the power routine does for every kind of operand and got several of them wrong. `my Mu:D $j = any(1, 2); say $j ** 2` printed `any(any(1, 2), any(2, 4))` instead of `any(1, 4)`, a native uint square wrapped to 0, a Proxy was fetched once per operand, and a Num underflow Failure became 0. It also blocked native lowering, so `my int $x; $x ** 2` was over ten times slower than the `pow_i` it lowers to now. The legacy optimizer still has its own version of the rewrite, so those cases are todo'd for legacy in the tests.

In a 3 million iteration loop `$a ** 2` goes from 0.56s to 0.23s for an Int (`$a * $a` is 0.17s) and from 0.56s to 0.30s for a Num, `$a²` goes from 0.76s to 0.35s, and a native int square goes from 0.57s to 0.04s. An Int to any other power pays one extra comparison, about 6% on `$a ** 3`.

The new `Num:D ** Int:D` candidate is narrower than a user `**` multi such as `(Real $a, Int $b)`, so for a Num base and an Int exponent it now wins over one, and a user multi on `(Num $a, Int $b)` is ambiguous with it. `Int:D ** Int:D` and `Rational:D ** Int:D` already behave this way for an Int or a Rational base.

author: gregmarra
body:
Adds `actions/labeler@v7` so any pull request that changes files under `pwa/` gets the existing `PWA` label on open, push, or reopen.

- `.github/labeler.yml`: `PWA` when any changed file matches `pwa/**`.
- `.github/workflows/labeler.yml`: runs on `pull_request_target`, so PRs from forks are labelled too. That's safe here because the labeler only reads the changed-file list and never checks out or runs PR code. Permissions are limited to `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write`.
- It never removes labels (`sync-labels` stays off), so a hand-applied `PWA` label sticks.

**Note:** a `pull_request_target` workflow runs from the base branch, so it can't run on this PR itself. It takes effect for PRs opened or pushed after this merges. Existing open PWA PRs were labelled by hand.

## Squash commit message

Label PRs that touch pwa/ with PWA automatically

author: csorianoai
body:
## P0 — el inventario de Mapaal

Defecto medido en producción: **el batch concede `autos.inventory.list` y a `/api/v1/autos/*` no llegaba ninguna petición.** La pantalla se cerraba sola antes de pedir nada, y le mostraba **"Inventario bloqueado: DEFAULT_DENY"** a un usuario con el permiso concedido. El frontend no estaba restringiendo: estaba **inventando una denegación**.

## Verifiqué las cuatro mediciones del coordinador contra `9bc5baba`. Las cuatro coinciden

| Afirmación | Verificado |
|---|---|
| `setDealerAccessContext` en `lib/dealer/access-context.ts:122`, sin llamadores fuera de tests | ✓ `git grep` sobre `app`, `components`, `lib`, `contexts`, `hooks` → sólo su propia definición |
| el login (`contexts/AuthContext.tsx:100-112`) sólo guarda el tenant | ✓ guarda token, auth, tenantId, tenantName, role y plan. **Ni `dealer_id` ni `organization_unit_id`** |
| `resolveDealerAccessContext` → `no_dealer` con `"DEFAULT_DENY"` en `:200-207` | ✓ literal |
| `inventario/page.tsx:13` y `:24-25` bloquean por el contexto local; `:29` inventa `DEFAULT_DENY` | ✓ literal |

Un dato extra que encontré y conviene saber: **en `staging` el contexto todavía emite `NO_ORGANIZATION_UNIT` en MAYÚSCULAS** (`lib/dealer/access-context.ts:48,223`), mientras el backend manda minúsculas. Por eso uso `isAccessUnverified` y no un `===`: reconoce las dos formas. Mi #553 unifica la ortografía, pero no está en staging.

## Los tres cambios

1. **El acceso lo decide sólo el batch.** El contexto local ya no participa. El `dealerId` se sigue necesitando — el contrato privado es por dealer — pero para **construir** la petición: se lee con `selectedDealerIdentity`, que devuelve los ids **aunque falte la unidad organizativa** (`:255-262`). La unidad la resuelve el backend; el cliente no la exige.

2. **Ningún código inventado.** Donde había `?? "DEFAULT_DENY"`:

   | Situación | Qué se muestra |
   |---|---|
   | error del contrato de acceso | su propio `reason_code`; si no trae, el HTTP status dicho como tal |
   | `isAccessUnverified` | "No se pudieron verificar tus accesos" |
   | clave ausente en `results` | denegado, diciendo que **falta la decisión** |
   | denegado sin `reason_code` | se dice que no indicó motivo |

3. **Concedido pero sin dealer en la sesión no es una denegación.** El permiso está; falta un dato de la sesión. Se dice "No se pudo identificar el dealer de tu sesión", con `role="status"` y **sin ningún enlace**.

## Mutaciones ejecutadas

```
volver a condicionar a resolved.status === "ready" ...... 4 failed / 12 passed   ← la que pide el packet
reponer el `?? "DEFAULT_DENY"` ......................... 1 failed / 15 passed
comparar el código a mano en vez del reconocedor ....... 2 failed / 14 passed
pedir el inventario sin dealerId ....................... 1 failed / 15 passed
revert ................................................. 16 passed
```

## Rompí un suite previo y lo arreglé — conviene mirarlo

`tests/components/dealer-management/DealerInventory.test.tsx` tenía dos casos que **fijaban literalmente** `"Inventario bloqueado: DEFAULT_DENY"`: estaban midiendo el defecto. Conservé lo que valía de cada uno (que **no** se pida el inventario) y cambié lo que afirman — clave ausente → "falta la decisión" y **sin** `DEFAULT_DENY` en el texto; denegado con `DEFAULT_DENY` → se muestra, porque ahí **sí** lo dijo el backend. Esa diferencia es la que el packet viene a marcar.

## Verificación

```
npx jest tests/app/InventarioSoloBatch.test.tsx + DealerInventory.test.tsx → 21 passed
npx jest tests/app tests/components/dealer-management tests/lib/access tests/lib/dealer
                                                                         → 286 passed / 33 suites
npx tsc --noEmit  → limpio
npx eslint        → limpio
```

Queda un suite rojo **previo y ajeno**: `tests/app/public/consent/_components/SelfieCapture.test.tsx`, 4 failed. Medido en staging limpio con `git stash`: falla idéntico sin mis cambios.

## GR-12, medido

```
$ git diff --shortstat origin/staging...HEAD
 3 files changed, 454 insertions(+), 22 deletions(-)
$ git diff --name-only origin/staging...HEAD | cut -d/ -f1 | sort -u
app
tests
```

## Aviso de solape

**#534 toca este mismo fichero** (le añade la entrada "Nuevo vehículo" y un batch de dos claves). El que entre segundo necesita rebase de `app/autos/dealer/inventario/page.tsx`. Si este P0 entra primero, al rebasar #534 re-aplico su CTA sobre esta estructura.

**P0b no lo empiezo** hasta que me pases la forma del login/me que mide el backend.

Sin merge.

## 요약
worktree를 지우는 곳이 없어서 레포 캐시 정리(#61 `RepoCacheCleanupJob`)가 구현·배포를 거친 캐시를 회수하지 못하던 문제를 해결합니다(TODOS V1.1 "worktree 보존 정책").

- **성공하면 바로 정리합니다.** 구현은 PR 생성 보고 뒤에 지우고 로컬 `task-N` 브랜치도 함께 삭제합니다. 배포는 빌드·실행 뒤, 디자인은 수확 뒤에 지웁니다.
- **실패분은 디버그용으로 남깁니다.** 매일 02:30 `WorktreeCleanupJob`이 만든 지 7일 지난 worktree를 지웁니다.
- 스펙 `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-worktree-retention-design.md`, 계획 `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-worktree-retention.md`

### 제거 절차 — `WorktreeService.discard` / `discardUnderLock`
- 레포 락 안에서 진행합니다(기존 `remove`는 락 밖이었음). 순서는 `git worktree remove --force` → 남은 폴더를 링크·정션을 따라가지 않고 삭제(`RepoCacheCleanupJob.deleteTree`) → `git worktree prune` → 구현 worktree면 그 작업의 로컬 브랜치 삭제.
- 브랜치는 `-` 경계로 정확히 매칭합니다. `task-1`을 정리해도 `task-12-…`는 지우지 않습니다.
- `git worktree lock`이 걸린 worktree는 지우지 않습니다. `.git`을 읽지 못하면 잠긴 것으로 봅니다.
- 즉시 정리는 best-effort입니다. 실패해도 작업 결과에 영향이 없고, 남은 폴더는 주기 정리가 다시 시도합니다.

### 주기 정리 — `WorktreeCleanupJob` (worker)
- `worktree-root/.worktree-cleanup.lock`을 잡은 프로세스 하나만 정리합니다.
- **진행 중 조회는 fail-closed입니다.** `GET /worker/active-worktree-tasks`가 실패하면(네트워크·4xx·404·빈 본문) 그 회차는 아무것도 지우지 않습니다.
- 정확히 `{a}/{b}/{task|deploy|design}-{id}` 형태만 대상입니다. 링크·정션이나 이름이 다른 폴더는 손대지 않습니다. 점으로 시작하는 이름은 루트 바로 아래에서만 건너뜁니다(`owner/.github`도 대상). 읽지 못하는 폴더는 그 하위만 건너뜁니다.
- 판정은 순수 함수 `WorktreeCleanupPlanner`가 합니다. 기준 시각은 max(폴더, `.git`) mtime입니다. 레포 락은 `tryWithRepoLock`으로 비차단으로 잡고, **락 안에서 나이를 다시 판정**합니다(그사이 재시도가 worktree를 새로 만들었으면 남김).
- 회차 로그: `worktree 정리 완료 — 삭제 / 진행 중 / 기간 미달 / 사용 중(락) / git lock / 판단 불가 · 실패`

### API — `GET /worker/active-worktree-tasks` (`ROLE_WORKER`)
- 구현중·디자인중·배포중·배포중지중이면서 **삭제되지 않은** 작업의 `[{id, status}]`를 돌려줍니다.
- 스펙 원안은 "soft-delete와 무관"이었습니다. 하지만 진행 중에 삭제된 작업은 결과 보고와 stale 회수 모두에서 빠져 상태가 영원히 안 바뀝니다. 그러면 그 worktree와 캐시를 영구 보존하게 됩니다. 그래서 삭제된 작업은 제외하고 스펙을 정정했습니다. 방금 삭제된 작업의 worktree는 7일 나이 판정이 보호합니다.

### 설정 — `WorkerProperties.WorktreeCleanup`
| 환경변수 | 기본 | 비고 |
|---|---|---|
| `WORKTREE_CLEANUP_ENABLED` | `true` | |
| `WORKTREE_CLEANUP_CRON` | `0 30 2 * * *` | `-`면 끔. 잘못된 식이면 부팅 실패 |
| `WORKTREE_CLEANUP_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` | 비우면 7. **0 이하면 부팅 실패** |

워커 스케줄 풀은 5에서 6으로 늘렸습니다(스케줄 작업 7개).

## 테스트
- 신규 테스트:
  - `WorktreeCleanupPlannerTest`(이름 해석·7일 경계·mtime 규칙)
  - `WorktreeServiceDiscardTest`(실제 git: 제거·접두 번호 보호·git lock·고아 폴더·예외 삼킴)
  - `WorktreeImmediateDiscardTest`(성공만 정리, 보고 뒤 순서)
  - `WorkerServiceWorktreeActiveTest`
  - `WorkerActiveWorktreeTasksIntegrationTest`(Testcontainers: 네 상태만, 삭제분 제외, 키 없으면 4xx)
  - `WorktreeCleanupPropertiesTest`(기본값·빈 값·0·잘못된 cron)
  - `WorktreeCleanupJobTest`(오래된 것만 삭제·진행 중·조회 실패·git lock·레포 락 점유·**락 안 재판정 경합**·이상한 이름·점 레포·고아·잡 락·끔)
  - `WorkerHttpClientMaskTest`(빈 본문은 실패)
- `./gradlew test`(Windows): 781개 중 실패 3·skip 176. 실패 3개는 첨부 심볼릭 링크 권한 테스트로 main과 같은 기존 실패입니다. skip은 Docker가 없어 돌지 않은 Testcontainers 테스트가 대부분이고, 심볼릭 링크 권한이 없어 skip된 테스트도 있습니다. **새 통합 테스트는 CI에서 처음 돌아갑니다.**

## 남긴 것
- TODOS에 "worktree 삭제를 레포 락 밖으로"를 추가했습니다. 지금은 락을 쥔 채 삭제해서, 같은 repos-dir을 쓰는 다른 워커 프로세스가 60초 타임아웃에 걸릴 수 있습니다. PC당 워커 1개인 지금은 영향이 없지만, 멀티 워커 도입 전에는 필수입니다.
- 별도 작업: 기존 `WorktreeService.deleteRecursively`가 Windows 정션을 따라 들어가는 버그(이 브랜치가 만든 것은 아님).

## 배포
1. **API 먼저, 워커 나중.** 워커가 옛 API를 만나면 404가 나고, 정리 회차만 건너뜁니다(잘못 지우지 않음).
2. 라이브(Windows): API·워커만 재기동하면 됩니다(프론트 무관). 첫 02:30 회차에 9/22에 만든 `task-1`이 지워집니다. 걱정되면 `WORKTREE_CLEANUP_ENABLED=false`로 배포하고 목록을 확인한 뒤 켭니다.

author: comilionas
body:
Wave DEP-6, PR B of three. It clears the last three open Dependabot alerts (91, 92, 94: GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9, medium) by moving vitest **3.2.6 → 4.1.11**, the floor the owner chose (5.x was declined). The alerts were unreachable here: the suite runs `vitest run` in the node and jsdom environments, with no browser mode and no dev server. `npm audit` is now **0**.

## Two 4.x changes that would have weakened the suite (neither is in the migration guide)

1. **The full-suite guard went inert.** `tests/full-suite-guard.ts` implemented the `onFinished` reporter hook, which 4.x removed. The method still type-checked, so with the guard unported, a probe config that expects one file more than it runs exited **0**. The guard is now on `onTestRunEnd`, typed through `Reporter['onTestRunEnd']` so the next removal fails typecheck. The same probe now exits **1** naming the missing file, and **0** when nothing is missing.
2. **`vi.spyOn` returns a live spy, call history included** (3.2.6 made a fresh one). A test could pass on calls an earlier test made. Two places relied on the old behaviour, and both failed loudly:
   - `zim-service-lifecycle.test.ts` now restores spies after each test, as 56 other files already do.
   - `zim-ipc-session.test.ts` now uses an explicit `mockClear()` instead of a second `spyOn` in the same test.

   To rule out a silent case, the full suite ran once more with a temporary setup file that wrapped `vi.spyOn` and logged every spy handed back with calls in it. It logged **none**; a positive control logged exactly one.

## Other ports

- **Windows CI forks cap:** `poolOptions.forks.maxForks: 2` → `maxWorkers: 2`, because 4.x dropped `poolOptions` and the old key would have been ignored while its log line kept printing. Resolved through vitest's own `createVitest`, it reads 2 with `CI=1` on win32 and is unset otherwise.
- **CI job timeout:** 4.x creates the worker RPC with no timeout, so the `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` flake can't recur, and nothing ends a run whose main process stops answering. `ci.yml` had no job timeout (GitHub's default is 6 h), so `build-and-test` now has `timeout-minutes: 30`. The slowest leg takes about 9 minutes.
- **Sharding:** `shardTestFiles` follows 4.x `calculateShardRange`, which gives the same halves for `--shard=i/2`. A new unit test runs the installed vitest's own `BaseSequencer.shard` over the real suite for 2–5 shards and demands the same split.
- **Coverage:** `coverage.include: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}']`, because 4.x dropped `coverage.all`. Without it, a never-imported file would vanish from `test:coverage` instead of showing 0 %.
- **Types:** 52 type errors in 13 test files, none at runtime. `ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>` now means `Mock<Procedure | Constructable>`, so those files use vitest's `Mock`, which is what the old idiom meant under 3.x.

## Lockfile and packaging

- **Lockfile:** a plain bump installs vitest 4 under `apps/desktop/node_modules`, because `@vitest/coverage-v8` 3.2.6 pins `vitest` 3.2.6. That breaks `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`, which imports `vitest` from the root without declaring it. A two-step bump puts vitest at the root. Result: 17 entries move, 2 are added and 38 are removed (3.x only). The lockfile is stable on a re-run.
- **Exclusion:** root `tinyexec` 1.3.1 is then production-reachable only via mermaid, so `electron-builder.yml` adds `!**/node_modules/tinyexec/**`.
- **Pre-existing leak, now closed:** master's `app.asar` already shipped `@antfu/install-pkg`'s `tinyexec` 1.2.4. electron-builder 26 lays nested packages out at the asar's top level, past the `@antfu/**` exclusion, and `packaging.test.ts` checks lockfile paths, so it never saw this. A fresh `package:win` of this PR has PR A's asar entry list minus exactly those 6 entries, and no other package escapes an exclusion. That test gap is logged as a follow-up.

## Verification

- Fresh `npm ci`, typecheck, build, then the full suite: **478 files, 7,899 passed / 86 skipped / 7,986**. That is the baseline plus the one new sequencer pin, and per-file passed and skipped counts are otherwise identical. The real-Electron PDF smoke passed 8/8.
- `package:win` asar diff against PR A, as described above.

## Docs

- `architecture.md` DEP-6 record: the vitest row is now marked fixed, and a new §5 covers PR B.
- `packaging.md`: the guard trap and the forks cap.
- `BUILD_STATE.md`: the DEP-6 entry is updated (preamble 193/200).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: the bullet now mentions the test runner.

author: claudio712005
body:
O `apply` da esteira Infra parava antes de criar qualquer coisa:

```
Error: Output refers to sensitive values
  on outputs.tf line 17:
  17: output "db_jdbc_url" {
```

Confirmei na AWS que **nada foi criado**: sem ECR, sem SSM, sem security group, sem RDS. É erro de
plan, não de criação — o `apply` nem começou a agir.

## Causa

```hcl
output "db_jdbc_url" {
  value = aws_ssm_parameter.db_url.value
}
```

O atributo `value` de `aws_ssm_parameter` é **sensível no schema do provider**. Ler esse atributo
contamina o output, e o Terraform recusa output sensível sem `sensitive = true` explícito.

O conteúdo, porém, **não é segredo**: `jdbc:postgresql://<endpoint>/<banco>`, sem usuário nem
senha. Marcar o output como `sensitive` esconderia um valor que não é secreto e tiraria dele a
única utilidade, que é ser lido pela esteira e por quem opera.

### Correção

A URL passa a ser um `local`, usado nos dois lugares:

```hcl
locals {
  jdbc_url = "jdbc:postgresql://${aws_db_instance.this.endpoint}/${aws_db_instance.this.db_name}"
}
```

O parâmetro do SSM e o output consomem o mesmo `local`. Uma fonte, sem duplicação e sem herdar
sensibilidade.

## Segundo defeito, que ia aparecer no apply seguinte

`db_engine_version` estava fixo em **`16.4`**, que **não existe mais nesta conta**. Consultei:

```
postgres 16.x disponíveis:  16.9  16.10  16.11  16.12  16.13  16.14  16.15
describe-db-engine-versions --engine-version 16.4  ->  None
```

Versão menor fixa quebra o apply a cada expurgo da AWS, numa data que ninguém controla — é o mesmo
tipo de armadilha do identificador de conta no código. O default passa a ser **`16`**: o RDS
escolhe a menor disponível na criação, e a família do parameter group segue `postgres16`.

## Verificação

Rodei `plan` **de verdade** contra a conta, numa cópia do diretório com backend local, para não
tocar no state da esteira:

| O que | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `terraform plan` | `Plan: 13 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy` — sem erro |
| `db_jdbc_url` | output comum, `(known after apply)` |
| `engine_version` no plano | `"16"`, com `engine_version_actual` computado |
| `describe-db-engine-versions --engine-version 16` | resolve para a família `postgres16` |
| `db.t3.micro` + `gp3` em 16.9 e 16.15 | ordenável, mínimo de 20 GB — é o que o código pede |
| `terraform fmt -check -recursive` | passa |

A cópia de teste foi apagada depois.

## O que esperar na próxima execução

O apply vai criar de fato, e a RDS leva de cinco a dez minutos. Depois dela o job `Banco` roda em
sequência: cria o Secret do banco a partir do SSM e aplica o baseline do Postgres e do Mongo.

author: google-labs-stitch[bot]
body:
## Summary
Refactored `NotificationCollectorService` to enforce a maximum queue capacity of 100 entries (`MAX_QUEUE_SIZE`) and a 15-minute time-to-live (`MAX_AGE_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000L`) expiration policy. Automatically prunes expired items during notification capture and queue draining, capping heap memory usage and discarding stale unencrypted notifications.

## Changes
1. **`NotificationCollectorService.kt`**:
   - Added constants `MAX_QUEUE_SIZE = 100` and `MAX_AGE_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000L`.
   - Updated `addNotification` to prune expired items (`pruneExpired`), reject already expired notifications, and evict the oldest entry (FIFO) when queue capacity reaches 100 before inserting new notifications.
   - Updated `drainQueue` to filter out and discard notifications older than 15 minutes before returning data.
   - Added `clearQueue` helper to reset internal queue state during test runs.

2. **`NotificationCollectorServiceTest.kt`**:
   - Added comprehensive unit tests validating:
     - Hard queue size cap at 100 entries with FIFO eviction.
     - Automatic TTL pruning during capture (`addNotification`).
     - Automatic TTL pruning during queue draining (`drainQueue`).
     - Duplicate detection & resubmission after item expiry.
     - Queue clearing state reset.

3. **Gradle Build Configurations**:
   - Added `testImplementation("junit:junit:4.13.2")` to `app/build.gradle.kts`.
   - Updated JVM target compatibility settings in `android/build.gradle.kts`.

## Verification
- Executed local unit tests via `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest -x compileFlutterBuildDebug`.
- All unit tests in `NotificationCollectorServiceTest` and `NotificationRedactorTest` pass cleanly.

author: josephvelasquez48
body:
Each traffic dot was an SVG circle moved every frame, so Chromium repainted the whole map (boxes, lines and text) 16 times a second. On the Pi the map view used 33% of a core at 16 fps.

- **The dots now draw on a canvas over the SVG.** It has `pointer-events: none`, so taps still reach the boxes. The SVG only changes when a status does, every few seconds.
- **Each line's path is sampled once, every ~3 px.** Dots interpolate their position from that, instead of calling `getPointAtLength` for every dot every frame.

**Checked in a preview:** dots on the phone line land at y 552–559 against the line at 556, and DNS dots follow their curve. Dashboard tests: 21 passed. The Pi figure is measured after deploy.

author: ncimino
body:
> **Tip history:** `a7468c9` (OGRE reviewed: REQUEST_CHANGES) → `2c49cce` (`--no-ff` merge of #291 @ `fca598a`, so `validation.yml` runs on this PR into `merge/nik-mac`) → **`1a25a0c`** (OGRE fixes). **OGRE approved at `1a25a0c`.** The diff also includes #291's workflow changes (`validation.yml`, `branch-name-check.yml`, `auto-pr-to-main.yml`, `.github/scripts/auto-pr.sh`). They drop out once #291 is folded into `merge/nik-mac`.

---

## What
MCP tool-pack children get an **env allowlist by name** instead of the whole AnythingLLM container environment. The deploy playbook can only register servers that go through that allowlist.

**`spawnMcp`** (`storage/mcp/_lib/spawn.js`, template + beta-weown-chat + dev-weown-anythingllm copies). It used to pass `{ ...process.env, ...envPatch }`. `childEnv()` now passes only:
- `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `TERM`, `LANG`, `LANGUAGE`, `TZ`
- `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`, `NODE_ENV`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `SSL_CERT_*`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, and the proxy variables
- **uv/npm by name only:** `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, `UV_PYTHON`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `npm_config_cache`/`NPM_CONFIG_CACHE`, `npm_config_prefix`/`NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX`
- the `LC_`/`XDG_` prefixes

author: ahmethakanbezir1
body:
Fixes #1249.

`_calculate_sigma` currently squares float32 residuals in float32. This makes small representable residual scales produce zero-width native prediction intervals and large ones produce infinite endpoints. Square in float64 before summing; retain the existing NaN handling and degrees-of-freedom calculation. This does not claim to fix arbitrary extreme float64 intermediates elsewhere in the models.

The focused regression uses a four-point alternating series: all three one-step residual magnitudes are equal, so the expected sigma and normal interval widths have a direct analytic reference. It checks fit/predict and forecast at small, ordinary and large scales for float32 and float64, with zero absolute tolerance. It is placed in `action_files`, which the actual wheel CI collects.

Validation on Windows / Python 3.12.14 / NumPy 2.5.3 / SciPy 1.18.1:
- Current-main baseline: 2 failures and 4 controls passed.
- Final CI-selected regression plus existing `action_files/test_fit_predict.py`: 10 passed.
- Models, utils and simulation modules: 229 passed, 7 existing warnings (this run included the same six regression cases before moving them into the CI-selected directory).
- Both configured pre-commit hooks, Ruff and mypy, passed; git diff check passed.
- Editable package was built from this checkout without build isolation, using the pinned Eigen submodule and MSVC 2022 C++ compiler.

Distributed Spark/Ray/Dask tests, other operating systems, full package suite, and documentation build were not run locally. Dependency setup used project runtime requirements and the necessary test/build tools, not the complete dev group.

Disclosure: this contribution was investigated, implemented and validated autonomously with OpenAI Codex assistance; it has not had independent human review. Codex is recorded as co-author. I will maintain the change and respond to review feedback.

author: codegoddy
body: Automatic generation rewrote the zoom track with no way back, and the editor had no undo at all: a Detect pass that replaced a dozen clips, a drag that slid one, and a strength slider sweep each had to be repaired by hand. **A bounded snapshot history for the zoom track.** A step holds the clips, the selection, and the pending clipboard — the clipboard travels with the track because Cut removes a clip and holds it for a paste, so undoing a cut has to put the clip back *and* drop the pending paste instead of leaving the editor dimmed waiting for a clip the user just took back. The stack holds 64 steps and drops the oldest past that; undo here is a safety net for the last few edits, not a document history. **One step per thing the user did.** Discrete commands take their own step. A stream of updates — one timeline drag, one slider sweep — coalesces into a single step when it arrives within 350 ms of the previous one, so a drag is not 40 steps deep. A command that lands mid-drag ends the burst rather than folding into it, and a step that could not have changed anything is not recorded, so Ctrl+Z always makes progress. **A Detect pass is one step.** `redetect_zoom_clips` records a single step and then runs placement inside it, so one Detect — including the pass that runs when the editor opens a recording — takes one Ctrl+Z to take back. Undoing the pass that ran on open does not make it run again, because the reviewed flag is not part of the step. **Ctrl+Z from anywhere in the editor.** An `EventControllerKey` on the window in the bubble phase drives undo and redo, accepting Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y for redo, and reading the key through its Unicode value so a backend that folds Shift into the keyval still gets redo. A focused text entry keeps its own Ctrl+Z, and when there is nothing left to undo the key travels on rather than being swallowed. **Anchors and undo agree.** Generated clips follow their footage (see #90), so a restore has to re-project: a step is captured before the edit that takes it, and a composition edit after that point has already moved the anchored clips. Undo and redo therefore re-run the projection after restoring, which lands a restored clip on the footage its anchor names rather than on the composition slot it was captured at (`undoing_a_zoom_edit_keeps_the_clip_on_its_footage`). **Tests.** A drag and a slider sweep each collapse to one step, a command that changed nothing records nothing, a generation pass takes one step and the on-open pass does not come back, undoing a cut drops the pending paste, a reopened project starts with nothing to undo, undo/redo land anchored clips on their footage, and the key mapping covers Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y and the keys that are not ours. The window test pins the controller's installation the way the popover sweep is pinned. Steps are runtime-only and are never written to the project. `cargo test` is green (1364 lib tests, plus the integration suites), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reports only the pre-existing `needless_borrow` and `field_reassign_with_default` warnings in `canvas_render.rs` and `background_panel.rs`. Out of scope: undo covers the zoom track, which is what automatic generation rewrites. Timeline edits (trim, cuts, segment order) are not on the stack. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

body: ## What The Refunds tool from `docs/SPEC.md`, built as the reference tool other tools copy: `src/tools/refunds/` (`manifest.ts`, `migrations.ts` with seed, `queries.ts`, `actions.ts`, `refunds.test.ts`, `index.ts`) plus pages under `src/app/tools/refunds/` (list with status filter, new request, detail with approve/reject and the refund's audit trail). Registered in `src/tools/index.ts`. ```ts requestRefund(user, { chargeId, amountCents, reason }) // refunds:request // amount > $5,000 → refused "escalate to finance" (failed audit, nothing written) // amount > remaining → refused; remaining = charge − refunded − pending requests // amount ≤ $100 → refund() now, status executed // else → status pending_approval + ctx.requestApproval({ kind: "refund" }) approvals.refund = { permission: "refunds:approve", onApprove: refund() + executed, onReject: rejected } ``` Decision details (who, when, reason) live on the platform `approvals` row; the refund row keeps `approval_id` / `payment_refund_id`. Pages only read via `queries.ts`; all writes go through the action or the approval kind. ## Permissions and approvals - `refunds:view`: support_agent, finance_approver, auditor - `refunds:request`: support_agent - `refunds:approve`: finance_approver - Thresholds in the manifest: `autoApproveCents = 10_000` (≤ $100 executes immediately), `maxCents = 500_000` (> $5,000 refused). $100.01–$5,000 needs `refunds:approve`; the requester can't decide their own (platform `decideApproval` + DB `CHECK`), so Rio's own request waits for Ben. ## Assumptions - Seed: three pending (Ana ×2, Rio ×1, with matching pending `approvals` rows), one executed (with its `payment_refunds` row and `charges.refunded_cents` bumped), one rejected by Ben. - `onApprove` calls `refund()` again at decision time, so a request that no longer fits the charge fails and the approval stays pending (transaction rolls back). - Amount is entered in dollars on the form and parsed to integer cents in the server action; an unparsable amount is passed through so the action rejects and audits it. - No platform changes made. One suggested for a later platform PR: `applyMigration` in `src/platform/db.ts` commits the migration before calling `seed`, so an interrupted tool seed would not be retried on restart; running `seed` inside the same transaction fixes that for every tool. ## Evidence - `npm run check` passes locally: typecheck, lint, 36 tests (15 new: tier routing, over-refund incl. pending, Ben approves/rejects Ana's, Ana lacks the permission, Rio can't approve his own but Ben/Rio can approve Ana's, double decision refused, denied/invalid input audited, seed shape). CI runs the same. - `npm run build` succeeds; `/tools/refunds`, `?status=…`, `/new`, `/[id]` return 200 against a seeded DB, unknown id → 404, a kyc_analyst sees the access error. author: attilathefun
body:
The CLI takes the command line a host passes to `claude -p`, and took several of its options silently: parsed, stored, and never read.

**`--permission-mode` and `--permission-prompt-tool`: kept, not implemented, and no longer silent.** Visor passes `--permission-mode acceptEdits --permission-prompt-tool mcp__visor__approve --mcp-config …` for a session in its manual mode, so the options have to be taken. Honouring them would mean an MCP client (to reach the prompt tool Visor serves) and a permission model for the tools; that is a feature, not a fix, and it is not in this change. What is in it is that nobody is left thinking they applied:

- stderr, at launch: `openrouter: --permission-mode acceptEdits is not enforced: openrouter has one mode, and in it tools run without asking.` and the like for `--permission-prompt-tool` and `--mcp-config`. (`bypassPermissions` is the truth and gets no note. The notes avoid the word "error", which Visor takes on stderr for a failure.)
- The `init` line carries what is in effect, as Claude Code's does: `"permissionMode":"bypassPermissions"` and `"mcp_servers":[]`, whatever was asked.
- `openrouter --help`, a table in the README, and the comments in `Options.swift` say which options are taken and not acted on, and why.

**`--include-partial-messages` now does what it says.** The `stream_event` lines (`message_start`, text deltas) were printed always. They are printed with the option, as in Claude Code; without it only whole `assistant` messages are. Visor passes it.

**`--max-turns N` now does what it says.** It was taken and dropped. It sets the rounds of tool calls a turn may take (the agent's `maxRounds`, default 24), and a turn that uses them all ends with `"subtype":"error_max_turns"`, Claude Code's name for it. `StreamJSON.result` takes a `ResultKind` (`success`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_turns`) in place of a Bool.

**The parser.** `Options` moved to its own file and names every option it knows. An option it does not know is still ignored, so a host's extra switches do no harm, but is noted on stderr. An option that needs a value and has none (`--model` at the end of the line was read as a switch) and a `--max-turns` that is not a number above zero are refused with exit 2. `-h` works (it was a positional argument; the `flags.contains("h")` it was meant to reach could not be reached).

## Verified

`swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors && swift test -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` passes: 74 tests. New ones:

- Visor's manual-mode command line parses with nothing unknown and nothing taken for a prompt, and yields exactly the three notes; `bypassPermissions`, `--verbose` and `--dangerously-skip-permissions` yield none; no note contains "error".
- Unknown options are ignored and noted; commands, `-m`, `-h`, `--print` and `--name=value` parse; a missing value and five bad `--max-turns` values are refused.
- Without partial messages a turn prints `assistant` and `result` only, and the message keeps the id its log line has. A turn with `maxRounds: 2` asks twice and ends with `error_max_turns`. The `init` line has `permissionMode` and `mcp_servers`.
- By hand, with no key and a scratch `OPENROUTER_HOME`: Visor's manual-mode command line prints the three notes on stderr and the `init` line on stdout; `--max-turns 0` and a trailing `--model` exit 2; `-h` prints the help.

author: rjungemann
body:
## Summary

Continues #1010 on the open reports. Five are archived and two are narrowed, so `docs/reported/` goes from 32 open reports to 27 (28 after the one `main` added since). `main` is merged in at `622be837`, after #1010 landed.

**Archived**

- **`stm-inside-closure-captured-tvar-undeclared`**: `collect_free_vars` silently dropped every capture under an expression kind it had no case for, so the lambda was lifted with no captures. That covered `stm`, `atomically` and the `tvar/*` forms, plus `select`, dynamic `binding`, `with-handler` and `compose-handlers`.
  - Result: `(fn [] (atomically (stm (tvar/write tv 5))))` was invalid C (`'tv_5' undeclared`). Dynamic `binding` and `with-handler` over a capture failed the same way.
  - Both of the walk's `default:` cases now fall back to `cps_visit_children`.
  - Fixed alongside: the walk's two work stacks were a fixed 256 entries with no bounds check. A lambda body that is a 300-form `do` overflowed the heap inside the compiler. The stacks now grow.
  - Found on the way: `(with-handler (handler ...) body)` now elaborates to the `handle` it means. As its own node it was refused as a builtin's operand and inside a capturing lambda.
  - Found on the way: the interpreter read `HandleExpr.shallow` uninitialized on every resume through a handler value (UBSan). It is now zeroed.
  - `TUR_TRACE_EVICT` names the STM kinds instead of printing `EX_#73`.
- **`buf-puts-breaks-the-incidental-nul-invariant`**: every `Buf` append keeps `data[len] == '\0'`, and `buf.h` now documents it. A new `buf_truncate` shortens a buffer without breaking that. `buf_put_quoted` is back to `buf_puts`, the exact swap the report described:
  - `tests/spice-c-sources-tests.sh` passes 10/10.
  - With the old `buf.c` it fails with the original `strlen` heap overflow.
- **`lock-tracks-ref-not-resolved-commit`**: `tur fetch` checks out the commit `tur.lock` records, not the branch tip.
  - It first fetches the bare SHA; if the server refuses, it fetches the branch's full history and checks the commit out from there.
  - It never falls back to `:ref`. If the commit is gone, the fetch fails, names `tur fetch --update`, and removes the clone.
  - New `tur fetch --frozen` (the `npm ci` / `cargo --locked` shape) fails if the lockfile would change and never writes it.
- **`try-share-links-never-encode`**: `pako` was never loaded, so Share always failed. `web/share-codec.js` uses the browser's own `CompressionStream` with the same link format, so links minted by a build that had pako still decode. Encoding and decoding are now async.
- **`wasm-arm-suppresses-cmake-policy-min`**: fixed by a5edd6df, but never archived.

**Narrowed**

- **`emitted-c-indirect-calls-are-not-type-exact`**: the `-fsanitize=function` sweep across all fixtures went from 16 traps to 9. Seven were fixed:
  - A `nil`-returning function passed where the slot is `(fn [...] A)`. A bare function now gets a `void`-callee adapter. A capturing closure gets a `{shim, handle}` wrapper whose shim returns the zero word. The wrapper lives on the stack when the sink keeps nothing, and on the heap inside a CPS body, where the DK entry frees it. Two fixtures: `region-scope-void-body`, plus the new `nil-closure-into-erased-result`.
  - A thin call through a function value now spells a function-typed parameter `int64_t`, as the function's definition does: `annotated-fat-lambda-param`, `sf-let-bind-with-inner-call`.
  - A closure with a narrow result (`bool`, say) packed into a concrete `tur_poly_fn_t` sink now gets an adapter at any arity: `fn-value-carrier-fat-seams`, `hkt-cata-fmap-byvalue-carrier`.
  - A by-value result of 16 bytes or less, boxed for a concrete sink, now takes the typed shim on every host, not just Win64. A concrete `(fn ...)` struct field now counts as a concrete sink: `fat-dispatch-parametric-monomorph-return`, `fn-field-carrier-shim-read-typed`.
  - The remaining 9 fall into three groups, each needing a design choice; the report has the table:
    - `ptr<void>` standing in for a function type.
    - A function value stored in a generic struct field and later read by a spec.
    - The stdlib's untyped `^fat` inline-C comparators.
- **`httpd-residual-request-hardening`**: 6 of the 10 items are fixed:
  - The header scan no longer rescans the whole buffer on every `recv` (it was O(n²)).
  - The async server's writes now time out after 5 s per wait, like its reads, and close the connection on failure.
  - An oversized method or version is refused with 400, and an oversized path with 414.
  - `Connection` is parsed as a token list, so `closed` no longer counts as `close`.
  - The Basic-auth example no longer leaks which usernames exist.
  - `mw-log` escapes control bytes.

  Items 3 and 4 need a default chosen; 9 and 10 are enhancements.

- [ ] No codegen change (skip the snapshot section below)
- [x] Yes — codegen changed, snapshots regenerated in this PR

Emitted C changes only for the shapes fixed above. Regenerating every `expected.c` and the runtime split changes nothing, so this PR has no snapshot commit. `stdlib/docstrings.tur` is regenerated; it had also fallen behind other modules' docstrings.

author: brandonburr
body:
Fixes #427

## What changed

**1. Progress in the action bar.** `pipeline/progress.py` gains `reporting_steps(cb)` / `step(what)`, a context-var step reporter. `verify_driver._run_build_step` (clone, checkout, pnpm prefetch, Rust toolchain/crates prefetch, docker build) and `compile_preflight` (fetching the diff, resolving default-branch HEAD, running `compile_cmd`, re-running it over the pristine base) name each step to it. The new `prospector_app/backend/merge_progress.py` holds each live merge's current step in memory, and `GET /api/merge/pr/{n}/progress` serves it. While a live merge is in flight, `PRActionBar` polls every 2s and shows `⏳ <step>… · running since <time>` under the button.

**2. A bounded wait.** Every base-image build step now has a timeout (`BUILD_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` = 40 min). When a step runs out, it raises a `BuildFailure` that names the step and carries its partial output tail. The compile preflight records that failure and the gate blocks the merge, as it does for any build error.

**3. A record when the merge starts.** A live merge writes a `merge` Activity event with `status: "started"` and its `head_sha` before the compile preflight runs. `store-read activity pr <N>` therefore shows a merge in flight. The Activity view has a tooltip for the new status. It doesn't count as landed or failed.

**4. The two silent refusals are logged.** `merge gate:` and `pre-flight:` refusals now go to Activity as `blocked`, the same as other outcomes.

**Also:**
- A second live merge of the same PR is refused (and logged) while the first is still running.
- The action bar now always clears its spinner. If the request itself fails, it shows an error chip.

## Not done
- **Ask 5 (moving the preflight off the click path into a job):** this changes the architecture, so it's left for a supervised decision.
- **Containers can outlive a timeout:** when a `docker run` step times out, killing the CLI may leave the container running until it exits on its own. `docker build` is cancelled when its client disconnects.

## Tests
- New `prospector_app/backend/tests/test_executor_merge_progress.py` covers:
  - both refusals are logged
  - `started` comes before `merged`
  - steps are visible while the merge runs
  - a second merge of the same PR is refused
  - progress is cleared when the merge raises
- New tests in `pipeline/tests/test_progress.py` (reporter scoping, a failing reporter) and `test_verify_driver.py` (the timeout's message and default, a step reaching the reporter).
- Local gates: pytest 5263 passed; ruff clean; pyright 0 errors; `pnpm run build` passes; eslint reports nothing on the changed files.

author: stephenlutar2-hash
body:
## What was measured on `main`

`weighted_geometric_mean` against the 60 szl.lambda/v1 golden vectors: **25/60** — every valid value correct; 10 invalid inputs returned a value; 25 raised a `GateError` with prose only, so a receipt could not say *why* the gate refused. Separately, `True` was accepted and read as `1.0` (bool is an int subclass; the contract says it is not a number). Measured by [szl-evidence-core](https://github.com/szl-holdings/szl-evidence-core) `lambda-divergence`.

## What is deliberately not changed

This function is **wider than the contract by design**: values above 1 are allowed (it is homogeneous of degree 1, `G(c·x) = c·G(x)`, and the existing tests pin that) and weights are normalised by their sum. Those are the 10 "returned a value" vectors and they are not bugs here. `AxisEvidence` enforces the contract's `[0, 1]` domain for the governance gate, so `evaluate_lambda_gate`'s Λ agrees with the v1 reference within `1e-12` — now pinned by a test on the spec's `nominal` golden vector (`value_f64 3fed3035e27f23fe`).

## What changes

- `GateError` gains a `.code` (contract code or `None`), keeping the message.
- Every refusal names its code **in contract precedence**: `LAMBDA_EMPTY` › `LENGTH_MISMATCH` › `TYPE_INVALID` › `NONFINITE_AXIS` › `AXIS_OUT_OF_RANGE` › `NONFINITE_WEIGHT` › `WEIGHT_NONPOSITIVE` — so the code does not depend on which fault appears first in the sequence, and a zero axis beside an invalid one reports the invalid one rather than vetoing.
- `bool` and other non-reals are rejected (`LAMBDA_TYPE_INVALID`).
- `math.fsum` replaces `sum` for axis-order invariance (values may move by one ulp; the existing `places=12` assertions hold).

## Evidence

`python/tests`: 236 → **240 passed, 92 subtests** (4 new: codes in precedence, zero-does-not-mask-invalid, bool rejection, gate path equals v1 reference).

## Boundary

Λ remains Conjecture 1 (`lambdaNeverATheorem` untouched). No digest, receipt or threshold changes.

author: arggon
body:
Implements **task-cleanup-declared-services** (ADR 0019 layer 2, parent story `parallel-worktree-runtime-isolation-ports-state-services`). Do NOT merge — coordinator review first.

## Manifest shape (ADR 0019 left it open — decided minimally, recorded)

A single scalar declaration in the tracker `.convention.yml`:

```yaml
x-worktree:
  services: true    # the per-worktree project IS <repo>-<item-id> (compose name: "${ARGGON_WORKTREE_ID:-}")
  services: myapp   # pattern-doc naming (name: "myapp${WORKTREE_SUFFIX:-}") → project <base>-<repo>-<item-id>
  services: false   # (or absent) → nothing declared: cleanup never invokes Docker
```

Rationale: the reaper needs only the project **name** — `docker compose -p <name> down` resolves the project through container labels, no Compose file and no YAML parsing — so the declaration is exactly that name (ADR 0019: "the pattern is a name and a manifest"). The base is validated at parse time against Compose's project alphabet (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`); derivation lowercases the whole name (Compose lowercases project names — verified live, Docker 29.7.2, 2026-10-01). Recorded in `convention.md` §Worktree bootstrap.

## Reap semantics

- For each **removable** entry (done/cancelled + merged branch — unchanged qualification), BEFORE `git worktree remove`: `docker compose -p <project> down -v --remove-orphans`, cwd = repo root, bounded 120s. Covers stale-record residue (dir gone, stack possibly alive).
- **Already-gone project** = graceful no-op: the same command exits 0 with a "No resource found to remove" warning (verified live: Docker 29.7.2 / Compose 5.5.1, 2026-10-01) — no probing.
- **Absent docker CLI (ENOENT)** = report-only degradation for the run: `compose.dockerUnavailable: true` in `--json`, a `note:` line in human output, never a failure.
- **Reap failure** (e.g. daemon down): per-item, non-fatal, on BOTH surfaces — `pruned[].action: "failed"` + `error` AND `failures[]` (the #515 bounded-envelope discipline, `boundedEnvelopeText`); the worktree/branch/record pruning still proceeds; exit code stays 0 (task-cleanup-json-exit-code unchanged).
- **Preservation**: with a declaration present the executor sees EXACTLY the derived names — the primary checkout's own project and any undeclared adopter project are never passed to Docker; with no declaration Docker is never spawned at all (kernel never probes/invokes what the convention didn't declare).

## Payload (additive within schemaVersion: 1)

`cleanup --json` gains `compose: { declared: "true" | "<base>", dockerUnavailable?: true }`, present only when the repo declares services; successful reaps surface as `pruned` entries `reaped compose project <name>`. The MCP `arggon_cleanup` tool spawns the CLI, so it inherits the behavior.

## Impact class

**Behavioral** ([ADR 0016](ArggonManager/docs/adr/0016-adopter-upgrade-channel.md)): a new `x-worktree.services` convention key and an additive `cleanup --json` field — agents/adopters re-learn both. Skill sources untouched (copies stay byte-equal). Docs updated in the same PR: README cleanup section, `convention.md`, `json-output.md` (prettier-clean), `worktree-services.md` ("Planned" row → Shipped + §4 paragraph).

## Evidence

- `npm test` — 2081 passed (9 new compose-reap tests: no-declaration no-invocation, canonical + base derivation, adopter preservation, ENOENT degradation, both-surface failure, stale-residue reap + already-gone no-op, CLI envelope, human no-docker end-to-end on a docker-less PATH; plus convention parse + lib derive units). CI-safe: no daemon needed anywhere.
- `npm run lint` green; `npm run build` green; `npm run check:plugin` green (kernel modules are inlined into the vendored bundle → regen commit `chore: regen plugin bundle`, as prescribed); `npm run smoke:native-start-cold` green; `npm run arggon -- validate` ok:true.

## Findings for review

1. **Native parity gap (follow-up):** the OpenCode plugin's `nativeCleanup` keeps its own prune loop and does NOT reap Compose (safe by construction — report-only path). Deliberately out of scope per the item's file fences; the derive helper (`worktreeComposeProject`) is exported from the kernel so the plugin can adopt it trivially.
2. `worktree.test.ts`: hoisted the `initCleanupRepo` fixture to module scope (shared by the new describe) — no behavior change.

author: ivankoelho
body:
## Objetivo
Fase 3A da integração X2: **descoberta assíncrona de pedidos** para oportunidades convertidas antes de o pedido existir (o X2 é D-1), **apuração do frete** e **correção da comparação de data**. Nota de design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-fase-3a-xprocess-descoberta-design.md`.

## Descoberta
O job diário (`RunXProcessReconciliation`, depois da varredura dos vínculos) procura, por documento (`/api/clientes` → `cod_cliente` → `/api/vendas`), o pedido de oportunidades **convertidas, sem nenhum vínculo, convertidas há no máximo 7 dias**.

Só vincula automaticamente quando **todas** as regras valem:
- status do pedido `SEPARACAO`, `SEPARADO` ou `FECHADO` (`CANCELADO` nunca abre vínculo novo);
- `data_venda.Date >= data de abertura da oportunidade` (por data, fuso da Bahia);
- nenhum vínculo já rastreia o pedido;
- vendedor **só veta**: o dono tem `XProcessSellerCode`, o pedido traz `cod_vendedor` e eles diferem → fora; sem código de um dos lados, não bloqueia;
- **exatamente 1 pedido candidato e exatamente 1 oportunidade elegível** entre as oportunidades do mesmo documento (de qualquer contato; CPF repetido é permitido desde a Fase 2). 0 ou mais de 1 de qualquer lado → nada é vinculado e o pedido segue como candidato manual;
- lista de `/api/vendas` com exatamente 1000 linhas é tratada como possivelmente truncada → nunca associa automaticamente (a API não tem paginação nem ordem garantida);
- oportunidade aberta nunca é vinculada nem convertida; a descoberta **nunca substitui, desfaz ou edita um vínculo existente**.

Ao vincular (transação): vínculo `link_source=auto` com `match_reason`, ponteiro na oportunidade e evento `xprocess_linked`; em seguida a reconciliação normal roda na mesma rodada (status, `realized_value`, frete). A oportunidade continua `convertida` com `conversion_source=manual`.

## Vínculo manual e candidatos
- `PUT …/xprocess-link` aceita oportunidade `convertida` (antes só `aberta`); recusa (409) um pedido já vinculado a outra oportunidade.
- A lista de candidatos também funciona para `convertida`.
- **Correção de data:** a comparação passa a ser por data. `data_venda` é sempre `T00:00:00`, então uma venda do mesmo dia da abertura era descartada.

## Um pedido nunca alimenta duas oportunidades
Índice único parcial `idx_sales_opp_xlink_open_order` (organização, `cod_empresa`, `num_pedido`) em vínculos abertos, **criado só se não houver duplicados** (o upgrade não falha por dado antigo; testado em cópia de banco existente, com e sem duplicados), mais checagens na aplicação e uma guarda na reconciliação.

## Frete
`vl_frete` passa a ser lido; a soma por pedido vai para `valor_frete` no vínculo e aparece junto do pedido (painel do contato e formulário X2 da oportunidade). **Nunca entra em `valor_vendido` nem em `realized_value`.** Sem relatório de frete.

## Schema (aditivo, `sales_opportunity_xprocess_links`)
`valor_frete numeric` (nullable), `link_source varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'agent'` (vínculos existentes ficam `agent`), `match_reason text`, índice acima. Tipo de evento novo `xprocess_linked`. **Nenhuma permissão nova.**

## Fora desta entrega
`/api/separacoes-produtos`; sincronização de vendedores com usuários; `realized_quantity` automática; mapeamento Unit ↔ loja X2 (Fase 3B); correção de `consecutive_not_found` (por dia, marca de rodada persistida), que é independente do reconciliador. O "motivo de não ter vinculado sozinho" na lista de candidatos **não** foi incluído.

## Testes
- `xprocess_discovery_test.go`: 17 testes (mais subcasos) com um servidor X2 simulado **no formato real coletado** (`vl_frete`, `data_venda` à meia-noite, `CANCELADO`, lista de 1000 linhas): vínculo único; venda do mesmo dia; idempotência; cada trava (data, cancelado, dois pedidos, fora da janela, cliente ausente, lista truncada, vendedor divergente); vendedor só veta; aberta intocada; ambiguidade entre contatos com o mesmo CPF; a data elimina outra oportunidade; oportunidade antiga e sem vínculo não bloqueia; pedido já rastreado; sem documento não chama o X2; isolamento entre organizações; fuso; guarda da reconciliação; vínculo manual em convertida; 409; candidatos em convertida.
- `pkg/xprocess`: 2 testes (frete somado à parte do total; frete ausente ou inválido vale zero).
- `go build` e `go vet`: OK. `vue-tsc`: OK; Vitest 47/47; ESLint nos arquivos alterados: sem avisos; `npm run build`: OK.

A suíte Go continua com somente as 3 falhas já conhecidas, que não vêm desta fase: `TestServeLoginBackground_RejectsSymlink` e `TestApp_ServeMedia_RejectsSymlink` (limitação do Windows ao criar symlink; também falham em `development`) e `TestUpdateContactChatbotMessage_SetsTimestampAndResetsReminder` (pré-existente e intermitente).

**O E2E de navegador não foi executado**, e a descoberta não foi exercitada contra o X2 real (só contra servidor simulado com o formato das amostras reais).

- lang 파일에 세 명령을 추가한다. 첫 `$string` 줄 위 CodeLens, 전구(Refactor) 메뉴, 명령 팔레트로 실행하고, 언어와 무관하게 모든 lang 파일에서 동작한다.
  - **알파벳순 정렬**: UTF-16 코드 단위 비교, 안정 정렬, 저장. 위 주석·빈 줄·꼬리 주석은 문자열을 따라가고, 머리말과 deprecated 주석 뒤는 제자리.
  - **영어 파일 순서로 정렬**(영어가 아닌 파일): `lang/en` 같은 파일의 키 순서, 없는 키는 맨 뒤. 저장.
  - **누락 번역 추가**(영어가 아닌 파일): 영어에만 있는 문자열을 위 주석과 함께 파일 끝에. 저장하지 않음.
- MDLCode 1.6.3의 `sortStringsAlphabetically`·`sortStringsInOrderOfEn`·`addMissingTranslations` 규칙(구간 계산, 삽입 위치, 개행 처리, 문법 오류 시 무동작, 버튼 위치)을 그대로 따른다.
- 버튼은 `csmscode.strings.sortCodeLens`로 끈다. 버전 0.31.0.

## 검증
- MDLCode 알고리즘을 php-parser 위에 옮긴 재현본과 글자 단위 비교: `csms45`·`dghulxp` lang 파일 2,586개(영어 쌍 1,373개)와 경계 사례를 섞은 무작위 파일 33,000개에서 차이 0건.
- 정렬로 바뀌는 실제 파일 864개는 정렬 전후를 PHP로 실행한 `$string` 배열이 같다.
- 단위 테스트 747개 통과. 통합 테스트(버튼·명령)는 CI에서 돈다.

author: manuaudio
body:
Fixes #14000.

`omarchy-install-gaming-retroarch` always writes `video_driver = "vulkan"`. RetroArch treats a Vulkan context it can't create as fatal, so on a GPU with no Vulkan device it never starts. In the report, an iMac12,2 has a Radeon HD 6770M on the legacy `radeon` driver and an HD 3000, and RetroArch logs `[Vulkan] Failed to enumerate physical devices`.

An installed ICD isn't a usable device. `install/hardware/vulkan.sh` picks Vulkan drivers by `lspci` vendor string, so that iMac has `radeon_icd.json` and `intel_icd.json` while neither GPU enumerates. For the same reason, `omarchy-hw-vulkan`, which only checks for ICD files, isn't enough here.

The installer now:

- adds `vulkan-tools` to its package list
- keeps `vulkan` when `vulkaninfo --summary` reports an integrated, discrete or virtual GPU
- otherwise writes `glcore`. The reporter confirmed `glcore` starts on that machine and keeps the Slang shader backend, so the `crt-royale` preset the installer configures still applies.

A CPU-only device (lavapipe) is deliberately not treated as Vulkan support. RetroArch would start on it, but software Vulkan is far slower than the GPU's OpenGL.

### Testing

New `test/shell.d/retroarch-install-test.sh` runs the real installer in a temporary `HOME`, with `omarchy-pkg-add` and `nautilus` stubbed and `vulkaninfo` stubbed per case:

- integrated and discrete GPU → `vulkan`
- CPU-only device → `glcore`
- no device (`vulkaninfo` exits 1, as it does here with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` pointing nowhere) → `glcore`

The `glcore` cases fail against the previous installer. Shellcheck is clean. On this machine (Alder Lake UHD), `vulkaninfo --summary` reports `PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_INTEGRATED_GPU`, so it keeps `vulkan`. I don't have the iMac hardware, so the `glcore` result on that GPU comes from the reporter's own test.
