## Why

A backend function approval returns a tool reference with `type: "function"`. The SDK rejected that response because `ToolApproval.tool` accepted only built-in and MCP references. This also prevented `resume_chat()` from reaching the resume endpoint.

## Scope

Add `FunctionToolReference` and `ToolExecutionReference` for approval response data. Keep approval policy overrides restricted to `ToolReference`, so functions still use the default chat approval policy.

## Verification

- Regression tests parse function approvals through synchronous and asynchronous HTTP clients.
- Runtime validation and a negative typing fixture reject function policy overrides.

author: apojomovsky
body:
Closes #840

Cycle-count bench ladder: 15 kernels plus a PID scenario and per-core
interrupt cost, timed in `crates/sim` between volatile marker stores,
gated by a checked-in `cycle_baseline.toml` with the size ladder's
semantics (fail on growth, `STRICT_CYCLE_BASELINE` headroom in CI,
`CYCLE_BASELINE_ONLY`-scoped updates, `SPEED_REPORT_JSON` dump with
flash words per kernel for tooling). Every row is baselined under both
`-Os` and `-O2` (68 rows), using the profile mechanism #866 added.

Markers are plain volatile stores (`bench_mark` 1/2, address off
`--map`), so the private comparison times the identical binary shape
in MPLAB SIM off the same MAP file. Kernels are strict C99
(`gcc -std=c99 -fsyntax-only` clean, modulo freestanding `void main`,
the repo-wide fixture convention) with volatile inputs and sinks
pinning the work between the marks under both profiles.

Selected `-Os` cycles (PIC18 / PIC14): mul-u8 18/128, mul-u16 40/332,
mul-u32 110/689, divmod-u8 308/356, divmod-u16 650/752,
divmod-u32 2044/2676, shift 590/540, memcpy-32 2587/3739,
memset-32 1534/2239, strlen-strcmp 2289/2730, crc16 13704/17594,
switch16 98/73, struct-scan 406/534, u16-dec 1838/2808,
pid-step 313/1289, scen-pid-update 776 (PIC18),
isr-latency 39/24, isr-roundtrip 83/49. `-O2` differs where shaping
pays: divmod-u8 300, divmod-u16 634, switch16 74, scen-pid-update 736,
strlen-strcmp 2081, pid-step 305.

Trust the ruler (hand checks against the asm): PIC18 u16 multiply
measured 39, hand count 39 (MULWF 1, MOVFF/CALL/RETURN 2, single-word
1); PIC14 copy measured 5, hand count 5. No sim cost-model defect
found, none filed.

Deferred (not dropped): menu-tick and control-pass scenarios hang in
the sim on `epic_tick_delay_ms` spinning for a timer flag the sim does
not model (probed to `gpio4_delay_us`, same unmodeled class as #859).
Filed as #873 (dispatch-only, sub-issue of #835, blocked by #859)
rather than fixed here, per the coordination note on this ticket.

## Review

Reviewer: `CycleLadderReview` (separate agent, no stake in the change).
Question: does this ladder measure what it claims
(volatile-marker-pinned cycles with folding-proof fixtures,
deterministic sync-based ISR injection, profile-aware Os/O2 baselines
with size-ladder-identical update/strict/report semantics) without
breaking repo gates (rustfmt, check-warnings, prose rules, C99-plain
kernels)? Budget: expected 15 min, hard limit 45 min.

Findings:

- Advisory: bare ISR case names passed `CYCLE_BASELINE_ONLY`
  validation but match no measured row (rows exist only as
  `-latency`/`-roundtrip`), so an update run would recompile the whole
  ladder and change nothing. Resolved: the filter now seeds only the
  suffixed keys for `Kind::Isr` rows; verified bare names fail fast
  pre-measurement and a scoped single-row update reports no changes.

No blocking findings.

author: yovermarkt
body:
## Qué es

Bloque 2 del plan aprobado por el dueño (2026-10-01): **un staging en internet**, el mismo servidor en un entorno «staging» de Railway contra su propia base (Supabase gratis), por unos 3 USD/mes ya aprobados. Sirve para dos cosas:

- que el dueño revise los cambios **en su teléfono**;
- que los desarrolladores de las apps Flutter tengan un servidor de pruebas, porque nunca se desarrolla contra producción.

Este PR es el **código**. La infraestructura (proyecto de Supabase, entorno de Railway y variables) se crea después de fusionarlo, con las credenciales fuera del repositorio.

## Cambios

- **`UMBANI_ENTORNO=staging`** (`esStaging`):
  - la franja STAGING también se pinta en Railway;
  - **la tarjeta nunca cobra de verdad**: con `PAYPHONE_MODO=produccion` el staging se queda sin tarjeta.
- 🔐 **El candado de la base** (`config/identidad-de-la-base.ts`): antes de abrir el puerto, y por tanto antes de las tareas de fondo, se le pregunta a la base quién es (`server_settings.entorno`, fuera de `ALLOWED_KEYS`):
  - un staging sin marca **no arranca**;
  - producción con marca **no arranca**;
  - si la base no responde, el staging no arranca y producción sí.
  - Comprobado de verdad: sin la marca, el staging sale con código 1.
- **Permisos de la siembra:** antes se devolvía todo también a `anon`. Eso deshacía los 135 `revoke` de las funciones del dinero y abría `server_settings` a la clave pública. Ahora solo reciben permisos `postgres` y `service_role`.
- **`staging-remoto.mjs`** tiene tres órdenes: `preparar` (con guardia triple para no tocar nunca producción), `subir` (despliega la rama en revisión) y `humo`.

## Verificación

- 49/49 recorridos con el candado y los permisos estrictos.
- 3675/3675 pruebas, de las cuales 14 son nuevas del candado, la franja, la tarjeta en staging y el guardián del orden del arranque.
- Lint sin errores, tipos y knip en verde.

## Qué NO toca

- El esquema y las migraciones: la marca solo la pone la semilla del staging.
- Producción solo cambia en una cosa: antes de abrir el puerto lee una fila de `server_settings` (~30 ms). Su base no lleva marca, así que arranca igual.

author: betweentwomidnights
body:
Continuation was the slow path testers kept hitting (5 minutes on an 8060S). Profiling a gary4juce-shaped `/continue` on the 5070 Laptop showed most of the cost was work whose result was discarded, not model math. This trims that, without changing what the model computes.

8-bar audio continuation of a 25 s clip, Q4_K_M, both adapters:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA | 46.1 s | 31.1 s |
| Vulkan | 37.1 s | 32.2 s |

Natural length (180 s ceiling, 204 s returned) on Vulkan: 169 s → 153 s. At that length the remaining cost is the length itself, adapter overhead and flow attention, which are the next round.

**What changed**

- **Planning margin covers only added bars.** `planning_overrun` multiplied a continuation's whole target, prefix included: a 10-bar clip continued by 8 planned 36 bars. Now 26.
- **CUDA's KV cache grows in 1024-row buckets.** CUDA decode attends over every allocated row so it can replay graphs, and planning allocated its 9000-token budget up front: ~10k masked rows per token, and planning ran at half Vulkan's speed on the same GPU. Other backends allocate as before.
- **Only the logits a phase can sample are computed.** Semantic decode needs 32,769 of 184,704 rows (one contiguous run). lm_head was a tenth of each decode step, plus a 740 KB copy per token.
- **The LoRA `scale` op is skipped at 1.0.** That's both shipped adapters: ~200 no-op kernels in every decode step and flow evaluation.
- **The flow writes its K/V into the AR cache in place** instead of concatenating the whole cache in every layer of every ODE evaluation. Bit-identical.
- **Every job logs a one-line timing summary** (no debug variable), for testers to paste from gary4local's log.

**A CUDA bug this surfaced:** at a KV length that's a multiple of 256, ggml-cuda decodes with its vector FA kernel, which replays wrong logits from a captured graph (top-1 disagreed with CPU on 30% of steps). The cache stays off those lengths. That's also what broke the 256-rounded window tried before v0.2.0, which was blamed on partial views.

**Verification**

- `ctest`: 16/16.
- Teacher-forced 1900+400 tokens with the instrumental adapter, against CPU: CUDA max |Δlogit| 0.41 (was 0.41), Vulkan 0.36 (was 0.36). Repeated CUDA sessions in one process agree exactly; before the 256 fix they didn't.
- The flow change and the logit slice are bit-identical end to end on Vulkan (output hash unchanged with the other changes toggled off). The scale skip lets Vulkan fuse matmul+add, which moves logits by ≤0.004.
- The flow fixture test (`yue2-flow-test`) crashes on main too; its fixture is a 1.3 KB stub. Not touched here.

author: as19git67
body:
After a photoTAN during the statement fetch, an account that was linked long ago showed up under "Noch nicht zugeordnete Bank-Konten". Both causes sit on the resume path only, and in the reported case the first one triggered the second.

## What happened (from the production log)

The bank reported four accounts, all as `Miscellaneous`: a giro, a savings account, a depot under the giro's account number, and a credit card. The fetch did the giro, then paused on the savings account for a coupled TAN with the depot and the card queued. After the TAN, the queue entry for the depot (`number:Miscellaneous`) resolved to the first record with that number, the giro, so the giro was fetched a second time and the depot not at all. Persist then saw one snapshot for that number whose kind (`sonstige`) matched neither linked account exactly; without the depot snapshot to claim its own row, two candidates were left and the giro was reported as unknown.

## 1. The paused account and the queue resolved to the wrong record

- New `bankAccountKey()` = `number:type:subAccountId`, used for the paused account (`pendingTan.accountKey`, stored as `fetch_context.currentAccountNumber`) and for the queue.
- `findBankAccount()` resolves those keys and still accepts the older `number` / `number:type` entries of sessions that are already open.

## 2. Persist's fallback depended on which snapshots were in the batch

When no candidate matches a snapshot's kind exactly, persist falls back to the sole unclaimed `finance_account` with that number. A resume only carries the accounts behind the pause, so a sibling that would have claimed the other candidate can be missing.

- `FetchResult.bankAccountKinds` lists every bank-side account with its effective kind (from `runFetchAccounts` and `resumeFetchAfterTan`).
- The fallback no longer offers a candidate whose kind belongs to a sibling account with the same number. Without that information it still refuses to guess.

## Tests
- `finance/fints-client.test.ts`: pause stores keys that tell same-number accounts apart; resume continues on the record it paused on; the production order (giro, savings with TAN, depot under the giro's number) fetches the depot after the TAN, not the giro again; a queue entry from an older session still resolves.
- `finance/statement-persist.test.ts`: a lone resume snapshot matches its account once sibling kinds are known; without them it stays unknown.
- No new `tsc` errors in the touched files.

## Known unrelated failure
`npm run test` in the cloud sandbox: 361 of 362 files green. `trip-planner/plans-reach.test.ts` fails with 4–6 "Test timed out in 5000ms": each of those tests takes about 4.6–5.5 s there (all eight pass with `--testTimeout=60000`), and it fails the same way on unmodified `main`. This PR touches nothing under `trip-planner/`; the slow tests need their own fix.

author: ashplayer-1415
body:
Two commits, squash-merged into one: the change, then the release.

0.1.21 read an agent's trace from a file. Most production agents are someone's own wrapper, in any language, and many run where handing over a file is the wrong shape, so `assurance serve` takes what they send and answers what a workflow asks.

**What changes.**

- `assurance serve` listens on 127.0.0.1:4318, where OTLP/HTTP exporters send by default:
  - `POST /v1/traces`: OpenTelemetry traces as any OTLP/HTTP exporter sends them, protobuf or JSON, gzipped or chunked;
  - `POST /v1/runs`: run record lines, as JSON lines, one object or an array, each naming its run, with what it would not take said line by line;
  - `GET /v1/runs` lists the runs; `GET /v1/runs/<id>` is `assurance audit --json` of one, with a `verdict`: the gates it fails and, for those `?fail_on=` names, whether it passes. `?format=text` gives the report as text.
- What it is sent is kept as it came, in two files in its store (`~/.local/state/assurance/runs` by default, `--store` for another), and each audit reads them with the readers `assurance audit` uses. The command and the endpoint share one `audit` and one `failed_gates`, so an exit code and a verdict cannot disagree.
- It asks for no credentials, and says so when told to listen beyond this machine; it takes at most 32 MB a request, before and after gzip; its files are the user's alone; it queues 128 connections, not socketserver's 5.
- OTLP protobuf is read without a protobuf package (`assurance_budget.otlp_protobuf`).
- The `assurance` command forwards `serve` and lists it on its start screen (cli 0.6.4); mcp 0.5.4 only raises its cli floor, by the sibling-floor rule.

**Checked:**
- The official Python OTLP exporter's own requests, captured and kept in `tests/fixtures/otel`, decode to the same spans protobuf's own library reads from them. The SDK job now also sends the official exporter's protobuf, gzipped, to the endpoint, where a skip fails.
- Live: a Python agent on the OpenAI SDK, traced by OpenTelemetry's instrumentation and sent by the official exporter (protobuf, gzip); a Node.js agent sent by the official JS exporter (JSON); and run records by curl. Each was audited: the Python agent's "The tests pass." held against its failed `pytest -q`, the Node agent's claim with nothing against it, the curl run's claim held against its failed `make check`; and `curl … | jq -e .verdict.passed` stopped on the curl run.
- 23 tests in `test_serve.py`: every endpoint and refusal, gzip, chunked, a gzip bomb, an exporter's retry read once, eight agents sending at once, the files' mode, and every gate failing, with each exit code agreeing with the verdict. `--fail-on-loop` had no test before. 31 deliberate breaks of the change, each caught; four needed sharper tests first. A concurrency test was once reset with socketserver's queue of 5 on macOS, and not again in six reruns, so the queue's size is held by an assertion of its own.
- Full suite on 3.12: 1661 passed; on 3.10: 1641 passed, 22 skipped. `mypy --strict` clean on every package; `claude plugin validate` passes for the plugin and the marketplace. All four packages built and `twine check` passes; installed fresh on Python 3.12 and 3.10, `assurance serve` took the official exporter's requests and answered with the verdict.
- Not yet: it has no authentication of its own, so it is for one machine, or behind something that authenticates; and each audit reads the store's files whole, which suits one machine's runs, not a fleet's.

After merge: tag `budget-v0.2.17`, `cli-v0.6.4` and `mcp-v0.5.4`, and once they are on PyPI, `assurance-v0.1.22`.

author: marcus-levin
body:
Sanitized facts can still identify a fictional site through a rare combination. This adds an offline shadow evaluator that measures local and scripted-judge true/false flags, misses and abstentions, and returns generalization recommendations with no policy authority.

The development corpus contains 39 synthetic records: 33 evaluated cases, six background records, 16 distinct sites and eight quasi-identifier dimensions. Every handle occurs in another record. Combination keys include both dimension and handle; reports and judge requests exclude those handles and site references. Only the module-issued question set is accepted. Foreign tenants, malformed input and judge failures refuse or abstain conservatively. Recommendations never transform content, release bytes or choose policy.

An independent native Pi reviewer approved source `8cbdec964928895b6b2c9dd3dfc8c661d8c8b34c` after reproducing and verifying the earlier corrections. Validation: 28 focused groups and 618 repository tests passed, with build, typecheck, fixture guard, dependency audit, real SBOM and all 17 synthetic release cases. Coverage for this module was 100% lines, 93.03% branches and 100% functions. Independent probes re-derived 40/40 count combinations and found no singleton handles or verdict changes across the correction.

This advances #12 with development evidence only. The judge is a local script; no hosted-model quality, real population risk, utility, latency, cost or held-out score is claimed. A risk flag can have no actionable recommendation when every candidate dimension is universal. Tenant-reference shape is bounded, while trusted integrations must still mint privacy-safe references. Human promotion, real external-judge authorization and #39 custody/freeze remain open.

A separate native Pi reviewer approved published head `2676dfe6c5ea749d4c2cc58fcc1131f26ff5cf35` and independently verified exact tree/blob equality with the approved source. [CI run 36966943199](https://github.com/Marcus-Levin/hylja/actions/runs/36966943199) passed. This new PR remains open for human review.

Publication uses the GitHub connector because local Git push authentication is unavailable. Published tree `411a74ab135870c5e6300e45d2bbb4efdf5dd2ef` exactly matches local authored head `8cbdec964928895b6b2c9dd3dfc8c661d8c8b34c`; the connector changes commit identity.

author: wilmergaspar
body:
## Motivo

Un análisis real de MIRI (`jw01192006001_03105_00002_mirimage_cal`, F1000W) con **93 fuentes puntuales** salía `needs_spectrum` y marcado como candidato, aunque las fuentes puntuales solas bastan para pasar el FDR. Además se pidió: elementos intuitivos, detección de patrones sin alucinar, una biblioteca de firmas de radio y una ventana Fibonacci con alerta.

## Cambios (`CHANGES.md` 52–60)

### Semáforo de descubrimiento (`discovery.py`)
- **Niveles:** 🔴 no válido · ⚪ sin estructura · 🟠 sin confirmar · 🟡 explicado por un confusor · 🟢 estructura robusta · 🟣 alerta de pionero.
- **Regla clave:** una comprobación que no se pudo hacer cuenta como **no superada**. Sin esta regla, el JSON de MIRI salía 🟢.
- **Fuentes puntuales enmascaradas** y FDR repetido:
  - ruido + estrellas: de hasta 3/4 a 0/4 tras enmascarar;
  - filamentos + estrellas: tras enmascarar da lo mismo que los filamentos solos.
- **Otras comprobaciones:** réplica con otra semilla, picos de difracción, artefactos, zonas vacías y procedencia.
- **Novedad:** se mide frente a JSON previos que sube el usuario (mínimo 5).
- **JSON:** `is_candidate` sigue al semáforo.

### Ventana Fibonacci / φ (`golden.py`)
- **Ángulo áureo (137.508°)** entre fuentes, con nulo por permutación:
  - espiral de Vogel: p ≤ 0.004;
  - puntos al azar: p = 0.12–0.71.
- **Razones φ/φ²** entre picos del espectro radial, con nulo de picos al azar:
  - la primera versión **no distinguía φ de 3/2** y se descartó;
  - ahora solo cuentan los pares resolubles a ±5 %;
  - con 1024 px: φ p = 0.001, 3/2 p = 0.41–0.46, ruido p = 0.83–1.0.

### Señales de radio (`radio_signals.py`, `radio_page.py`, nuevo modo en `app.py`)
- **Biblioteca de firmas** generadas por su ecuación física: púlsar, ráfaga dispersada (K_DM = 4.148808 ms GHz² pc⁻¹ cm³), portadora con deriva Doppler y RFI (DM = 0, deriva 0).
- **Detectores calibrados** (durante la calibración se encontraron y corrigieron cuatro errores, detallados en CHANGES 59):

  | Detector | Calibración medida |
  |---|---|
  | Periodicidad | 1.2 % de falsas alarmas (nominal 1 %), ruido rojo 1/100, púlsar 20/20 |
  | Dispersión | ruido 2/110, DM recuperado 497–503 sobre 500 |
  | Deriva | ruido 0/20, derivas exactas 5/5 |

- **Periodo** con incertidumbre por plegado (error real ≤ 0.33 σ); el cruce con catálogos CSV (ATNF psrcat, CHIME/FRB) usa esa incertidumbre.
- **Catálogos públicos:** se enlazan; la app no se conecta a ellos.

## Pruebas
- `pytest tests`: 76 pasan, incluido el nuevo `tests/test_discovery_golden_radio.py`.
- App en navegador, modo imagen: la simulación MIRI de estrellas sale 🟡 (6/7 comprobaciones) y las pestañas φ y Novedad funcionan.
- App en navegador, modo radio: los 5 ejemplos de la biblioteca se clasifican bien; la carga de CSV y .npy y el cruce con catálogo funcionan; sin excepciones.

author: cantona
body:
## What

Adds `direction = "auto"`. A fixed split direction only fits one screen: an agent pane that is wide on a landscape monitor is tall on a portrait one, and splitting it right leaves two columns too narrow to read a diff in.

With `auto`, each time a review opens (`review_changes` and `show_changes`, both through `herdr::open_review_pane`), the server runs `herdr pane layout --pane $HERDR_PANE_ID` and splits:

- `right` when the pane is at least twice as wide as tall in cells (`CELL_ASPECT = 2`, since a cell is about twice as tall as wide);
- `down` otherwise.

That splits along the longer side, so both halves stay closer to square. The pane is measured at open time, not at startup, so moving the session between screens needs no restart.

If herdr can't report the size (nonzero exit, non-JSON output, pane missing, rect without width/height), the tool call returns that error and no pane is opened. That is the same path a failed `herdr plugin pane open` takes. The handoff socket is still removed in `prepare_handoff`. I chose failing over falling back to a guessed side so a broken layout call shows up instead of being hidden.

`herdr pane layout --pane` and its `result.layout.panes[].rect` shape are present in herdr v0.8.0 (`src/cli/pane.rs`, `src/api/schema/panes.rs`), the plugin's `min_herdr_version`. The default stays `right`, and `right`/`down` configs make no extra herdr call.

## How was it tested

- [x] `cargo test` passes locally: 197 tests. New tests cover:
  - the 2:1 boundary (`160x80` splits right, `159x80` down);
  - picking the pane by id;
  - unusable layout output (non-JSON, missing width/height, error exit);
  - `open_review_pane` passing the measured direction to `--direction`;
  - no `plugin pane open` after a failed measurement. Replacing the `?` with `unwrap_or("right")` makes that test fail.
- [x] Tested the review loop live in herdr 0.9.1: I ran `tests/e2e/mcp_client.py` with `direction = "auto"` on a 160x86 agent pane. The server called `pane layout --pane wX:p1`, opened the pane with `--direction down`, the pane connected, and the review timed out as configured. I also ran it with a `herdr` wrapper whose `pane layout` exits 1: the tool returned `isError: true` with herdr's error text, no pane opened, and the socket file was removed. A live `right` split was not exercised because no wide pane was available. Unit tests cover that branch.

## Checklist

- [x] Build is warning-free (`cargo build --release --locked`)
- [x] Docs updated: `direction` row in `docs/configuration.md`
- [x] No code copied from AGPL sources (e.g. annot)

author: blairham
body:
Refs #5157. That issue stays open: the file's next front is `disable -r`, which is the parked #5267.

All rows were measured against zsh 5.9.2 (`/opt/homebrew/bin/zsh -f`) on 2026-10-02.

1. **`typeset -h +g -m '*'` in a function makes a local of every name a listing writes.** This includes the produced parameters and the tables: `argv`, `pipestatus`, `keymaps`, `SECONDS`. After `unset -m '*'`, a bare `typeset` lists only what the function declares next, which is exactly the file's first chunk. Without `+g`, a match is still reached where it is.
2. **Under `POSIX_BUILTINS`, `readonly -p` uses the standard's form.** It writes `readonly name=value` for scalars and lists no arrays or tables at all, so zsh's own read-only tables drop out of the listing. zsh's `readonly` is `typeset -r` under another name, so it never reached `ReadonlyListing`. It now does, and the option moves that axis.
3. **`typeset -p` takes a layout number.**
   - `-p1` writes an array, a table or a tied array one element per line, two spaces in, and `=()` when empty.
   - `-p 1` (detached) reads the `1` as the number, and `-p0` is the plain form.
   - `-p2` is `bad argument to -p: 2` with status 1.
   - The layout applies to that one command only.

E03posix goes from 0 to 6 of its 18 chunks under the reference's own driver, and the seventh is the `disable -r` refusal.

The tests are in `dialect/zsh/posixlistings_test.go`, and each row was rechecked against real zsh. All 11 mutants were killed.

One thing recorded and not fixed: `typeset -p keymaps` after `typeset -h +g keymaps` writes nothing here, where zsh writes `typeset keymaps=''`. The file never asks for it.

Исправлен дефект, из-за которого надписи о сборе древесины, камня и железа (`+N WOOD`, `+N STONE`, `+N IRON`) оставались висеть в месте сбора и не исчезали.

В `ResourceTree.spawn_damage_text()` и `ResourceRock.spawn_damage_text()` ветка `custom_text != ""` напрямую задавала `popup.get_node("Label3D").text` и `modulate`, в обход `popup.setup_text(custom_text, custom_color)`. В результате Tween подъёма/затухания не создавался, а обратный вызов `queue_free()` никогда не планировался.

### Внесённые изменения
1. **`scripts/resource_tree.gd`**:
   - В `spawn_damage_text()` при `custom_text != ""` вызывается штатный API `popup.setup_text(custom_text, custom_color)`.
   - Добавлен защитный guard `if not get_parent(): return`.
2. **`scripts/resource_rock.gd`**:
   - В `spawn_damage_text()` при `custom_text != ""` аналогично вызывается `popup.setup_text(custom_text, custom_color)`.
   - Добавлен защитный guard `if not get_parent(): return`.
3. **`tests/integration/test_resource_pickup_notifications.gd`**:
   - Комплексный интеграционный набор GUT автотестов (10 тестов), проверяющий:
     - Жизненный цикл уведомлений дерева (`+4 WOOD`), камня (`+4 STONE`) и железа (`+2 IRON`): появление, подъём по Y, затухание прозрачности и гарантированное удаление ноды через `queue_free()`.
     - Корректность работы с `resource_multiplier` (начисление и текст уведомления).
     - Предотвращение дублирования надписей при повторной попытке сбора.
     - Независимое завершение нескольких одновременных уведомлений.
     - Регрессию свободных ресурсов (WOOD, STONE, IRON, MAGIC STONE) и чисел урона.
     - Корректность паузы/возобновления и очистки при смене сцены.
4. **`tools/capture_issue_54_notifications.gd`**:
   - Инструмент автоматического захвата ключевых кадров и видеозаписи процесса сбора ресурсов и жизненного цикла уведомления.

---

## Чек-лист критериев приёмки (Acceptance Criteria)

- [x] Для дерева, каменного и железного месторождения проверен реальный путь `harvest()`: корректный текст/цвет, движение вверх, уменьшение прозрачности, освобождение узла (`test_resource_pickup_notifications.gd`: `test_tree_harvest_notification_lifecycle`, `test_stone_rock_harvest_notification_lifecycle`, `test_iron_rock_harvest_notification_lifecycle`).

| USD/CNY | DEXCHUS (H.10 kuru) | 2018–2019 ticaret savaşı ve 2019-08 devalüasyonu |

## 问题

`tests/manual/test_feishu_real.py:17` 把一个真实的飞书群机器人 webhook token 写成模块级常量：

```python
FEISHU_WEBHOOK = "https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/<36字符>"
```

该文件被 git 跟踪、位于**公开仓主干**（`zlxlabs/VideoTranscriptAPI`，visibility=PUBLIC），任何人 `git clone` 后打开文件即得该凭据，无需挖掘历史。

该 token 曾同时存在于本机 `config/config.jsonc` 与 n305 生产配置中。2026-10-02 维护者已重置机器人，旧 token 现返回 `code:19007 Bot Not Enabled`；生产两端也已切到新值。**止血已完成，本 PR 负责把明文从主干移除。**

## 改动

- webhook 改从环境变量 `FEISHU_WEBHOOK` 读取
- 新增 module 级 `webhook` fixture：未设置时整个模块 `pytest.skip`
- 5 个测试全部接入该 fixture，无裸用

## 已锁定决策

- 凭据来源与真实生产配置分离：**不从 `config/config.jsonc` 读**（那会让「跑测试」与「碰生产配置」耦合）

判据有约束性（喂基线版本验证）：

```
$ git show HEAD~1:tests/manual/test_feishu_real.py | grep -cE open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{36}

$ git grep -nE "open\.feishu\.cn/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{36}" -- tests/ src/ docs/ skill/ config/
（零匹配，退出码 1）
```

`make test` → EXIT=0；AST 解析 → exit=0。

## 遗留

- 维护者已决定**不做** git 历史清理，因此旧 token 仍留在历史 commit 中（已失效）
- 主干另四处 token 形态字符串经核实为 3–10 字符占位符，不在本 PR 范围

author: pemarroquin
body:
## What this does

Four independent failure paths that could lose a run's territory, fixed:

### 1. Claim retry queue (`src/lib/claim-queue.ts`)
A new queue for tile claims that fail *after* the run saves. Before this, if the claim call failed (network drop, app backgrounded), the run was saved but the territory was never awarded — silently. Now `uploadRun()` enqueues failed claims; `flushClaims()` retries on every open. Never abandons (slow-retry daily past 8 attempts, drops only on server's final `rejected`/`tooOld`).

### 2. Upload queue never abandons (`src/lib/upload-queue.ts`)
`MAX_ATTEMPTS` was a hard delete threshold. Now past 8 failures a run drops to **slow retry once per day** instead of being erased. Fresh runs are sorted first (fewest attempts) so a perpetually-failing run can't block everything behind it.

### 3. Every saved run in Places I've been (`src/app/profile/history.tsx`, `src/components/achievements-view.tsx`)
History used `fetchMyVisitedCells` — only claimed runs. Now uses `fetchMyFences` with `pathCells` (derived from `raw_path`). A run that missed the 12 h claim window still draws its ground.

### 4. All your ground on both boards (`src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`, `src/lib/local-leaders.ts`, `src/components/district-map.web.tsx`, `src/components/district-map.tsx`)
Leaderboard and Local Leaders now show your holdings everywhere, not just inside the selected place. Ground outside the selected place renders faded (0.16 fill / 0.3 stroke). Rivals and the card remain scoped to the selected place only.

---

## Supporting changes

- **`src/lib/territory.ts`** — `buildFence()` falls back to a convex hull (`hullFence()`) when turf throws on a self-crossing route. A run ≥ 300 m now always gets a fence.
- **`src/lib/territory-sync.ts`** — `pathCellsOf()` derives tiles from `raw_path` triples; `reclaimUnclaimedRuns()` reclaims runs saved inside the 12 h window that never claimed (once per session).
- **Migrations** — `20261001120000_late_claims_within_7_days.sql` (extended window, tested) and `20261001130000_revert_late_claims.sql` (restored 12 h, Pedro's call) are both applied and verified in production.

## Commits
- `9d9d1ffc` Never lose a run's territory to one failed claim or upload
- `30543d52` Draft: late runs claim weakly for 7 days
- `7fa2e46d` Fix: broken verify-query comment line
- `86033118` Every saved run shows in Places I've been; territory stays 12 h
- `e1531355` Record the late-claims revert as applied and verified
- `4c44536b` See all your ground on both boards; rivals only in the selected place

## Test plan
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [ ] `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- [ ] `npm test` — 570 tests pass
- [ ] `npx expo export -p web` — clean build

body:
## Why

Entry 3 read Chan's Example 6.2 on a 2026 download, and every level it computed landed high. That measured a gap between two vendors' downloads and could not say whether his figures reproduce at all. His own `example6_2.xls` has been committed as `data/spy_chan.csv` since #124, and nothing read it.

This run reads it. Every figure he printed from a series reproduces at the precision he printed it, so this is the repo's first exact reproduction of a leverage. It also explains why the 2026 download misses.

Closes #138

Part of #159, whose Entry 3 instance this corrects. See `## Scope`.

## What

1. **`python -m chan.kelly_leverage --chan`** reads his workbook column. `--dated` now defaults to nothing under `--chan`. The old default of `2026-09-18` made the reader refuse every `--chan` run, which the audit of #138 measured before this branch existed.
2. **The report's caveat depends on the vintage as well as the window.** On Chan's window and his workbook it says the gap column is a reproduction. In the same sentence it says a zero means his arithmetic is right on his data, and nothing about whether 2.528 is a leverage anyone should carry. The 2026-download caveat now points at `--chan` rather than at #138.
3. **Gaps round before they are signed**, so a figure landing a rounding below his prints `+0.000` rather than `-0.000`. Three of the eight rows land below on his data.
4. **`compare_vintages`** joins two closes of one symbol on the days both hold and counts what each side lost. Nothing in `chan.series` could, because `aligned_closes` takes two tickers and has no `dated` argument. The `--chan` run prints the comparison, labelled as carrying neither a gap nor a verdict.
5. **The provenance comment** for `example6_2.xls` sits beside `VINTAGE_DATE`, with the mirror, the commit it was read at and the workbook's sha256. It also warns about the different series in the same mirror's `SPY.xls`.

## Evidence

Everything below is on `spy_chan.csv`, saved 2008-01-29, over 1993-01-29 to 2007-12-28. `tests/test_kelly_leverage.py` pins all of it.

| Figure | Chan printed | His data gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean annual return | 11.23% | 11.2307% |
| Standard deviation | 16.91% | 16.9131% |
| Excess return | 7.231% | 7.2307% |
| Sharpe ratio | 0.4275 | 0.427523, and 0.427580 under the population form, which prints 0.4276 |
| Kelly leverage | 2.528 | 2.5278 |
| Levered growth | 13.14% | 13.1388% |
| Unlevered growth | 9.8% | 9.8005% |
| Half-Kelly | 1.26 | 1.2639 |
| Worked example | \$252,800 | \$252,775.87, which is \$252,800 once the leverage is rounded to 2.528 first |

Set against the 2026 download over the same window:

- Both vintages hold the same 3,758 days, so the join drops nothing from either side.
- The annual means differ by 0.0641 percentage points and the standard deviations by 0.0014.
- The ten largest daily differences carry 108.5% of the summed difference. Eight of them raise the 2026 mean, and each falls on a quarter-end month's third Friday or the trading day after.
- Days in SPY's quarterly dividend months carry 100.4% of it.

The suite stands at 963. Every change to the new code that the review's mutation pass tried now fails a test, apart from three that are equivalent on the committed data. The review comment lists what the four lenses found and what changed.

## Scope`.

1. **`python -m chan.kelly_leverage --chan`** reads his workbook column. `--dated` now defaults to nothing under `--chan`. The old default of `2026-09-18` made the reader refuse every `--chan` run, which the audit of #138 measured before this branch existed.
2. **The report's caveat depends on the vintage as well as the window.** On Chan's window and his workbook it says the gap column is a reproduction. In the same sentence it says a zero means his arithmetic is right on his data, and nothing about whether 2.528 is a leverage anyone should carry. The 2026-download caveat now points at `--chan` rather than at #138.
3. **Gaps round before they are signed**, so a figure landing a rounding below his prints `+0.000` rather than `-0.000`. Three of the eight rows land below on his data.
4. **`compare_vintages`** joins two closes of one symbol on the days both hold and counts what each side lost. Nothing in `chan.series` could, because `aligned_closes` takes two tickers and has no `dated` argument. The `--chan` run prints the comparison, labelled as carrying neither a gap nor a verdict.
5. **The provenance comment** for `example6_2.xls` sits beside `VINTAGE_DATE`, with the mirror, the commit it was read at and the workbook's sha256. It also warns about the different series in the same mirror's `SPY.xls`.

## Evidence

Everything below is on `spy_chan.csv`, saved 2008-01-29, over 1993-01-29 to 2007-12-28. `tests/test_kelly_leverage.py` pins all of it.

| Figure | Chan printed | His data gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean annual return | 11.23% | 11.2307% |
| Standard deviation | 16.91% | 16.9131% |
| Excess return | 7.231% | 7.2307% |
| Sharpe ratio | 0.4275 | 0.427523, and 0.427580 under the population form, which prints 0.4276 |
| Kelly leverage | 2.528 | 2.5278 |
| Levered growth | 13.14% | 13.1388% |
| Unlevered growth | 9.8% | 9.8005% |
| Half-Kelly | 1.26 | 1.2639 |
| Worked example | \$252,800 | \$252,775.87, which is \$252,800 once the leverage is rounded to 2.528 first |

Set against the 2026 download over the same window:

- Both vintages hold the same 3,758 days, so the join drops nothing from either side.
- The annual means differ by 0.0641 percentage points and the standard deviations by 0.0014.
- The ten largest daily differences carry 108.5% of the summed difference. Eight of them raise the 2026 mean, and each falls on a quarter-end month's third Friday or the trading day after.
- Days in SPY's quarterly dividend months carry 100.4% of it.

Fourteen mutations of the new code each turned the Kelly tests red. They covered:

- the `--dated` default and the `--chan` pass-through in `main`
- the caveat branch and the negative-zero rounding
- each `compare_vintages` field
- the comparison's inputs and its column order

## Scope

- **Entry 3 gains rows 18 to 30 without renumbering.** Its section of unpinned figures shrinks to the two that need the workbook's as-traded column: 1.9341 and the 1.68 points. Both now point at #192, as do `README.md`'s write-up item 2 and `docs/design.md`'s fallback-clause section.
- **#159's Entry 3 instance is corrected here and nothing else of it.** Rows 29 and 30 had to join the shared list of rows that are not replications. Adding them while leaving out 16 and 17 would have written a list known to be wrong. So that list now names all seven, and the count in the intro reads seven, following the reading Entries 2 and 4 use. #159 keeps its check of the other entries' lists, and the question the review raised of which reading the intro's count means.
- **No blog post changes.** `blog/kelly-leverage-on-spy.md` says no test reproduces the 1.93 yet, which is still true.
- **No vintage, manifest line or checksum changes.**

## Notes

markdownlint was not run locally because no Node is installed. CI runs it. The repo's own tilde, table and line-reference sweeps are clean, and so is `tests/test_markdown_hygiene.py`.

author: ayxuerui
body:
Second of three stacked pull requests (base: `feat/owned-skills-carry-supporting-files`, so the diff shows only this layer). Adds the runner that fans a plan or a question out to three model CLIs. It is not registered in `SKILLS`, so `ctxr init` does not write it and nothing observable changes.

## What changed

`templates/skills/ctxr-second-opinion/`, none of it read by `src/`:

- **`run.mjs`**: zero-dependency Node, run as `node run.mjs`, so it needs no exec bit. Critique mode sends a plan to three roles (architect on `claude`, skeptic on `codex`, pragmatist on `agy`); poll mode sends one question, optionally through two or three taste lenses.
  - No shell anywhere: an argv array plus stdin. `agy` takes its prompt as one argument, with a guard against the 128 KiB limit.
  - Each critic runs in its own empty scratch directory under a timeout that kills the process group. `claude` runs with no tools, `codex` in a read-only sandbox. `agy` has no mode that removes its ability to act, so it gets the directory and terminal restrictions only. I tried its headless `--mode plan` and it still wrote a file, so neither is treated as containment.
  - Each critique is validated against a contract. A critique whose findings cite nothing in the plan (no step id, no verbatim quotation, no `path:line` the plan names) is marked **blind** and not counted; an `APPROVE` with no findings stays valid. A `REJECT` carrying a resolved critical finding is flagged as a veto.
  - Results are written as `critique-A/B/C.md` in shuffled order. Role and model appear only in `manifest.json`, and stdout never names them. This is aimed at the measured tendency of a judge to favor its own family's writing.
  - Fewer than two valid critiques exits `2` and prints `PARTIAL`; a failed critic is recorded with its cause and never replaced by another model.
- **`critic-contract.md`, `personas/*.md`, `lenses.md`**: the prompt fragments `run.mjs` reads. Personas carry stance-plus-integrity clauses: the skeptic concedes a sound plan, the pragmatist keeps necessary complexity.
- **`test/unit/second-opinion-runner.test.ts`**: 24 tests, one per spec scenario, against stub `claude`/`codex`/`agy` executables first on `PATH`. They cover isolation, a 20 KB plan full of shell metacharacters arriving byte-identical with the parent process confirmed to be `node`, anonymizing and shuffle, timeout and exit failures, blindness, vetoes, quorum, and preflight.
- Spec and design amended to match what was built (blind-evidence wording, poll files named by model, the `agy` finding).

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- Every runner test sets `HOME` to a temp dir. One of my early tests let the runner's `~/.local/bin` PATH fallback reach the real CLIs and ran real models for about 170 seconds; that is fixed, and the comment says why.
- Codex's login on the machine I built this on had expired, so the `codex` path is exercised only against the stub. The real-CLI dogfood run is still open in `tasks.md` (4.5).

## Verification

`npm run typecheck`, unit suite (82 files, 1029 tests), the full integration suite (25 files, 109 tests) and `openspec validate … --strict` pass on this branch.

author: chrisrogers37
body:
## What changed

This builds what the owner decided on 2026-10-02 from the hardening note (`documentation/plans/2026-10-01-session-store-hardening.md` §3). There are three pieces. Each went through simplify, code review and verification, and the findings are folded in.

### 1. Instruction screen (note §1)

`lib/claudna/screen.py` matches the shapes an injected instruction takes:
- text addressed to the assistant;
- role tags;
- a download piped to a shell or interpreter;
- a remote script to run;
- a decoded payload;
- someone's secrets sent somewhere.

It matches on NFKC text with invisible characters stripped, and it leaves ordinary facts and practices alone. Each of the 9 patterns has attack cases it must catch, and there are 16 benign look-alikes that must pass.

- **Where a summary is written:** a knowledge block that trips the screen is dropped whole. A journey or procedure string is replaced with `[withheld: instruction-like text]`. A new `summary.screened` lifecycle event records counts, pattern ids and fingerprints, never the text. 0.23 readers skip it as an unknown kind.
- **Text from before the screen:**
  - Harvest re-checks blocks, so a tripping block is never captured or held.
  - The review digest re-checks ledger and held lines, so they're never offered for promotion.
  - Summaries 0.23 wrote (prompt `segment-summary/1`) are screened where every summary reader passes (`project.segment_states`, `rollup.read_archived`). That covers export, `show` and `list`.
  - A rollup now carries `screened: true`. It's an extra key, not a new tag, so 0.23 `list` keeps its titles. Readers recompute past an unmarked rollup, and the background sweep rewrites it once, including for fully retired sessions.
- **Also:** the summarizer prompt asks the model not to quote or paraphrase instructions (`segment-summary/2`). The digest no longer ranks an item higher for `asserted_by: user`, because the model picks that label. Harvest's `Memory:` line counts blocks withheld at write and on read.

### 2. Store cleanup (note §2, ranks 1–2)

- `checkpoint.noted` and `segment.json`'s `counts.checkpoints` are removed (nothing ever wrote them).
- `segment.sealed`'s optional `sha256` and the projected `transcript.sha256` are removed (never set). `segment.json` is now `claudna.segment/2`.
- A 0.23 store upgrades on its own: readers re-fold a `/1` projection, the sweep rewrites it once, and `session_store check` flags it as a warning, not an error. `check` still treats any other tag, or a file that isn't a JSON object, as a problem.
- `trigger` and `summary.completed`'s three copied fields stay. A 0.23 reader sharing the store (a session still running the old plugin) requires them. I checked this against 0.23's own `classify`: it marks a line without them `invalid`. So dropping them waits for an envelope major.

### 3. Ironclad routing

The description now names the premise question. It points a live stress test with no plan to `/claudna:adversarial-review`, and choosing between approaches to `/claudna:weigh-development-paths`. The routing-matrix `known_failure` marker is gone. The catalog budget rises to 12,034.

## Why

- **The screen:** a transcript can carry someone else's text, and a summary could bring an instruction back as a remembered fact. It can then become a vault draft, or a promotion candidate ranked by a label the model chooses.
- **The cleanup:** the who-reads-this audit found fields with no writer.
- **Ironclad:** the premise question never routed to it.

## Testing done

- [x] Tested locally with `claude --plugin-dir` and `claude -p`:
  - **Live summarizer:** I ran it on a README carrying a planted `curl … | sh` "convention". The model recorded only that an injection attempt existed and kept the real fact (deploys from `main` to Fly.io).
  - **Live routing eval on Sonnet:** 11 of 12 cases pass. The premise row picks ironclad in about 84% of attempts across runs (9 of 10 in the last). Under the 2-of-3 rule it fails a given run about 7% of the time, as it did on the full run here. Before this change it was 0%.
  - Four other ironclad lens rows outside the eval set (mission fit, duplication, precedent, cost) still route to no skill, as they do on `main`.
- [x] `make check` passes (1876 tests). The Python 3.9 runtime suite passes (757).
- [x] **0.23 compatibility, checked against 0.23's code (`559e7f0`):**
  - every lifecycle line this branch writes classifies as `ok`;
  - `summary.screened` is skipped as an unknown kind;
  - 0.23 `list` still shows a 0.24 rollup's title;
  - 0.23 `check` reports `/2` segment files as problems, as an older checker meeting a newer format does, and its readers re-fold them.
- [x] Each new guard was removed in turn, and a test caught every one:
  - the write-side screen;
  - the digest and harvest read-side screens;
  - the rank change;
  - the shared read-point screen.

## Checklist

- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated under `[Unreleased]`
- [ ] Version bump: left for the release PR
- [x] No hardcoded paths, tokens, or credentials

## Summary
- User reported the app felt constantly stuck/slow after V8.19.83 (X4 adaptive KNN).
- Root-caused to `getBestConfigForProfile()` in `x4-native.js`: its cache validity check reused the existing `datasetSignature()` helper, which includes `state._persistenceUpdatedAt` — a timestamp that `saveState()` bumps on nearly every state-mutating interaction anywhere in the app, not just when a profile's own `actualDraws` change.

## Summary

Phase 0 of the crypto desk plan (jjhervey2310/lmc-mining#41, approved): make the existing trading/research code trustworthy before any strategy work. No strategy rules changed; no live order placed; no secrets created.

### Bugs fixed (look-ahead / correctness)
- `comp-data.ts` oversell minted cash: a sell credited the full `qty` while the position dropped by `min(qty, held)`. Replay extracted to `lib/comp-replay.ts` (pure, tested); cash now credits only what was held.
- Partial-bar contamination: `comp-trader.ts` SMA20/mom7 and `breakout_scan.py` regime read today's incomplete bar. Both now use completed bars only.
- BTC relative strength joined by array index in `backtest.py:72` → timestamp join.
- Same-bar fills in `backtest.py`, `backtest_house.py`, `backtest_breakout_full.py` (signal at close *t*, fill at close *t*) → fill at bar *t+1* (open where candles have one, next completed close for CoinGecko close-only data); entry bar's own low is now checked against the stop; a signal on the last bar is no longer tradeable; cached candle files are filtered for the partial bar on read.
- Hard-coded `DENVER_OFFSET_H = -6` (wrong for 7 MDT months) → DST-aware `denverWeekStartIso()`.
- Expired Sept-2026 CPI/FOMC blackout and half-size defaults baked into `timing/route.ts` → inert defaults; windows live in `desk_config` only.

### Security — `/api/fund/buy`
- Admin secret accepted **only** via `x-admin-secret` header on `fund/buy` and `fund/loop-toggle` (was also `?secret=` → Vercel logs / browser history). `desk-live.tsx` now sends the header on every fund call.
- Client `usd` can no longer exceed the ruled size: all sizing goes through `lib/desk/sizing.ts::clampOrderUsd` (requested ≤ ruled ≤ cash ≤ max(10% book, $10)). Tested.

### New foundations
- **Market-time rule** (one place each side): `lib/desk/market-time.ts`, `desk-loop/market_time.py` — `completedBars`, `alignIndex` (timestamp joins), `assertCompleted`, `LookAheadError`. Tests deliberately violate the rule and must fail.
- **Explicit costs**: `lib/desk/costs.ts`, `desk-loop/bt_costs.py` — `maker_fee / taker_fee / spread / slippage / venue / tier` are required inputs; legacy backtest results now carry an `ASSUMPTIONS |` stamp line. No fixed Kraken 0.22/0.38 anywhere.
- **Broker contract**: `lib/brokers/types.ts` (`getQuote/getBalances/getOpenOrders/placeOrder/cancelOrder/getOrder`); `kraken.ts` and `coinbase.ts` are explicit stubs (throw `BrokerNotImplemented`, `configured() = false`), `robinhood.ts` wraps the existing client, `manual.ts` records intents. No network, no keys.
- **Tests**: vitest added (`npm test`, 19 tests) + Python unittest (`npm run test:py`, 11 tests); `npm run typecheck`.

body:
The HiRes workflow can now estimate a full target-gene list in separate jobs and return one combined expression matrix per cell type. `genes_per_chunk` sets the maximum genes in each job, with a default of 1000. The last list can be smaller.

Each native job keeps the full mixture, signature, fractions, and cohort. The merge task checks gene coverage, sample and cell labels, window sizes, input checksums, and sampling settings. The workflow remains WDL 1.0. Files stay typed through task localization. The split and merge tasks include logs, and additional outputs expose every chunk's lists, checks, and native logs. The input example and Terra guide describe the new settings.

author: chouyoudou
body:
## Research task

Implements `paper-721fa2a1b8b1b60dbf4da234` (DOI `10.1002/advs.202409093`) as a transferable static-structure mechanism rather than a material-specific model.

## Scientific scope

The feature is limited to:

- radius-gated periodic coordination-network connectivity and quotient-graph translation rank;
- deterministic host-only grid-clearance summaries;
- explicit finite-component host/guest center and surface contact geometry.

It does not infer or model energetic content, detonation, sensitivity, synthesis, optimization, oxidation state, charge, adsorption, transport, or stability. Missing guests, hydrogens, solvent, and occupancies are never inferred.

## Fixed public interface

`periodic-host-guest-geometry/1` emits 18 fixed, finite, interpretable scalars from an ordinary VASP 5/6 POSCAR. Guest-only channels use typed zero when no finite guest exists, with applicability carried by `host_guest_present_ratio` and metadata validity fields.

The host partition retains every periodic component, including detached or interpenetrated nets. If no periodic component exists, all largest finite components are the documented fallback host so equal-size ambiguity does not depend on atom order.

## Provenance and method distinctions

- Connectivity terminology is cross-checked against Larsen dimensionality and mature ASE/pymatgen aliases, but this is an independent fixed-gate cycle-translation-rank implementation.
- The pore metric is deliberately a finite canonical-grid approximation; it is not Zeo++ `Di/LCD` or `Df/PLD` and vendors no Zeo++/Voro++ code.
- Bond gates use attributed Cordero covalent radii.
- Non-bonded surface radii are an exact transcription of the pinned MIT-licensed pymatgen-core radii data file; the upstream MIT notice is reproduced.
- Guest cavity fit and tied-contact directionality are explicitly marked as PHGG treatments/inspired definitions.

## Verification

- 16 unit tests cover 1D/2D/3D rank, fallback and multi-net host selection, radius-boundary behavior, exact triclinic minimum images, periodic unwrapping, translation/permutation invariance, symmetric contact ties, multiple guest components, VASP scale modes, validation errors, and CLI schema.
- A dedicated GitHub Actions workflow runs the public path on 1000 deterministic synthetic structures across five analytic families, checks all 18 scalars for finiteness and semantic expectations, validates the artifact contract, and uploads exactly one qualification artifact containing `samples.csv`, summary, manifest, README, and source evidence.

## Files

All changes are additive under `descriptors/`, `docs/`, `examples/`, `scripts/`, `tests/features/`, and the dedicated workflow.

author: shantanujumde
body:
https://linear.app/meet-ai-app/issue/TUR-5/codex-runner-notes-run-and-sync-run

Adds `CodexHarness`, the `Harness` implementation for Codex, in `crates/agent/src/codex.rs`. Also adds the Codex MCP approval finding to SPEC A11.

## What it does

- **Notes run:** `codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules -s read-only [--model <m>] --output-schema <file> -o <file> -`. The prompt goes in on stdin. Codex reads the schema from one temp file and writes its reply to another; both sit in a folder next to the empty working folder, and both folders are deleted when the run ends. `--ignore-user-config` and `--ignore-rules` were agreed with Shann. They mean the notes run loads none of the user's MCP servers, plugins, hooks or `.rules` files, which is what A11 asks for.
- **Sync run:** the same command without those two flags, so the user's `~/.codex/config.toml` loads. Each `mcp__<server>__<tool>` in `allowed_tools` becomes `-c mcp_servers.<server>.enabled_tools=[...]`. That only narrows the servers it names; a server name that would need TOML quoting is skipped. Closing off the user's other MCP servers and pre-approving the tracker's tools is [TUR-16](https://linear.app/meet-ai-app/issue/TUR-16).
- **`models()`:** the list from `codex debug models` (models marked `visibility: list`, in Codex's priority order). If the command fails, the list is empty. If no model is set, `--model` is left out and Codex picks its own default (`gpt-5.6-terra` on 0.152.1).
- **`detect()`:** TUR-6's `detect::codex(binary_path)`. A configured binary runs through `process::cli_command`, so its own folder is first on the child's `PATH`.
- **Failed runs:** Codex repeats the whole prompt on stderr, so every stderr line that is also in the prompt is dropped before it goes into `CliFailed`.

## MCP approval spike (SPEC A11, "Measured 2026-10-02")

`codex exec` always runs with `approval: never`. An MCP tool call is **refused, not asked**: "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never". The server never receives the call, and Codex still **exits 0**. Adding `-c mcp_servers.<server>.default_tools_approval_mode="approve"` lets the call through with no window. No code depends on this; whoever wires Sync decides. The spike used a local fake MCP server only, so nothing outside this Mac was touched.

## Tests

- 14 unit tests in `codex.rs`: arguments, tool narrowing and TOML quoting, the stderr prompt filter, model list parsing, reading the reply file.
- 12 tests against a fake `codex` script (`tests/codex_fake.rs`). body:
## Problem
Research reports existed, but strategy-bound AI advice could still invent prices, lacked an independent review artifact, and had no frozen provenance suitable for later forward admission.

## Minimal complete solution
- keep the existing stock AI route and dispatch explicit `research` / `advice` requests (legacy `alert` remains Research-compatible)
- build BuyPoint signals and deterministic TradePlan candidates only on the server
- accept only a server-issued `plan_instance_id`; reject AI price/confidence fields and invalid citations
- apply deterministic position and signal-status guards before returning Advice
- keep base Advice and Review schemas, caches, timestamps, calls, and JSONL artifacts separate
- coalesce concurrent identical requests so one reviewed Advice uses at most one base call plus one review call
- persist frozen evidence, missing/freshness inputs, strategy digest, plan identity/instance, and forward cutoff without storing a later eligibility decision
- add the Advice/Review UI, strategy selector, blocking-review state, and server-only formal TradePlan display

## Compatibility
- default requests remain the existing Research contract
- legacy `purpose=alert` remains supported as Research
- existing buy-point responses are unchanged; their assembly now delegates to the shared service
- historical Advice fails closed until strategy definitions have PIT history

## Validation
- backend affected suite before review fixes: 109 passed
- reviewer fixes: 26 passed, including 4 concurrent reviewed requests => exactly 2 provider calls, shared run/review IDs, one history artifact each
- frontend targeted: 25 passed after the final cache-flow regression fix; affected ESLint, TypeScript, and production build passed
- `./scripts/ci.ps1 -Mode Auto`: frontend full suite, ESLint, TypeScript, and build passed; backend full had 2839 passed / 1 skipped / 1 unrelated concurrency failure in `test_taiwan_live_runner.py`, and that unchanged test passed immediately when rerun alone (1/1)
- desktop smoke passed for Research/Advice switching, server strategy loading/selection, review toggle, no formal price before a server plan, and zero console errors
- `git diff --check` passed; production secret candidates 0 (one fixed test fixture literal only)

- no Live AI/provider request was made
- forward admission, deterministic outcome persistence, same-plan statistics, and immutable reflections are the next WP3/WP4 package

author: jdaugherty
body:
Fixes #16464

## Problem

In a Hibernate 7 inheritance tree with three or more levels (`Vehicle` → `Car` → `SportsCar` / `Sedan`), queries on the intermediate class ignore the rows of its subclasses. `Car.count()`, `Car.list()`, criteria, dynamic finders and HQL return only the `Car` rows.

`RootBinder` added every subclass in the tree to the root `RootClass`. Hibernate finds a class's subclasses through its direct superclass (`PersistentClass.getSubclasses()` recurses through each class's direct subclasses), so the intermediate class had no subclasses in the mapping model.

## Fixes

- **Hibernate 7, nested subclasses (#16464):** each subclass is now added to its own superclass. The root still sees the whole tree through Hibernate's recursion, with no duplicates. Hibernate 5 already binds subclasses this way (`parent.addSubclass(subClass)` in `GrailsDomainBinder`).
- **Hibernate 7, join table collections of a subclass:** a unidirectional `hasMany` of a table-per-hierarchy subclass failed with `Column "C1_0.CLASS" not found`. `HibernateToManyEntityOrderByBinder` put the discriminator condition on the join table, which has no discriminator column. The condition is now only bound to one-to-many collections, as in Hibernate 5. This also affected two-level hierarchies.
- **MongoDB, loading by id through a subclass:** `Car.get(id)` of a document saved as a `Vehicle` returned an object built from that document instead of `null`, because the id lookup did not restrict on `_class` like queries do. Both the codec and the mapping engine now apply the same `_class` restriction to the id lookup (`MongoQuery.createClassFieldQuery`). This also affected two-level hierarchies (`City.get(location.id)`).

## Tests

- TCK `InheritanceSpec` has a three-level hierarchy (`FleetVehicle` → `FleetCar` → `FleetSportsCar` / `FleetSedan`, plus a `FleetGarage`). It covers queries, loads and associations typed to the intermediate class, and loading a superclass instance through a subclass, on every GORM implementation.
- `IntermediateSubclassQuerySpec` (Hibernate 7) covers all three inheritance strategies: queries and loads on the intermediate class, associations typed to it (lazy proxy, join fetch and collection), and root and leaf queries.
- `RootBinderSpec` checks the direct subclasses of the root and of the intermediate class, and that the root sees each subclass once.
- `HibernateToManyEntityOrderByBinderSpec` checks that the discriminator condition is bound to one-to-many collections and not to join table collections.
- `SubclassRetrieveByIdSpec` (MongoDB) checks loading by id through each class of a hierarchy with both the codec and the mapping engine.

Each fix was mutation-checked: reverting it fails the new tests that cover it.

- Ensure prompt write operations to `main` are concurrency-safe and never overwrite a target that changed since the proposal.  
- Require full revalidation and read-after-write verification before reporting success so verified snapshots are reliable.  
- Provide atomic multi-file reset semantics rather than sequential Contents API commits to guarantee all-or-nothing behavior.

### Description

- Add guarded, read-after-write prompt mutation logic in `src/server/prompts/github-store.ts` including bounded retries for unrelated branch advances, target-blob validation that rejects changed targets, unknown-outcome reconciliation, immutable read-back validation, and a `PromptMutationConflict` error.

author: zachcp
body:
Implements `molgpu-sept-egp.15`, the cutoff half split out of egp.10. Finding: `docs/findings/2026-10-02-efield-cutoff.md`.

**API (experimental):** optional `cutoff` / `switchWidth` (Å) on `ElectrostaticsOptions` and `<EField>`. The **exact sum stays the default.**

**Physics:** the CHARMM switching function `S(r)` runs between `cutoff − switchWidth` (default 2 Å) and `cutoff`. It is **C¹ at both ends**: unit tests check value and derivative continuity, `S′` against finite differences, and `E = −dφ/dr` in the switching region. It is applied by the CPU reference, by the WGSL `kernel` (`sumPoints`), and by the new `sumGridCutoff` entry.

**GPU:**
- `<EField>` orders summed rows along a 2 Å Morton curve of the structure's own positions. That is a locality hint only.
- `tileBounds` reduces each 64-atom tile's box from the **live** packed positions every pass.
- `sumGridCutoff` gives each workgroup a 16×4×4 sample brick. It checks 64 tile boxes per step, compacts the tiles within the cutoff into workgroup memory, and sums only those.
- Motion can only cost speed, never correctness.
- I used this in place of the shared GPU cell-list sort the bead suggested: it needs no GPU sort, scan or bounds readback.

**Results** (`run-efield`):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| GPU vs switched f64 reference | ≤ 3.1e-7 of peak (vacuum 6/10 Å, distance 8 Å, Debye 8 Å) |
| Error vs exact sum (300-atom cloud) | vacuum 38–40 %, distance 7.2 %, Debye 23 % of peak |
| 128³ × 50k, distance | exact 1251 ms → **12 Å cutoff 416 ms (3.0×)**, 13× the pre-egp.10 baseline |

These numbers are why exact remains the default.

**Checks:**
- Browser: `run-efield` passes (including the new case 1b and the cutoff timing case).
- `deno task test` (497 passed), `typecheck`, `typecheck:components`, `check:hardening` (`api.txt`: the new options and fields, `COULOMB_CUTOFF_BRICK`) and the `jsr:check` dry run pass.

author: cherishwins
body:
## Why

The live app was serving wrong prices. Commit 28e57a3 ("update HDB resale price as of 16 Jul") changed `FEATURE_NAMES` in `app.py` and `scaler.joblib` to a 58-feature layout. It dropped `postal` and `flat_model_MAISONETTE` and changed the case of the flat model names. `model.bst` was never retrained to match: it last changed in 75cc42c, and it has `num_features() == 60`. It also uses `postal` heavily: f1 has 139,082 splits. XGBoost accepts a bare vector of the wrong length without complaint, so nothing failed and every price was off.

Here is one real sale to show the size of the error. Blk 163 Simei Rd (postal 520163) is a 4 ROOM, Model A flat of 104 sqm on storey 07–09, with a lease from 1989. It resold in June 2025 for **S$645,000** (data.gov.sg). The unfixed app priced it at S$434,052, 33% too low. Across 63 real May/June 2025 resales in postal mode, the median absolute error was 31.2%.

## What changed

### 1. [major] Features, scaler and model disagree (8867649, fd82117)
- **Layout.** `FEATURE_NAMES` (60 entries, `postal` at index 1, upper-case flat models), the `!= 60` check, `scaler.joblib` and `DATA_INGESTION_DATE = '30-06-2025'` are restored from 75cc42c, the commit that last shipped `model.bst`. The choice of layout rests on evidence, not a guess:
  - model.bst has 60 features.
  - The restored scaler has the same 60 `feature_names_in_`, in the same order.
  - The scaler is byte-identical at 75cc42c and afb06f0.
  - 28e57a3 touched only `app.py`, `scaler.joblib` and `postal_data.json`, so no retrained model was ever paired with the 58-feature layout.
  - Apart from the new guard, `git diff 75cc42c HEAD -- app.py` is empty, so no UI change was lost.
  - The 16 Jul `postal_data.json` additions are kept. They are lookup entries only.
- **Startup guards.** A mismatch is now fatal: `st.error` + `st.stop`.
  - Model guard: the app refuses to start when `xgb_model.num_features() != NUM_FEATURES`.
  - Scaler guard: the app refuses to start when the scaler's `feature_names_in_` are **missing** or differ from `FEATURE_NAMES`. It fails closed (fd82117, from review). A scaler fitted on a bare array records no names, so it cannot prove a match.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_prediction.py` uses `unittest` + Streamlit `AppTest` and needs no new dependency. It has 5 tests:
  - The known transaction is priced within 15%.
  - The app starts clean, and the Flat Model default is `IMPROVED`.
  - A dropped feature stops the app: "Model expects 60 features but the app builds 59".
  - A reordered scaler stops the app.
  - A scaler with no feature names stops the app.
  - `run_app` clears `st.cache_resource` before each run. Without that, a temp copy of the app was served the previous run's cached scaler and the scaler guard tests passed vacuously.
- **Proof.**
  - Blk 520163 is now predicted at **S$668,574** (+3.7%).
  - Across the same 63 resales, median error falls from 31.2% to **2.3%** (p90 5.1%), with 100% within 20%.
  - Against the unfixed e5d2bb1, the suite fails.
  - Before fd82117, the missing-names test failed, which confirms the fail-open; after it, the test passes.
  - The price check can actually fail. Postal and storey_avg were swapped consistently in both FEATURE_NAMES and the scaler, which passes both guards. The known-transaction test then fails with "predicted S$ 823,025, sold for S$ 645,000".

### 2. [minor] Flat Model default fell to '2-room' (8867649)
The default looks up `FLAT_MODELS.index("IMPROVED")`. Restoring the upper-case names makes that lookup resolve. The test asserts `IMPROVED`; on e5d2bb1 it fails with `'2-room' != 'IMPROVED'`. The live browser run shows "Flat Model default: IMPROVED".

### 3. [minor] `|| true` masked a failed pip install (d67539b)
The line is now `pip install -r requirements.txt && (pip uninstall -y nvidia-nccl-cu12 || true)`. In a shell check, `sh -c 'false && (x || true)'` exits 1, while the old form exits 0. The rebuild logged "Successfully uninstalled nvidia-nccl-cu12".

### 4. [minor] `chown -R` duplicated the 67 MB model into a second layer (d67539b)
`useradd` now runs first, the app files are copied with `COPY --chown=appuser:appuser`, and the `chown -R` is gone. `docker history` shows a single 67.7MB `COPY --chown ... model.bst` layer and no chown layer. The process runs as uid 10001 and the container is healthy.

## Live proof (through Caddy, rebuilt image)
- `GET https://hdb.localhost/` returns 200, `/_stcore/health` returns 200, and the `/_stcore/stream` upgrade returns `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`.
- The running container's image matches the rebuilt `hdb-price-predictor:onebox`, and `/app/app.py` hashes the same as HEAD.
- Playwright Chromium: page 200, websocket opened, no alerts on load, Flat Model default IMPROVED. The inputs were postal 520163, June 2025, 104 sqm, storey 8, 4 ROOM, MODEL A, and the result was **"Predicted Resale Price S$ 668,574.44 For 4 ROOM in TAMPINES (Expected: June 2025)"**.

## Deliberately left alone
- **Town mode is still inaccurate.** This is the default, with the postal toggle off. `app.py` feeds `postal = 0.0`, which is below the scaler's trained minimum of 50004. Over the same 63 resales, town mode has 24.6% median error, and for blk 520163 it predicts S$819,455. This behaviour predates the regression (it is present at 75cc42c) and it was not a listed issue. Fixing it is a product decision with three options: send NaN (6.6% median error offline), use the town's median postal code (3.5%), or require a postal code.
- **The model guard checks the count only.** `model.bst` stores no feature names, so a same-length reorder shipped together with a matching scaler would pass both runtime guards. Pinning the names would mean re-saving the 67 MB model or adding a new sidecar artifact. That is a design choice beyond this fix. The known-transaction test catches such a reorder, as the mutation proof above shows, and the README says so.
- The sklearn warning "X does not have valid feature names" is pre-existing: the app passes a NumPy array to the scaler. It is harmless and out of scope.

## Checks run
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, run in the app image: 5 tests, OK. The repo has no CI, lint or typecheck config, so this suite is its first check.
- The image was built under the shared build lock with a sandbox-only helper. The helper rewrites apt sources to https in a throwaway Dockerfile copy, because the plain-http `deb.debian.org` gets 405 from this sandbox's proxy. **The committed Dockerfile was not built verbatim here.** It has the same apt line as before this PR.
- `ONEBOX_BUILD=0 ./up-all.sh hdb`: healthy. `smoke.sh`: hdb 200, websocket 101.

author: onelpawarai-x
body:
## What this does

Adds the **MCP Connect** button to the home page, right next to *New session*, and wires it to the MCP Hub panel from #104.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/app/src/pages/home.tsx` | one button, plus `openMcpHub()` |
| `MCP Hub/lib/runtime.ts` | new; adapts ZYRAXON’s MCP service to the panel |
| `MCP Hub/plugin.ts` | exports `bindRuntime` |

The host change is deliberately tiny: one function and one button. The Hub itself lives entirely in `MCP Hub/`, and the runtime adapter means it never reaches into the app.

## How it behaves

1. Click **MCP Connect** on the home page.
2. The panel lists every app: 17 curated, plus a search over 9,580 registry servers.
3. Click an app. The panel asks the runtime to begin OAuth.
4. The runtime opens the browser at **that app’s own consent page** (for example Notion opens `api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize`).
5. The user presses **Allow**.
6. The code returns to the local callback on port 19876, the token is stored, and `mcp/catalog.ts` converts the server’s tools into agent tools at runtime.

Steps 3 to 6 need nothing from the user except pressing Allow: all six zero-setup apps register the client automatically.

## Verification

- Type-check passes with the SolidJS JSX runtime.
- Runtime tool injection is proven in `MCP Hub/scripts/verify-injection.mjs` (6 checks, 0 failures): tools are discovered, converted to agent tools with valid schemas, and actually called — `github_list_pull_requests` returned the real list of open pull requests on this repository.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

Ecosystem roulette run on **DB::ORM::Quicky 0.1.4**, locked on #10045.

- Zen slice `$<>` / `$/<>` of a lazy Match stringified it; it now returns the Match (as Rakudo does).
- In a double-quoted string or an `s///` replacement, `$<>[0]` was read as the named capture `""` plus a literal `[0]`. It now parses as `$/` followed by the subscript.
- Root cause for the dist: its SQLite column introspection does `$cols ~~ s/ ^ .*? '(' (.*) ')' .*? $ /$<>[0]/`, which produced `"[0]"`, so no columns were found and a second `save` tried `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` on an existing column.

## Result

By direct run (the ledger record is deliberately not touched, per roulette rules): rakudo passes all 3 baseline files, and mutsu now passes `t/01_sqlite.t` (13/13), `t/02_joins.t` (11/11) and `t/03_sqlite_no_quotes.t` (13/13). Before the fix all three died with 0 tests run. No residue to file.

Regression test: `t/regex/match/match-zen-slice.t` (9 tests, same results under `raku`).

## Gate

`scripts/dev gate` verdict: **pass** (checks, fmt, lint, test, roast; roast known-env: 4).

Stacked on #147 (`codex/load-memory-bounding`), this PR adds a synthetic, no-network RSS regression acceptance only. It does not change production load behavior, deploy configuration, or live-load execution.

Focused performance-contract gate passed; live+accumulator pair passed in 5.956s; hostile and compatibility tests passed in normal and `python -O` modes; ruff, py_compile, docs, catalog and diff checks passed.

body:
## Summary
- Add a lightweight Windows notification-area controller using the upstream icon, Japanese/English menu labels, and Open/Start/Stop/Update actions. No NuGet dependency, resident PowerShell, or periodic polling.
- Register the tray for the desktop user's sign-in. Keep UI/browser unelevated; elevate only AllUsers management actions. Safely replace the tray after updates without terminating the updater.
- Stop auto-adding Start-menu actions and remove only the eight legacy English/Japanese names, preserving unrelated shortcuts.
- Fix a demonstrated CurrentUser startup false-exit: retain Process objects and use HasExited, rather than treating temporarily unavailable Process.Path as termination. Add per-launch diagnostic logs.
- Preserve secret config permissions; users without env access may read only a sanitized public URL hint.
- Build/test a PR once, then validate exact source tree, run/job provenance and immutable artifact hashes on main and publish the identical four assets. No repeated build/test gate when qualified inputs match. Invalid evidence fails closed; missing/stale/fork evidence uses fresh qualification.

## Verification
- 54 offline CI promotion regressions passed
- 13 isolated startup workflow cases passed
- Static audit, updater orchestration and dependency reuse tests passed
- C#5/helper command/localization checks and 101 tray harness assertions passed locally
- actionlint passed; independent integration/security reviews addressed
- Windows qualification passed: 841 compiled-tray assertions, both install scopes, empty-cache legacy reuse, actual legacy CPU-to-DirectML dependency transition, startup registration and old-menu cleanup
- The initial CI-only run exposed the old startup race; this revision fixes it rather than blindly rerunning unchanged tests

Release target: v3.2.2.5. GPU hardware verification remains separate; CI runs CPU inference and DirectML policy mocks.

## Released and verified

author: jonbaldie
body:
## Summary
- Treat IMF-fixdate, RFC 850, and asctime Expires dates representing the Unix Epoch as already expired (hit-for-miss).
- Correct the Cache-Control override matcher to recognize the actual `s-maxage` directive as well as `max-age`.
- Extend hostile E2E coverage for static and non-static responses and both freshness overrides.

## Root cause
Varnish parses these valid epoch HTTP-dates as timestamp zero without replacing the default TTL. The format-only invalid-Expires guard therefore missed them, allowing the default freshness to survive. The previous Cache-Control matcher also spelled `s-maxage` as `s-max-age`, so the shared-cache override was not recognized.

## Tests
- `make test-hostile-zero-ttl`
- `make test-vcl-compile`
- `HOSTILE_SURROGATE_ESI_PORT=18089 COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT=1 make -j1 test test-e2e-hard`

Closes #121

body:
## El fallo
«Unirme con un código» (desde Hoy y desde `/`) abría la pestaña Granjas, y Granjas decía **«¡Utiliza el cuadro superior…!»**: el formulario estaba **encima de las pestañas**, ocupando sitio en todas, Hoy incluida. Había que subir y adivinar.

**Ahora**:
- el formulario vive **dentro de Granjas**;
- al llegar por «Unirme con un código» el foco va al campo del código, tanto desde `/` (`state.pestana`) como desde Hoy (`onUnirse`);
- abrir Granjas con el ratón o con las flechas **no** mueve el foco: no se le roba a quien navega las pestañas con el teclado;
- el estado vacío ya no habla de un «cuadro superior».

## La cabecera, de paso
- Tenía su propia barra de XP («XP: 600 / Siguiente: 1000 / 0.0%») y la pestaña Hoy, justo debajo, otra en otro formato («Nivel 4 · 0 / 400 XP»). Ahora la cabecera usa **la misma `BarraNivel`** y, debajo, «600 XP en total». El E2E de partida usa esa cifra para comprobar que no se sumó dos veces.
- A 360 px las cifras se juntaban («XP: 600Siguiente: 1000») y el lápiz tapaba la última línea. En móvil el lápiz pasa arriba a la derecha.

## Refactor
ProfilePage pasa de 304 a **135 líneas**. Cada pestaña pide y gestiona sus datos:
- `PestanaHistorial`: página y `useMiHistorial`;
- `PestanaGranjas`: granjas, unirse, el código y los mismos toasts, incluido el de 429;
- `StatsTab` calcula sus precisiones;
- `useEditarPerfil`: solo los campos cambiados, con `''` → `null`;
- `lib/tiempo.js`;
- `pasosTour.js`.

Los componentes de presentación y sus tests no cambian.

**Cambio menor de comportamiento:** al salir de Historial o de Granjas se pierden la página del historial y el código a medio escribir. Antes se conservaban.

Corrijo lo que dije en la segunda ronda: el archivo tenía 304 líneas, no ~500, y **no tiene ningún `is_staff`**, así que D15 no choca con él.

## Pruebas
- `npm run verify`: **818 tests** sobre `dev` con #99 (803 antes de traerlo; la rama partió de 778). Nuevos: `ProfilePage.test.jsx` (formulario dentro de Granjas y no encima de las pestañas; foco con `onUnirse` y `state.pestana`, pero no con clic ni con flechas; tres de ellos fallan con el código anterior), `useEditarPerfil`, `PestanaGranjas`, `PestanaHistorial`, `StatsTab` y `lib/tiempo`.
- `npm run test:e2e`: **43 passed, 1 skipped** sobre `dev` con #99. El único E2E que cambia es `partida.spec.js` («XP: N» → «N XP en total»).
- Capturas a 360 y 1280 px de Hoy, Granjas, «Unirme» con el foco y la cabecera, revisadas.
- Con `dev` actual (#99 incluido). Fusiona limpio con #100.

El fallo y el refactor los hizo un subagente en su worktree. Front✳End revisó las capturas e hizo el arreglo de la cabecera.
