author: kurtseifried
body:
Part of #110. The setup scripts' half follows in CSA-Plugins.

## What it replaces

A fresh Windows run printed **nine lines of "Next steps" that were not steps**, then **~140 lines of per-server output after them**, with up to **four separate "restart Claude Desktop"** instructions and **three different formats** for "now go sign in". The one thing a person needs — *what do I do now* — was the only thing not presented as a list, and it had scrolled off by the time the run ended.

## The result

```
  What you need to do — 6 things
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  1. Restart Claude Desktop

  2. Sign in to Google Workspace
     In Claude, say:    sign me in to Workspace
     Or in a terminal:  csa-google-workspace-mcp login
  ...
  5. Skilljar needs a credential you have to be given
     In Claude, say:    check_access

  Re-run this installer any time; it updates everything it installed.
```

**"In Claude, say" leads.** Three of the four servers ship an `authenticate` tool that delivers the sign-in link *in the conversation*, and **no setup script mentioned it** — the CLI fallback was printed as the only route, to an audience that is mostly not CLI people. The command stays second because that path can be refused by the client.

**Dependency order is a property of the record** (10 restart, 20 sign in, 30 needs somebody else, 40+ the installer's own), so a writer needn't know what else exists. Restart is first because until it happens nothing below it exists. **Deduplication is keyed on the item, not the emitter** — which is what collapses four "restart Claude Desktop" into one.

## Both platforms, together

`check-parity` caught the Windows-only version immediately — *"step `Show-CsaTodoList` has no macOS equivalent"* — and declaring it `PLATFORM_ONLY` would have created **exactly the divergence #111 exists to find**. The bash half is pure text processing, so it was written and exercised here: identical list, same order, same dedup.

The nine non-steps are gone from Windows, and **macOS had already made that correction** and recorded why. That `re-run this script` line was missing on Windows entirely; the renderer prints it on both.

## What does not move

The per-server banners stay. gmail's two-directory explanation is a **grant notice** — the control that makes a broad default capability set a decision rather than a surprise. **The banner explains, the ledger instructs.**

## Three wrong versions, all about sorting

| Attempt | Why it was wrong |
|---|---|
| `Sort-Object -Property Raw -Unique` | dedups in one step but sorts by the property it dedups on → alphabetical within a tier |
| hashtable + `Sort-Object -Property Order` | **`Sort-Object` is not stable on Windows PowerShell 5.1** — `-Stable` is 7-only. Three sign-ins written workspace/gmail/zendesk rendered **in reverse** on the runtime that ships |
| routing `/mcp` through `Register-CSAMcpServer` | `check-duplication` rejected it — that function is shared across three scripts and only one has a renderer |

Stability is now constructed from an explicit read-position key, on both platforms, for the same reason.

Full suite green, both scripts parse, parity satisfied with the pair declared in `EQUIV`.

author: carlonzo
body:
Follow-up review of the Cronet/OkHttp bridging: per-request cost the bridge added, and the pieces the fifth rewrite site unlocked.

## Performance

The body path dominated everything else.

- **Deleted `UnregisteringResponseBody`.** It wrapped every response body in a `ForwardingSource` + a second `RealBufferedSource`, so each response byte crossed okio **three** times instead of twice, plus three objects per response. `OkHttpBridgeCallback` now owns the registration teardown itself.
- **Pooled direct read buffers** (8 idle, 256 KiB worst case), and **only released once Cronet has reported the request over**. `UrlRequest.cancel()` is asynchronous, so a buffer with a pending `read()` behind it must not go back to the pool - another response could take it and take a write that belonged to this one. Two regression tests cover the read-timeout and the cross-thread-close paths; both fail without the gate.
- **Header conversion fast path.** While no name repeats case-insensitively: no lowercased key, no per-name list, no `joinToString` per header. The first repeat promotes into the joining map, so the published `", "` / `"; "` (Cookie) rules are untouched.
- **`body.contentLength()` once per request**, not 4+.
- **`SarieLogger.isLoggable`** gates per-call message construction (default `true`, so nothing changes until a host opts in).

## Stock-parity gap closed

`callTimeout` now bounds the body, which stock OkHttp does and the bridge did not. An expired deadline throws `InterruptedIOException("timeout")` and cancels the engine exactly once.

Deliberately **not** re-implemented on the header phase: OkHttp enters its own `AsyncTimeout` before the chain runs, and that timer now reaches Cronet through the rewritten `RealCall.cancel()`, so a second implementation could only fire later than OkHttp's. The unit test pins the narrow claim (`BridgeTerminalPathTest.the header wait is bounded by the read timeout only, never by callTimeout`); the end-to-end shape is proven on device by `CronetSuite.callTimeoutBoundsAStalledBodyOverCronet`, which caught a wiring gap the JVM tests structurally could not see: `cronetPath` was never passing the deadline to the converter, so the body bound was dead in production while every unit test (which builds the callback directly) passed.

Stated as an approximation rather than claimed as parity: the body budget is anchored at request conversion, because `okio.Timeout` exposes no remaining-budget accessor at the 5.4.0 compile floor.

## New surface

- **Fifth rewrite site.** `RealCall.cancel()` keeps its body and gains one `CronetBridge.notifyCanceled`, spliced in front of `eventListener.canceled(this)` - not after it, because a host `EventListener` is user code that may throw, and that would leave the engine request uncancellable. `Call.addEventListener` rebuilds an aggregate listener inside a CAS retry loop, which was eight objects and a CAS loop per call purely to observe cancellation.
- **`SarieNetLog`** (`start(path)` / `start(path, captureMode)` / `stop()`). Runtime-only, because it acts on an engine that does not exist until after `build()`. Two explicit overloads rather than a default argument, so no public `start$default` synthetic is pinned into the ABI.

Everything else Cronet-only (QUIC options, network quality estimator, user agent, thread priority, QUIC hints) goes through the existing `configure` hook, which already hands the host the raw `CronetEngine.Builder`. Sarie mirrors none of that surface, and sets no default for it.

## Generated data removed

The first revision of this PR was +29k lines, ~26k of it Textifier `.txt` dumps under `plugin/src/test/resources/stock/` that no test reads.

- The rewriter tests now read stock OkHttp bytecode **out of the resolved jars at test time** (`ZipFile` + `getEntry`), so it can never drift from the dependency.
- **Every `.class` golden is deleted, for all versions.** They were the test fixtures, not decoration - but the dependency already carries them.
- The set of jars is derived from `RecipeRegistry`, not the version catalog. Taking it from the catalog would have made every plugin test fail the next time a pin was added, since the tests parameterize over the registry.
- `recipe-verification-report.md` deleted; the generator prints the verification table and per-version exclusion reasons to **stdout** instead, so "why was this version excluded" is still produced for whoever runs the script.
- `generate-fingerprints.sh` writes nothing into the repo any more (scratch moved under `build/`), and `catalog.yml` no longer `git add`s paths that no longer exist.


## Also from the review pass

- **Registration teardown is scoped to the attempt**, not the call: `requests.remove(call, registered)`. A late close from an earlier attempt (transport-failure retry, body closed after the follow-up started) can no longer remove a newer attempt's entry and leave a live engine request uncancellable.
- **One owner for the redirect teardown.** `RedirectBodySource` is gone; a 3xx body is a plain empty `Buffer` and `CronetBridge` unregisters the hop at header time, where Cronet has already canceled the engine request. The stale comment claiming the body owned it is gone with it.
- **No test-only counters in production**: `BodyBufferPool` lost `rentedCount`/`idleCount`/`allocatedCount` and the two atomics they kept alive on every rent. Pool behaviour is asserted through what callers can observe - buffer identity and reuse.
- `SarieNetLog.start` is two explicit overloads, so no public `start$default` synthetic is pinned into the published ABI.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./gradlew build` | green, incl. `assembleMinifiedRelease` |
| `:bridge:testDebugUnitTest` | 266 tests, 0 failures |
| `-p plugin test` | 94 tests, 0 failures, TestKit fixture builds included |
| `:bridge:check` | green (incl. apiCheck and lint) |
| `connectedDebugAndroidTest`, okhttp 5.5.0 / 5.4.0 | 0 failures |
| `connectedMinifiedReleaseAndroidTest`, okhttp 5.5.0 / 5.4.0 | 0 failures (R8) |

Device tests ran on an API-30 emulator, the same matrix CI uses.

## SSE

The origin gains an `/sse` route (3 events 2s apart, then close). `CronetSuite.sseEventsSurfaceOnArrivalNotAtEndOfStream` asserts the first event lands inside the first gap while the request still spans >=4000ms - the pair matters, because the first assertion alone could pass on a pre-buffered blob. Origin log for the device request: `proto=HTTP/2.0 status=200 duration=4.001s ua=okhttp/5.5.0`.

A partially filled chunk is surfaced on arrival and never withheld for the buffer: okio's `RealBufferedSource.read` does one source read and returns `min(byteCount, buffered)`, and `okhttp-sse` only asks for >= 1 byte. Two latent defects fixed while checking: a zero-byte `onReadCompleted` threw `IllegalStateException` out of a read, and a `byteCount` above `Int.MAX_VALUE` truncated.

## Reviewer notes

- `scripts/Caddyfile` and `scripts/slow-backend.py` are shared test infrastructure and this touches them. Additive: `/slow`'s behaviour and its `reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8444` form are untouched.
- **Environment gotcha, not caused by this PR:** a Caddy left running from before a `Caddyfile`/`gen-certs.sh` change serves stale config and yields a wall of `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`, because `startTestOrigin`'s health probe uses `curl -sk`. Worth making that probe verify trust rather than reachability.
- **Pre-existing, not fixed here:** `./gradlew -p plugin build` fails `validatePlugins` because `VerifyOkHttpPinTask` and `VerifyOkHttpFingerprintTask` carry no caching annotation. It fails the same way on `main`; CI runs `-p plugin test`, which is green.

## Not addressed

`CronetBodySource.read` can re-issue `UrlRequest.read()` after `onSucceeded` is queued, which real Cronet rejects with `IllegalStateException`. Pre-existing, does not fire on any covered path.

author: tsatsuamable
body:
# RFC 0009 tranche 3 slice 2: kernel-issued consumer identity + governed use minting

Implementation of the producer slice assigned by #862. Owner decisions (2026-10-02): first governed consumer = **descriptive statistics** binding to the existing `descriptive-summary/v1` profile; persisted format stays **archive-scoped** — one-`receiptId` `PersistedEvidenceUseV1`, multiple use records, no envelope shape change.

## High-risk pre-implementation adversarial contract

- Invariant: every governed V3 package this build exports commits a `uses` set in which each record names a consumer identity issued by the Rust kernel, a receiptId present in the same committed bundle, and the authority-required profile `descriptive-summary/v1`; the replay loader binds every use through `bindConsumerUsesV1` against the authority-owned policy (first registry entry) and refuses anything that fails to bind or resolve; a package not minted by this build keeps refusing with the existing typed codes; V1/V2 replay contracts and persisted shapes stay untouched.
- Authority / production path: consumer identity is issued only by the Rust kernel (`wasm/src/data/governed_consumer.rs`, constant `DESCRIPTIVE_STATISTICS_CONSUMER_ID`); the TS policy authority is `src/data/evidence/ConsumerPolicyRegistry.ts` mapping that consumer to `DESCRIPTIVE_SUMMARY_REQUIREMENT_PROFILE_V1`; the kernel attestation reaches composition only through the injected analytical execution port readout, so `composeGovernedEvidenceReceiptSnapshot` stays pure; the session-side export validator runs the loader's own binder over the bytes about to be committed.
- Primary failure modes: TypeScript deriving consumerId from column names or aliases; uses minted for receipts absent from the bundle; bound-but-unresolved uses accepted; enforcement widened to `consumer-policy` without a policy actually applied; persisted-format drift beyond the decided scope; breaking empty-uses V1/V2 paths or the live happy path; a registry entry without a producer; slice-1 falsifiers weakened instead of widened; TS-issued identity at capture time. Each is resisted by a mint-side/bridge/capture/composition/export-side refusal or a source-scan pin, detailed in the committed falsifiers.
- Falsifying evidence: production-path export of a governed package with minted uses then real-loader replay with `enforcement: 'consumer-policy'` (`tests/tec1-governed-use-minting-live.test.ts`, wasm lane); mutated-registry refusals on identical bytes (`tests/tec1-mutated-policy-refusal.test.ts`); the full minting-chain refusal suite (`tests/tec1-governed-use-minting.test.ts`); bound-but-unresolved export refusal through the real session export entry (violated-assumption receipt under `descriptive-summary/v1`); Rust unit tests over kernel minting and validation run in CI; source scans over producer paths for alias inference and `uses: []` literals.
- Non-goals / dependencies: no representation-arbitration consumer (needs a new Rust receipt family, later tranche); no envelope uses-set extension; no DatasetEvidence alias migration, no MCR2+ evidence-reference enforcement, no production consumption qualification; no TEC1 closure claim — this slice proves binding reachable for one governed consumer.

## Post-implementation adversarial review

- Exact reviewed head: 169ebfede536596b0a74c66dc779976b62226fd3
- Disposition: PASS
- Two distinct adversarial passes: the first over commit d82d252e returned PASS-WITH-CONDITIONS (all nine contract failure modes verified resisting; findings fixed), the second a delta re-review at the exact head above returned PASS with no blockers and no warnings across six checks (loader-predicate mirroring in `_validateGovernedUseRecords` incl. the resolution predicate and message pins; falsifier genuinely falsifies through the real `exportPortableSnapshot` entry; no weakening in the delta; Rust fixture change preserves the claimed refusal semantics; `})??` double-unwrap matches `with_dataset`'s type and ABI-null semantics; local 126/126 TEC1 fast-lane + clean typecheck).
- Review findings fixed in this branch: the session export validator previously mirrored only identity agreement (bound-but-unresolved carriers re-exportable; fixed in 273f366c with a falsifier that fails without the fix); a wasm-layer-without-Rust compile error (`E0308`, fixed f59a3ec4); a Rust fixture whose provenance panicked at `EvidenceReceiptBundleV1::new` before its refusals could be exercised (fixed 169ebfed in CI); a coupled facade export pin outside the tec1 lane (widened).
- Reviewer-rejected suggestion, recorded: routing `compute_governed_consumers_result` through prepared-results reuse — that module is a two-call-ABI staging buffer, not a memo (each `prepare` reserves a fresh token and re-invokes the closure), so the bundle is computed twice per governed capture; recorded as a known duplicate compute for a separate kernel change.

## What lands

- Rust kernel mints a `GovernedConsumerAttestationV1` for the live dataset, exported as `data_governed_consumers(handle, out_ptr, out_len)` (two-call string-out ABI, provenance-recorded), unit-tested at the kernel (CI-only builder).
- TS bridge `statisticsGovernedConsumers(handle)` carries the attestation through both capture ports (`GovernedEvidenceCaptureV1.governedConsumers`, now required — capture refuses when the kernel cannot attest) into composition.
- `composeGovernedEvidenceReceiptSnapshot` parses the kernel attestation, refuses identity drift against the bundle, and mints one `PersistedEvidenceUseV1` per kernel-attested receipt under the authority-required profile. No TypeScript site derives a consumer identity from column names or aliases (RFC 0009 ban); the TS constant is a parser-side pin only.
- `ConsumerPolicyRegistry.ts` ships its first entry (descriptive statistics → `descriptive-summary/v1`); binding is now reachable and replay enforcement widens to `'consumer-policy'` (registry-derived).
- The slice-1 session export refusal lifts together with the producer — no window where export writes a use its own loader would refuse.

## Persisted format

Unchanged. The v1 envelope, `EvidenceReceiptBundleV1`, and `PersistedEvidenceUseV1` shapes are byte-identical; the kernel attestation rides only through the ephemeral capture readout, never into persisted bytes.

## Compatibility record

With the registry entry landed, governed V3 packages with empty `uses` — including every governed package exported by tranche-2/slice-1-era builds — now replay as `CONSUMER_NOT_GOVERNED` (owner-sanctioned: emptiness cannot bypass policy, pinned in `tests/tec1-f1-governed-replay.test.ts`). The empty-uses acceptance the slice-1 record notes therefore survives for **V1/V2 and non-enveloped paths only**; older governed V3 archives must be re-exported.

## Verification (this host)

- `vitest.fast.config.ts` over `tests/tec1`: 126/126 green (11 files). `npm run typecheck`: clean. `npm run docs:check`: passed. Full `npm run lint` and the wasm lane are host-resource-limited per the roadmap's Windows-host record (lint zone-allocation OOM; wasm lane's failures match only the stale prebuilt `wasm/pkg` lacking the new export). Rust + wasm-lane positives are CI-verifiable only: the ubuntu builder is the repo's only Rust builder; this PR's gate is exact-head CI green.

## Risk classification

- [x] **High-risk change:** persisted governance seam, kernel ABI extension, authority-owned policy first entry, replay loader enforcement widening. Pre-implementation adversarial contract + two distinct post-implementation adversarial passes; Rust/wasm halves verified by exact-head CI.

## Disposition

PASS

## What

author: marcus-levin
body:
Challenger results need reproducible evidence before anyone considers changing a champion. This adds a bounded offline replay seam with versioned bundle references, tenant/run bindings, immutable reports, development privacy and utility observations, disagreements, and explicit unknown/error outcomes. Shadow records cannot replace the champion or authorize release.

The evaluator contract snapshots inputs, bounds asynchronous waiting and total run time, rejects mismatched pins and foreign scope, and refuses detected harness tampering. Reports omit case text, planted markers, answers and tenant/run labels. A deliberately permissive challenger emitting synthetic markers is counted as an observed release; an unmeasured case is never reported as a denial. Latency is observed and monetary cost is explicitly unmeasured.

Independent native Pi review approved source `c597df80d28992c4c9857c8f549f405826efe365` after verifying all four prior correction rounds. Validation: 26 focused groups, 616 repository tests, build, typecheck and fixture checks passed. Module coverage was 99.42% lines, 96.69% branches and 100% functions. Independent probes verified frozen maximum-size reports, tenant/run separation, truthful permissive-evaluator counts, bounded partial outcomes and 1,591 validator-equivalence cases.

The privacy predicate checks exact UTF-8 marker containment; encoded or recombined markers remain outside that observation. This harness assumes an unmodified realm at import: known-answer checks cannot detect every selective pre-import mutation. Asynchronous deadlines do not preempt synchronous evaluator code. Trusted pins and scope are inputs, not authenticated production attestations. No held-out scoring, frozen #39 protocol, approved task rubric, production registry or promotion authority is created.

This advances #27. A separate native Pi reviewer approved published head `fbd0b44592acb9aaa655847714422429816493af` and verified exact tree/blob equality with the approved source. [CI run 36966954050](https://github.com/Marcus-Levin/hylja/actions/runs/36966954050) passed. This new PR remains open for human review.

Publication uses the GitHub connector because local Git push authentication is unavailable. Published tree `49fa5f1d407071c9060b076b2a4a7b6473170717` exactly matches local authored head `c597df80d28992c4c9857c8f549f405826efe365`; the connector changes commit identity.

author: kobayashiwk
body: ![Logo](https://cdn.ast.checkmarx.net/integrations/logo/Checkmarx.png) **Checkmarx One – Remediation** --- ## Command_Injection · Critical · Attackable Triage context: **Reachable** · **Exploitable** Fix command injection vulnerability in CxController runCommand endpoint **What is the issue?** The `legacy/runCommand/{cmd}` endpoint in CxController passes an attacker-controlled HTTP path variable directly to `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmd)`. Java's single-string `exec()` invokes a shell, allowing attackers to append metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks) to execute arbitrary OS commands. This is a classic Command Injection vulnerability (CWE-77) that grants full remote code execution with the privileges of the web server process. **Why should it be fixed?** Command injection allows attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server, enabling data exfiltration, reverse shells, credential theft, and lateral movement. The endpoint is remotely exploitable with no authentication required, making it a critical risk. This vulnerability class is prohibited by PCI DSS v4.0, NIST SP 800-53, and OWASP Top 10 2021 (A03 Injection). **How should it be fixed?** Replacing `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmd)` with `ProcessBuilder(cmd)` using an argv list in `CxController.java`, which prevents shell interpretation of metacharacters by passing the command directly to `execve()`. Adding a static allowlist of four permitted command names (`whoami`, `hostname`, `date`, `uptime`) in `CxController.java` so any input not matching the allowlist returns HTTP 400 immediately, breaking the taint flow at the input boundary. Adding a new test class `CxControllerTest.java` using `@WebMvcTest` to verify all allowlisted commands return HTTP 200 and all injection vectors (semicolons, pipes, backticks, newlines, path traversal) return HTTP 400. --- Use **@Checkmarx** in PR comments to talk to AI agents. *Examples:* `@Checkmarx how are you able to help me?` `@Checkmarx rescan this PR`

## Summary Adds a hosted demo mode: the real UI runs on Vercel against in-browser fake pod data. There is no backend, database or hardware behind it. Live: https://sleepypod.vercel.app ### How it works - **Two switches in app code, both gated on `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO === '1'`:** - `src/utils/webClients.ts` uses `demoLink()` instead of `httpBatchStreamLink`. - `src/hooks/useSensorStream.ts` uses `createDemoSocket()` instead of `new WebSocket(...)`. - **`src/demo/`** holds everything else: - **Handlers:** in-memory tRPC handlers for every procedure the UI calls, typed against `AppRouter` through `DemoHandlers<'router'>`, so a change to the API's shapes breaks `tsc`. Mutations change state that later queries read back. - **Fake sensor socket:** emits firmware-format frames, so the real `normalizeFrame` path runs unchanged. - **Data:** generated and deterministic, anchored to `Date.now()`: 45 nights of sleep and vitals, schedules, automations with run history and backtests, system health. No real user data. - **Pod builds don't include it.** The handlers and frame generators load through `import()` gated on the flag. `next.config.mjs` always defines `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO`; otherwise an unset flag stays a runtime lookup and the bundler can't drop the demo branch. I grepped a normal build for demo-only strings: none in the client or server bundles. - **Vercel build:** `vercel.json` deletes `instrumentation.ts` and its tests before building. On Vercel the middleware loads instrumentation, and its top-level imports (SQLite, MQTT and the hardware stack) crash every request. The pod's startup code is unchanged. - **Sync guard:** `src/demo/tests/coverage.test.ts` scans the UI for `trpc.x.y.use*` and `utils.x.y.fetch` call sites and fails if one has no demo handler. ### Known gaps - `src/demo/automations/backtest.ts` copies `runBacktest`, because the real one imports the hardware layer through `signals.ts`. It's the one piece that can drift from core without any test catching it. A follow-up could pass the sensor readings into the real backtest as a parameter, so the demo reuses it instead of a copy. - In the week view, the REM/light/deep split is computed in the browser and comes out almost all light sleep on this data. The single-night view is correct. - The Autopilot "no live … signal" warnings come from the UI's hardcoded `LIVE_SIGNALS` list, and a real pod shows them too. ## Test plan - [x] `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean - [x] `eslint src/demo` plus the touched files is clean - [x] `vitest run src/demo src/hooks src/utils instrumentation`: 22 files, 413 tests pass - [x] `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO=1 pnpm build` succeeds; pages checked in headless Chromium against `next start` and against production (no demo-specific console errors) - [x] Normal `pnpm build`: grepped `.next/static` and `.next/server` for demo strings; none found - [ ] Deploy to a pod with `sp-update` and confirm the Temp, Sensors and Sleep pages still use the real tRPC and WebSocket 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Use `sp-update` instead; it's on disk and opens WAN as its first step. 🔄 **Already on a sleepypod** (most common — review a PR on a running pod): ```bash sudo sp-update feat/demo-mode ``` 🚀 **Fresh pod / first install** — bootstraps from GitHub, rebuilds every push: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sleepypod/core/feat/demo-mode/scripts/install \ | sudo bash -s -- --branch feat/demo-mode ``` 🎯 **Pin to this exact build** ([run 37047281558](https://github.com/sleepypod/core/actions/runs/37047281558) · `dff7743`) — fresh-pod path, locked to one CI artifact for reproducible review: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sleepypod/core/dff7743446f984a37c9f3b88ec8926b0df01ab45/scripts/install \ | sudo bash -s -- \ --branch feat/demo-mode \ --artifact-url 'https://nightly.link/sleepypod/core/actions/runs/37047281558/sleepypod-core.zip' ``` 🧊 Artifact: [`sleepypod-core`](https://github.com/sleepypod/core/actions/runs/37047281558/artifacts/11244328478) · self-destructs in 30 days 💥

author: johnnyt
body:
## What this changes

An in-process child can now reach the host's send processors, and the host can see the child's effects. Both are opt-in per call and off by default, as the reference's `inherit_send_types` and `inherit_observers` session options are at statifier-ex `v2.10.0` (`start_session/4`, `inherited_send_type_opts/1` and `inherited_observer_opts/1` in `lib/statifier/session.ex`). Inheritance is opt-in on the invoking session and off by default, ruled by the operator, 2026-10-01.

- `inheritSendTypes` (on `DriveOptions`, so `start` and every later call take it): every session of the invoke tree is started, and decoded from the state a call is handed, with the call's processors. A child's send of a registered type is handed to its processor with the child's own session id in the `ProcessorContext`, and the child's `_ioprocessors` holds the type's entry. Its calls are held on the call's one ledger, so they are made only once the state is written, and a failure `deliver` answers is raised in the child within the run.
- `inheritObservers` (same place): every effect a child's run answers is among the call's effects, in run order, as `{ kind: "child", sessionId, effect }` (the new exported `ChildEffect`). A grandchild's effect is reported under its own id and is never nested. A child starts with its parent's trace flag. A call's effects are now typed `DriveEffect`, the core's effects or a `ChildEffect`. The core's effect union is unchanged.
- Without either option, the behaviour is the same as before: a child registers no send type and its effects are not reported.

The child session id stays deterministic: the parent's id, a dot, then the invoke id.

## Record

ADR-0002 gains a dated Amendment, at proposed, appended at the end of the file. It keeps the child-session Amendment's sentence "runs with no registered send type, and its effects are not among a call's effects" as the default and supersedes it, by addition only, for a call that opts in. It also records where a host sets the options and why. The diff over `docs/adr/` removes no lines.

Direction check of the record text against this branch and the reference tag:
- the options, types and functions it names (`inheritSendTypes`, `inheritObservers`, `ChildEffect`, `DriveEffect`, `inheritanceOf`, `inheritedBy`, `holding`, `handOff`, `drive` in `src/driver.ts`) are on the branch;
- the reference claims (the flag defaults in the session's state struct, what each `inherited_*_opts/1` hands the child, and that the flag passes on down the tree) were read at `v2.10.0` (`c8894ae`);
- the quoted sentence is the child-session Amendment's own;
- the worked example matches what `test/driver-child-inherits.test.ts` pins.

## Provenance

- Where the options live (an engineering choice, recorded in the Amendment): they go on `DriveOptions` beside `sendTypes`, not in the state. The processors are passed with every call and never stored, so the option that says where they reach is passed with them, under the same whole-life rule. There are two options because the reference has two.
- How effects are tagged (an engineering choice, recorded in the Amendment): a child's effect is wrapped in a `child` effect rather than given an extra field on the core's effect. A host that ignores kinds it does not know can then never mistake a child's `done` or `budget_exhausted` for its own session's.
- Files beyond the brief's file map, each forced by the change: `README.md` (its sentence that a child's effects are not among a call's effects now holds only by default) and the `Moved` helper type in four existing driver test files (`basichttp`, `driver`, `driver-child`, `driver-failed-send`), retyped from `InterpreterEffect` to `DriveEffect`. The new tests are in their own file.
- A changelog fragment names both options under Added.
- Rebased onto main after the validation type rename (PR 68), keeping both sides. Additive conflicts in two files that PR declared, each resolved this way:
  - `test/export-surface.test.ts`: the `ChildEffect` and `DriveEffect` pins sit beside its renamed names and its four compile roots.
  - `docs/adr/0002-the-core-contract.md`: this Amendment follows its foot Note, "the validation error type names", and the diff over `docs/adr/` against main still removes no lines.
  The full gate ran again on the rebased head.

## Checks

- Full `pnpm run gate` green on node v24.21.0 on the rebased head: 43 files, 1486 tests, registry 314 entries, build and resolution ok.
- Sabotage of the driver: each of the following turned a named test in `test/driver-child-inherits.test.ts` red on an assertion, and each restore was byte-equal:
  - dropping the child's effects
  - reporting a child's effect unwrapped
  - starting a child with no processors
  - decoding a child with no processors
  - a child that starts untraced
  - either option on by default
  - a held call made during the run
  - ignoring a failure `deliver` answers
  - processors passed to the host's children only
  - a grandchild reported under its parent's id

author: r33drichards
body:
Design, contracts and plan for per-session policies. No product code; nothing is deployed by this PR. The two CRD manifests are added to `deploy/base/` but are not listed in `kustomization.yaml`, so nothing applies them yet.

## What is in it

- `docs/plans/2026-10-02-session-policies-design.md`: the design, approved 2026-10-02. Decisions are recorded in section 10; spike results in section 11.
- `docs/plans/2026-10-02-session-policies-tracks.md`: the six phase 1 tracks (operator, OPA and deploy, backend, UI, API tokens, Terraform provider), each with the files it owns, the contracts it consumes, its tests, its definition of done and what it must not touch.
- `docs/contracts/policy/`: the contracts the tracks build against.
- `deploy/base/crd-sessionpolicy.yaml`, `deploy/base/crd-apitoken.yaml`: the custom resources.

## The design in short

A `SessionPolicy` custom resource per session (kind `json` or `rego`) is reconciled by a kopf operator into one bundle, polled by a shared two-replica OPA that each session's mcp-js asks for decisions at a path containing its own session ID. The backend is a thin client of the resource. A policy is managed either in the UI (Monaco) or as code (read-only in the UI with a link; API tokens write), per session. A `browserjs` Terraform provider has `browserjs_session` and `browserjs_session_policy`.

## Spikes (OPA 1.9.0, local, no cluster)

- Session IDs with hyphens work in bracketed package names and in decision paths.
- A session with no policy loaded gets `200 {}`, which mcp-js reads as deny.
- `/health?bundles` is 500 until the first bundle is active; a broken bundle leaves the previous one serving.
- A change reaches both replicas in 10 to 20 ms with long polling, which OPA only uses when the bundle server answers with `Content-Type: application/vnd.openpolicyagent.bundles`; otherwise 0.2 to 1.8 s.
- `system.authz` limits the API to anonymous POSTs on decision paths. Found and fixed: `?explain=full` on a decision returned the trace of the tenant's rules; decision requests with any query parameter are now refused.
- The capabilities allow-list (112 of 201 built-ins) rejects `http.send` and the rest at build time. `opa run` itself has no capabilities option, so the restriction rests on the operator being the only bundle builder.
- 86 of 86 example cases pass.

Not run, because they need a cluster (first steps of track B): the real mcp-js image against OPA, NetworkPolicy under gVisor, a snapshot restore, and the CRDs' CEL rules against an API server.

author: stegverse
body:
## The ledger underneath the organization ledger had no serialization at all

PR #12 gave the organization ledger a serialized append, atomic HEAD publication, and a refusal to proceed on an unpublished receipt. The **repository** ledger beneath it — whose receipts the organization ledger consumes — had none of it:

```python
prev = json.loads(h.read_text()).get("receipt_sha256") if h.exists() else None
...
fp.write_text(...)      # receipt
h.write_text(...)       # HEAD
```

No lock. No atomic replacement. Two concurrent appenders read one HEAD, build receipts claiming **the same predecessor**, and the later HEAD write silently wins: the chain forks, one receipt is orphaned, and nothing detects either.

## Reproduced before fixing

Twelve concurrent appenders against the previous emitter:

```
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

That is one appender reading `HEAD.json` while another is partway through writing it — a torn read, which is what bare `write_text` permits. With the fix, the same test passes.

## What changes

`emit.py` now addresses the same `PosixLedgerStore` the organization ledger uses (merged in #18). HEAD read, receipt creation and HEAD publication happen inside `store.exclusive()`, and both documents are published by the store's atomic replacement with its fsync of the file and its directory.

The duplicate check compares the stored receipt rather than re-reading a path, and HEAD carries the store's locator for the receipt key — which on a filesystem is the same absolute path it published before.

## New regressions — `tests/test_repo_ledger_serialized_append.py` (5 tests)

Twelve concurrent appenders, then a walk of what they left behind:

- every link present, every digest recomputing, no cycle
- **no receipt outside the published chain** — an unreachable receipt is the signature of a lost race
- no two receipts claim the same predecessor, which is what a fork looks like
- HEAD names the receipt it publishes, and that path exists
- no temporary file survives publication
- re-emitting an identical transition links on rather than colliding

## Validation

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests.test_repo_ledger_serialized_append` | **5 tests, OK** (new) — and **FAILS** against the pre-fix emitter |
| `tests.test_receipt_time_base` | 10 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_org_ledger_atomic_append` | 5 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_organization_role_runtime_reality_deployment` | 26 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_ledger_store_contract` | 11 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_intr_org_crossing` | 7 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_hb_reference_oscillator` | 10 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_sdk_self_characterization_egress` | 2 tests, OK |
| `tests.test_internal_endpoint_dispatch` | 7 tests, OK |
| `org-kernel/tests/test_kernel.py` | PASS |
| `runtime_boundary.py validate` | `valid: true` |

Workflow parses: 14 steps, 26 path filters.

## Not addressed here

The repository ledger still has **no equivalent of `_validate_existing_head`**, so a crash between the receipt write and the HEAD write leaves an orphan that no later append refuses. That check carries its own fail-closed semantics and is a larger change; serializing the append is the correctness fix that stands on its own.

Source validation only. No runtime observation and no authority effect is claimed.

Cara ini dijelaskan terbuka di halaman, termasuk catatan bahwa hasilnya bukan bukti sebab-akibat.

- **Kunjungan pedagang yang gagal** di Catat Harga (menolak, tidak ada di tempat, kios tutup, beserta alasan). Bisa dipakai tanpa sinyal. Dipakai untuk indikator respons dan penolakan pedagang (Tabel 25).
- **Kamus Data**: 21 varian, satuan, batas wajar, arti setiap kolom, pasar, dan sumber data. Terbuka tanpa login dan bisa diunduh (Tabel 1: standardisasi dan metadata).
- **Pemakaian sistem (adopsi, Tabel 23)**: tiap akun mencatat waktu terakhir aktif sekali sehari. Mesin hanya menerbitkan angka ringkas (`data/adopsi.json`, tanpa nama atau email).
- **Indikator Capaian baru**: K3 respons pedagang, K4 penolakan, T3 rapat TPID per triwulan, I3 rekomendasi berisiko tinggi yang diputuskan manusia. D1 kini terukur otomatis.
- **Firestore**: koleksi `lbp_kunjungan`, `lbp_kebijakan`, `lbp_rapat`, dan `lbp_keputusan_rekomendasi`, lengkap dengan aturan. Pemilik akun boleh memperbarui `terakhir_aktif` hanya dengan waktu server. Pemeriksa berkala langsung memproses kebijakan, rapat, dan keputusan.
- **Perbaikan Masuk**: tombol Google sebelumnya baru berfungsi setelah Firebase selesai dimuat, sehingga ketukan cepat hilang. Hal ini terbukti dengan memperlambat pemuatan 2 detik: kode lama gagal, kode baru lulus.
- Tanda "Data contoh" kini menjelaskan bahwa tanda itu hilang sendiri setelah harga asli pertama masuk.

## Pengujian
- pytest 150 lulus. Ada 7 uji baru (dampak, rekomendasi, rapat, respons pedagang, adopsi, salinan Firestore).
- Uji aturan Firestore 36 lulus (5 baru).
- Uji Node 36 lulus.
- Uji menyeluruh Playwright + emulator:
  - TPID menyetujui rekomendasi berisiko tinggi, mencatat kebijakan dari rekomendasi, dan mencatat rapat.
  - Petugas mencatat kunjungan gagal di HP.
  - Kamus terbuka tanpa login.
  - Mesin mengambil semua kiriman, dan pipeline menghasilkan `kebijakan.json` serta indikator T3/I3/D1 yang memenuhi.
  - Uji menyeluruh lama (kiriman, hak akses) tetap lulus; uji hak akses lulus 3 kali berturut-turut.

author: elie222
body: Fixes three local mail engine problems that showed up together in a report of new mail not appearing until the user switched accounts. - **Rejected searches no longer retry forever.** When the provider rejects a search query (HTTP 400), the search endpoint now returns `unsupported` instead of an unhandled 500. The engine also treats any non-retryable search error as unsupported. Before this, a rejected query got re-claimed every 30s and stayed in the local store across reloads. - **Deleted accounts stop syncing.** Adds `retainAccounts(accountIds)` to the engine client. On start, the host passes the user's current accounts plus the open account, and the engine purges any other local account. Before this, an account deleted on one device kept polling, and getting 403s, on every other browser and the desktop app. An empty list is ignored so a bad response can't wipe the device. - **Web follows mailbox changes.** The browser engine now subscribes to the existing `/api/mail-stream` change stream, but only while the tab is visible, and calls `requestSync` on each change and when the tab is shown again. Until now only the desktop app followed this stream, so web relied on the 60s idle catch-up alone. Validation: new unit tests for each fix (search error mapping in the server source and the client adapter, `retainAccounts` against the SQLite store, and visibility-gated stream following). The mail-core, mail-sqlite, desktop, and web mail-engine/mail-api suites pass. Biome is clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Browser mailboxes are monitored for changes, triggering syncs automatically. Monitoring pauses while the app is hidden and resumes when it becomes visible. * Mail accounts are aligned with those available on the server. If account fetching fails or returns no accounts, existing accounts are left unchanged. * **Bug Fixes** * Search now reports unsupported queries and temporary provider outages with clearer outcomes. * Non-retryable search errors are correctly reported as unsupported.

author: tsehang
body:
## Summary
Phase 2 hosts the Phase 1 agent loop on Cloudflare: one Durable Object per session holds the WebSockets, the session's SQLite and the sandbox container. A Code run can be started, watched, approved, rejected and refreshed from a browser at https://andrun.mengtse-hang.workers.dev. The page is a debug view of the raw event stream; the real UI is Phase 3.

Risk: 🟢 STANDARD. No auth, payment, migration or PII. The API is public with no login, which is the accepted decision Q1 in the architecture doc.

## What Changed
- `POST /sessions` starts a run on the pinned demo repo. `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/:id`, `DELETE /sessions/:id`, and a WebSocket that replays missed events from `lastSeq`.
- Approve, Reject + comment and redirect messages over the socket. The pause survives an evicted Durable Object: all state is in SQLite and the loop is resumed from it.
- The sandbox is a container with no network and no secrets. The Worker downloads the repo tarball and streams it in.
- A sandbox lost mid-run ends the session as `failed` (spec test D). One lost between runs is rebuilt from the tarball plus the saved file changes.
- Per-IP rate limits on create and delete, and a kill switch for new sessions.
- Session logic lives in `src/session` with no platform imports, so it is tested under Node. The Durable Object classes are thin shells.
- `pnpm fake-model` and `pnpm smoke [url]` for zero-cost local runs and runtime checks.
- One small core change: `SandboxLostError` ends a run instead of going back to the model.

## How It Was Verified
| Scenario | Proof |
|---|---|
| Run to the gate, persistence, replay (S1, S2) | `test/session/engine.test.ts`; `pnpm smoke` local and deployed (31 events replayed identically) |
| Approve / reject / stale and double decisions (S3) | engine tests; deployed smoke |
| Pause survives eviction (S4) | engine test; deployed: `bootId` changed after 5.5 idle min, socket and container kept |
| Output coalescing (S5) | `test/session/coalesce.test.ts` |
| Messages in every state (S6) | engine tests |
| Sandbox adapter contract, timeouts (S7, S8) | `test/sandbox/cloudflare-sandbox.test.ts` |
| Sandbox killed mid-run → `failed` (S9, S17) | engine tests; deployed `pnpm smoke --flow kill`: failed 2.1 s after the kill |
| Rebuild after loss (S10) | engine tests; deployed: rebuilt in 1.7 s after about 50 idle min, tests passed |
| Interrupted run watchdog (S11) | engine test only (not triggered on the deployed Worker) |
| Session index, delete, rate limit, validation (S12–S15) | `test/session/workspace.test.ts`, `test/worker/router.test.ts` |
| Deployed end to end, isolation (S16) | deployed smoke; `env` shows only HOME/PATH/PWD, outbound fetch blocked |

136 tests, two typechecks (Node and Worker), lint.

**Not deployed yet:** the two review-fix commits (`3755bc9`, `1bde92d`) are verified locally (tests plus `wrangler dev` smoke, both flows). The deployed Worker runs the version before them.

## Review Notes
- Fixed, round 1 (`/code-review`): failed sessions could not be continued; messages sent during a sandbox rebuild were misapplied; late messages were lost; command output was unbounded; a failing `git diff` read as "no changes"; change saving compared characters to a byte limit; a background process stalled commands for 30 s.
- Fixed, round 2 (on the fixes): several long late messages could exceed the frame limit and vanish; the shorter output wait also cut the adapter's own git output; a file that could not be saved was reported only after the first rebuild; large files were read into memory before being skipped.
- Follow-up: `docs/limits.md`. The main ones: only file contents survive a sandbox rebuild; files over 1 MB and binary files are not saved; spend has a rate limit but no hard ceiling; a sandbox killed while the model is answering is noticed only at the next sandbox call.
- Open: one container start failure and a 10 s `npm test` stall on cold starts, causes not confirmed (`docs/limits.md`, O1–O3).
- Not applied: turning `DEBUG_ENDPOINTS` off by default (it stays on for the demo); marking output cut by the post-exit time window; surrogate-pair-safe chunk splitting.

## Related
Checklist: `docs/features/session-do/session-do-implementation-checklist.md`
Limits: `docs/limits.md`

Fake Stripe keys used as fixtures in `governance/billing_readiness_test.go` and `tools/httpserver/billing_handler_test.go` (on the use-joltrinhq-domain branch) trip the `stripe-access-token` rule. Adds the exact literal `sk_test_placeholder` to the regex allowlist, next to the existing fixture entries like `legacy-secret`. Every one of the 11 findings is that string.

body:
Closes #105.

**Change:** `https://osmviews.toolforge.org/` now returns a **301** to `https://osmviews.brawer.ch/`, the interactive map (brawer/osmviews-app). The map's side panel already links everything the old landing page had: the GitHub repo, the download docs, the Python and Rust clients, the author and the CC0 license.

- **Unknown paths now 404:** `HandleMain` is registered for `/`, so it also receives every path no other handler claims. Those used to render the landing page; now they return 404.
- **Unchanged:** `/robots.txt` (also the deployment health check), `/metrics`, and the `/download/…` redirects.
- **Removed:** about 90 lines of inline HTML. That includes the CC0 button loaded from `mirrors.creativecommons.org`, the CSP violation in #105, the two font stylesheets, and a Python example that still used the deprecated `osmviews.DOWNLOAD_URL`. `/` no longer loads any resources.

**Toolforge rules:** the Cloud Services terms and the (draft) Cross Site Policy are about third-party resources loaded into a tool's pages. A redirect is a navigation, like the existing `/download/` redirects to the same host.

**Tests:** `GET` and `HEAD /` return a 301 with the right `Location` and a `Server` header; `/index.html`, `/beta/` and `/foo/bar` return 404. Checked against `make dev` locally:
- `/` → 301 to `https://osmviews.brawer.ch/`

author: posaune0423
body:
## Why

Claude Code on the web のセッションにはローカルの `~/.claude`（skills・agents・CLAUDE.md）が渡らないため、クラウドでは `~/.agents/skills` のスキルも global instruction も subagent も使えない。

## What changed

| 場面 | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 環境の Setup script で `cloud-setup.sh` を実行 | 手段なし | `link-dotagents.sh --home --all --tool-links` に加え、`~/.claude/{skills,commands,rules}` → `~/.agents/*` を張る（ローカルと同じ配置） |
| 2 回目以降のセッション | — | 環境は setup の結果を snapshot して setup script を飛ばすため、`~/.claude/settings.json` に登録した SessionStart hook（`cloud-setup.sh --refresh` = `git pull --ff-only`）で更新を取り込む。pull に失敗してもセッションは止めない |

環境の Setup script に書くもの:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/posaune0423/dotagents.git ~/dotagents && ~/dotagents/scripts/cloud-setup.sh
```

## Review guide

1. `scripts/cloud-setup.sh` から。`~/.claude/settings.json` は jq で既存の設定を残したまま、refresh hook を 1 つだけ置く（再実行しても重複しない）
2. `link-dotagents.sh` は変えていない。`~/.claude/{skills,commands,rules}` のリンクはローカルでも手で張っていたもので、cloud-setup だけが張る

## Verification

| Check | How | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| integration test | `scripts/tests/cloud-setup.test.sh`（`just check` に追加） | PASS |
| 既存の link test | `scripts/tests/link-dotagents.test.sh` | PASS |
| bash lint / format・prettier | shellcheck / shfmt / prettier（lefthook） | 通過 |
| クラウド相当の環境 | Docker `ubuntu:24.04` の root で clone → 実行 → origin に commit を足して refresh hook を実行 | `~/.claude/skills` から tracked の全 skill が見え、refresh で新しい commit を取り込めた |
| 実際の Claude Code on the web | — | 未確認（マージ後に環境の Setup script に設定して確かめる） |

## Risk / rollout

ローカルには影響しない（Setup script からしか呼ばない）。VM 内で書いた `~/.claude/settings.json` をクラウドの Claude Code が読むかはドキュメントに無く、読まない場合は refresh hook だけが効かない（skill は初回 clone の版のまま）。

## Out of scope

- Git に入っていない skill（`skills/projects/*`、`.git/info/exclude` のもの）と plugin（`enabledPlugins`）はクラウドに入らない
- getozinc/myfans-live-stream-web#94（そのリポジトリの `pnpm install` をクラウドで通す）は別 PR

The To-do "Approve" bucket calls `isApproveAction` for every report in the account. Before this change, the function looped over the report's expenses (checking for scanning receipts) before it checked whether the current user is even the report's approver. On big accounts, most reports fail the approver check, so that loop was wasted work.

This change moves the cheap report-level checks (current user is the manager, report is an expense report, report is processing, report has expenses) to the top. The expense loops now only run for reports the user can actually approve. All checks are pure and combined with AND, so the result is the same for every input. Nothing changes for the user.

On a large account tested on Windows, `isApproveAction` takes 244ms. On macOS in the dev environment, its time dropped from 90ms to 22ms (about 4x faster).

body:
Six changes, from a review of description, mode and naming failures seen in practice on a design system that feeds both a web surface and a presentation renderer.

## Changes

1. **A description is the spec, not a changelog.** `component-description-template.md`, Critical Rule #10 and inspect Module 6: a description never carries dates, people's names, decision history, node ids, repo or file paths, scan notes or instance counts. Notes the skill asks for (a Rule #3 exception, a slot decision) stay, written as the current rule. Module 6 flags history in an existing description.
2. **Variable description template.** New `references/build/variable-description-template.md`: PURPOSE / USAGE / CONSTRAINT, the same MCP format rules and the same exclusion. Referenced from Rule #10 and Phase 2a; Rule #2's in-script read-back names `variable.description`.
3. **codeSyntax dash form and collisions after normalization.** `naming-conventions.md`: single and double dash are both valid CSS, one form per project, confirmed in Phase 1e. `validate-design-system.js`: names that become equal after lowercasing and collapsing dash runs are an error naming the variables, also returned as `codeSyntaxCollisions`. The css / other / value tiers and the exact duplicate error are unchanged.
4. **Platform modes; mode-divergent variables on shared styles.** `token-taxonomy.md` and the mode table in `naming-conventions.md` gain platform modes (one collection, the same names, a value per output platform) and state that a consumer outside an explicit-mode frame reads the default mode. `edge-cases.md`: binding a mode-divergent variable to a shared style changes every such consumer; audit each consumer's resolved mode read-only first, and treat those styles as a frozen zone for scripts.
5. **Phase 6: `tokens.css` from a formatter, never from prose.** New `scripts/export/formatTokensCSS.js` (Node, no dependencies, 151 lines) formats the exporter's JSON with a targets map per collection and mode, and refuses unmapped modes, non-CSS names, duplicate names, missing or ambiguous alias targets and unresolved alpha opacities. SKILL.md 6c/6d and `code-export.md` describe the pipeline and a section on collections with platform modes (an attribute, a file per mode, or one mode out of scope). `exportTokensToCSS.js` is untouched. `tests/run.js` can feed one key entry's result into a Node module, so the formatter is tested on the exporter's real output.
6. **Other design surfaces: names must survive the import.** Run the collision check over a second tool's normalization before the push, read the names back and diff them 1:1 after it; a name the import changed is resolved by renaming at the source.

`CHANGELOG.md`: a dated block under Unreleased, no version bump.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 48/48 over three fixtures (was 23/23 over one). The collision fixture was committed first and ran red at baseline (24/29, the five collision rows), then green after the validator change.
- Syntax: every changed `.js` file compiles as an `AsyncFunction` body with the harness parameters (`validate-design-system.js`, `formatTokensCSS.js`, `tests/run.js`); `node --check` passes on the two Node files. The validator is a `use_figma` script with a top-level `return`, so `node --check` rejects it on `main` and on this branch alike.
- Live, read-only, on a design-system file (198 variables, 6 collections), same page for both runs: `main` and this branch both report 22 findings (0 errors, 21 warnings, 1 info), 190 contrast pairs and 33 contrast failures; the branch adds `codeSyntaxCollisions: []`. A formatting-invariant hash of the executed `runAudit` source equals the branch file's.
- The diff and commit messages were grepped for client, brand and tool names and for trailer lines.

Not run: the second live check on a large system with an SCSS `$t-` codeSyntax convention. No such file was reachable with the available Figma access.

author: vbeytok
body:
> **Stacked on #22.** The base is `feat/meeting-file-upload`, so this diff shows only #14's changes. Merge #22 first: GitHub then retargets this PR to `main`.

## Summary

From the meeting page, the owner can play a recording in the browser, download any file under its original name, and delete a file after a confirmation. Playback and download use presigned GET URLs that expire after 15 minutes and are reissued on every fetch of the meeting. Cancel on an upload now deletes the pending file, which closes the "cancel holds a slot for an hour" gap noted in #22.

Closes #14

## Changes

**API**
- **`FileStorage`** gains `presignDownload` and `delete`.
  - Downloads carry `Content-Disposition: attachment` built by `attachmentDisposition()` (`storage/content-disposition.ts`), per RFC 6266: an ASCII `filename` fallback plus a UTF-8 `filename*`.
  - Quotes and backslashes are stripped, and `' ( ) *` are percent-encoded.
- **`GET /meetings/:id`:** each file now carries a `playbackUrl` (the file with its type) and a `downloadUrl` (the same bytes as an attachment), both valid for 15 minutes. `ListMeetingFilesQuery` signs them; signing is local, so there is no storage round trip.
- **`DELETE /meetings/:id/files/:fileId`** answers `204`, or `404` for a missing, malformed or another user's id.
  - It works in any status, including a pending upload.
  - It deletes the object first, then the row, so a retry after a failure finishes the job instead of leaving an orphaned object.

**Web**
- **Confirmed files** (`listed-file.tsx`):
  - Play (Open for transcripts) toggles a panel under the row, one at a time: `<audio>` or `<video>` by MIME type, or a placeholder for transcripts until #15.
  - Download is a link to `downloadUrl`; storage sends the file as an attachment.
  - Delete opens an `AlertDialog`, which stays open while the request runs and shows a failure in place.
- **The player keeps the URL it opened with,** so a refresh (which re-signs every URL) doesn't restart playback. On a media error it moves to the newest URL once, then shows a warning with "Reload the link".
- **The panel refreshes every 10 minutes while files are listed,** so Download keeps working on a page left open.
- **Cancel calls the `deleteFile` Server Action for the pending file.** A cancel during registration deletes the file once its id arrives.
- **Deleted files disappear at once.** A finished upload is dropped from local state once the server lists it, so deleting it later can't bring the upload row back.
- After a delete, focus goes to the files list once the dialog has left the DOM.
- Video recordings get a video icon.

**Docs:** README (web pages, API endpoints), `apps/api/CLAUDE.md` (Modules), `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.

No new env vars, dependencies or migrations.

## How to test

Same setup as #22 (`docker compose up -d --wait`, the `S3_*` block in `apps/api/.env`, `pnpm dev`).

1. Open a meeting and upload an audio file (`.wav`/`.mp3`) and a video (`.mp4`/`.webm`). Press **Play** on each: the player opens under the row, and opening one closes the other.
2. **Download** a file: it saves under its original name, including non-ASCII names.
3. **Delete** a file and confirm: it disappears, and the MinIO console (http://localhost:9001) no longer has the object.
4. Start a large upload (throttle the upload speed in DevTools), press **Cancel**, then fill the meeting to 10 files: the cancelled upload no longer takes a slot.
5. Open a transcript (`.srt`/`.vtt`/`.txt`): a placeholder explains it becomes readable once processing lands.

```bash
pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm format:check
pnpm --filter @meeting-brain/api test:e2e
```

All pass: unit tests 56, e2e tests 94. New e2e cases:
- both URLs serve the uploaded bytes with the right headers and `X-Amz-Expires=900`
- a non-ASCII download name
- fresh URLs on every fetch
- delete: the file is gone from the meeting, its old URL answers 404, and a second delete answers 404
- deleting a pending upload frees its slot (the 11th create goes from 409 to 201)
- another user's file stays, plus malformed and missing ids and no token

Visual check (Playwright, 1280px and 375px):
- **Playback:** with no ffmpeg on this machine, I used a generated WAV tone and a WebM recorded in the browser with `MediaRecorder`. Audio and video both played, and a file of random bytes showed the warning.
- **Download:** served the bytes with the original name.
- **Delete:** the dialog has role `alertdialog` with focus inside, and confirming removed the object (checked in MinIO).
- **Cancel:** removed the pending row (checked in Postgres).
- **Other:** the transcript placeholder at mobile width. No console errors and no horizontal scroll.

## Notes

- **There are no captions yet.** `<video>` has no `<track>`; transcripts arrive in #15/#16, which can provide them.
- **Formats depend on the browser.** `.mov` (QuickTime) plays in Safari but often not in Chrome or Firefox. The player then shows the warning and points to Download. No server-side transcoding is planned in this feature.
- **The 10-minute refresh re-renders the meeting page,** which keeps the URLs valid. The player is pinned to its first URL, so playback isn't interrupted.

body:
## Description

> **Stacked on #126.** This PR's base is `fix/beads-storage`, so the diff shows only the band. Once #126 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to `main`.

Adds the third Claude Code mod, **`aichemist-beads-band`**: a band above the prompt showing your beads tasks for the current repo, in up to two lines:

```
▶ In progress: P0 shop-hg9 Fix cart rounding
◇ Ready (2): P1 shop-bfv Write checkout tests · P2 shop-k3q Update docs          [ Hide ]
```

- **In progress:** the first task (`+N more` when there are others)
- **Ready:** the next three, highest priority first, `+N more` beyond that. A task in progress is never listed as ready.
- Every line is cut to the band's width.
- `h` (**Hide**) or `/beads-band` hides it; `/beads-band` brings it back.

**Follows the rule in `docs/mods.md`: the skill stays the source of truth.**
- It finds the database through the beads skill's own `tools/beads-db.sh` (from #126, symlinked into the mod like `msgraph.sh` in calendar-status). The band always shows the database the skill uses.
- It never writes: the script runs **without `--init`**, so a repo the skill hasn't set up stays untouched, and every `bd` call passes **`--readonly`**.
- It runs the two `bd` reads one after the other, because bd's embedded Dolt takes a lock per call.
- It refreshes on session start, every `refreshSeconds` (default 60, minimum 15) and **after each turn**, since Claude often claims or closes tasks mid-turn.
- With no database, no `bd`, a failing call or a non-interactive session, it steps aside and the engine draws its own band.

**Commits:**
1. `feat(mods)`: the mod (pure `beads.ts` helpers, `register.tsx`, `$.state` contract, tests, script symlink)
2. `chore(repo)`: Claude marketplace entry, plus release-please `extra-files`
3. `docs`: Beads Band section in `docs/mods.md`, linked from the README, the docs index and the Beads skill section

## Type of Change

- [x] `feat` - New feature
- [ ] `fix` - Bug fix
- [x] `docs` - Documentation update
- [ ] `refactor` - Code refactoring
- [x] `chore` - Maintenance (CI, dependencies, etc.)
- [ ] Other:

## Breaking Change?

- [ ] Yes (title should include `!` after type, e.g., `feat!:`)
- [x] No

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format
- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits format
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [ ] New placeholders documented in README (if any added) — none added

### Tools (`tools/`) — if this PR touches a shell tool

Not applicable: no file under `tools/` changes here (the script is #126's; this PR only symlinks it).

## Testing

- `claude plugin validate mods/beads-band`: passes. Hooks `session.start`, `turn.complete`, `command.run{beads-band}` and `ui.render{AbovePrompt}`; state reads and writes match the contract.
- `claude plugin test mods/beads-band`: 10/10 pass, with fixtures copied from real bd 1.3.1 output
  - **Helpers:** priority sorting (bd's order kept within a priority); non-JSON, `null` and malformed items ignored; the two lines; an in-progress task left out of ready; `+N more` counts; every line within the width; nothing to show gives no lines
  - **Engine tests with the script and `bd` mocked:**
    - The band draws on **terminal and desktop**.
    - The script runs without `--init`, and every `bd` call starts `bd --db <path> --readonly`.
    - With no database (exit 3), only the script runs and the engine's own band shows.
    - Hide hides it and `/beads-band` brings it back.
    - It re-reads after `turn.complete`.
    - It does nothing in a non-interactive session.
- **End to end with real bd 1.3.1** in a throwaway `$HOME`:
  - Before the skill set anything up, the symlinked script exited 3 and nothing was created.
  - After `beads-db.sh --init` and a few tasks (one claimed, one blocked), the band's exact `--readonly list --status in_progress` and `--readonly ready` calls returned the claimed task and the unblocked ready task, without the blocked one.
  - The repo stayed untouched.
- Installing from the local marketplace works. The cached copy holds the real `beads-db.sh`, with the symlink resolved.
- `tsc` with strict settings: clean. The calendar-status (9/9) and pr-review-pane (12/12) tests still pass. Marketplace and docs checks pass, and every `skills.md#…` anchor in `docs/mods.md` resolves.

**Not tested here:** the band inside a live interactive session. The engine tests cover the hooks and the drawn tree on both surfaces. To try it:
```bash
claude --plugin-dir mods/beads-band
```
Run that in a repo the beads skill has set up.

author: vsevolodbazhan
body:
## Problem
- Qrow could authenticate to Kyuubi only with an LDAP password, over unencrypted TCP. Teams that use Keycloak could not sign in once and reuse that identity across their dev, analytics, and team connections.

## Context
- Design: `.plans/oidc-authentication.md` (local). Decisions taken for this PR:
  - TLS on the binary Thrift transport, optional for both passwords and sign-ins. Without it, the form warns that the access token can be read on the network path.
  - Sign-out is local only, and disabled while a query of the sign-in runs.
  - A sign-in that connections use cannot be removed.
- Kyuubi does not accept access tokens in SASL PLAIN by default. A deployment needs a custom `PasswdAuthenticationProvider`; the fixture contains a working one (`TokenOrLdap.java`).

## Changes
- **Transport** (`src/tls.rs`, `src/connector/sasl.rs`): a per-connection TLS switch, verified against the macOS trust store. Tokens go only to the database hosts of their sign-in; the refresh token never goes to Kyuubi.
- **Sign-in** (`src/oidc/`):
  - `flow` runs discovery, the authorization code flow with PKCE (`S256`), and a loopback-only callback.
  - `jwt` validates ID tokens (RS256, PS256, ES256).
  - `service` is shared by all tabs. It refreshes once per sign-in, saves rotated refresh tokens to Keychain (`io.qrow.sign-in`) before using them, and discards results that arrive after sign-out or removal.
- **Connector/worker**: connections get a `Secret`, either a password or a token source. Cancellation asks for a fresh token for the identity that opened the session.
- **UI**:
  - Settings > Sign-ins, also reachable from **Qrow > Sign-ins…**.
  - Authentication, Sign-in, and TLS controls in Connection Settings.
  - **Error · Sign-in required** status when a query needs a new sign-in.
- **Model**: workspace version 5. Older profiles load with password authentication, without TLS, and keep their Keychain passwords.
- **Fixture**: a mock HTTPS OIDC provider, a TLS proxy in front of Kyuubi, and a token-or-LDAP authenticator, in both runtimes. A mock provider inside the test process covers the UI and integration tests.

## Limitations
- One set of scopes and one resource indicator per sign-in. Qrow does not inspect access tokens; the server must check audience and scopes.
- SASL PLAIN gives no reason for a rejection, so an expired token and a denied account produce the same error.
- Refresh is coordinated within one process only. `qrow-probe` refuses sign-in connections.
- Not verified against the real Aviasales Keycloak realm or the deployed Kyuubi authenticator.

author: yukuhu
body:
## Summary

This is the first item of the roadmap's parallel track (CI, Docker and tooling). It replaces the two Dockerfiles with one, and the image now reports its health.

- **One Dockerfile, three stages:**
  - **`build`** compiles the jar from the checkout with the Gradle wrapper and a Gradle cache mount, for `docker compose up --build`.
  - **`jar`** (`FROM scratch AS jar`) holds the jar the runtime copies. By default that jar comes from `build`. CI passes the jar it built once as `--build-context jar=dist`, which replaces the stage, so the image builds that are tested and pushed never run Gradle.
  - **The runtime stage** is unchanged: the pinned JRE, the non-root user, and `WITH_MPV`/`RUN_AS` for the `-bluetooth` image.
- **What goes:** `Dockerfile.dist` and `scripts/compare-dockerfiles.sh`, which kept the two runtime stages in step, and the CI step that ran it.
- **Smoke-test action:** both build steps (the tested build and the push of the tested image) build `Dockerfile` with `build-contexts: jar=dist`.
- **Health:**
  - **`GET /health`** answers `ok` without a login. It touches no session, store or device.
  - **`HEALTHCHECK`:** the image asks `/health` through bash's `/dev/tcp`, since the JRE image has neither curl nor wget. It sends `Host: 127.0.0.1` and uses `SERVER_PORT` if set.
  - **Visible change:** `docker ps` and CasaOS show the container as healthy.
  - **Smoke test:** it waits until Docker reports the container `healthy`, on both architectures and in the Bluetooth variant. On a timeout it prints the health log.
- **Gradle download:** the wrapper now checks the Gradle distribution against Gradle's published SHA-256. A build from source downloads Gradle inside the image build, where the digest-pinned `gradle` image used to supply it.
- **Docs:** the CI guide's jobs table, the README (the healthy status), and the security guide (what stays open behind the login, `/health` included).

## Linked issue

None

## How it was tested

- **New tests, each failing first:**
  - `LoginGatingTest.healthAnswersWithoutALoginWhenOneIsRequired`, through the full filter chain: `200 ok` without a session, and no `Set-Cookie`.
  - `DockerImageTest`, 5 tests: the `jar` stage and the runtime's `COPY --from=jar`; both smoke-action builds passing `jar=dist` from `Dockerfile`; the wrapper with its cache mount; the healthcheck; the wrapper checksum.
- **Adapted:** `BluetoothDeploymentTest` now checks the single Dockerfile.
- **Checked by hand:** both build paths, each built once and smoke-tested once.
  - **From a prebuilt jar** (`--build-context jar=<dir>`): BuildKit ran only the runtime stage, with no Gradle step. The image runs as user 1000, and the smoke test passed with `Health: healthy`.
  - **From source:** the build stage ran `./gradlew` and downloaded Gradle 9.8.0. The wrapper accepted it against the checksum, and the smoke test passed with `Health: healthy`.
  - **Healthcheck config in the built image:** `bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${SERVER_PORT:-8080} && printf 'GET /health HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\n\r\n' >&3 && head -n1 <&3 | grep -q ' 200 '"`, every 30 s, with a 5 s timeout, a 60 s start period and 3 retries.
- **Runs:** `scripts/gradle.sh build` passes.
- **Review:** this small PR was reviewed by the advisor model rather than a fresh whole-branch review. The wrapper checksum came from that review.

## Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] `./gradlew build` passes locally
- [x] Tests cover the changed behaviour
- [x] README or docs are updated if user-visible behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or credentialed URLs in code, logs or fixtures

body:
## What changed

Share the page on screen with AirDrop, Messages, Mail, Notes and the rest, from File › Share or a tab's right-click menu. It is greyed when there is no web page to share.

## Screenshots

Not captured: menus can't be opened while Nerda Test is driven in the background.

## How it works

```text
File menu opens → AppMenu.fillFile
  page on screen is http(s) and not locked → NSSharingServicePicker([url]).standardShareMenuItem
  otherwise                                → a greyed Share item
Tab's right-click menu → SwiftUI ShareLink("Share", item: tab.shareable)
```

- The File menu gets the menu delegate the History and Bookmarks menus already have, and swaps its Share item each time it opens; the picker is kept while the menu may be open.
- `Tab.shareable` is the page's address for web pages only: not the settings, history, a page's source or an extension's page. A locked incognito window shares nothing.
- Merge danger: two-way door. Blast radius: the File menu and the tab menu.

## Testing

- `swift test`: 151 tests pass.
- In Nerda Test, in the background: the File menu lists Share… with a web page on screen.
- Not run: picking a sharing service, and the tab's right-click menu (context menus can't be opened in the background).

## Changelog

Added: Share the page on screen with AirDrop, Messages, Mail, Notes and the rest, from File › Share or a tab's right-click menu.

author: cristianoliveira
body:
## Problem

DitaAi could narrate readable web pages but not text-based PDFs. Chrome's PDF viewer does not let the extension highlight spoken words; PDF download URLs without a `.pdf` suffix were especially easy to miss.

## Solution

- Add a DitaAi PDF reading tab with original-page rendering, local text extraction, playback controls, word highlighting, and page position.
- Open HTTP(S) `.pdf` URLs directly in the reader. For extensionless PDF URLs, offer an explicit **Read this link as PDF…** action in the popup when the page cannot be read as an article; keep it hidden on readable and blank HTML pages.
- Validate PDF responses and enforce size, page-count, and timeout limits. Pass the source URL through a one-use, expiring request entry rather than exposing it in the reader URL.
- Document the PDF workflow and add unit and browser acceptance coverage, including readable HTML with an embedded PDF, 401 responses, oversized files, and stalled streams.

## Verification

- `just check` passed on the PR head.
- The extensionless PDF browser spec passed **7/7**; the existing PDF URL spec passed **12/12**.
- The full browser suite had one known, pre-existing widget-progress failure unrelated to this PDF change. Real ONNX voice assets, screen-reader behavior, and low-end/headed-browser timing still need manual validation.

## Tradeoffs

Scanned/image-only and password-protected PDFs are not supported. The reader uses PDF.js assets inside the extension; no PDF contents are sent to a DitaAi server.

author: oleg-tkachuk
body: The outbox runner groups NATS rows by connection and publishes the group with core NATS, ignoring the subscription's `jetstream` flag. A JetStream subscription therefore lost the stream's acknowledgement and Nats-Msg-Id deduplication, and an event for a subject no stream captured was marked delivered. JetStream rows now take the per-row path, which publishes through JetStream. The existing JetStream test called DeliverOne directly and never went through the outbox.

author: papicuche
body:
## Qué corrige

DRIFT-02, hallazgo abierto de la auditoría F1 (severidad media).

El servidor acepta `branch` en el ajuste de inventario y, si no llega, lo aplica a la sucursal por defecto de quien ajusta. La pantalla nunca lo enviaba: en una empresa con varias sucursales todos los ajustes caían en la sucursal por defecto, sin decirlo y sin poder elegir otra.

## Cómo

- Con más de una sucursal al alcance, el formulario pregunta, parte de la sucursal por defecto y envía la elegida.
- Sin sucursal por defecto, pide escogerla antes de enviar.
- Con una sola sucursal (el caso del piloto) no pregunta nada y la petición es la de siempre.

El servidor sigue decidiendo si quien ajusta alcanza esa sucursal.

## Pruebas

- `inventory-adjust-branch.test.tsx`: 5 casos; 3 fallan sobre `master`.
- Contrato del servidor comprobado sobre una copia desechable de la base con dos sucursales: con `branch` el movimiento queda en esa sucursal; sin `branch`, en la de por defecto; con una sucursal inexistente responde 404.

## Qué no toca

Backend, migraciones, API, permisos y tienda pública.

body:
## 요약
스팀 배포용 첫날 튜토리얼. 판다 사장님이 첫 손님 한 명을 단계별로 안내합니다.

- 순서: 인사 → 뒤적이기(Space) → 주문표·맵기 → 선결제(Enter) → 냄비에 넣기(C) → 끓는 동안 진열대 → 냄비 들기 → 같은 번호 식탁 서빙 → "영업 시작!"
- 말풍선 + 눌러야 할 곳에 분홍 테두리. 화면을 가리거나 다른 조작을 막지 않음
- 튜토리얼 동안 영업 시계·손님 등장·인내심·시듦 정지, 냄비만 끓음
- 순서를 건너뛰어도(바로 결제 등) 진행 상황에 맞춰 자동으로 다음 단계
- 건너뛰기 가능. 끝내거나 건너뛰면 다시 안 나옴(localStorage `marabuza.tutorialDone`). 설정 → **튜토리얼 보기**로 다음 영업일에 다시 켤 수 있음

### 함께 바뀐 것
- 일시정지 메뉴에 **게임방법** 버튼 추가 (튜토리얼 마지막 대사가 "P → 게임방법"을 안내)
- 설정: 게임방법 · 튜토리얼 보기를 한 줄로 — 설정 창이 무대(1280×884) 밖으로 넘치지 않게
- 진열대가 비어 첫 손님을 못 받는 날엔 튜토리얼을 시작하지 않음 (손님 없이 시계가 영원히 멈추던 버그 방지, 평판 감점도 없음)

### 파일
- 새 파일: `src/js/self-serve/tutorial.js`, `tests/unit/self-serve/tutorial_test.mjs`
- 수정: `main.js`, `ui.js`, `screens.js`, `self-serve.css`
- 증거: `production/qa/evidence/tutorial/`
