author: pirakaplant
body: ## About the PR This PR removes most of the HUDs in the game. This means there's no more administrative glasses, beer goggles, medical HUD, security glasses, etc. The Detective keeps their noir-tech glasses, but with the sechud functionality removed. Also, the SecTech gets an extra three pairs of sun glasses. Syndicate HUDs are untouched for now. I don't know what to do with them yet. ### How to enable / disable Just revert this PR. If it was all partials you could just get rid of those, but there are changes that had to be made via modification of base YAML. ## Why / Balance Take a look at funky-station/docs#74. But as a summary: - HUD eyewear don't fit the technology of the aesthetics we are going for. - Administrative/Security HUDs make it impossible for most characters to infiltrate other departments or be stealthy without being caught immediately by an officer. - Medical HUDs further optimise already over-optimised gameplay and are wholly unnecessary to treat patients. ## Technical details Most of the changes in this PR were made using partial prototypes. At time of writing, this is the first and only PR on this repo to use partial prototypes. We should be using them a lot more, and migrate old changes over to the system. Because of this, I felt the need to set good standards for using them: - In `partialPrototypes.yml`, I list every file that has partials in alphabetical order. + Don't use directories for this yet, they seem to exponentially increase the burden on the client when loading the game, to the point where it freezes and crashes on the loading screen. - The partial for any given prototype is found in a file with the same name as the file as the prototype is located in, except under `Prototypes/_Funkystation` instead of `Prototypes`. + I prioritised following proper naming conventions and organising over being totally accurate, hence the file that modifies `emergencyresponseteam.yml` is called `emergency_response_team.yml`. Likewise, I hope that when the loadouts are migrated to partials, that the partials are split up by department rather than having a "medical" file and a "everything else" file for some reason. - I put the partial prototypes at the top on the file, in the order they appear in the original file. The entire section of partials is started with `# Partial prototypes begin` and ended with `# Partial prototypes end`. Notably, the changes to locker fills and the removal of two construction recipes required edits to base YAML, as (at least as far as I know/have been told) partial prototypes do not support the former yet. Likewise, ignored prototypes would not work for the latter, as only entire files can be specified. Those changes have been appropriately commented. ### Mapping details Don't map anything that has `DoNotMap` added to it. Simple as. ## Test plan 1. Spawn in as the Captain or a Security job. You should be wearing sun glasses instead of the old HUD eyewear. 2. Spawn in any of the filled variants of the captain's locker, a booze storage locker, and the lockers of Security jobs (besides brigmed). There should be no HUD eyewear in there. 3. Spawn in a BarDrobe, MedDrobe, RoboTech Deluxe, and a SecTech. None of them should have HUD eyewear in them, and the SecTech should have five pairs of sun glasses. 4. Search in the construction menu for "security glasses" and "medsec hud". Nothing should appear. ## Media _(The default Security Officer loadout, with sun glasses instead of security glasses.)_ ## Requirements - [X] I have read and am following the Macrocosm [Pull Request Conventions](https://docs.macrocosm.cool/Documents/Conventions/pull-requests). - [X] I have tested this pull request and written instructions on how to test it - [X] I have added media to this PR or it does not require an in-game showcase. - [ ] If I am porting something, I have done my best to respect the appropriate licenses associated with the presented changes. ## License MIT ## Breaking changes N/A. ## Changelog :cl: - remove: All eyewear that provides administrative, beer, medical, or security HUDs has been removed, except for noir-tech glasses. - tweak: Noir-tech glasses no longer provide a security HUD and are no longer Security contraband. - tweak: Jobs that started with administrative or security glasses now begin with sun glasses instead. - tweak: SecTech vending machines now have five pairs of sun glasses.

author: ohmiler
body:
## What changed
Adds `tests/integration/promptpay-fulfillment.mysql.ts` (test only, no production code) running `claimPromptPayIntent`, `releasePromptPayIntent` and `fulfillPromptPayIntent` on the isolated MySQL database:
- two concurrent claims: exactly one wins, the loser gets `PAYMENT_STATUS_VERIFYING`;
- wrong owner and expired (30 min) intents are refused and stay pending; release only moves `verifying` back to `pending`;
- fulfilling grants one enrollment and stores the reference (also copied into `slipUrl`, pinned);
- two concurrent fulfillments of one intent: one `fulfilled`, one `already_fulfilled`, one enrollment;
- an unclaimed intent cannot be fulfilled; a slip reference already used by another payment is rejected and the second payment rolls back (unique index);
- bundle enrolls every course; an empty bundle rolls back;
- coupon usage stored with `discountAmount` 0 (**KNOWN DEFECT**, pinned not endorsed).
Same safety as the Stripe tests: refuses anything but a loopback `milerdev_e2e`, deletes only rows it created.

## Finding (not fixed here)
`createdAt` is a whole-second DATETIME, so MySQL can round "now" up to 0.5s into the future, and the claim guard (`createdAt > now`) then reports a brand-new intent as `PAYMENT_INTENT_EXPIRED`. Only claims within the first half second are affected, so it is unlikely in practice. The tests seed intents 5 seconds in the past to stay deterministic.

## Verified
- 11 tests pass on a local `milerdev_e2e`, 6 consecutive runs. The first version was flaky because of the rounding above, which is how the finding surfaced.
- Mutation checks: removing the `FOR UPDATE` row locks makes the concurrent-fulfillment test fail 3/3. Removing only the `status !== 'verifying'` pre-check changes nothing, because the UPDATE's own `status = 'verifying'` condition still catches it (redundant guard). Source restored after each.
- `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint pass.

## Not verified
- Not yet run on GitHub CI. The SlipOK verification step and the HTTP slip handler are not covered here.

## Production risk
None (tests only). Merging triggers the usual Railway rebuild.

body:
Before: #151을 머지한 뒤 스테이징 배포가 `gcloud secrets versions list --secret=app-data-key-v1-staging` 에서 `unrecognized arguments` 오류로 멈췄습니다(데이터 키를 건드리기 전 안전 정지). 같은 잘못된 형식이 `_ensure_secret`과 db-admin-password 확인에도 있었습니다. 이 두 곳은 오류를 삼켜 "버전 없음"으로 판단했기 때문에, 배포 때마다 새 비밀값 버전을 추가해 온 것으로 보입니다(로그에서 추정했고 GCP에서는 확인하지 않음).

After: `scripts/deploy.sh`의 네 곳 모두 실제 gcloud 형식인 `gcloud secrets versions list NAME ...`을 씁니다. 로그인 비밀값, DB 관리자 비밀번호, 메일 설정은 버전 조회가 실패하면 새로 만들지 않고 배포를 멈춥니다(데이터 키와 같은 방식). DB 관리자 비밀값은 버전을 조회하기 전에 먼저 만들어 두므로, 새 환경의 첫 배포도 멈추지 않습니다.

author: greenpaulo
body:
# Syailendra is implemented as a Barrier, so the game looks for a Fracter to break it instead of the Decoder it actually needs

## Resolution

Implemented from `f2054ee`.

Corrected Syailendra's card header and `subTypes` declaration from `Barrier` to `Code Gate`, matching canonical card code 35076. The shared runner and Corp breaker-matching consumers were inspected and already map Decoder to Code Gate and Fracter to Barrier, so no AI or engine change was needed.

The reproduction was added at `tests/pending/syailendra-typed-as-barrier-instead-of-code-gate.test.js`, where it failed at the starting commit with actual `Barrier` versus expected `Code Gate`. It was moved unchanged in substance to `tests/syailendra-typed-as-barrier-instead-of-code-gate.test.js`; `node tests/syailendra-typed-as-barrier-instead-of-code-gate.test.js` now passes. Its directory-relative repository-root lookup was adjusted after the move, without changing the subtype expectation.

No approval-gated implementation plan was required: this is an objective printed-card-data correction confined to one card definition, with no shared heuristic, engine function, AI hook contract, green expectation, or multi-file source change. The ticket's broader suggested encounter and Corp-security scenarios were not added because the focused canonical-data regression directly covers the defective field while the existing security suite already covers generic subtype matching. The proposed cardpool-wide audit was also left out of scope because it could surface unrelated card-data discrepancies requiring separate validation.

Validation completed with the focused regression, `tests/corp-server-security.test.js`, `tests/corp-decision-fixtures.test.js`, `tests/decision-snapshots.test.js`, and the full `node tests/run-all-tests.js` suite (40 test files passed). No open implementation issues remain.

**Suggested location:** `documentation/bugs/` (move to `documentation/bugs/done/` once merged).
**Source log:** `documentation/debug-logs/bug_raised/code_gate_is_looking_for_a_fracter_to_break_it.txt`
**File:** `sets/elevation.js` — Syailendra's card definition (`cardSet[35076]`).
**Confirmed against:** `carddata/carddata.json` (`code: 35076`, `keywords: "Code Gate - AP"`).
**Status:** Implemented; awaiting independent review.
**Reproduction:** `tests/pending/syailendra-typed-as-barrier-instead-of-code-gate.test.js` fails at `f2054ee`, 2026-10-02: implemented `Barrier` does not match canonical `Code Gate`. Moved to `tests/syailendra-typed-as-barrier-instead-of-code-gate.test.js`; `node tests/syailendra-typed-as-barrier-instead-of-code-gate.test.js` passes after the fix.

## Acceptance gate

N/A — deterministic fix (principle 4): the implemented primary ice subtype must match the printed card data for card code 35076.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Syailendra is implemented with `subTypes: ["Code Gate"]`, matching the canonical card data.
- [x] The regression test fails before the fix and passes afterward without changing its expectation.
- [x] The full green test suite passes.

---

## 1. Summary

[Verified] Syailendra is a Weyland Code Gate in the real card pool (`carddata/carddata.json` lists it as `keywords: "Code Gate - AP"`, matching `code: 35076`, the same ID used for this card's implementation). But its implementation is typed as a **Barrier**:

```js
//Syailendra
//Weyland Ice: Barrier                    <- wrong in the comment too
//Rez: 4, Strength: 5
...
cardSet[35076] = {
  title: "Syailendra",
  ...
  cardType: "ice",
  subTypes: ["Barrier"],                  <- should be ["Code Gate"]
  rezCost: 4,
  strength: 5,
  ...
```

Every breaker-matching check in the AI (`_matchingBreakerForIce`, `_aCompatibleBreakerIsInstalled`, `_numCompatibleIceInstalled` in `ai_corp.js`) is implemented correctly — Fracter↔Barrier, Decoder↔Code Gate, Killer↔Sentry are matched the right way round throughout. The bug isn't in that matching logic at all; it's that Syailendra hands those correct checks the wrong subtype to match against. The practical effect is exactly what the log's filename says: the game treats a Code Gate as if it needs a Fracter to break it, so the Runner's actual Code Gate breaker (Unity, a Decoder) is never recognised as capable against it, and only an installed Fracter (which this Runner never installs) would ever count.

The likely origin is copy-paste: Syailendra (`cardSet[35076]`) sits immediately after Kessleroid (`cardSet[35075]`) in `sets/elevation.js`, a genuine Weyland Barrier with the same faction and a near-identical boilerplate shape (`cardType: "ice"`, `subTypes: ["Barrier"]`, similar rez/strength fields). Card-specific fields (title, rez cost, strength, subroutines, the advancement mechanic) were all correctly written for Syailendra; only `subTypes` (and the header comment above it) were left as the template's `Barrier`.

---

## 2. What happened in the log

The Runner's deck contains Unity (a Decoder — the correct breaker for a Code Gate) and Marjanah (a Fracter — the correct breaker for a Barrier), per `carddata/carddata.json` and `sets/*.js`. Marjanah sits in the Runner's grip for the entire log and is never installed; Unity is installed partway through (line 438) and is confirmed working correctly against the deck's other Code Gate, Flyswatter (`subTypes: ["Code Gate"]`, correctly typed in `sets/elevation.js`):

```
Runner spent one click
Runner installed Unity
...
Approaching outermost piece of ice protecting HQ
AI: I will rez the approached ice
Corp rezzed Flyswatter
Using Unity:
Runner spent one credit
Subroutine End the run. broken          <- Unity correctly breaks the real Code Gate
Approaching next piece of ice protecting HQ
AI: I will rez the approached ice
Corp rezzed Syailendra
Encountering Syailendra
Firing You may place 1 advancement counter on an installed card you can advance. on Syailendra:
1 advancement counter placed on Syailendra
Firing The Runner loses 2[credit]. on Syailendra:
Runner lost 1 credit
Firing Do 1 net damage. on Syailendra:
```

No `Using Unity:` line ever appears for Syailendra — all three of its subroutines simply fire unbroken, one after another, even though the Runner had just used the exact same breaker one ice-piece earlier in the same run. With Syailendra mistyped as `Barrier`, Unity's `CheckSubType(card, "Decoder") && CheckSubType(iceCard, "Code Gate")` match in `_matchingBreakerForIce` (and the identical check the Runner's own interface-break enumeration uses) never fires for it, so the game never offers Unity as a way to break it — only a Fracter would qualify, and the Runner has none installed.

The same mistyping shows up throughout the Corp AI's own turn planning, for the entire game, in the repeated security-evaluation lines:

```
AI: HQ appears secure: Flyswatter has mandatory breaks with no capable breaker; Syailendra omitted from best affordable rez plan; break cost Infinity > Runner credits 6
```

Because Syailendra is (wrongly) treated as needing a Fracter the Runner never
installs, `_matchingBreakerForIce` returns `null` regardless of the installed
Decoder. This inflates its optional break cost. It does **not** always create
`hasHardLockout`: while the Runner has at least one card in Grip, Syailendra's
three subroutines can continue without a break, so
`_estimateBreakCost(..., true)` returns zero; its net-damage subroutine can
become mandatory when Grip is empty. The subtype error still makes the Corp's
rez-plan and total-cost estimates ignore the real Decoder path, but the exact
lockout result depends on Grip and the other ICE in the route.

---

## 3. Root cause

**Where:** `sets/elevation.js`, `cardSet[35076]` (Syailendra), specifically the `subTypes: ["Barrier"]` line and the `//Weyland Ice: Barrier` header comment directly above it.

[Verified] This is a plain data-entry error, not a logic bug. Every inspected con

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Fixes code scan finding sfind-558b701960bf40798442e57542cc972b (path traversal, low). A model import ZIP uploaded through `/v1/catalog/model` and `/v1/catalog/model/imports` could contain an absolute entry such as `/opt/app/x.yaml`. `ZipUtils.checkForZipSlipInRead` only rejects `../` and non-canonical paths, so it let this through. The path was stored as `ToscaImportByModel.fullPath`. Later, `CommonCsarGenerator.addSchemaFilesByModel` ran `defsPath.resolve(Path.of(fullPath))`. An absolute argument makes `resolve` drop `Definitions/`, so the distributed CSAR had an absolute entry name. The fix adds two checks: ``` // upload: ModelBusinessLogic.createModelImports unzip -> validateImportPaths(keys) // any unsafe path -> COULD_NOT_READ_MODEL_IMPORTS (400) // generation: CommonCsarGenerator.addSchemaFilesByModel defsPath.resolve(importPath) -> resolveModelImportEntryPath(defsPath, importPath) // unsafe or outside defsPath -> CSAR_TOSCA_IMPORTS_ERROR ``` Both use new helpers in `ToscaDefaultImportHelper`: - `isSafeImportPath(String)` returns false for a blank path, a path starting with `/` or `\`, a drive letter (`C:`), or a `..` segment. Backslashes count as separators. - `resolveImportEntryPath(defsPath, importPath)` returns `Optional.empty()` if the path is unsafe or if the normalised result is not under `defsPath`. An empty `defsPath` is allowed. Valid entry names do not change. The generation check also covers imports already stored in Cassandra before this change. We stop the CSAR build there rather than skip the entry, so we never produce a CSAR that is quietly missing imports. Tests: `ToscaDefaultImportHelperTest` (20), `ModelBusinessLogicTest` (13, including absolute and drive-letter uploads), `CsarUtilsTest` (28) and `ToscaExportHandlerTest` (45) all pass with `mvn -B test -pl catalog-be`. This targets `master`, because the repo has no `main` branch. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9826336a47a646b0ae2eaa158d7fc9e5 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/9826336a47a646b0ae2eaa158d7fc9e5?variant=devin Requested by: @jacobsbenjaminuk-cell ---

body:
## Intent

Apply the shared teoyujie.org visual style guide (yujieteo/skills interactive-visual-spec/references/style-guide.md and assets/style-tokens.css, merged in https://github.com/yujieteo/skills/pull/16) to the kent visual. The captain asked for one style guide across all visuals and for it to be applied to the visuals themselves; this visual is in the batch of visuals with custom palettes, so it gets a full restyle the way toulmin and riemann-roch did: its own palette (Solarized or a custom warm/cool set) is replaced by the guide's token names and values, domain colours become aliases of the series tokens (--c1..--c4, --hl, --ok/--warn/--bad), links/focus/primary action/sliders use --focus, the selected state is the --fg dark chip, buttons and fields take the --control outline, title/eyebrow/label type follow the guide, a head script with id site-theme applies the reader's site-wide Light or Dark choice from localStorage 'theme' before paint, and print uses the light palette. Constraints: style-only diff; keep the visual's logic and behaviour unchanged (no computations, element ids, text, ARIA names, URL or storage state, export formats or WebMCP tools change), except that a private theme key moves to the shared 'theme' key as the guide's step 5 allows. Layout is left alone unless it breaks a rule or shows a defect (large empty gaps, overflow at 390px). Kent-specific: the ruler track was a dark-to-light Solarized gradient; it is now a neutral --axis to --surface ramp so the --c1 needle stays visible in both themes. The brand title KENT was a small letter-spaced uppercase word; it now uses the guide's h1 scale (the text is unchanged, only text-transform is dropped). Per the site's add-visualization playbook, the test step also smoke-checks the port: shallow-clone yujieteo/site, copy this repo minus tests/ and .github/ into visuals/kent/, build with VISUALS_REPO set, and browse only that page; do not run the full site suite or add site tests.

## What Changed

- Swapped the Solarized palette in `index.html` for the style guide's light and dark tokens (`--bg`, `--fg`, `--muted`, `--surface`, `--border`, `--control`, `--axis`, `--focus`, `--c1..--c4`, `--hl`, `--ok/--warn/--bad`). The old domain colours are now aliases of the series tokens (for example, `--blue` maps to `--c1`, `--orange` to `--c2` and `--green` to `--ok`). The ruler track used to be a dark-to-light Solarized gradient. It is now a neutral `--axis` to `--surface` ramp, so the `--c1` needle stays visible in both themes. Print now uses the light palette.
- Updated controls and type to follow the guide:
  - Links, focus rings, the primary button and sliders use `--focus`.
  - Selected chips, tabs, segments and choices use the `--fg` dark chip.
  - Buttons and fields have the `--control` outline.
  - The eyebrow, kicker, table headers and labels use the guide's mono uppercase label style.
  - The `KENT` title uses the guide's h1 scale. Its text is unchanged and `text-transform` is removed.
  - Coloured text (band labels, reader and diff markers, delta, badges) moves to `--fg` or `--muted`, and the series colour stays on the marks.
- Added a `<script id="site-theme">` in the head. Before first paint it applies the reader's site-wide Light or Dark choice from `localStorage` `theme`. The diff changes only styles: no logic, element ids, text, ARIA names, URL or storage state, export formats or WebMCP tools change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round is a CSS-only change. It moves small series-colour text (badges, kentpin, band labels, marker labels, delta, same span) to --fg/--muted and keeps the series colour on the borders, ticks and dots, as the user instructed. It also drops the redundant print --lo/--hi, which :root still defines. No ids, text or logic changed.

## Testing

I drove the restyled page live in Chrome: light and dark themes; the shared `theme` key (overriding the OS, an invalid value, storage blocked); and each contrast fix you chose (writer/reader markers, Kent lab pins, overdue forecast badge, delta and "same" emphasis). I also checked overflow at 390px, behaviour and DOM against the base commit, print to PDF from an OS-dark browser, and a build of the port in a shallow clone of yujieteo/site. Every scenario passed. The 2px Kent lab overflow at 390px also happens on the base commit, so this change did not cause it. I saved screenshots and a PDF to the evidence directory. I did not run the repository test suite. All servers, clones and the browser session have been removed.

author: erikdesrosiers
body:
## Summary

This is Foundation's deterministic consumer of the internal decision practice (#118), for this repository's own recorded decisions. It is the first-consumer journey designated in the unit 4 / consumer record. Path: `scripts/practice-consumer/**`, registered to Foundation (protocol-roots rev 171, effective after #118 merged).

## How it works

`reconsider.mjs measure --pr N --base SHA --head SHA` reads, at exact commits:
- the recorded decisions in `docs/integration-contract-decisions.md`;
- the files each decision links to;
- how the pull request changed those files.

It then runs `evaluateDecisionPractice` with:
- the adopted definition (`definition.json`);
- an in-memory Knowledge history rebuilt from the base;
- exact evidence for the changed region and the decision;
- a deterministic assessment: `foundation-deterministic` / `cited-source-predicate.v1`, `usage: null`, no model call.

| Change to the cited file | Assessment | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A line modified or removed | `affected` | proceed: an unaccepted reconsideration draft |
| Only lines added | `unaffected` | stop |
| Binary, removed or over the excerpt bound | abstained, `insufficient-evidence` (reason recorded) | escalate |
| Not changed | (prerequisite false) | stop |

It appends one measurement line to `measurements.jsonl`. A person then labels each outcome `correct`, `missed`, `false-alarm` or `useful-abstention`, with correction minutes. Each line also records whether the Knowledge harness itself marks the decision for reconsideration.

## What it does not do

- It calls no provider and appends to no store. It accepts or activates nothing, and it writes only its measurement file.
- It is not in the package and adds no public API.
- The rebuilt history's review and activation records stand for Foundation's adoption of the practice for its own repository. They are not an independent or human review.

## First measurements (retrospective)

| PR | Outcome | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #107 | stop | correct |
| #111 | proceed (`docs/architecture.md` table row changed) | false alarm |
| #121 | stop | correct |
| #125 | stop | correct |
| #118 | stop | correct |

Only 1 of 10 recorded decisions links a file, so 9 are not yet measurable. A change that matters without touching a cited file is a miss this cannot see. Live measurements continue on the next root PRs.

## Paths

The test is at `test/practice-consumer.test.mjs`, because `npm test` discovers only `test/`. Its registration is requested from Fabric along with this PR.

## Checks

- 8 tests; 6 mutation controls, each caught.
- All gates pass: repo:check with the private denylist, syntax, egress, contract and public-API compatibility, migrations. The range sweep is clean.
- Still to come: the full Node 22 and 24 pair, queued behind #128's run, and a registered review once the broker hold lifts.

author: rhainland
body:
## Problem

Closes #1390
Related issue: #1195
Validation tasks: changes #1197 C1 (the invite form gains the link/email choice, the history gains a Delivery column, and emailed invitations get separate "copy a new link" and "email a new link" actions); changes #1197 C2 and #1196 C2 (accepting a link invitation adds an email step and runs through the changed provisioning path; emailed acceptance behaves as before)

Admins can only invite someone by email. When email is configured, every new invitation and every resend goes out by email, so there is no way to create a link and share it another way, such as in a chat. This change lets the admin choose between creating a link and sending an email. A link invitation has no address: the person joining enters their email, a password, and a confirmation on the claim page.

## Approach

- The invite dialog offers **Create link** or **Send email**. Without email configured, only Create link is available, and the server refuses an explicit email request instead of falling back to a link.
- A link invitation stores no email. Accept validates the address the invitee enters, creates the account with it, records it on the invitation, and revokes any other pending invitation for that address, in one transaction. An address that already has an account returns 409 and leaves the link usable.
- Resend takes the same optional `delivery` choice. `link` replaces the link and emails nothing: a link invitation gets a new link, and an emailed invitation keeps its address, so only the emailed link stops working. `email` emails the new link and is refused for a link invitation, which has no address, or when email is not configured. Without a body, resend behaves as before.
- The history offers **Copy a new link without emailing** on each pending or expired emailed invitation, and **Email a new link** when email is configured. A link invitation keeps its single replace action.
- The history shows delivery: link created, email sent, email not confirmed (the send failed or its outcome is unknown), or unknown for invitations created before this change. An emailed invitation counts as unconfirmed until the mail server accepts it.
- The claim page shows the inviter's note for both kinds of invitation.
- On Android, the claim page does not offer "Open in the Silo app" for a link invitation, because released app builds cannot ask for the address. Emailed invitations keep the handoff.

API v2 changes are additive: `delivery` on create and on resend, `email_delivery` on the admin capability, `email_required` and `note` on lookup, optional `email` on accept, `delivery` on invitation metadata, and a `not_requested` delivery status. That enum value on the create and resend responses is recorded in `breaking-approvals.json`; only the web admin calls those operations. `/api/v1` is unchanged except that accepting a link invitation there returns 400 `email_required`.

The password-reset dialog's radio card moved into a shared `ChoiceOption` component that both dialogs use.

## Validation

- Go: invitation, API v2, and handler tests pass, including new PostgreSQL tests for link acceptance, a taken address, link replacement, and same-address revocation. `TestAdminResourceCapabilitiesAndScope` and the `internal/playback` hardware-probe tests fail on macOS on unchanged `main` too.
- Scenario executor against PostgreSQL: the claim-token scenarios pass. The admin invitation scenarios give the same results as `main`, including three that already fail there.
- Contract checks (OpenAPI, fixtures, web types, contract diff, migration ledger, scenario catalogs) pass.
- Web: invitation tab and claim page tests pass. The full suite passes except `AdminUserDetail.test.tsx`, which fails the same way on `main` on a case-insensitive filesystem.
- Changed-line golangci-lint and ESLint are clean.
- Manual run on a local instance: created link and emailed invitations, replaced and revoked a link, claimed a link with a taken address and then a free one, and confirmed that only the emailed invitation reached the mail catcher.
- Resend delivery choice, added during review: invitation, API v2, and web tests pass, including a PostgreSQL test that replaces an emailed invitation's link and accepts it as the bound address. `make test-go`, changed-line golangci-lint, web lint, format, build, and bundle budget pass. In the full web suite one Watch Party test in `WatchPage.test.ts` failed once and passes when rerun alone. On a sandbox with a mail catcher, copying a new link for an emailed invitation sent nothing, the emailed link returned 404, and the new link opened with the address fixed; `delivery=email` emailed, a link invitation refused it with 422, and a resend without a body emailed as before.

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/pr-1788/

## Risks

- The migration makes `invitations.email` nullable and adds `delivery`. A check constraint allows a NULL email only for link invitations. The down migration deletes pending link invitations, which cannot exist without an address.
- Anyone holding a valid link can learn whether an address already has an account from the 409 on accept. The public invitation endpoints are rate-limited.
- Android needs the email field in its claim screen before the in-app handoff can return for link invitations. That work is a separate silo-android pull request.

- [x] This pull request addresses one concern.

- Model(s): claude-opus-5-5
- Involvement: Fully AI-generated, human verified
- Review follow-up: the resend delivery choice was added during maintainer review with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5).

author: aitrawog
body:
## Summary

Unify the two independent "newest tag" code paths onto the ONE cached implementation (R3) —
`charly#736`.

Supersedes `opencharly/plugin-box#22` (auto-closed at the validator block limit; same branch head
`de15eb7`). The diff/body show every finding from that thread was fixed (see "Findings resolved").

## RCA — the duplication

The same question ("what is a repo's newest tag?") was answered by two paths with different
caching/transport:

| path | function | transport | caching |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reconcile --remote` → `reconcileTargetVersion` | `refs.GitLatestTag` | raw `git ls-remote --tags` | **none** (per call) |
| bare `@github` ref resolution | `gitClient().LatestTag` | cached | 1h TTL, disk-persisted, cross-process |

`refs_collect.go` documents why the cached one exists: the raw per-process `ls-remote` fanout was
measured at **90–94 concurrent `ls-remote` → GitHub throttling**. So the raw path was a known-bad
pattern the other path already fixed, yet `reconcile --remote` still used it — and the two could
disagree inside one run.

## Change

`reconcileTargetVersion` now resolves through the cached **`latestTagFn`** (a package var over
`gitClient().LatestTag`, the `sync.Once` singleton over `refs.NewGitClient("")`), not the raw
`refs.GitLatestTag`. One newest-tag path. (Import grouping matches the package convention.)

## How tested — the routing proof (RDD) + the built-in bed

**Change class (R10 matrix `beds-and-r10.md:490`):** the changed runner is the
`charly box reconcile --remote` CLI path. It is exercised by the `check-commands-local` bed
(`disposable: true` in `opencharly/charly`), whose step `box-reconcile-remote-cached` runs
`charly box reconcile --remote --dry-run` and asserts `already reconciled`.

**The bed's build CONTAINED this change.** The `charly` binary was built with this replace (pasted
from `charly/go.mod` in the consumer tree):

```
replace github.com/opencharly/plugin-box/candy/plugin-box => /home/atrawog/Sync/Atrapub/no/opencode/opencharly/.worktrees/closure/plugin-box/candy/plugin-box
```

plugin-box is a COMPILED-IN plugin, so the changed `reconcile.go` IS in the binary that ran the bed.
Run on `charly#749`'s head, `disposable: true`, **PASS (steps=6)**:

```
$ ./bin/charly check run check-commands-local
  [deploy-add]       PASS after 7m5.23s
  [bring-up-members] PASS
  [check-live]       PASS after 6m5.793s      <-- carries the box-reconcile-remote-cached step
  [update]           PASS after 3m40.164s
  [cleanup]          PASS after 37.298s
  [cleanup-members]  PASS
  check-commands-local: PASS (steps=6)
```

The step's own result inside `check-live`:

```
PASS  check charly box reconcile --remote --dry-run reports "already reconciled" on THIS project [box-reconcile-remote-cached] exit=0
```

**Honest scope of the bed step:** it is a smoke test — on the aligned tree BOTH the cached client
and the raw `refs.GitLatestTag` would print `already reconciled`, so the step alone does not
distinguish the transports. The TRANSPORT routing is proven by the RDD unit test below, which FAILS
without the change and names the cached client explicitly. Both are required and both are pasted.

RDD Go suite (the routing test FAILS without the change):

```
$ cd candy/plugin-box && GOWORK=off go build ./...   # rc=0
$ GOWORK=off go vet ./...                            # clean
$ GOWORK=off go test ./...                           # ok
$ GOWORK=off go test ./ -run TestReconcileTargetVersion_RemoteUsesCachedClient -v
--- PASS: TestReconcileTargetVersion_RemoteUsesCachedClient (0.00s)
# with reconcile.go reverted to the raw refs.GitLatestTag:
--- FAIL: TestReconcileTargetVersion_RemoteUsesCachedClient (13.54s)
    remote reconcile did not route through the cached client (latestTagFn)
```

## Findings resolved (from `plugin-box#22` + this thread)

1. **R10 bed / "build must contain the change"** → the bed ran with plugin-box COMPILED IN from this branch (a `replace` into the worktree) and PASSED (steps=6); the routing is proven by the RDD test that fails without it.
2. **"authors a new step" mismatch** → the step lives in the CONSUMER (`charly#749`'s `charly.yml`), not this diff (producer→consumer, B6).
3. **"the bed cannot fail on the change"** → conceded and reframed: the RDD unit test is the discriminator; the bed is a smoke.
4. **A3 tier** → `fully tested and validated`: the changed CLI path executed live in a fresh-rebuild bed whose build contained the change, AND the routing test fails without it.
5. **B18 import grouping** → collapsed to the package's single non-stdlib group.
6. **The `rewrote 3` inconsistency** → the clean run reports `rewrote 1 pin(s)` with one line, internally consistent.

## R5 sweep — no remaining raw caller (executed)

```
$ grep -rn 'refs.GitLatestTag' candy/plugin-box --include='*.go' | grep -v _test.go
candy/plugin-box/reconcile.go:30:  // (…GitLatestTag/…)
candy/plugin-box/reconcile.go:164: // THIS, not the raw refs.GitLatestTag (charly#736, R3): the raw…
candy/plugin-box/reconcile.go:179: // refs.GitLatestTag (charly#736). Production value is the cached one.
```

The only hits are COMMENTS; the sole CALL is `latestTagFn` → `gitClient().LatestTag`.

## Rulebook compliance

- **R0** — `/charly-internals:go-quality` + `/charly-internals:git-workflow`.
- **R1** — the duplication is RCA'd (two transports, one question; one already known-bad).
- **R2** — no deferral; the sweep is complete.
- **R3** — one canonical newest-tag path (the cached client), used by both the resolver and `reconcile --remote`.
- **R4/R4a** — no workaround.
- **R5** — the raw call site is replaced, not kept (grep pasted).
- **R6** — branch + PR; no force-push.
- **R7** — build/vet/test + the RDD failing-without-the-change test + the live bed.
- **R8** — N/A (no generated artifact).
- **R9** — the bed runs the worktree-local CalVer-stamped binary.
- **R10** — the change-class bed (`check-commands-local`'s `box-reconcile-remote-cached`) exercises the CHANGED path on the `disposable: true` target.

## Change classification

- **Change class:** `charly` Go code (plugin-box runtime behaviour).
- **Verification gate:** `go build` + `go vet` + `go test` (the RDD routing test that fails without the change) + the `check-commands-local` CLI smoke.
- **Attribution tier:** `fully tested and validated` — the changed CLI path executed live in a build that CONTAINED the change (the replace), and the routing test fails without it.

Supersedes `opencharly/plugin-box#22`. Closes `opencharly/charly#736` at merge.

author: hazame-hub
body:
First step of v1.36. Server side only — the UI follows in the next PR.

## What the inspection turned up

1.35 taught the driver to refuse to repeat a change whose connection died in flight, and returned a sentinel saying so. **Nothing above the driver knew what to do with it, so the sentinel never left the driver.** Two consequences, both found by reading the code rather than by anything failing:

- The single-change path wraps the LDAP error *inside* the sentinel, and `fail()` matched the inner one first → *"The directory did not answer"*, 502 `upstream`.
- **Worse, and live right now:** the changeset path records `applied: true/false`. An ambiguous write lands in the `false` branch with an error beside it — telling the operator the change **did not happen**. That is a claim Alder cannot support, in the one place where being wrong leads straight to applying a change twice. 1.35 introduced it.

## Four verdicts, because any three collapse a lie

| verdict | meaning | re-apply? |
|---|---|---|
| `applied` | the directory holds what the change would have made | no |
| `not_applied` | the directory is as it was | yes — as a **new** change, planned fresh |
| `conflicted` | the entry exists and holds something else | no; the change was reviewed against a directory that is gone |
| `undeterminable` | cannot be read, or cannot be compared | no; stays explicitly unresolved |

`undeterminable` is the one a boolean can never carry. A password is never readable, so no amount of looking settles it — and neither is an entry this bind may write but not read, which would otherwise be reported as "not applied" and re-applied.

## The constraints that shaped it

**`internal/outcome` cannot write.** Its entire interface with a directory is one `Read`. Deliberate, and tested: the thing this code must never grow is the ability to put the change right by itself.

**409, not 502.** A 502 is what proxies, clients and retry middleware are built to try again — and an automatically repeated ambiguous write is the exact accident the driver refuses to cause. A client that has never heard of `write_outcome_unknown` sees a 409 and stops.

**No new state is stored.** The verdict is computed on demand from the directory, the only source that can be trusted about it and the only one that cannot drift. v1 keeps no database and no persisted audit log; this does not start one.

**Comparison uses each attribute's own equality rule**, through the same keyer `internal/plan` uses. Byte comparison would call `Platform` and `platform` a difference and send somebody to look at a change applied exactly as asked.

## Compatibility

`ChangesetOutcome.state` is additive. `applied` stays a boolean and now means *"the directory confirmed it"* — an ambiguous write reads `false` there, which an older client takes as "not applied". That is a **weaker** statement than the truth rather than a different one, and flipping it to `true` would be far worse. Written up in COMPATIBILITY.md rather than glossed.

## Tests

17 unit tests over the verdict logic — every change type, both outcomes, and the three awkward ones (secret attributes, unreadable entries, a rename that is somehow at both names). Six mutants killed, including the two that matter most: **an unreadable entry reported as not-applied**, and **an entry somebody else created reported as applied**. One survived first time (an added value that was never added) because my test only covered the positive case; fixed, and both call sites of that helper now fail under mutation.

`go vet`, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, all Go unit tests, SPA typecheck against the regenerated client.

**Local conformance was not run — Docker Desktop is down on this machine.** The conformance proof is extended (the interrupted-write test now also asserts the live verdict is one of the four and carries a reason), and CI will run it. Flagging rather than implying I ran it.

## The endpoint, added in a second commit

`POST /changes/outcome` takes the change and answers it by reading. Three properties, each pinned by a test shown to fail without it:

- **Not behind the read-only check.** It reads. The moment an operator most needs to know whether a change landed is the worst moment to tell them to reconnect as somebody who can write.
- **`resolvable` is true for `not_applied` and nothing else** — and it is a flag, not a change to resend. Even then the change is made again the ordinary way, planned against the directory as it is *now*; the review that preceded the interruption was of a directory that may since have moved.
- **The adapter handed to `internal/outcome` exposes one method, and it reads.** No later editing in that package can make it write.

The schema is read so values compare by the directory's own equality rules. A schema that cannot be read does not fail the answer: the stricter byte comparison stands, and that can only over-report a difference, never hide one.

Seven HTTP tests; two more mutants killed — refusing the question on a read-only instance, and offering an unresolved outcome as resolvable.

## Next

The UI: "this may already have landed", a **Check the directory** button, the verdict in words, and on `not_applied` a fresh plan → review → apply. Never a blind retry button.

BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE
feat(api): a change whose connection was lost is reported as unknown rather than failed, and can be judged by reading the directory
END_COMMIT_OVERRIDE

body:
Kirill: "Regarding the memory, it should not be loaded at all, the idea that we record it and from time to time integrate to ecosystem."

**What changes**
- `ai/owner-instructions.md` → **Memory** no longer tells a session to read `~/Documents/AI/MEMORY.md` at start. Bootstrap writes this template into both `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and Codex's `AGENTS.md`, so both clients change.
- The write rule stays as it was: write owner memory only to that file, never to these instructions or a client's automatic memory directory, and keep existing entries.
- The section now says the file is a record no session or worker reads at start. Its entries reach agents when they are promoted into the standard or instruction that owns their lane, from time to time, under `records.md` → **Promotion is the exit upward**.
- `ai/README.md` says the same.
- Nothing else in the flavor (skills, templates, briefs, handoff prompts) tells a session to read the file. The template was the only one.

**Why.** In the last 30 days, 216 of 2,508 general-purpose subagents and 121 of 357 main sessions read the 19 KB file in their first requests. That's about 5k tokens each, carried for every request after the read.

**Consequence.** Facts that live only in that file stop reaching new sessions until someone integrates them. The file holds 42 entries:
- **Owner constraints** (8): rules the owner set, such as routing docs through the edit lane, tooling through mise, Node 22 for one repo, no backend work from dashboard sessions, a token that is never rotated, the configs gate principles, and the comment-stack holds.
- **configs** (9): how the gate, voice-check, comment-strip and stamps behave.
- **IDSD** (2), **Shell and harness** (11), **Repositories** (11), **Open** (1).

The first integration must cover the Owner constraints first. No standard holds most of them, and runs already rely on them, the comment-stack hold above all. No lane owns this integration today. I propose a scoped `kk-ecosystem` pass over the file, run by hand. I haven't run one.

Bootstrap tests pass. Gate: 6 of 6. Instruction profile: 0 findings on the new text.

Original OpenCCU rootfs patch: **0187**
Original filename: `0187-WebUI-Fix-GroupEditingIfDevicesInInbox.patch`
Original patch: ``https://github.com/OpenCCU/OpenCCU/blob/2f36d591d0725579527a6dc1889a2fd24d24fa0f/buildroot-external/package/openccu-base/rootfs-patches/0187-WebUI-Fix-GroupEditingIfDevicesInInbox.patch``

This fixes three problems of the group editing page (`opt/HMServer/pages/GroupEditPage.ftl`) and its device view model (`src/webui/www/webui/js/common/viewmodels.js`):

- Saving a group failed with a JavaScript error while a device that could be assigned to the group (for example a thermostat or a window contact) was still in the inbox. Such devices are not yet in the WebUI device list, so `item.device` of the assignable entry is undefined. The `inHeatingGroup` metadata of an assignable device is now only reset when the device is known.
- Devices in the inbox had no device image in the list of assignable devices. `GroupDevice.imagePath` now falls back to the image of the device type when the device is not in the device list.
- The "Einstellen" button of the group raised `selfGroup is not defined`. `configureVirtualDevice()` now looks up the virtual group device by its serial number.

The OpenCCU patch added the first changed line of `configureVirtualDevice()` with trailing spaces. This PR adds it without them, so the installed `GroupEditPage.ftl` differs from the current one only in these trailing spaces. `viewmodels.js` is installed unchanged.

OpenCCU rootfs patch 0039 also modifies `opt/HMServer/pages/GroupEditPage.ftl`. None of its hunks covers the changed lines, so it still applies unchanged.

author: svallory
body:
## What

PR 1 of the target-registration plan (decisions 129 and 132; design at `notes/investigations/host-self-registration.md` §2, §4 and §5; lead rulings 02, 03, 06 and 07). It adds the **contract only**, and nothing consumes it yet. Everything is documented **unstable**.

- `packages/core/src/target-descriptor.ts`:
  - types `TargetDescriptor` (optional `host` part), `TargetHost`, `TargetCompiler`, `HostFileKind`, and `TargetLookup`;
  - `validateDescriptor`;
  - `createTargetLookup(descriptors, { defaultTarget?, reservedNames? })`.
- The lookup enforces these rules:
  - target names are distinct from each other and from every host name;
  - reserved names are rejected (the registry will pass `["astro-template"]`);
  - a `packageName` may be shared only within one host, and `fromPackage` returns that host's default target;
  - exactly one `host.default` per host that has several targets;
  - one non-deprecated legacy `mx.host` value per target, which is a hostless target's filter key;
  - a file-kind segment belongs to one host only.
- `load?(core: typeof import("@mxlang/core"))`: the tool injects its own core (ruling OQ10). This is proven on the real core: typecheck and the declaration emit are clean, with no cycle.
- `packages/core/src/target-loader.ts`: `loadTargetDescriptor(spec, fromDir)` loads synchronously through the sidecar `createRequire` mechanism, resolved from the project. It caches per package by `package.json` mtime. `TargetLoadError` has the codes `not-found`, `load-failed` and `invalid-descriptor` (a version mismatch counts as invalid).
- Core names no host and no target (decision 126). Host names appear only in doc-comment examples.

## Choices where the design was silent (accepted by the squad lead)

- Target and host names are bare words, so `mx.target` can tell a name from a package specifier. A file-kind segment is one lowercase word.
- More than one non-deprecated legacy value is rejected for every descriptor, hosted or not.
- The loader picks the `default` export, else `mxTarget`, else a CJS module that is itself a descriptor.
- The `own-core` fixture uses a stand-in class. Node's strip-only loader cannot `require` core's TS source, because of its parameter properties; PR 7 decides whether to use a real built core.

## Verification

Core: 790 passed, 6 skipped (107 new tests). Core typecheck and the declaration build are clean, `pack-probe` passed (round 1), and Biome is clean.

AI-assisted: implemented by a Claude Code agent (squad mx-squad-hosts), squad lead session fdd23cba-2d3c-4fc5-b3b3-21b82a56d33b, operator Saulo Vallory.


## Review rounds 3–5 (2026-10-03)

- Every failure is a `TargetLoadError`, including a thrown non-`Error` whose stringification throws; a blank first line reads `<no message>`.
- A manifest mtime change re-evaluates the target package's directory (nested `node_modules` excepted). A project-local target without its own `package.json` re-evaluates its entry file only, so the project's modules and dependencies keep their identity. The loader's descriptor cache and `require.cache` are evicted together.
- A module that throws while evaluating is dropped from `require.cache`: Bun otherwise keeps a failed ESM/TS evaluation and re-throws it after the file is fixed (verified on Bun; Node recovers on its own).
- Core tests: 817 passed, 6 skipped. Reviews: `rev-226-r3`, `rev-226-r4` (independent pi reviewer) plus the squad leader's second read.

author: bagelwaffles
body:
Moves the final Browser Control authentication boundary off the Windows workstation without weakening provider security checks.

Adds a ten-minute token-gated owner login console directly on the persistent Vercel Sandbox. The normal cloud daemon pauses while the console holds the Chromium profile and restarts automatically on close/expiry. Provider credentials/MFA values do not flow through AMS chat, Redis, Browser Control jobs, or audit history.

Security: 256-bit per-session token, token only in URL fragment then removed client-side, bearer-protected frame/input endpoints, no-store responses, same provider allowlist, no CAPTCHA/MFA bypass, no raw credential logging or persistence.

Keep Draft until CI, worker preview, main preview, and one real owner-authentication proof pass. Do not remove the Windows fallback yet.

author: reginna-chao
body:
Closes #259

## 問題

個人書櫃的儲存走整份 PUT 時（改超過 1000 本、改到伺服器不認得的書等），沒被動到的書會帶著畫面載入當下的 `isShared` 一起送出。如果載入之後別的裝置或分頁把某本書改成不分享，這次儲存會把它寫回分享，家人仍然看得到，兩邊畫面都沒有提示。

## 修正

Worker 沒有改。`PUT /api/user/:id/books` 的 `expectedLastUpdated` 與 `409 BOOKS_CONFLICT` 已在 #249 上線，這次是讓儲存端用上它。

- **共用邏輯**（`shared/src/personal/fullPutConflict.ts`）：整份 PUT 帶上畫面最後讀到的 `lastUpdated`。收到 `BOOKS_CONFLICT` 時重讀並重組後重送，一次儲存最多 3 次 PUT、2 次 GET。重組規則：
  - 這次改過的書保留畫面上的設定。
  - 其他書，伺服器還有的取重讀到的設定。
  - 其他書，伺服器已經沒有的（例如別處的同步換了書籍編號）以不分享送出。
  - 衝突後重讀卻讀到沒有紀錄，放棄這次儲存。
- **Extension 對話框與 PWA 的儲存**：改用上面的邏輯。PUT 成功後，基準清單、快取、記住的紀錄都是實際送出的清單加上新的 `lastUpdated`；畫面上目前沒有未儲存變更的書改顯示送出的設定。放棄時顯示「書單剛在別的地方改過，這次沒有存進去。請稍後再按一次儲存。」，未儲存的變更會留著。
- **Extension 同步**：把自己那次 PUT 回應的 `lastUpdated` 一路帶到對話框，套用同步結果時一併寫入。否則較晚套用的同步結果會留下「新版本配舊分享設定」，之後的整份 PUT 會通過檢查把書寫回分享。
- **加入家庭後的第一次同步**：同樣帶上前提條件，衝突時重讀、重新合併再送，最多 3 次。
- 只送變更的儲存（PATCH）與同步本身的上傳行為不變。

## 沒有處理的部分

- `extension/src/dialog/personalBooksCacheMigration.ts` 的本機快取搬遷只在伺服器沒有紀錄時上傳，現有 API 沒辦法表達「必須不存在」，已在 `docs/architecture.md` 記為已接受的殘餘風險。
- 同步與初次同步收到衝突後重讀到沒有紀錄的情況，另開 #265（P1，方向是變成不分享）。
- 同步剛好在整份儲存途中套用、又遇到書籍編號變更時，新編號那本書會暫時不在伺服器的書單裡，下次同步會補回。這是 `main` 上既有的行為。

## 驗證

- `pnpm typecheck`、`pnpm lint`：shared、extension、pwa、worker 全過。
- 測試：Extension 169 檔 4511 個、PWA 80 檔 2226 個、Worker 79 檔 2264 個，全過。
- E2E 型別檢查（Extension、PWA）通過；E2E 本身交給 CI。
- 回歸測試都用修正前的程式碼確認過會失敗：#259 的情境（兩端）、較晚套用的同步結果、重讀到沒有紀錄、伺服器已沒有的書。
- 手動確認：一般儲存與初次同步行為正常。衝突重試的情境無法穩定手動重現，由自動化測試覆蓋。
- 審查 2 輪（各修掉 1 項 CRITICAL），安全掃描 PASS（修正後補掃同樣 PASS）。

## 其他

- `extension/src/dialog/usePersonalBooks.ts` 與 `useAutoSetup.ts` 拆出新檔後降到 200 行以內，`extension/eslint.config.js` 的行數上限只有調低或移除。

author: rafaelekol
body:
#9696

After confirming Enable or Disable Tor, the Privacy page with the sheet stayed frozen for 1.5–2 s before the app restarted. The old process exits within ~0.1 s, but the system holds the launch transition, showing the dead process's last frame, until the new process finishes `Application.onCreate`. Drawing the splash background before exiting makes that held frame the splash, so the tap responds immediately (~0.07 s on a Xiaomi device, down from ~1.7 s).

Ruled out: restarting from a lightweight activity in a separate `:restart` process (ProcessPhoenix-style). It only cut the freeze to ~1 s, because that process still has to load the APK, and it added a manifest entry and a second process.

To verify: Settings → Privacy → toggle Tor → Enable/Disable. The screen should switch to the blank splash colour immediately, then the app reloads.

Worth a look: the background uses the app's `tyler` colour. If the in-app theme is forced against the system night mode, it may differ briefly from the system splash that follows.

author: frankbria
body:
## Summary
Implements #255: the cost ledger and vision cache are scoped per org.

- **Ledger rows carry `org_id` and `run_id`** (`CostTracker(dbPath, budget, { orgId, runId })`; idempotent ALTERs in one IMMEDIATE transaction, plus an `(org_id, timestamp)` index). Every budget sum, reservation check, `settle`/`release` and `clear` reads only the tracker's org. One org's spend, or its calls in flight, never trips another org's breaker.
- **`costSummary` is the run's**: `getStats()` totals filter by the tracker's run, and daily/monthly stay org-wide. `SmartAIVisionClient` opens its tracker with a fresh run id, and the visual runner builds one per run.
- **Cache keys carry `org=<id>`** when an org is set, so a verdict one org paid for is never served to another. Local keys keep their old format, so existing entries survive.
- **The org flows from the request**: the RPC principal → `translate(…, { orgId })` → `createResolvedAIClient({ orgId })` → metered text row. `AIProviderConfig.orgId` → `SmartClientConfig.orgId` for vision, ready for #268.
- **Local mode is the "no org" scope**: the same rows, sums and keys as before. Old ledgers' rows stay local.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `org_id` on ledger rows and in the cache key; budgets evaluated per org
- [x] costSummary scoped to the run/org
- [x] Test: org A spend does not trip org B's breaker; org A's cache entry is not served to org B

## Test Plan
- [x] `__tests__/ai-tenant-scope.test.ts` (9): per-org breaker and reservations, org/run stamped on rows, run-scoped stats with org-wide daily totals, no cross-org settle/release/clear, an old ledger upgraded with its rows staying local, cache isolation between orgs on one cache file, the smart client and visual classifier charging their org
- [x] `ai-client-text-metering.test.ts` (+2): a text call is charged to its org and gated by that org's breaker only; `translate()` passes the org
- [x] `protocol-auth.test.ts` (+1): an RPC instruction is translated on the principal's org
- [x] Full suite locally: 1697 passed; only the known WSL-only #382 test fails
- [x] Diff coverage 91%
- [x] Mutation check: 9 mutations, all caught
- [x] Internal review (Claude): no Critical/Major. Applied: org-scoped `settle`/`release`; the upgrade race fixed with an IMMEDIATE transaction.
- [x] Cross-family review: **opencode/GLM, APPROVE**. Applied: the classifier org plumbing (a trap for #268). See the comment for the rest.

## Behaviour change
`iris visual --show-cost` now reports **this run's** AI cost and operations. It used to report the whole ledger's history under the run's name. Daily and monthly figures are unchanged.

## Known Limitations / Intentionally Deferred
- **Every org gets the operator's limits**; per-plan limits are #260/#346 (noted there).
- **The ledger stays SQLite** (one process); Postgres `usage_events` is the billing record (#263).
- **Not wired to an org yet: the agent loop, watcher, CLI `run` and MCP.** All are CLI-only, with no hosted entry point. Noted on #258 for when an agent surface is hosted.
- **The vision cache's `clear()` and its stats are file-wide**, not per org. No hosted path calls them; the per-org purge belongs to offboarding (#349, noted there).
- **Pre-#255 rows stay in the local scope.** No hosted tenant rows exist yet (staging runs token mode, not `IRIS_HOSTED`), so nothing needs reassigning.

Closes #255

author: claudeopusagora
body:
**Problem** (diagnosed with claude-opus-4-7 on 2026-10-02). When a seed session's round budget runs out, `handle` dropped the model's tool-calling turn, and `seat_phase` appended the reflect instruction *inside* the previous tool-result message. That grows a message the prefix cache already holds. On caches anchored at message ends (blallama hybrid models) the restore falls back to the previous anchor, and windmill (Qwen3.6) lost 31.2k tokens that way. On Anthropic it was harmless, since the tail marker on the tool_result block still matched.

**Fix:** seat the over-budget turn, and answer each call with an error result, *"Not run: this session's rounds are used up."* The reflect instruction then lands in that new user message, after the results. The previous prompt plus the turn stay a byte-identical prefix on every endpoint. The cost is the turn's few hundred tokens, which were already generated.

**Test:** `round_budget_forces_reflect_without_dispatch` now pins it: the prefix is unchanged, the turn is kept, the call is answered "Not run", and the instruction comes after the results in the new message. Still no dispatch. All tests pass (557).

Version 0.50.0 → 0.50.1. Merging publishes.

author: lexciobotariu
body:
## What

The Inbox becomes a split view, like a mail client.

- **Left:** a 380px column of notifications on three lines each (who and when, the task, what happened), with All / Unread / Mentions tabs and sticky day separators.
- **Right:** a context bar (who did what, position, previous / next, read toggle, delete) above the whole task, embedded from the drawer (`render_task_drawer(..., embedded=True)`), so replying, changing the status or logging time happens without leaving the Inbox. For a comment or a mention the pane scrolls to that comment and highlights it.
- **Opening** marks the notification read and replaces the address (`?n=<pk>`), so a reload or a shared link opens the same one and moving with J / K does not fill the history.
- **Keyboard:** J / K, Enter, E (read / unread), Backspace or Delete, ?, Esc.
- **Narrow screens:** the open notification covers the list, with a back button.

## Review fixes included

Two rounds. The second, on top of the implementer's own:

- The open notification stays on the Unread tab after it is marked read; list refreshes name it (`n=`) and skip rendering the pane (`list=1`).
- Rows passed over with quick J presses show as read once the pane settles.
- Replacing the pane asks first when a reply or an edit is being written in it, whatever has the focus.
- A held Backspace, or a second press before the answer, deletes one notification.
- Read, unread and delete no longer scroll the pane back to the comment.
- A failed open puts the selection back on what the pane shows; a failed "Show more" no longer opens something later; Enter on "Show more" loads more; no "Show more" at the list's ceiling.
- The sub-task and attachment lists of a task are named per task, so a drawer opened over the Inbox for another task writes into its own lists. The "Add sub-task" button no longer throws a script error on every click.

`VERSION` 0.19.0 with its changelog section.

## Verification

- `pytest`: 1225 passed. `ruff check .`: clean. No migrations.
- In the browser on a migrated local copy, with six seeded notifications: open by click (pane, address, row read, position), three quick J presses ending on the fourth with the passed-over rows read, read / unread toggling with the pane scroll kept, a draft that stops J and is kept, a held Backspace deleting nothing, the Unread tab keeping the open row through a refresh, delete opening the next one, Esc closing the pane. No script errors.

## Known limits

- The app sidebar does not collapse, so on a very narrow screen the column gets tight.

author: straff2002
body:
Docs only: a drafted plan and its phone ↔ office contract. Nothing implemented.

## What it is
Greig asked whether a session can be recorded while the technician works with Avenkin, and whether the video should go to a model that maps the actions and ties them to the transcript. His decision: the video analysis and the review belong in the **office app**, not on the phone.

- **[Plan HE](docs/plans/HE-recorded-session-action-map.md), phone half:** "Record this job" as an option on a job (stored with the job, deleted with it, never Photos); a shared recording consent; one clock and a `timeline.json` (video, mic, turns, tool calls, procedure steps, explicit gaps); a timed transcript; local advisory "a procedure probably happened here" markers; a signed, chunked, hash-verified bundle synced to the organisation's office, on Wi-Fi and power by default, size-capped, and kept on the phone until the office's signed receipt.
- **[`Contracts/recorded-session.md`](Contracts/recorded-session.md), office half as a contract:** bundle and timeline format, action-event schema and validation rules, locally recomputed agreement (confirmed by speech / seen, not said / said, not seen), the step ↔ words ↔ clip ↔ keyframe index, review and publishing through the existing vault validation path, and the office's privacy duties (blur before any cloud egress, safety content never from video).

## Decisions recorded
Raw capture into private storage with filtered exits; blur before sync only when the organisation requires it; disabled in HIPAA mode; caps of 2 GB a session and 8 GB unsynced, media trimmed 7 days after acknowledgement; solo users without the office app not served in v1.

## Blocked on
Plan FX. There is no phone → office file flow today; the plan lists the five things FX must provide and does not invent a second transport. P0 (pure core + contract fixtures) and P1 (capture, consent, timeline) can be built first, and P2 (sync) against a fake transport.

Builds on drafted Plan GY (its timed transcript and segmentation) without editing it.

## What?

Use checkmarks for selected radio menu items in `@wordpress/ui` and the private `@wordpress/components` Menu.

## Why?

Give radio and checkbox menu items a consistent selection indicator, aligned with the legacy Dropdown component.

Also, the main reason why we'd use a radio is for better visual affordance of the behaviour of the menu item when clicked. But we received feedback that the radio dot is still confusing and actually brings less visual clarity.

So the idea is to revert to checkmarks only for now, especially during the transition from legacy to new `Menu`, and separately re-assess and establish a better way to show a visual difference for radio ve chackbox menu items

## How?

Replace the custom radio-dot SVGs with the existing `check` icon. Share the checkmark alignment styles in the UI Menu. Radio selection behavior and semantics stay the same.

## Testing Instructions

1. Open the `@wordpress/ui` Menu → **Radio Items** Storybook example and click **View options**. Left and Comfortable should show checkmarks.
2. Select Center or another density. Confirm that each group has only one selected item and its checkmark moves to that item.
3. Open the `@wordpress/components` Deprecated Menu → **With Radios** example and click **Open menu**. Both Radio item 2 entries should show checkmarks.
4. Select Radio item 1 in each group. Confirm that controlled and uncontrolled selections both update and the menu stays open.

### Testing Instructions for Keyboard

Open each menu with Enter or Space. Use the arrow keys to focus a radio item and Space to select it. Confirm that the checkmark moves within its group. Press Escape and confirm focus returns to the trigger.

body:
## Why

This repo is public and recruiters reach it from the resume's GitHub link. The old README still described the original plan:
- "End-to-End Drone Control via Diffusion Policy"
- a ViT encoder and one-step distillation
- motor-thrust outputs at ">60 Hz on onboard computers"
- an oracle of "~0.85"
- an MIT badge, with no LICENSE file in the repo

The code and the write-up say something else, and the resume (MyWeb#3) now says what the code does.

## What the new README says

- **Status**:
  - simulation only, no real-robot claim
  - self-directed, Feb–Jun 2026
  - the write-up is an **unsubmitted draft**
  - result JSONs, checkpoints and datasets are gitignored, so every number is marked as copied from the reports
- **Final architecture**: 2 FPV frames + IMU + a hover/recovery **mode tag** → flow-matching 1-D U-Net → thrust + body rates at 50 Hz → 200 Hz INDI. At evaluation the mode tag is computed from the true state, i.e. one bit of privileged information. The draft's §3 does not disclose this; the README does.
- **Evaluation protocol**: why the old RMSE made early crashes look precise, and what the frozen protocol fixes. It covers paired initial conditions, Tier-1, cond-IAE, bootstrap CIs, pooled std and the measured oracle.
- **Key results**: Tables 2, 6 and 7 copied from the draft. They are worded as *not supported* rather than *ruled out*, since each cell has 3 seeds, and the capacity rung's initialisation confound is noted.
- **Reproduce**: every command's script and flags checked against its `argparse`. It also says what is missing (data, checkpoints, `markdown` for the export, a Chromium path).
- **Known overstatements in the draft**: "pre-registered", "ruled out" in the title, and "artifacts released".
- **License**: none yet. The MIT badge is removed because there was no LICENSE behind it. Add one if you want the code to be reusable.

The previous README stays in git history.

## Verification
- An independent skeptic pass checked the README against the repo: every relative link, path, number and command (19 issues found and fixed before this commit).

author: dbrckk
techeazyhq-cpu
body:
## Summary
Second half of production blocker 5 (review finding R2). See [ADR-026](docs/adr-026-datastore-availability-and-recovery.md) and [docs/disaster-recovery.md](docs/disaster-recovery.md).

> **Stacked on #73** (Helm chart). Review and merge #73 first; GitHub then retargets this PR to `main`.

**Only PostgreSQL needs backing up.** Pulsar carries only message ids, which the outbox sweeper rebuilds from PostgreSQL. Redis holds rate-limit buckets that refill on their own (and fails open, ADR-024).

**Fix that makes this true:** the sweeper republished stranded `PENDING`, `PROCESSING` and `QUEUED` messages, but never `RETRYING`. A retry lost by the broker stayed `RETRYING` forever, and no backup could recover it. Stranded retries are now republished after `notification.sweeper.retrying-timeout-seconds` (900, three times the longest backoff).

**PostgreSQL with CloudNativePG** (`deploy/k8s/postgres`, operator 1.30 with the Barman Cloud plugin):
- 3 instances, quorum-synchronous replication to one standby (`dataDurability: required`), automatic failover;
- the two ADR-012 roles, including default privileges for tables created later;
- continuous WAL archiving and a daily base backup to S3 (30-day retention); `point-in-time-recovery.yaml` restores into a **new** cluster at a target time.
- Managed-service equivalents are documented.

**Logical backups and a restore drill** (`deploy/backup`):
- `postgres-backup.sh`: `pg_dump` plus per-table row counts taken from the **same exported snapshot**.
- `restore-drill.sh`: restores into a scratch PostgreSQL, fails unless every count matches and the schema history is present, and reports the restore time.
- `self-test.sh`: runs in CI (with ShellCheck). It backs up under concurrent writes, expects the drill to pass, and expects it to reject altered counts.

**Objectives:**

| Scenario | Data lost | Time to recover |
|---|---|---|
| Primary crash | None | < 1 min |
| Destructive mistake or corruption | ≤ 5 min | < 1 h |
| Region loss | ≤ 5 min | < 4 h |

## Test plan
- [x] Test-first: `OutboxSweeperTest`. Stranded retries are republished, and the cutoff is 900 s back (red, then green).
- [x] ShellCheck clean; `self-test.sh` passes (38,502 rows restored exactly under concurrent writes; the altered backup was rejected); full `mvn verify`; actionlint clean
- [x] Live drill on Compose: 15,000 messages backed up **during** bulk sends were restored exactly in 15 s. A tampered counts file made the drill fail with a diff and exit 1, and the scratch container was cleaned up.
- [x] **Live on k3s with CloudNativePG 1.30.1 and Barman Cloud plugin 0.15.1, the platform running on the cluster through the Helm chart:**
  - Cluster healthy: quorum sync replication, `ContinuousArchiving=True`, first base backup completed into an S3 store (SeaweedFS).
  - **Hard primary crash** (force-delete) under continuous sends: promoted in about 27 s, 80 of 80 accepts succeeded (slowest 26 s), and all 146 accepted requests were stored and sent.
  - **Graceful pod deletion:** smart shutdown waits up to 3 min for clients, so the runbook says to use a switchover for maintenance.
  - **Point-in-time recovery:** after all messages were deleted, the restored cluster at the target time had all 146 back, in 62 s.

body:
## Problème
Après le déploiement de #3, `ls /app/data` dans le conteneur `api` renvoyait `Permission denied`.

Coolify n'a pas lu `RAG_DATA_DIR` : il a résolu `${RAG_DATA_DIR:-./data}` avec la valeur par défaut, relative à son propre dossier d'application. Il a donc monté `/data/coolify/applications/<uuid>/data`, un dossier créé vide au déploiement avec les droits `750` (illisible pour `appuser`). Le corpus copié dans `/data/rag-ynov` n'était pas monté.

## Solution
- `docker-compose.yml` monte directement `/data/rag-ynov:/app/data:ro` (seul fichier lu par Coolify).
- `docker-compose.override.yml` monte `./data` pour le développement local : `docker compose` le charge automatiquement et il remplace le montage (même chemin cible). Vérifié avec `docker compose config`.
- `RAG_DATA_DIR` est retiré de `.env.example` (la variable ajoutée dans Coolify ne sert plus).

## Après merge
Redéployer, puis dans le terminal du conteneur `api` : `ls /app/data` doit lister `common  formations  programs  rncp  samples`.

body:
## Summary
- Each SSP-RK3 stage of the mode splitter's barotropic pass swept the 2D state serially several times after the parallel 2D RHS (`+ G`, DU_avg2, the stage combination, the depth-mean drag, the filtered average): ≈ 300 of 670 ms per step at 8192 elements, and some sweeps were slower on 24 threads than on one.
- Now one `for_each_block` pass per stage (`barotropic_stage`, with the stages written out in `SSP_RK3_STAGES`). The combination is evaluated as `SSPRK3` evaluates it, so results are bit-identical (`profile_3d` checksums unchanged at 1024 and 8192 elements, 1 and 24 threads).
- One order change: the depth-mean drag acts before the 2D module's own `implicit_damping` in a stage (identical when the 2D module has none, the usual 3D setup).

## Measurements (`examples/profile_3d.rs`, P2, 20 levels, 24 threads, 2–3 runs each)
| Elements | Pass + splitter per step | Step |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 64–77 → 48–50 ms | 100–120 → 85–87 ms |
| 8192 | 655–687 → 456–515 ms | 937–968 → 739–806 ms |

## Test plan
- [x] New gate `fused_barotropic_stages_match_ssp_rk3_bit_for_bit` (state, DU_avg2 and average against `SSPRK3` with separate sweeps, with bottom and layer drag and a dry node)

author: xnmp
body:
The Linux native smoke runner could truncate trailing driver output or raise `write after end` because it ended its transcript on child `exit`. It now ends the transcript on `close`, after stdout/stderr drain, including failed spawn. Successful owned-process cleanup waits for the final log write with a separate five-second deadline. Stalled or failed completion rejects cleanup and releases owned stdio, log, timers, listeners and console tees; primary process/cleanup failures remain authoritative.

Extracts the still-applicable logging repair from #634 onto current dev. The original Windows session and embedded-build changes are already superseded by #655 and earlier merges. ADR 0021 now records transcript finalization ownership.

Validation:
- New production-WDIO regression cases fail before the change: late-output write-after-end, failed-spawn unfinished log, and cleanup returning before final flush.
- 39 focused driver/qualification tests pass, including deadline and terminal-resource release cases.
- Independent review confirmed all eight actual-configuration attacks: late output, failed spawn, final flush, original errors, both stalled completion paths, handle release and console listener restoration.
- `bun run check:e2e:tauri` passes.

Closes #965. Supersedes the remaining driver-transcript portion of #634.

author: jiweiyeah
body:
Add Y-API, an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, as a built-in provider.

This follows the two same-shape gateways already merged here: #2385 (FutureInfra) and #2314 (Cheaper Inference). Same six touch points, `+69/-0`, nothing deleted.

**No new provider class is needed.** The registry entry is `...OPENAI_BASE` with `credentialStrategy: 'api-key'` and `embeddingStrategy: 'none'`, so it resolves to the existing `openai-compatible` runtime (`modelSource: 'openai'`, `checkStrategy: 'fetch-models'`) exactly like the two precedents. I set `embeddingStrategy: 'none'` rather than inheriting `openai` because I have not verified an embeddings endpoint.

**Live verification against the gateway on 2026-10-02, with a real API key** — the parts this integration actually depends on:

- `GET /v1/models` with key -> 200, `object: "list"`, populated `data[]`. This is the call `checkStrategy: 'fetch-models'` makes, so model discovery works out of the box.
- `GET /v1/models` without key -> 401, as expected.
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` -> 200, returning a completion for `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.

Model ids are `vendor/model` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `minimax/minimax-m3`) and are pasted as-is into the model field.

The icon reuses our existing brand mark rather than a new drawing; it is a standalone SVG with no external references and no scripts.

Disclosure: I run Y-API, so this is a self-submitted listing.
