author: starkaiindia-source
body:
## What was wrong

A shop paid ₹799 for Yearly and was sent to the Plans page and asked to pay again.

The payment had activated correctly. The webhook wrote the account as `active / yearly`, expiring a year on, and the server answered `paid` for that uid. Nothing in the payment or activation path was at fault, and no data needed repairing.

The fault was in the browser. The page asked `/api/access` as soon as the catalogue had loaded — before Firebase had restored the signed-in session. Measured on production: the request leaves at ~415 ms and the Firebase SDK only starts downloading at ~417 ms. With no ID token the server truthfully answered the signed-out free view, and the browser kept that as the subscriber's tier for the rest of the page. Opening a group then sent a paying shop to Plans. Every subscriber hit this on every page load.

## What changes

**The entitlement in the browser**
- `src/data/access.js` waits for the session the browser expects before asking, keeps an answer only if the account that asked is still the account on the page, and asks again when the account changes. A visitor with no session is still answered at once and does not load the sign-in SDK.
- A 401 on a request that carried a token is refreshed and retried once; it is never read as "this account is free".
- `src/app.js` redraws the open group or matched device when the tier changes, and re-reads the plan when the account screen and the paywall disagree.
- The Plans page says a plan is already active before showing prices. The account page no longer draws a padlock beside features a subscriber has.

**The entitlement on the server**
- `api/access.js` answers 401 for a token it could not verify, instead of a 200 describing a signed-out visitor.
- `resolveEntitlement` (`api/_schema/entitlement.js`) is the single definition of who has access, on which plan, until when and from what source. Every route and the admin table read it.

**Assigning a plan by hand**
- `POST /api/admin/subscription` assigns ₹99 Monthly, ₹799 Yearly or Lifetime, extends a running plan, and revokes access. Requires `subscriptions.write` — `super_admin` and `admin` only.
- Lifetime is admin-only: not in the catalogue that sells, not listed by `/api/plans`, refused by `/api/create-order`. No payment, no expiry.
- A manual assignment writes the entitlement, a subscription record and an audit entry in one transaction, and never writes to `payments`.
- User page: **Assign / Change Plan** and **Revoke access**. User table: plan, status, expiry, source.

## Not changed

- The free tier: three searches a day, then refused.
- No new collection, no migration. No new top-level `api/*.js`, so the deployment stays within the function limit.

## Follow-up outside this PR

`firestore.rules` closes the new mirror fields to the browser. None of them grants access on its own, so this is hardening; it is deployed separately with `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules`.

## Tests

454 pass (392 before).

- `src/data/access.test.js` reproduces the race against the real `access.js`; 7 of its 11 cases fail on the previous code.
- `api/_lib/subscription-entitlement.test.js` drives the real handlers through an in-memory Firebase for the sixteen acceptance scenarios: each plan grants search, results, groups and group details; no plan, an expired plan and a revoked plan do not; admin assignment, change, extension and revocation; a verified ₹799 payment.
- `api/_lib/subscription-staff.test.js` switches the staff registry on and proves `support` and `analyst` are refused.

Also verified in a browser against the real client and the real handlers with an in-memory database: before the fix a paid account is redirected to Plans; after it the group opens with its devices. A real Google sign-in against production was not part of that check.

author: arnab-netizen
body:
## Root cause
`buildBusinessConditionProfile()` fell back to unrelated domain risk:
- `survivalRiskScore` took the max risk across ALL domains when no recovery/finance/cashflow score existed.
- `executionRiskScore` took the average risk across ALL domains when no operations/sop score existed.

So Strategy/Marketing/Sales risk could be presented as "survival risk", and Finance/Marketing/Strategy risk as "execution risk".

## Contract change
- `survivalRiskScore: number | null`
- `executionRiskScore: number | null`
- `null` explicitly means **NOT MEASURED**. A measured `0` remains different from absence of measurement.

## Allowed domains
- Survival: `recovery`, `finance`, `cashflow` (max of applicable)
- Execution: `operations`, `sop` (max of applicable)

## Behaviour changes
- Reassessment cadence: a null category contributes no risk but is never read as safe; the relaxed 30-day cadence requires both categories measured (otherwise 14 days). Measured high risk and insufficient data still give 7 days.
- Portfolio: an unmeasured-survival business is not a "safe investment" candidate, raises no survival/execution alert, and sorts after any measured survival risk.
- UI: owner page shows "not measured yet"; portfolio table shows "n/m".

## Explicit non-changes
- Owner Decision ordering unchanged; priority classes unchanged
- Domain score formulas, domain confidence formulas and thresholds unchanged
- No universal cross-domain score introduced; no schema/migration

## Known compatibility change
External/untyped consumers of the profile JSON that expect numeric `survivalRiskScore` / `executionRiskScore` may now receive `null`. In-repo typed consumers were found via `tsc` and handled.

## Local test evidence (commit eeeb43a)
- `tsc --noEmit`, eslint (changed files), `lint:ratchet`, `governance:scan`, `npm run build`: all exit 0
- owner-condition + owner-spine + owner-decision + owner-portfolio non-DB tests: 38 files / 695 tests pass (new `business-condition-risk-measurement.test.ts` covers the 16 required cases)
- DB-backed tests not run locally (configured DB rejected by the safety guard, not bypassed); left to CI.

body:
## Résumé
`eslint` est passé de **95 erreurs et 68 avertissements à 0**. Un nouveau workflow **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** fait échouer toute PR qui réintroduit une erreur ou un avertissement ESLint (`npm run lint`, `--max-warnings=0`) ou une erreur TypeScript (`npm run typecheck`). Il prend environ 1 à 2 minutes et tourne indépendamment des tests E2E.

> ⚠️ Plusieurs fichiers sont aussi modifiés par #26. Je fusionnerai `main` dans cette branche dès que #26 sera mergée, puis je relancerai lint et E2E.

## 🐛 Bugs trouvés en route
1. **Sécurité, épinglage de classe** (présences et devoirs) : `removePinnedClass` supprimait par **id seul**. Tout utilisateur connecté pouvait donc retirer la classe épinglée d'un autre enseignant, même dans une autre école. La suppression est maintenant filtrée sur l'enseignant (`session.memberId`).
2. **Boucle de rendus** (dialogue Salles de la page Classes) : un `useEffect` dépendait de `rooms ?? []`, un nouveau tableau à chaque rendu. Une école **sans salle** déclenchait donc un rendu en boucle. La comparaison se fait maintenant par contenu.
3. **Budget** : le sens du tri n'était jamais affiché. Une flèche montante ou descendante apparaît désormais sur la colonne triée.
4. **Dialogue de devoir** (enseignant) : un rechargement du devoir pendant l'édition réinitialisait les champs saisis, à cause d'une dépendance sur l'objet. La réinitialisation est maintenant liée à l'ouverture et à l'id.
5. **Import Excel** : un `useCallback` avait des dépendances incomplètes, avec un risque de closure périmée.

## Refactorisations (comportement inchangé)
- **12 `setState` dans un `useEffect`** :
  - état dérivé : présences enseignant et admin ;
  - ajustement pendant le rendu : TeacherForm, HomeworkDialog, salles ;
  - option `values` de React Hook Form : PaymentFormDialog ;
  - remontage par `key` : EditWageRecordDialog ;
  - hook partagé `useCurrentMinute` (`useSyncExternalStore`) : horloges admin et parent ;
  - **3 exceptions documentées**, pour de vraies synchronisations avec un système externe : lecteurs audio Coran et préférences de colonnes en `localStorage`.
- **`watch()` → `useWatch()`** dans 5 formulaires (le React Compiler est réactivé sur ces composants).
- **Autres règles React** :
  - refs lues pendant le rendu (éditeurs d'annonces et de programme) ;
  - composant défini pendant le rendu (calendrier) ;
  - prop `children` détournée (`MarkAsPaidDialog` → `linkedChildren`) ;
  - `Date.now()` et `Math.random()` pendant le rendu.
- **Corrections mécaniques** : 5 `any`, 72 entités JSX échappées, 56 variables ou imports morts, 4 `eslint-disable` devenus inutiles.
- **Configuration ESLint** : les artefacts générés (`.next-e2e`, rapports Playwright) et `docs/` sont exclus. Avant, `eslint .` remontait plus de 22 000 faux problèmes.

## Tests
- Nouveau `e2e/finance/budget-edit.spec.ts` : création puis modification d'un paiement (formulaire pré-rempli), et le formulaire de création qui repart vide. C'est la refactorisation la plus risquée.

- [x] `npm run typecheck` : OK

- [ ] CI verte (nouveau job lint/typecheck + E2E)

author: 0xmhha
body:
Documentation and configuration cleanup. No behaviour changes: the only code
edits are comment text, one test's heading list, and a renamed case directory.

## What was wrong

Several documents described a tree that no longer exists. `CHAIN-BRINGUP.md`
had a central table naming four env declarations and four cases, and all eight
were gone. `tests/README.md` opened with a block about a Go testkit model
deleted on 2026-09-01, and pointed at `env/README.md`, which does not exist.
`SPECS.md` was a 603-line progress report for a migration that finished,
counting 134 legacy cases against `testkit.Cases()`, deleted on 2026-09-06.

Others were wrong about the current code. `tests/README.md` named
`RegisterAction`/`RegisterAssertion` in `internal/testhelper`, which do not
exist, and claimed test assets inline private keys, which they no longer do.
`SPECS.md` said the file name is the case id (it is not, for 44 cases, and
`tests/tc/README.md` says they are deliberately separate), listed four values
for `requires` where twenty are in use, and named `applicableChains`, which no
case uses, instead of `skipsOn`, which 79 do.

`env/docker/README.md` gave the container firewall's p2p range as 30301-30304.
`firewall.sh` sizes that band from the slot count, so the default settings open
thirteen ports.

## What this does

Rewrites the documents against the tree, in the language each already used,
and translates the Makefile, `workspace-config.sample.yaml` and the testnet
guide to English. `RUN-EACH.md` and `common/HOW-TO-USE.md` are merged into one
`HOW-TO-USE.md` whose per-case command list is generated by a new
`scripts/gen-case-commands.py`, so it cannot drift again -- the old file said
209 cases when there were 197. All 190 generated local commands were checked
with `--plan`.

`tests/env/` is deleted. It had no consumer: `tests/lib/common.sh` was gone,
`CHAINBENCH_TEST_ENV` was read only by itself, and all nine variables were
unread. The server set took over its job, and the convention it carried moved
to `docs/SECURITY_KEY_HANDLING.md`.

`effectivegasprice/` becomes `effective-gas-price/`, matching every sibling
under `post-v1.0.0-change`. The address corpus golden and the command list are
regenerated; the two docs citing the current path follow. The
`legacy-port-audit` pages keep the old spelling, because they record the
retired Go suite's own paths.

`.precommit-allow` loses a path that no longer exists and gains the two tracked
files the hook still blocks.

Finally, comments in six files attributed the port scheme, the firewall
allowlist and the sshd port to a named company test environment, and three
documents said what had been removed from them and why. The technical values
are this project's own configuration and stay; the attribution and the removal
notes are gone.

## Verification

`make check` passes. The 197-case docker sweep ran at 181 pass / 1 fail / 15
blocked; every one of those sixteen was explained and none is a defect in a
case. Three were a directory this branch renamed while the sweep was walking
the tree, and they pass under the new path. Twelve are the two groups the guide
says to run separately: go-wemix needs the poa server set, and the five testnet
cases need an RPC address the sweep cannot supply. The single failure is
`signature-compat-across-swap`, which asserts the client version changes across
a binary swap and has no second build to swap to.

The allocator was checked against the port budget it has to respect: 30 nodes
over 15 servers place two per server, 60 fit, 61 is refused, and a fifth node
on a four-slot server is refused rather than given a port it cannot use. That
placement was then run for real -- 20 stablenet nodes, 20 wbft nodes, and 30
stablenet nodes with two on every server, all producing blocks.

author: wyrtensi
body:
Stage 4c of the EOP work: per-recipient delivery status and bounce marking (R-17).

## What
- Migration `0084_message_delivery_status.sql`: table `message_delivery_status`, the last known outcome per (account, Message-ID, recipient). It holds state, source (`log`/`dsn`), code, a short diagnostic, and each source's latest details side by side. The later event wins; on a tie a failure wins.
- Log capture rides on the 5-minute node alert job's shared Postfix log read, with no new reader or timer. It covers `message.sent` letters of node mailboxes from the last 7 days. A letter is matched by the `cleanup message-id=` line, only within a queue entry whose envelope sender is the mailbox or one of its aliases. Each recipient gets state, relay host/IP/port, the remote reply, TLS (level, protocol, cipher) and EOP's acceptance (`InternalId`, `Hostname`). A capture failure never touches the alerts or the Healthchecks ping.
- DSN marking follows RFC 3464/6533 and works for every account:
  - It runs at sync time, detecting the report from the BODYSTRUCTURE the sync already fetches.
  - The original Message-ID comes from the returned `message/rfc822` envelope, then `In-Reply-To`, then `References`, and last from a `text/rfc822-headers` part.
  - Only the small `message/delivery-status` part is fetched, in the background.
  - Marks are per recipient: `failed` means not delivered, `delayed` is a soft state, other actions mark nothing.
- `GET /api/mail/messages/:id/delivery` is open to anyone who can open the letter:
  - the server resolves everything itself and returns no raw log lines;
  - only node mailboxes get the log lookup;
  - coverage is one of `found`, `stored`, `gone` ("the node log no longer covers this letter", never "delivered"), `not_found` or `unavailable`.
- Shared code dictionary `services/mailNode/deliveryCodes.js` (5.7.64, 5.7.711/AS(2204), 5.7.233, 5.7.232, 5.4.1, 5.4.14, 4.x/5.x classes). `nodeAlerts.js` uses it, matching unchanged.
- `parsePostfixEntry` gains `pid`, `delays` and `tls`. mailcow's log carries no pid, so TLS is matched by `host[ip]:port` plus the delivery's connection time. A reused connection shows "not in log".
- UI:
  - a "Delivery details" expander in the open sent letter;
  - "Not delivered" / "Delivery delayed" markers in the list;
  - en/ru strings and demo data.
- fake-EOP answers in EOP's 250 shape (`250 2.6.0 <msgid> [InternalId=..., Hostname=...] ... Queued mail for delivery`).
- Docs: requirements 5.7 and R-17 status, runbook 6г.

## Verification
- Backend: lint clean; vitest 3887 passed.
- Frontend: lint clean; 3792 passed; build OK.
- fake-EOP: 33 passed.
- Stand, with branch code in a throwaway container and a scratch DB:
  - an accepted letter captured relay, TLS (TLSv1.3) and InternalId;
  - a recipient-denied DSN marked both recipients failed 5.4.1;
  - all coverage states were reproduced.

author: romen-adama-dev
body:
## Problema

En Obsidian seguían saliendo proyectos y personas de prueba ya borrados (Estudio Delta, 11LabsDLK, Carmen…). CouchDB y el vault del servidor coinciden (53 notas vivas), así que no eran notas sueltas: eran **enlaces** de lo que genera el plugin de memoria para sí mismo (`entities/index.md`, `reports/relationship-graph.md`, `reports/stale-pages.md`…, sin regenerar desde el 23-09) y de `Núcleo 🖤.md`, un `index.md` antiguo renombrado desde el móvil. Esos enlaces rotos aparecen como nodos fantasma, y los índices hacen de estrella en el centro del grafo.

## Cambio

- `infra/livesync-bridge/private-paths.patch`: opción `privatePaths` (expresiones regulares sobre la ruta del vault) en el peer de almacenamiento. Esos archivos no se suben a CouchDB; si ya se habían subido (tienen `file-stat`), se borran de allí al arrancar el puente, y los cambios que lleguen del móvil a esas rutas se ignoran.
- `livesync-init.sh`: privados `index.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `WIKI.md`, `inbox.md`, `.gitignore`, `entities|concepts/index.md`, `reports/`, `syntheses/`, `_views/`, `.jarvis/` y `sources/` salvo `sources/proyectos/` (actas a la espera de su proyecto).
- Imagen `jarvis-livesync-bridge:c3760be-privadas`.
- El Mapa (`red.py`) y `docs/OBSIDIAN.md` ya no piden filtros en la vista de grafo; nueva fila de solución de problemas.

En Obsidian queda solo el árbol: 🧭 Mapa → Empresas / Conocimiento (metodologías, glosario, temas, directivas) / Servicios.

## Pruebas

- `docker build` de la imagen (incluye `deno check main.ts`): OK.
- Clasificación de los 54 archivos actuales del vault con las expresiones: 20 privados, 34 sincronizados (todo el árbol).
- `pytest`: 231 OK, 1 omitido.
- **Sin desplegar** en la VM (falta permiso): `docker compose up -d livesync-init livesync-bridge` y comprobar en el log `is private now, deleting it from the other peers`.

  * If saved window coordinates are no longer visible on a display, the app can restore the window to a reachable position.
  * A window-state save failure no longer prevents workspace or credential changes from being saved.

author: os-simaogoncalves
body:
This PR publishes three skills as Beta skills in the Claude, Kiro and Cursor plugins: two Mentor-driven app-building skills, `outsystems-design-to-app` and `outsystems-spec-driven-build`, and `outsystems-custom-code`, which covers building, testing and deploying C# External Logic libraries.

### What was happening
* All three skills lived only in the experimental skills repository, so no supported harness could install them from here.
* The app-creation steps in design-to-app and spec-driven-build called `app_create`, which the MCP server no longer exposes.

### What was done
* Copied all three skill folders unchanged from the experimental repository into `claude/skills/`, `kiro/outsystems/skills/` and `cursor/skills/`, one identical copy per harness.
* Marked all three as Beta: `[Beta]` at the start of `description`, `maturity: beta` under `metadata`, the agreed disclosure paragraph right after the frontmatter (linking the [Beta Features Agreement](https://www.outsystems.com/legal/beta-features-agreement)), and `(Beta)` / `[Beta]` in `agents/openai.yaml`. custom-code's `description` was unquoted, so it is now single-quoted; otherwise the leading `[Beta]` would parse as a YAML list.
* Added a "Beta skills" section to `README.md` with the agreed paragraph and one entry per skill.
* In design-to-app and spec-driven-build, replaced every `app_create` reference with `mentor_start_session` → `mentor_create_asset`, including its required `portfolioKey`, and removed details that only applied to `app_create` (`blank=true`, `clonedFromTemplateKey`, the 0.14.0 template note, `OS-APPS-40018`). The rest of each flow is unchanged. custom-code needed no tool changes.

### Test Steps
1. `diff -r` each skill's Claude copy against its Kiro and Cursor copies: identical.
2. Parse each `SKILL.md` frontmatter and `agents/openai.yaml`: valid YAML, `description` starts with `[Beta]`, `metadata.maturity` is `beta`.
3. `claude plugin validate ./claude`: passed.
4. Compare every OutSystems tool name in the three skills (`allowed-tools`, `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `templates/`) with the live `tools/list` of an ODC tenant (59 tools). design-to-app names 20 tools, spec-driven-build names 12 and custom-code names 6 (`auth_status` and the `extlib_upload` / `extlib_status` / `extlib_publish` / `extlib_logs` / `extlib_contents` family). All of them exist. No `app_create` reference remains.
5. `app_list { detailed: true }` on the same tenant returns a `portfolioKey` field, which the new create step points to.
6. `git merge-tree` against `main`: merges cleanly.

### Screenshots
Not applicable: skill and docs files only.

### Status

**Done**
- [x] All three skills copied into the Claude, Kiro and Cursor plugins, identical across the three copies
- [x] Beta markings on all three skills: `description` prefix, `maturity: beta`, disclosure paragraph with the terms link, `openai.yaml`
- [x] README "Beta skills" section with the agreed paragraph, listing all three skills
- [x] Every tool name the three skills reference exists on the live MCP server; no `app_create` left

**Left to do**
- [ ] Bump the version in all five manifests (`main` is at 1.2.0). Without a bump, `claude plugin update` reports "already at the latest version" and existing users never get the new skills.
- [ ] Load each plugin in a live client (Claude Code, Kiro, Cursor App) and confirm all three skills appear and trigger.
- [ ] Run the create path end to end on a non-demo tenant. Two things are unverified:
  - whether `mentor_create_asset`'s result carries the new app's key, which design-to-app and spec-driven-build tell the agent to capture;
  - both skills create the app in one session, then later open a second session and `mentor_load_asset` it, leaving the first session open. Confirm that a second session can load a new, unpublished app, or change the flow. This is the session model, which is planned for a follow-up.
- [ ] Remove internal references from the shipped files: 38 mentions of, and links to, the private `OutSystems/claude-oml-tool` repository (mostly in `references/gotchas/`); internal workspace paths (`projects/portable-agent-skills/...`) in design-to-app's `references/mcp-flow.md` and `references/gotchas/publish-validator-rejections.md` and in spec-driven-build's `SKILL.md`; internal terms in both `tests/test_publish_contract.py` files. custom-code has none; the two repositories it links to (`OutSystems/UltimatePDF-ExternalLogic`, `OutSystems/vanguard-xml-to-json`) are public.
- [ ] Clear what the Claude plugin directory validator flags in the `claude/` copies (see AGENTS.md): `~/.claude/cache/...` home-folder paths, shell variables in commands (`$CACHE`, `$LOG_DIR`, `${RUN_ID}`, `$SKILL`, `$APP_KEY`, `$PROMPT`), an image file name in backticks in design-to-app's `references/gotchas/icon-coverage-checklist.md`, and two example icon file names in code blocks in custom-code's `SKILL.md` (the `IconResourceName` sample and the project-structure tree).
- [ ] Fix references to things that don't ship in this repo: `CONVENTIONS` sections (§4b, §7b, §8, §8.4) and the sibling skills `outsystems-mentor-copilot`, `outsystems-deploy-preview`, `outsystems-app-architecture`, `outsystems-app-documentation` and `outsystems-change-planner`.
- [ ] Decide on the `tests/` folders in design-to-app and spec-driven-build: they ship inside the plugins to users, and no CI in this repo runs them.
- [ ] Align the skills with the live schemas beyond tool names:
  - `mentor_get_run`: live statuses are `working` / `succeeded` / `failed` / `cancelled` / `not_found`. The skills use `running` / `cancelling` and the fields `details`, `events_limit`, `truncated` and `pollAfterMs`, none of which are in the schema.
  - `publish_status`: live `outcome` values are `in_progress` / `success` / `build_engine_error` / `unknown`. The skills poll for `success` or `failed`.
  - `OS-*` codes: design-to-app's `references/mcp-flow.md` says an `OS-BEW-*` / `OS-DPL-*` code means the server's retries were exhausted. The server's instructions say it is the build's own result.
  - custom-code says `Server is busy, retry shortly` on `extlib_upload` arrives as a `ValidationError`. The main OutSystems skill says current servers return a `CapacityError` with `data.code = "server_busy"`, and only older servers a `ValidationError`.
- [ ] custom-code's Deploy section carries its own setup recipe, which predates the plugin-declared server: `claude plugin install` without `--config tenant_hostname`, then `claude mcp add -s user`, plus a Codex recipe. The skill ships inside the plugin, so it could point at the main OutSystems skill's setup instead.
- [ ] `allowed-tools` lists `mcp__outsystems__*` names in all three skills. The plugin-declared server names its tools `mcp__plugin_outsystems_outsystems__*`, so on the plugin path the pre-approvals don't apply.
- [ ] spec-driven-build: `mentor_create_asset` has no mobile asset type, so the old `Mobile` app kind has no equivalent.
- [ ] Describe the new skill folders, and the rule that keeps each skill's three copies identical, in `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Noticed, out of scope: the test prompt at `CONTRIBUTING.md:123` uses `mentor_start` and `publish_start`, which the live server doesn't expose.

### Harness coverage

| Harness | Outcome |
| :-- | :-- |
| Claude Code | Recorded gap: ships under `claude/skills/` through the plugin's `skills` key, and the manifest validates. Not yet loaded in a live session (see Left to do). |
| Claude Desktop | Recorded gap: same plugin as Claude Code, not tested. All three skills run shell commands and write files (custom-code also needs the .NET SDK and Docker locally), which the Chat tab can't do. |
| Kiro Chat | Recorded gap: ships under `kiro/outsystems/skills/`, which Kiro loads as `skills/*/SKILL.md`. Not yet loaded in Kiro. |
| Copilot in VS Code, CLI and Visual Studio | Not shipped: Copilot receives one file, `copilot/skill.md`, so there is no place for a multi-file ski

author: siy
body:
Fixes #1824

Test-only. `ClusterEventOwnerFailoverTest.eventsRaisedAcrossOwnerDeath_areLandedHeldOrCounted_neverSilentlyLost` asserted `landed <= delivered`, which omits held events (publish outcome unknown, may already have landed). CI reds reconciled exactly to delivered + held = accepted with every tag landed once.

- Oracle is now `landed <= delivered + held`.
- New: held must reach 0 within the landing bound (so held events are re-sent and settle), then no tag landed twice and every sent tag landed. The relaxed bound cannot hide a redelivery stall.

Evidence: unmutated 2/2 green (held=0 at the read in that run, so the settle wait was not exercised with held>0; not observed naturally). Mutation (drop `held.decrementAndGet()` in `ClusterEventRedelivery.retry`; restored, count verified 1): the test goes red at the settle await (held=46, retried>0 so the earlier retried assertion stays green); the other test stays green.

author: schiste
body:
## Summary

Leases inform; only an explicit lease held by a session that is actively working refuses, and nothing refuses in a `verify-only` repository. One rule, `LeaseRefusalPolicy`, now decides every lease refusal: `leases claim`, `leases plan` (`would_conflict`), planned leases at `start --path`, guarded exec and submit.

## Problem

On Mockup (verify-only, v0.8.14) all four `leases claim` calls exited 3 after 5–10 minutes. `claim_lease` refused on **any** other session's overlapping lease, whatever its kind, its holder's liveness or the promote mode. Mockup had 42 stale sessions holding 2,622 implicit leases, and 13 holding 57 explicit ones. #475 had made only `submit` informative under verify-only. Claim, plan, planned start (both the broker check and the store's transactional recheck) and guarded exec each kept their own stricter rule.

## Behaviour

| Other session's lease | auto / manual | verify-only |
|---|---|---|
| explicit, holder **active** | refuses claim, plan, planned start and exec; refuses submit only if the edits conflict (unchanged from #475) | warning |
| explicit, holder idle | warning | warning |
| explicit, holder stale, exited or closed | warning ("not live") | warning ("not live") |
| implicit (derived from edits), live holder | warning | warning |
| implicit, stale holder | omitted | omitted |

Each warning names the holder, its status and the reason, and includes `aethyme broker advanced note send --session <me> --to-session <holder> --message "…"`. `leases claim --json` gains `warnings[]`; text output prints one `note:` line per warning.

The store's planned-lease recheck mirrors the rule in SQL against the stored status. Planning first persists liveness transitions, so a session that went stale since the last status pass no longer reads as `active` there.

## Tests

- New `tests/lease_claim_policy_e2e.rs` (7 tests):
  - a verify-only claim over a working holder's explicit lease succeeds with a warning and the coordination command;
  - outside verify-only, the same claim still refuses;
  - a stale holder's explicit lease never refuses a claim;
  - a live session's implicit lease never refuses an explicit claim;
  - leases implied by a stale session's old edits are not reported;
  - a planned start is refused neither by a stale holder nor under verify-only;
  - guarded exec does not fail on a stale holder's explicit lease.
- **Neuter checks:** disabling each part fails its own test. The parts are the verify-only branch, holder liveness, lease kind, the stale-implicit filter, the store recheck, persisting liveness, and the exec policy.
- `leases_e2e`'s claim-conflict test now pins the explicit-working-holder case.
- 297 lease, claim, store, submit, handoff, finish, merge and ship tests pass, and 201 again after merging current `main`. The aethyme-enhance, testkit, help, JSON-snapshot and docs-drift suites pass 220/220.
- `cargo fmt --check` and workspace `clippy -D warnings` are clean.

## Docs

- `broker-workflows.md`: the claim rule.
- `cross-process-consumers.md`: the new `warnings[]` field and changed exit behaviour.
- The generated agent protocol template (`aethyme-enhance/src/agents.rs`), and this repository's regenerated `references/broker.md`.

## Contract

Contract decision: introduce
Contract justification: `leases claim --json` adds `warnings[]`; claim, plan, planned start and guarded exec no longer refuse on implicit leases, non-working holders, or anything under verify-only (documented in cross-process-consumers.md).

author: filipbolt
body:
## Summary

SDK half of decision **D7** on `OME-1251` (2026-10-02, reverses D3): archive-matched cache money is published, and the board sums **spend + reported saving + archive saving**. The board half is `OME-1382`, PR #1227.

- `CandidateResult` gains `cache_saved_cost_archive_usd` (summed from spans, like the reported saving) and `cache_unpriced_hits` (the Engine run summary's `cache.saved_cost.unpriced_hits`; `None` when no summary arrived). Both are in `to_dict`.
- The submission sends `cache_saved_cost_archive_usd` in its own field, omitted when absent, never added to the spend or the reported saving.
- **New published-cost rule** (narrows #1187 / `OME-1441`):

| cache hits | unpriced hits | spend priced | sent |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 0 | any | any | as before |
| > 0 | 0 | yes | **`complete`**, the spend as `run_cost_usd`, plus the savings |
| > 0 | 0 | no | `partial`, no amount |
| > 0 | > 0 | any | `partial`, no amount |
| > 0 | unknown (no summary) | any | `partial`, no amount |

- Archive money is now saving evidence: an unpriced run with only an archive saving is `partial`, never `unavailable`. The board refuses `unavailable` beside any saving (confirmed by #1227's author), so the old D3 status would have 422'd.

Refs: OME-1463. Spec: `docs/spec/2026-10-02-OME-1463-archive-cost.md`.

## Prior tests changed (owner approval, 2026-10-02)

Five existing tests encoded D3 ("archive money is never published / never evidence") and are rewritten for D7:
- `test_cache_saved_cost_submission.py`: `test_archive_money_never_reaches_the_result_or_the_board` → `..._reaches_the_result_and_the_board`; `test_the_archive_rule_holds_when_the_clock_reads_zero_point_five` keeps its pinned clock and now asserts the archive amount appears exactly once, compared as numbers (OME-1445 stays structural); the else branch of `test_no_evaluated_run_pairs_unavailable_with_a_saving` accepts either saving.
- `test_run_cost_status.py`: `..._only_archive_savings_derives_unavailable` → `..._derives_partial`; the asymmetry test → `test_either_saving_is_evidence_and_no_saving_stays_unavailable`.

`test_cached_run_not_complete.py` (#1187) needed no change: its results carry no summary count, so every hit case still sends `partial`.

## Review round 1 (2026-10-03)

- **P1, fixed: the completeness proof and the money came from different evidence.** The proof came from the engine's run summary, but the saving amounts came from span frames. The engine records a hit's saving on the summary before checking that its span exists, so a run could be sent as `complete` with no saving and ranked at $0. Both savings now come from the run summary. `cache_unpriced_hits` is published only when the summary is consistent: its coverage counts add up to the hits, each total is present exactly when its provenance had hits, and the run's final hit count matches. Otherwise the run goes as `partial`. A summary amount that isn't a decimal string stops the run.
- **P2, fixed:** the public `Span` docstring now separates the two raw measurements, which are never combined on an event, from the Scoreboard's reproduction-cost policy, which adds them once every hit is priced.
- 13 new tests in `test_archive_cost.py`, including the reviewer's exact case end to end. All of them failed first. Four mutations, all caught: amounts taken from spans, the consistency check removed, the final-hit check removed, a float amount accepted. One test from this PR's first commit set an inconsistent summary (2 unpriced on a 1-hit summary). Its setup now states a consistent 3-hit summary, and its intent is unchanged.
- Gates: `run_gates.py screamingface --base origin/main --skip-append-only` all green. The skip covers only the owner-approved rewrites listed above.

## Merge order

**Draft until #1227's D7 change is live on dev.** `ScoreSubmission` is `extra="forbid"`, so an archive-priced submission 422s against an older board. Check `cache_saved_cost_archive_usd` in `https://leaderboard.dev.screamingface.ai/openapi.json` before merging.

## Test plan

- 20 new tests in `tests/test_archive_cost.py`: decoder reads and validates the summary count from the real `cache_hit_contract` fixture; absent count stays unknown; the result carries and exports both fields; every row of the table above; the archive saving is never added to `run_cost_usd`.
- `run_gates.py screamingface --skip-append-only`: all 7 green (ruff, format, pyright, pytest with coverage >= 95: 2210 passed / 26 skipped, notebooks, build, distribution). The append-only check is skipped only for the approved prior-test rewrites and the public-surface snapshot.

author: nmh1988
body:
Closes #19

## Changes
- `app.py`: full chat turn: chat input -> `validate_input` + `validate_role` -> `STRATEGIES[strategy](role, type)` as system message + `build_user_prompt(...)` -> `llm.complete` -> reply. History lives in `st.session_state.history`; each turn keeps `content` (shown) and `sent` (sent to the LLM), so earlier user turns are re-sent inside their `<user_input>` tags.
- Double submission: `on_submit` puts the message in `pending`; the chat input is drawn disabled before the LLM call, the call runs in `st.spinner`, and every path ends in `st.rerun()`. The outcome is saved inside the spinner before any other `st` call, so a rerun requested mid-turn (sidebar click) resends the message instead of losing it. An unexpected exception clears `pending` so the input never stays locked.
- Blank role: sidebar warning right away and the chat input is disabled (T5.1 follow-up). "New session" button clears history.

author: shivam-tamboli
body:
Part 1 of #107. It doesn't close the issue on its own; see "What this doesn't fix yet" below.

## Changes
- **`services/chunker.py`**:
  - A new `_overlap_tail()` builds the carry-over between pieces by walking back from the end until it hits `self.overlap` **tokens**.
  - `_split_by_tokens` now uses it; it used to slice the last 100 **lines**, which copied almost the whole piece.
  - `_chunk_by_lines` already did this inline and now shares the helper.
- **`services/hybrid_search.py`**: `_drop_overlapping()` keeps only the best-ranked of overlapping windows of the **same symbol** (same file, name and chunk type, >50% of the shorter range shared). The reranker now gets a pool of `3 × limit`, so 5 results are still left after dropping.
  - It deliberately **doesn't** merge different symbols. My first version did, and verification caught it knocking out the synthesized `imports` chunk, which always claims lines 1–50.

## ⚠️ Re-indexing
**Repos indexed before this change keep their duplicate chunks until they're re-indexed** (re-import, or "Re-index ZIP"). The retrieval-side dedupe softens this until then, because duplicate windows share a symbol, but the extra chunks still cost embedding storage and crowd keyword search.

## Verification
- `pytest backend/tests`: **81 passed**, with 7 new tests:
  - a large class splits into ≈ tokens/900 pieces
  - consecutive pieces share ≤ ~100 tokens and move forward
  - near-identical windows collapse to the best-ranked one
  - adjacent chunks, other files and other symbols are kept
  - the limit still holds after dropping
  - The chunker tests fail on main; the dedupe tests error because the method doesn't exist there.
- Chunk counts from the real chunker on `pallets/itsdangerous/src`: **194 → 92** (`serializer.py` 125 → 27; the `Serializer` copies are gone).
- End to end, freshly indexing with the real model on a local API:
  - **itsdangerous** (the audit questions): sources went from 4–5 copies of one class to 5 distinct chunks across 1–3 files.
    - "main modules" and "key derivation / default hash" no longer hedge; the second names `derive_key`, its four derivation modes, and SHA-1.
  - **markupsafe** (never seen before): `escape` and `Markup` answers are specific.

## What this doesn't fix yet
Two answers still hedge: "how does expiry verification work?" and markupsafe's "is there a C speedup?". I traced both to the reranker, not chunking:
- Semantic search ranks the right chunks first (`timed.py: TimestampSigner/unsign`; `_speedups.c` and the imports chunk with the `_speedups` import).
- The Cohere call fails (`module 'cohere' has no attribute 'AsyncClientV2'` with the SDK installed locally). The **BM25 fallback then re-sorts purely by shared words**, ignoring the semantic ranking, and those chunks drop out of the top 5.
- Production is on the same fallback; its 0–4+ "scores" are BM25.

I'll fix that in a follow-up issue/PR and check #107's acceptance criteria there.

body:
The week total used to count one portion per cooked meal and treat leftovers as free, so it ignored household size and the leftover portions bought with each dish. Each planned meal now records the portions cooked for it (household × itself plus its leftovers), and the week total, store comparisons and onboarding budget all count every meal for the whole household. Each meal card, leftovers included, now shows that meal's price for the household. The recipe screen, when opened from the week, scales ingredients to the portions actually cooked, so a dish that also covers tomorrow's leftover shows enough for both. Week planner tests now check portions and the new total.

Six of the eight screenshots Orion and F-Droid link to were from **2026-09-04**. They predate the hero card styles, the nav work, scroll-by-default and the present bottom bar — so both stores were advertising an app a month out of date.

Captured on the emulator from the **0.6.0 debug build**, at the device's native 1080×2400, then scaled to 405×900 for the README. Deliberately not from a browser harness — these go to stores, so they should be the Android WebView rendering them, status bar and bottom bar included.

`06-pdf.png` is a real 354-page Arabic PDF that is no longer in any library on this machine, so it cannot be re-shot honestly. The fixed-page chrome in it is identical to the current build, so it is older rather than stale.

author: codesofakash
body:
## The lead

PageSpeed Insights crashed its own headless browser mid-audit
(\`Protocol error (Runtime.evaluate): Target closed\`) running against the
home page specifically, on both Mobile and Desktop. \`/about\` completed
normally with real scores (63/100/96/100). The home page's 3D hero canvas
is the one meaningful difference between them.

## What was actually costing something, removed

- **\`shadows\`** — every material in this model is \`KHR_materials_unlit\`
  with lighting baked into the texture, and nothing in this file sets
  \`castShadow\`/\`receiveShadow\` anywhere. Confirmed via grep before
  removing it. Pure overhead: shadow-map setup + a per-frame shadow pass,
  for a scene with zero lights capable of casting one.
- **\`preserveDrawingBuffer: true\`** — confirmed nothing in the codebase
  ever reads this canvas's buffer back (no screenshot/export feature).
  It disables the browser's normal buffer-swap optimization, which matters
  most here specifically: this is the only one of the project's four 3D
  canvases that redraws every single frame regardless of interaction (no
  \`frameloop="demand"\`), so the cost compounds continuously.
- **No \`dpr\` cap** — defaulted to the device's full, uncapped pixel ratio.
  Added \`dpr={[1, 2]}\`: a phone at DPR 3 would otherwise render 9x the
  pixels of DPR 1 for a visually marginal gain over capping at 2x.

All three are zero-visual-impact removals, not a quality tradeoff.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` clean
- [x] \`npm run lint\` clean
- [ ] After merge + deploy: **re-run PageSpeed Insights against the home
      page** — that's the real test of whether this fixes the crash, not
      local reasoning about what should help
- [ ] Visually confirm the hero still looks identical (no shadows were
      ever visible to begin with, so there should be nothing to notice)

Three jobs bounded; `verify` already declared 15 and is untouched. The RubyGems `publish` job gets 30.

Jobs without `timeout-minutes` run to GitHub's 360-minute default. Measured across this org, the median job finishes in 0.4 minutes and the slowest takes 19.6, so the default is roughly 18x the slowest job. Two hangs today each cost hours: an apt stall during a Playwright browser install, and a Homebrew job that fell through to compiling CPython from source.

This bounds every unbounded job at 20 minutes, 30 in release and deploy workflows where a hang can leave a package half-published, and 40 where a measured run already passes ten minutes.

Durations were read per workflow file over the last 20 completed runs, keyed on the pair of workflow file and job name. Two files in one repo can define jobs with the same name, so a cross-workflow sample misreads them.

Existing bounds are left alone. CI configuration only: no source, version or changelog change, so there is no changelog entry.

author: solarssk
body:
## Description

**Business context.** When an Organisation settings tab cannot load (General, Mail, External services, Notifications, Security, and the mail card in Event settings) it shows an error with a **Retry** button. A person using the keyboard or a screen reader who presses **Retry** and succeeds lost their place: the error and the focused button disappeared together, the browser dropped the focus on the page behind, and the screen reader had nothing to say about where it was. Now the focus moves to the tab's own panel, which a screen reader announces by name, and the next Tab goes to the first field. A person who had already moved on is not interrupted.

**Technical changes.**

- UI (`apps/admin/src/settings/PanelLoadError.tsx`): the card keeps a ref to its Retry button. A layout-effect cleanup (React runs it before the card is taken out of the page, so the Retry still holds focus and still has its tab panel above it) checks whether the Retry held focus and finds the nearest `[role="tabpanel"]`; a microtask then runs once the form is mounted and, only if focus is on `<body>` by then, gives the tab panel `tabindex="-1"` (when it has no `tabindex`) and focuses it. Focus that was never on the Retry, focus that has moved, and focus the new content has taken are left alone, and a card outside a tab panel does nothing. Every panel that fails through `PanelLoadError` gets this: General, Security, Mail, External services, Notifications and the Event settings mail card, each of which sits in a `role="tabpanel"`.
- Tests (`apps/admin/test/settings/SettingsPanelSkeleton.test.tsx`): 7 jsdom cases (focus moves to the tab panel, an existing `tabindex` is kept, focus elsewhere, nothing focused, new content takes focus, the Retry still there while busy or failed again, no tab panel). Each guard was mutation-checked against the whole file: removing it fails a test.
- Docs: the settings-panel bullet in `AGENTS.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (`[Unreleased]` > Fixed).

## How to test

- `npm test -w @admitto/admin` (and the rest of the gate: `npm run lint`, `npm run build -w @admitto/ui`, `npm run build -w @admitto/admin`, `npm test -w @admitto/ui`, `npm run docs:check`, `npm run coverage -w @admitto/admin`).
- Real Chrome (Playwright, `channel: "chrome"`) against the built admin with a stubbed API whose first `GET /api/admin/system-settings` returns 500: open `/admin/settings`, Tab to **Retry**, press Enter. Before: `document.activeElement` is `<body>`. After: it is `div[role=tabpanel][aria-label="General"][tabindex="-1"]`, and the next Tab lands on the first focusable control in the form. A mouse click on **Retry** ends the same way.
- By hand: make `/api/admin/system-settings` fail once (DevTools request blocking, then unblock), Tab to **Retry**, Enter, and press Tab again.

## What stays / known limitations

- A keyboard user sees the app's standard focus ring around the whole tab panel until the next Tab (the global `:focus-visible` rule); a mouse click shows none. It is the shared focus indicator, so it was left as is.
- A **Retry** that fails again keeps its focus as before (the button is never unmounted); this PR only covers the retry that works.
- Dialogs and popovers keep their own recovery (`useFocusRecovery`), and the one-line `RetryHint` is unchanged.

## Documentation impact

- [ ] Wiki updated
- [x] No Wiki update needed - the Wiki's recovery steps for a tab that could not load (press **Retry**) are unchanged; where keyboard focus lands afterwards is not described there.

---

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets / keys / passwords in the diff
- [x] No real personal data (seed/sample data uses synthetic `@example.com` addresses)
- [x] Tests pass locally (`npm test`; optional: `npm run coverage` to match CI)
- [x] New or changed functionality is covered by tests added to the automated suite
- [x] New fields containing personal data are justified and minimised (no new fields)
- [x] No PII in logs; token/QR contains no personal data
- [x] DB schema changes include a migration (no schema change)

author: youssefsfaims
body:
## Why

Support ticket **MS-027** (Luke Huber: take Jose Robles off Team Luke) showed the boards disagreeing with User Management and with each other. Teams came from three places: RepCard (Sales Leaderboard), a hand-typed `ROSTER` in `src/lib/repcard/org-chart.ts` (My Dashboard, Scoreboard, RepCard nickname translation, team→branch), and User Management (Org Chart, and the Course Leaderboard since #81). Every team move needed a code change, and Daniel Reyes's dashboard still shows Gunner's team.

Youssef decided on 2026-10-02 that **every board takes teams and branches from User Management**, the same data the Org Chart page draws. The typed list is deleted.

## The rules (all in `src/lib/repcard/org-chart.ts`, pure, 32 tests)

- **Only sales reps have a Team Lead.** A rep is on their lead's team and shows their lead's branch. Teams are named by the lead's **full name** ("Team Luke Huber").
- **Every team lead and every branch manager leads a team** and is on it. Branch managers are still **not** ranked on the Course Leaderboard.
- **A team lead's / branch manager's branch is the Branch on their own profile.** (User Management already derives a lead's Branch Manager from that Branch.) Links stored on team leads (e.g. Luke → Jonathan) are leftovers and are ignored.
- **A live sales rep set to "No Branch" is unassigned:** no team, no branch, whatever Team Lead is stored (Quinton Hill).
- **Marketing, C-level and Admin never have a team or branch**, even when they knock in RepCard (Naaman Taylor).
- **Deleted accounts** (soft-deleted, ~11/month) are kept in the org chart: a former rep keeps the team stored on their account (many old accounts have a blank Branch; the Team Lead still places them); a departed lead's team stays for past periods but is not offered as a current team; an active rep whose lead was deleted stays on that team, with a warning.
- **RepCard only places people with no app account** (e.g. Martin Ramirez, David Bolles): their RepCard team is matched to the app team its members are on, ties settled by the lead the RepCard team is named after ("Gunner", "Jon", "Mike M."). No typed aliases.
- Old Branch values ("Round Rock, Texas") are read through `officeToBranch`. The 12 such values in production were also normalised on 2026-10-02 (backup kept locally).

## What changed

- `org-chart.ts`: rewritten as `buildOrgChart()` + `repcardTeamMatcher()`; `ROSTER`, `TEAM_ALIAS`, `TEAM_OVERRIDES`, `TEAM_BRANCH`, `TEAM_LEADS`, `TEAM_NAMES`, `isBranchless` removed. `check-repcard-team-drift.js` removed (it compared ROSTER with RepCard).
- **Sales Leaderboard** (`compute.ts`, `pages/api/leaderboard.ts`, `LeaderboardBoard.tsx`): team/branch from the org chart; deleted accounts loaded for placement only (never "You" or photo). The API now returns `teams` (every live team, branch order) for the Team filter.
- **My Dashboard / Scoreboard** (`resolve.ts`, `dashboard.ts`, `scoreboard.ts`): a team lead's scope is their own team; a branch manager's is their profile Branch. Fixes Daniel Reyes's dashboard.
- **Course Leaderboard** (`board-data.ts`, `training/leaderboard.ts`): same org chart; branch now follows the team lead.
- **Reports and links:** the `TEAM_LEADS` translations are gone (team names are already full names).
- **User Management:** org chart warnings beside the existing RepCard notes (no branch manager for a lead's Branch; deleted or invalid Team Lead; rep's Branch differs from their lead's). Every branch manager appears in a rep's Team Lead picker and under the **Sales Team Lead** role filter. The "Also a Sales Team Lead" tick box is gone: picking Branch Manager sets `roles: ["branch-manager","sales-team-lead"]` automatically (all three current branch managers already have it, so nothing changes for them).
- `pages/api/public/team-leads.ts` (register page, phone sign-up) includes every branch manager.

## What users will see

- Team names are full names everywhere. On the Sales Leaderboard, Daniel Reyes, Cayden Roesch and Ben Johnson move from Gunner to Team Daniel Reyes; Ashton Foster joins Team Cooper Bledsoe; Valentin Grajeda (now Sales under Jonathan) counts for Team Jonathan Chambers.
- Daniel Reyes's dashboard shows his own team.

## Testing

- `npm run test:all`: **1684 + 121 passing**. `npm run build`: clean.
- Smoke test against a throwaway in-memory database (no production contact): **46/46 API checks** covering every rule above plus access (signed out 401, sales rep 403 on the warnings endpoint), and browser checks: Sales Leaderboard team filter (full names, filter to one team), User Management badges, warning messages, Team Lead picker, Sales Team Lead role filter, saving a role change to Branch Manager, Daniel Reyes's and Gunner's dashboards, and the dashboard "See all" link into the Course Leaderboard. No console errors.

## Mobile mirror notes for Krupali

**Needs a change: the five Sales Leaderboard (rankings) screens** — `rankings_screen.dart`, `sales_team_lead_rankings_screen.dart`, `branch_manager_rankings_screen.dart`, `clevel_rankings_screen.dart`, `marketing_rankings_screen.dart`. Each has its own typed copy of the old list:

```dart
static const Map<String, String> _teamLeads = { 'Gunner': 'Gunner McCullough', 'Luke': 'Luke Huber', ... };
static const List<String> _teamNames = ['Gunner', 'Luke', 'Jonathan', 'Mike Muscari', 'Cooper', 'Daniel Sabedra'];
```

After this deploy, `GET /api/leaderboard` returns `leaderboard[].team` as the lead's **full name** ("Luke Huber"), so a phone Team filter built from `_teamNames` ("Luke") matches nothing until the app is updated.

- Delete `_teamLeads`, `_teamNames` and `_teamLabel`.
- Build the Team filter options from the new response field **`teams`** (array of strings, already in branch order), plus any `leaderboard[].team` not in it (a departed lead's team that still has a rep), plus "(No team)" when a row has `team == null`.
- Show `row['team']` as is (it is already the display name).
- Dashboard links: `GET /api/dashboard` `scope.team` is now the full name too, so `RankingsLinkArgs(team: ...)` keeps working once the filter uses the new names. `scope.trainingTeam` is kept and always equals `scope.team`.

Acceptance: on the phone, Sales Leaderboard → Team filter lists "Daniel Reyes, Gunner McCullough, Jonathan Chambers, Luke Huber, Cooper Bledsoe, Mike Muscari, Daniel Sabedra"; picking "Daniel Reyes" shows Jose Robles and Daniel Reyes; a team lead's dashboard "See all" opens the board filtered to their team, not empty.

**Nothing to build:** Course Leaderboard screens (they read `rows[].team/branch` from the server), the register screen (the public team-lead list just gains branch managers), and the dashboard team chip (server-side).

author: kire21b
body:
## What
`find` costs agents fewer rounds, and every body it shows is bounded.

- **Batch ids.** `fael find a b c` and MCP `ids: [...]` print every body in one call. A bad id reports alone, the rest print, the call is an error (same as batch `close`). Bodies stop at the `find_tokens` budget; the first always shows and the cut line names the ids left.
- **Short lists show bodies.** A first page of one or two rows with no `--limit` shows bodies, but only when they all fit `find_tokens`; a fat row stays a title. `--limit` asks for titles back. The no-filter session brief is untouched.
- **Empty finds say why.** Each word, `--files` and filter is counted on its own, e.g. `no rows match — each alone: "decide.rs" ×0 · "heuristic" ×2 · a path? use --files`.
- **Misses are recorded.** An empty *text* search is appended to the machine-local `find-misses.jsonl` and listed by `fael stats --misses`. Decision 01M3ST4V defers a vector index "until a recorded miss", but nothing recorded one. Search itself is unchanged and stays deterministic.
- **`find --json` warns, never cuts.** It printed every row with its body and ignored the budget (~24k tokens on a 124-row log). It is the machine shape, so truncating would silently drop rows; over the budget with no `--limit` it now prints one `fael: N rows, ~T tokens of JSON` line on stderr. stdout stays pure JSON.
- **Constants ceiling 6100 → 6300 B** (measured 6215) for the new `ids` schema. It still sits just above the measure; the reason is in `schema.rs`.

## Behaviour changes to check
- A one- or two-row `find` now prints bodies. Four existing tests assumed titles for such lists and now pass `--limit`; two asserted the exact text `no rows match` and now match the explained form.
- `docs/architecture.md` and `--help` are updated, including the `close` MCP row that still lacked `ids[]`.

## Tests
New `tests/find_batch.rs` (batch ids, expansion, fat-body bounds, JSON warning, empty search and its record) and core unit tests for `expands` and `why_empty`. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` (host and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), `scripts/file-size.sh` and `cargo test --workspace` each exit 0.

author: memerson6158
body:
The first authoritative list of which `component_id`s this package can render — and the gate that keeps it honest.

## The defect this closes

A headless agent names a surface by `component_id`; this package draws it. **Neither side declared the valid set.**

eden-biz carries 15 recorded fixtures under `go/internal/agentintent/testdata/` using **10 distinct ids** across 28 occurrences, and its own integrity test (`fixtures_integrity_test.go:150`) asserts only that the field is non-empty:

```go
if strings.TrimSpace(fx.Intent.ComponentID) == "" { ... }
```

So an agent could emit `summary/pipeline`, the Go fixture test would pass, and nothing anywhere knew the renderer cannot draw it. The ids existed only as string literals in fixtures. **An unknown `component_id` was an undetectable condition.** This makes it detectable.

## Two entries, deliberately

```json
[ { "component_id": "error/refusal",     "widget": "EdenRefusal" },
  { "component_id": "list/appointments", "widget": "EdenAppointmentList" } ]
```

Eight of eden-biz's ten have no renderer here — `card/proposal`, `detail/appointment`, `detail/customer-history`, `list/customers`, `list/services`, `list/availability-slots`, `summary/pipeline`, `summary/scheduling`.

An honest two plus a working refusal path beats a hand-maintained ten of which eight would be lies. It also forces the refusal path to be real from the start rather than discovered at component ten — and `error/refusal` is already the second-most-used id in eden-biz's own fixtures (4 of 15), so it is exercised, not theoretical.

## Direction of the dependency

This declares what **eden-ui can render**; eden-biz checks its fixtures against it. Hard-coding eden-biz's fixture ids here would invert that and make the component library track the agent's test data.

## Why the declaration is hand-written

Two alternatives were considered and rejected, both for the same reason:

- **Parse the source for `componentId`** — a regex that stops matching is indistinguishable from a directory with nothing to declare.
- **Self-registration** — a component that forgets to register is invisible.

Both fail **open**. So the declaration is written by hand and `test/tool/emit_component_manifest_test.dart` proves it accounts for the directory **exactly**, in both directions: every `componentId` in source appears in the list (case 1), and every entry still exists in source (case 3). Adding a component and skipping the decision is what fails. Same pattern as `test/design/design_md_fresh_test.dart`'s token-file partition, including its vacuity guard.

The id always comes from the widget's own static — `(EdenAppointmentList.componentId, EdenAppointmentList)`, never a re-typed literal. A re-typed string is a second list, and a second list is the drift this exists to close.

## Evidence

**7 cases green.** Full suite 5033 passed / 41 skipped. `flutter analyze` clean on all three files.

**Case 1's failure mode proven by differential control**, not assumed. A probe component declaring an undeclared id:

```
Actual: Set:['probe/undeclared']
component_id(s) declared in source but missing from kDataDisplayComponents: probe/undeclared (_probe_component.dart)
00:00 +6 -1: Some tests failed.
```

Names the id **and** the file. Probe removed → back to `+7: All tests passed!`.

**Case 2 is deliberately absent from the test file**, and the file says so rather than leaving the gap silent: proving the undeclared-component mode requires a component that is not declared, and committing one would make case 1 permanently red. It lives as the recorded control above instead.

## Notes

- The emitter runs as `flutter test tool/emit_component_manifest.dart`, not `dart run` — the declaration transitively imports `material.dart`, so it needs the engine `flutter test` provides. Same constraint and same `test()`-wrapped `main()` device as `tool/emit_flutter_manifest.dart`, which this mirrors throughout.
- Output defaults to `build/agent-components.json` (git-ignored), overridable via `--dart-define=EMIT_OUT=`.
- Schema is locked and asserted key-for-key against `kComponentManifestKeys` rather than restated in the test — a second copy of a schema is how a schema drifts.
- Entries sort by `component_id` so the bytes are stable and a diff shows only real change.

## Not in scope

The eight missing components. This is the seam only.

author: coachtazbrown
body:
## Summary

Adds the complete `book-to-skill` converter as a Claude Code agent skill. This tool transforms books and documents (PDF, EPUB, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, plain text, RTF, MOBI/AZW) into structured agent skills by extracting frameworks, principles, techniques, and anti-patterns—enabling agents to reference and apply knowledge from documents on-demand.

## Key Changes

- **Core extraction pipeline** (`book_to_skill/utils.py`): 808-line module implementing document parsing, chapter detection (supporting English, Chinese, Thai, Korean, and Roman numerals), token estimation with CJK character awareness, and skill generation workflow
- **Multi-format parser support**: Dedicated parsers for PDF (with Docling, pdftotext, pypdf, pdfminer fallbacks), EPUB (ebooklib + zipfile fallback), DOCX (python-docx + XML fallback), HTML (BeautifulSoup + stdlib fallback), RTF, plain text, and Calibre-supported formats (MOBI/AZW)
- **Dependency management** (`book_to_skill/dependencies.py`): Intelligent optional dependency detection and installation prompts, with format-specific fallback chains
- **Security hardening** (`book_to_skill/sanitize.py`): Strips invisible Unicode codepoints and bidirectional formatting controls to prevent prompt injection attacks
- **Skill validation tools**: 
  - `tools/validate_skill.py`: Audits generated SKILL.md against host-specific rules (Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Amp)
  - `tools/scan_generated_skill.py`: Advisory scanner for prompt injection and unsafe authority patterns
  - `tools/discovery_tax.py`: Measures token efficiency gains vs. context-dumping strategies
- **Comprehensive documentation** (`SKILL.md`, `README.md`): Detailed usage guide, philosophy, four operational modes (full conversion, analyze-only, generate-from-analysis, update/fold-in), and step-by-step workflow
- **Configuration & CLI**: Centralized config (`book_to_skill/config.py`), CLI entry point (`book_to_skill/cli.py`), and Python package structure

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Multilingual chapter detection**: Regex patterns for explicit chapter headings in 6+ languages, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals with unit composition, Thai positional digits, and Korean statute-style numbering
- **CJK-aware token counting**: Separate heuristics for whitespace-delimited (Latin) vs. non-delimited (CJK) text to avoid 1000x underestimation on Chinese/Japanese books
- **Structural heading analysis**: Detects chapter hierarchy from Markdown/AsciiDoc/RST sources, deduplicates by depth, and selects the real chapter level
- **Prompt injection defense**: Hardened invisible-codepoint detection reused across extraction and validation tools to prevent drift
- **Graceful degradation**: Every format has a stdlib-only fallback; optional packages are detected and installed on-demand with user consent
- **Four operational modes**: Supports full conversion, analysis-only review, generation from prior analysis, and merging new content into existing skills

## Files Added

- Core: `book_to_skill/{utils,cli,config,exceptions,__init__,__main__}.py`
- Parsers: `book_to_skill/parsers/{text,html,pdf,epub,docx,rtf,calibre,__init__}.py`
- Dependencies: `book_to_skill/dependencies.py`, `book_to_skill/sanitize.py`
- Tools: `tools/{validate_skill,scan_generated_skill,discovery_tax}.py`
- Scripts: `scripts/{extract.py,banner.txt}`
- Documentation: `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE.md`, `pyproject.toml`

## Files Modified

- `.gitignore`: Added Python cache patterns for vendored agent skills

author: amirhosseinfarzin
body:
## Summary

- A pack's held slots now answer to signed references rather than to the vendor's bytes. Each reference
  states the origin, the request, the identity, the instant it was read and the bound the document signed
  for itself, the body digest, the chain digest, the arm that weighed it and the window it was weighed
  in, and a reader recomputes both digests rather than believing either.
- The manifest gains two members and a reader of an older pack is refused by name. The count that three
  texts quoted from before these members existed is corrected to the eight `pack.cddl` now names.
- The chain that arrives beside a served body can now travel with it. A retained answer carries the
  header's bytes exactly as they arrived, `chain` is present exactly when `chainSha256` is, and which of
  the two arms reads an answer stays the declaration's question rather than one this container answers.
- The byte arm that carries material beside its references is permitted by the layout and filled by no
  path a deployment runs. Whether a deployment may hand a service's bytes on is its own agreement. The
  offline proof and the published vectors do attach synthetic documents, from a vendor this repository's
  own fixtures generate, because a reader telling a pair from a body alone cannot be shown any other
  way, and the arm's documents say which paths do that and which never do.
- Four refusals of that arm are renamed to match the member they guard, and three new ones guard the
  references: a held slot that names nothing, a reference no attached material resolves to, and a bound
  outside the slot's own band. Each is raised before any of it is documented as a possibility.
- The published vectors now carry the case every other implementation has to reach: one accepted pack
  whose reference resolves to a served body beside the issuer chain that arrived with it, and a refused
  row for the arm whose chain is not the one its reference names, with both hexes in the detail. The
  guarantee over accepted rows asked that the arm be empty in each of them, which that row refutes; it
  now requires that every attached object resolve by the digest of the bytes beside it to a reference the
  same pack signs for, and fails if no accepted row attaches anything at all.
- `verify-receipted` reaches those readings from the command line. Two flags name a document and the
  chain that arrived beside it, the report states the slot and the digest each pair was checked against,
  the root it stood behind and the instant it was read at, and naming neither answers honestly that the
  material is unreached. The anchor demand that these readings satisfy ran only in the client's own path
  before this, so a policy's slot and text-shape demands did nothing at that verb.
- The synthetic vendor moved out of another package's test directory to `@ashaveri/fixtures`, which is
  where its only imports already put it, and every consumer reaches it by package name. No vector moved:
  the vendor derives its keys from a label, so the published bytes regenerate equal.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run test` green on this head
- [x] The CLI bundle builds and the offline proof passes against it, including the attached-pair arm
- [x] The generated-vectors job proves the published fixtures are byte-stable under regeneration

author: pascalandy
body:
## Problem

- A skill that must never fire on its own had no numbered practice. The rule sat inside "Invocation" in `skill-format.md`, so a review could not cite it, and it missed two cases: a common word like `plan` fires on everyday prompts, and an inner `"` ends a double-quoted description
- Asking `writing-for-agents` to improve an existing skill had no branch and no list to tick, so covering every best practice depended on memory

## Solution

- **BP_21 Invoke by a word**: ``Use only when explicitly invoked as `<word>`.``, the word in backticks, other quotes as backticks or single quotes, no actor. `skill-format.md` owns the rule; "Invocation" lists model-invoked, user-invoked, and explicitly invoked skills with their costs and points to it. The validator warns when an invoke-only description breaks the form or names "the user". Across the public skills it fires once, on `corey-mode`'s deliberate word trigger; invoke-only descriptions that skip "Use only when", such as `tavily`'s, are not caught yet (#335)
- **BP checklist**: the BP list is now a copyable checklist. "Create, edit, or improve a skill" starts by filling it for an existing skill and ends with every BP ticked; Review checks each applicable BP and keeps its report format; every workflow step ends on a done condition
- A fourth eval scenario improves the planted-mistake skill. The drift test now requires checkbox lines and contiguous IDs; 19 tests (20 cases) pass. Follow-ups: #335, #336

author: tactino
body:
## The question

E50 found the boundary transparent with state vectors. With camera frames, a uint8 image space, a CNN and frame stacking, does SB3 still end on the same weights through the bridge? And what do 16 frames a step cost?

## The answer

Yes, the weights are the same. SB3 PPO with CnnPolicy, 16 `AtariWrapper(ALE/Pong-v5)` environments, 40,960 steps:

| seed | weights | episodes | per vector step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `82f80c02…` both | 183, identical | +2.99 ms |
| 1 | `60acba42…` both | 176, identical | +2.60 ms |
| 2 | `6bf04095…` both | 183, identical | +2.98 ms |

Every check and prediction holds. Each step moves 16 frames of 7 KiB twice, since this client does not reuse observations. That costs about 2.8 ms on the loopback, or 10–11% of this short CPU run.

The run uses plugrl-bridges' `image_key` (PlugRL/plugrl-bridges#3). It is too short to learn Pong, and it is not meant to: it compares weights.

author: will383842
body:
## Identité

Auteur: A06
Relecteur: A09 exactitude · A09 securite
Couvre: REQ-GOV-014
Lot:

## Ce que fait cette PR

QA-T67, revendiquée par l'issue #469 (chemins au rattrapage 60), suite de QA-T55 : **la porte A du même sha se lit avec DEUX permissions, `contents: read` et `actions: read`** ; `checks: read` disparaît. La lentille sécurité a posé quatre conditions le 2026-10-02 ; elles sont tenues mot pour mot :

1. **La lecture des runs.** Ils viennent de `GET /repos/{dépôt}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=<sha>&event=push&branch=main`.
   - **Refus `hors_filtre`.** Si la forge rend un run hors de ce filtre, le refus est nommé, et ce run n'est jamais ignoré. Sont visés : un run d'une PR sur le même sha, une autre branche, un autre sha, un autre workflow que `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
2. **Le run le plus récent.** Il se choisit sur `run_number` puis `run_attempt`, des champs du SERVEUR, jamais sur une date ni sur l'ordre de la réponse.
   - **Refus `reponse_illisible`.** Il tombe sur un `id`, un `run_number` ou un `run_attempt` qui n'est pas un entier.
3. **Le run retenu et son job.** Le run doit être `completed` et `success`. Ensuite, `GET /actions/runs/{id}/jobs?per_page=100` doit rendre le job `gate-a` en `completed` et `success`.
   - **Refus nommés.** `gate_a_absent` si le run n'a pas ce job, `echec` s'il ne conclut pas en succès.
   - **Si rien n'est jugé dans la borne.** Un run absent, ou toujours en cours, est un refus nommé.
   - **Rien n'est imprimé.** Ni le jeton, ni les adresses appelées.
4. **La PAIRE est figée** par `un-seul-producteur-de-deploiement.spec.ts`. Une copie cassée de deploy.yml rougit si elle ajoute `checks: read` ou une écriture.

author: masterzen
body:
## What?

Add a `--sign-before-push` flag to `jj git push`, and the corresponding `git.sign-before-push` configuration. Both are modifiers of `git.sign-on-push`: when signing on push is enabled, the new option records the freshly created signatures in their own transaction, which is committed before the push starts, instead of keeping them in the
push transaction.

The push itself is unchanged: it runs in a fresh transaction on top of the signing one, and no signing happens there anymore. When nothing needs signing, no extra transaction is created and behavior is identical to before.

## Why?

With `git.sign-on-push`, signing happens inside the same transaction as the push. Signing rewrites the pushed commits (new commit IDs, reparented descendants), so when the push fails, the aborted transaction discards the signatures along with everything else.

This is painful with slow or interactive signing backends: a hardware key owner who misses the touch prompt during the push loses all the signing work and has to redo it on the next attempt, which makes it easy to get stuck in a sign/fail/repeat loop. With the new option, a failed push keeps the signatures and retrying finds nothing left to
sign, so the retry goes straight to pushing.

## Notes

- Possibly worth discussing in review: should the default eventually flip, or should `--sign-before-push` also work standalone without `git.sign-on-push`? It is deliberately scoped as a modifier for now.

body: The production fan in #104 proved the frozen blade child is correct and anchored at local Y=0. The failure is installation math: AI-authored transforms placed the child's long Y axis tangentially or rotated it out of plane. This patch adds a generic repeated-axis alignment contract (`radial`, `tangential`, `free`). For radial features the AI still chooses scale, center/radius and alignment intent, while the runtime enforces equal angular spacing, identical instance scale and mathematically correct long-axis rotation when the child's thin axis matches the inferred symmetry axis. No fan/blade geometry, dimensions or object-specific condition is hard-coded.

author: dborup
body:
Relates to #156.

## Problem

The `Verify proto syntax` step in `Go Build & Test` ran `apt-get update` / `install` with no timeout. A stalled mirror could hold the runner until the workflow-level limits kicked in (one PR run sat about 45 minutes in this step on 2026-09-30).

## Change

Only `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, 8 insertions and 2 deletions:

- `timeout-minutes: 5` on the `Verify proto syntax` step.
- apt runs with `-o Acquire::Retries=3 -o Acquire::http::Timeout=30` on both `update` and `install`, plus `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`.
- Explicit `::error::` and exit 1 if `protoc` is missing after the install.
- `timeout-minutes: 40` on the `go-test` job.

The loop that runs `protoc` over every `proto/*.proto` is unchanged. Triggers, permissions, other jobs, concurrency and fork guards are untouched.

## Job timeout rationale

`Go Build & Test` took 15.8 to 21.9 minutes (median about 20.7) over the last 12 completed runs. 40 minutes is roughly 1.8x the slowest observed run, so ordinary variance will not trip it, and it is far below the 6 hour GitHub default. The 5 minute step timeout is what actually bounds the apt hang. The proto step itself took 9 to 19 seconds in those runs.

## Alternative considered

Download a pinned `protoc` release and check its sha256. That removes apt entirely and is cacheable, but it adds a version and checksum to maintain and a new download dependency. Bounded apt with retries plus a step timeout meets the acceptance criteria with the smallest diff, so I chose that.

## Verification

- Workflow YAML parses (python3 yaml). actionlint is not installed locally.
- Fork guard count `github.repository == 'Kpa-clawbot/CoreScope'` is 9 before and after, and the diff of the guard lines is empty.
- The step's shell logic was run locally with the `sudo apt-get` lines removed: all `proto/*.proto` validate and exit is 0.
- A copy of `proto/` with an invalid `.proto` added makes the step exit 1 with the protoc error.
- With `protoc` off `PATH` the step exits 1 with `protoc not found after install`.

## Not verified

A real apt hang cannot be provoked in CI, so the fail-fast behaviour on a genuine stall is reasoned from the timeouts, not observed.

body:
## Summary

This PR resolves #3356 by adding configurable quiet hours for in-app push notifications, suppressing or deferring non-critical notifications while allowing critical alerts to bypass quiet hours.

### Changes Made
1. **Database Schema & Validations (`prisma/schema.prisma`, `src/lib/validations.ts`)**:
   - Added `quietHoursStart` and `quietHoursEnd` fields to the `User` model in `prisma/schema.prisma`.
   - Updated `userSettingsSchema` in `src/lib/validations.ts` to validate 24-hour time strings (`HH:mm`) for both `quietHoursStart` and `quietHoursEnd`.
2. **Quiet Hours Evaluation & Push Dispatching (`src/lib/pushNotifications.ts`, `src/lib/push.ts`)**:
   - Implemented `isWithinQuietHours()` supporting daytime, overnight intervals (e.g., 22:00 to 07:00), 12-hour/24-hour formats, and user timezones.
   - Implemented `isUserInQuietHours()` with fallback to existing notification window preferences (`notificationStart`/`notificationEnd`).
   - Integrated quiet hours check in `sendPushNotification()` before web push dispatch:
     - Non-critical notifications during quiet hours are suppressed and recorded with status `"DEFERRED_QUIET_HOURS"`.
     - Critical notifications (`isCritical: true`, `options.force`, or `options.ignoreQuietHours`) bypass quiet hours and deliver immediately.
   - Updated `sendVenueAvailabilityNotification()` to respect user quiet hours.
   - Added `src/lib/push.ts` re-exporting push notification utilities.
3. **User Settings API (`src/app/api/user/settings/route.ts`)**:
   - Added support for reading and updating `quietHoursStart` and `quietHoursEnd` in `GET`, `POST`, and `PATCH` handlers.
4. **Comprehensive Unit Tests (`src/__tests__/lib/pushQuietHours.test.ts`)**:
   - 13 unit tests covering daytime and overnight quiet windows, timezone conversion, AM/PM formatting, fallback handling, non-critical suppression, critical notification bypass, and venue availability push notifications.

### Testing & Verification
- Ran `npm test -- src/__tests__/lib/pushQuietHours.test.ts src/__tests__/api/notifications.test.ts src/__tests__/lib/notificationWindow.test.ts` (all 28 tests passing).
