author: fpresta0607
body:
## Why

The Overlord, 2026-10-02, on the board:

- The tip of the first queued card lay over the memory meter ("Memory free 6.0 GB").
- "make sure tooltips encompass full text", and of the tip's background, "not as transparent".
- "the goblin task panels, instead of close, should have a back button to navigate back to the CFO task panel, for any tasks in progress, paused or completed."

## What changed

### One tip for the whole board

- Every tip is now one box that floats over the whole page (`frontend/src/tips.ts`), shown for whichever part carrying `data-tip` the pointer or the keyboard's focus is on. Only cards had this; every other tip was drawn by a stylesheet rule inside its part (`[data-tip]::after`), where a scrolling box could cut it off, a window edge could run through it and a dimmed control made it see-through. That rule and its three per-place overrides are gone, with `CardTip.tsx`.
- **Whole text**: the tip grows to its text up to 320 px, or the window's width less 16 px, then wraps, breaking a long word if it must, at 16 px.
- **Inside the window**, on every side, and gone the moment the pointer or the focus leaves its part. A part inside the Command Center shows its tip inside that dialog, which is drawn over the page.
- **A solid surface**: `--tip-surface` (#10222a, a step lighter than the cards) with an opaque edge, `--tip-edge`. The old surface was the cards' own glass over near-black with a 28 percent edge, so a tip over a card read as part of it.
- **Never over the memory meter or another card's controls.** A card's tip opens over or under its card, whichever edge its part is nearer; it takes the other side when the first is not clear, slides along its card past what is in its way, and over the first card of Tasks may open past the meter. When no place is clear at its full width it is tried again no wider than its part. A tip too tall to be clear anywhere (a 240-character title between two cards) takes the place where it covers least, which is never the meter.
- A part pressed with a mouse or a pen shows no tip until the press is released, so a card being dragged shows none.

### Back on a task's panel

- The panel of anything but the CFO (a queued, running, paused or completed task, or a session on Orchestration) has **Back** in its corner where Close was: a button with a back arrow and its name. It returns the panel to the CFO's panel on the view that panel last showed (Task or Terminal; Task on the Board and Terminal on Orchestration when it has shown neither), keeps a maximized panel maximized, and hands the keyboard back to the card the panel was opened from, or to the panel when the card is hidden behind it.
- The CFO's own panel keeps Close, and so does the panel with nothing chosen.
- Escape outside a terminal does what the corner button does.
- Orchestration's separate "Back to CFO" icon at the panel's other corner is gone: Back replaces it.

README and docs/native-board.md say both.

## Before and after

Pictures of the real board in the browser tests' headless browser, on fixture data, at scale 1.5. They were taken after the merge, when this machine had the memory for a browser, and are kept in `docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4` by PR 296.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The first queued card's tip | ![Before: the tip lies over the memory meter](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/title-tip-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![After: the tip is under its card, on a solid surface, and the meter is clear](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/title-tip-after.jpg?raw=true) |
| A control's tip over a card | ![Before: Pause on the cards' own glass](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/control-tip-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![After: Pause on a solid surface with an edge](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/control-tip-after.jpg?raw=true) |
| A phone: the layout button's tip | ![Before: the tip runs off the window's edge](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/phone-tip-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![After: the tip is inside the window](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/phone-tip-after.jpg?raw=true) |
| A queued task's panel | ![Before: an X in the corner](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/task-panel-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![After: Back, with its arrow](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/blob/41515d88540755bf7e6ab91bd183b22a702c960b/docs/evidence/cg-board-polish-4/task-panel-after.jpg?raw=true) |

## The picture he sent with "encompass full text"

It is not a board tip: it shows the favicon and "Code Goblins" in the system's font, which is the app's own title as Windows or the browser draws it (a taskbar label, a tab or the window's title bar), and its text is whole.
So the rule was applied to every tip the board draws, and the walk below found the ones that broke it.

## What the walk found on main

`tips.spec.ts` points at every part with a tip on the board, the CFO's bar, the top bar, a task's panel, the Command Center and the Orchestration canvas, wide and at phone width, and measures the tip that is drawn. On main (run 37030915858):

- At phone width the layout button's tip ("Stacked layout") and the panel's Close tip left the window.
- In a task's panel at phone width, "Open working-one" (the link to the goblin a task waits on) left the window and was cut off by the panel.
- The first queued card's tip covered the memory meter, side by side and stacked.
- The tip's surface was a translucent gradient with a 28 percent edge.
- The wide walks, the Command Center and Orchestration held on main, and still hold.

The memory meter has no tips of its own.

## In the desktop window

Nothing here depends on a browser: pointer and focus events, a `MutationObserver` and fixed positioning, all of which WebView2 has.
Escape going Back is the board's own key handler; the window's disabled browser keys (F5, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+F, zoom) are not involved.
The Back tests run at 1707 CSS pixels wide at device scale 1.5. I did not open a window; cg-native-desktop-2 runs the in-window suite.

## Red first, then green

This machine had no room for a local browser run, so CI was the browser, on the CFO's word.

- Red: run [37030915858](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/actions/runs/37030915858) on the specs alone: 15 failed, 219 passed. The 15: nine in `panel-back.spec.ts` (all but "the panel with nothing chosen keeps Close"), the two alert tooltip tests in `goblin-alerts.spec.ts`, the teardown walk, and in `tips.spec.ts` the two phone-width walks named above, the two meter tests and the surface test.
- The first red run, [37028286447](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/actions/runs/37028286447), is not the proof: its tips tests failed because my fixture's question opened the Command Center over the board.
- Green before the gate: run [37041854838](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/actions/runs/37041854838) on head 0bf2a4da.
- Green on the final head: run [37054397268](https://github.com/fpresta0607/code-goblins/actions/runs/37054397268) on 6067bcfe, the frontend job with the whole browser suite and every Go shard.
- The meter tests changed after the red run: they first used a 165-character title, and now use the title that was on his screen and the longest the queue held that day. The earlier form failed on main for the same reason (the tip over the meter).

author: deedlefake
body:
## Why

kawa was a single `main` package at the repository root, so background scaling, `-out` parsing, layer surface placement, and text drawing could only be exercised through a running compositor. This moves the compositor into `internal/kawa` behind a small `cmd/kawa` and pulls those four pieces into packages that build without cgo and have their own tests. Runtime behavior does not change.

## Scope

- `cmd/kawa` parses the flags, starts the `PPROF_ADDR` server, calls `wlr.InitLog`, and runs a `kawa.Server`.
- `internal/kawa` is the old `main` package. `Server` has exported `Terms`, `OutputConfigs`, `Background`, and `BackgroundScale` fields and one exported method, `Run(ctx)`, which does not use its context. `Release` and `Shutdown` are now `release` and `shutdown`.
- `internal/bg` replaces `scaleFunc` and `parseScale` with `bg.Scale`, which implements `encoding.TextMarshaler` and `TextUnmarshaler` for `flag.TextVar`. The unused `scaleTile` is gone.

The `-out` strings that panic before also panic now.

author: a13xb0
body:
Independent of the other branches; it applies to `dev` on its own.

## Why

The MQTT page often shows the first companion as Node rather than the one stored, and saving the page then moves the feed to it. On a node with three companions feeding from the second, stock `dev` showed the wrong one on 6 of 10 fresh loads. The stored setting is right until that save.

## Cause

The page defaults Node to the first companion when none is stored, in an effect that runs when the companion list arrives. When the stored MQTT settings and the companion list land in the same render, the effect that applies the stored node and the defaulting effect run in one commit: the second still sees the empty node from before the first was applied, finds companions, and sets the first one, which wins.

## Fix

The default waits for the stored settings and only applies when they name no node. That matches the backend, where an empty node means the first companion.

## Testing

- Instrumented the two effects in the browser and saw the sequence above on each wrong load.
- After the fix, 10 of 10 fresh loads show the stored node (ScotBot, second of three), against 4 of 10 before.
- With no node stored, the page still shows the first companion on every load.
- `./build.sh` (with `tsc -b`) passes.

author: elicasta
body:
LumaRig 0.6.0 consolidates the Cloud backend, portable media/library work, Timeline and Visualizer fixes, controller pairing, live-show preflight, and release hardening into one release candidate directly against `main`.

## Local Media Library
- Native macOS/Windows media registry.
- Managed-copy and reference-in-place import modes.
- Nested logical folders, move/rename/delete-empty-folder operations.
- Missing-file detection and relink while preserving media IDs.
- Scoped native media playback with IndexedDB legacy/browser fallback.
- Heavy file copies and archive work run off the UI thread.

## Portable files
- `.lumarigsong`: one reusable Song Program and only its referenced media.
- `.lumarigshow`: one complete Show snapshot and only its referenced media.
- `.lumarigbackup`: full local program/library backup and referenced media.
- Staged/validated restore before program-state replacement.
- Same package formats on macOS and Windows.
- Import conflicts create separate Song/Show copies instead of silently overwriting different content.

## Visualizer + blackout regression
- Show Creator Preview explicitly takes playback authority from Timeline before rendering.
- Selecting a Creator section no longer recreates the Timeline playback layer.
- Runtime blackout state is tracked independently from delayed physical-DMX polling.
- Blackout buttons use a fail-safe aggregate state: if runtime/native status disagree, the next press resolves toward RELEASE instead of being able to latch another blackout.
- Browser E2E permanently covers the 2.7 stale-Timeline-blackout Creator Preview regression.

## Screen media + NDI/video inputs
- LED/projector screen media has persistent Fit, Size, X, and Y framing plus Reset controls.
- Still images, solid colors, test patterns, Timeline media, and live video inputs share the screen-source model.
- NDI path uses an OS virtual video input / NDI Webcam Input bridge.
- Video-input scan preflights camera permission, avoids surfacing raw WebKit permission text, prefers concrete virtual-camera device IDs, and gives restart/privacy-settings recovery instructions.
- macOS bundle carries camera usage text/entitlement.
- Tauri explicitly handles Camera/Microphone WebView permission requests.
- Permission UI can open macOS Camera Privacy or Windows Webcam Privacy settings.

## Timeline + UI cleanup
- Timeline track height is persistent from 44–140 px.
- Slider and Compact/Normal/Tall presets remain available.
- New direct vertical drag separator resizes all Timeline tracks; keyboard resizing is supported.
- Existing splitter, Cue contextual-menu, long-label and responsive-layout cleanup remains intact.
- Native Visualizer and Video Output windows now share fullscreen behavior.

## Visualizer rendering
- Existing volumetric beam renderer now adds a camera-facing true-cone silhouette so beams remain visible at grazing/side camera angles.
- Surface spill becomes incidence-aware and stretches into an ellipse at shallow beam angles.
- Existing depth-sorted crowd geometry remains, with cached crowd placement to reduce per-frame layout work.
- High/quality render modes keep their existing LOD behavior.

## Show reliability + preflight
- Persisted Show validator now enforces supported collection limits instead of allowing oversized files to bypass editor limits.
- Boundary tests cover 200 cues, 100 Songs, 100 Timeline Shows, and 1000 Timeline clips, and reject the next item past each limit.
- Sanitization caps oversized cue/recording collections.
- Visualizer and Video Output native windows automatically target a secondary display when one is available.
- Native display topology is exposed to the app.
- LIVE > System now has RUN SHOW PREFLIGHT.
- Preflight checks blackout, physical/virtual DMX, missing media, assigned live-video inputs/permissions, display count, Visualizer errors, and Show size.
- Browser E2E covers the preflight panel.

## Shared transport + linking
- TransportEngine and ConnectionManager remain the single authority layer.
- Timeline, Tracks, MIDI, Studio, LumaLive/Ableton and ProPresenter all participate in shared transport ownership.
- ProPresenter local API now parses the official presentation transport time in seconds.
- ProPresenter claims transport only after sustained playhead movement, ignores one-off seeks as play-state evidence, and releases after sustained stillness or explicit pause/rewind.
- ProPresenter UI exposes playhead position and whether LumaRig is FOLLOWING / PAUSED / STANDBY.
- LumaLive remains the Ableton-facing transport bridge.

## LumaRig Cloud account
- Desktop sign-in persists a normal Supabase session without writing the password to LumaRig settings.
- QR / six-digit controller pairing sits behind the signed-in account.
- Every desktop has a stable UUID, Cloud heartbeats, and device/audit metadata.
- Song metadata supports artist, BPM, musical key, arrangement, and notes.
- Online edits sync into reusable Song Library data and matching Songs already inside the active Show.

## Safety / live behavior
- Desktop remains the lighting authority.
- Local saves happen independently of Cloud.
- Cloud/session/network failure does not stop local Show operation or DMX.
- Anonymous paired controllers remain distinct from permanent account users.

## Validation
- Main frontend tests/build and native tests have passed on recent heads.
- Windows x64 frontend tests/build and native Tauri compile have passed on recent heads.
- Browser E2E covers Creator Preview blackout handoff, Visualizer popout state, screen framing, Timeline density, and NDI permission recovery.
- The latest consolidated head is still gated by the current CI run before this draft should be merged.
- Physical second-monitor behavior, real DMX hardware, and multitouch show operation still require real-machine/show testing.

## Canonical Cloud backend
- Canonical Supabase project: `lmldxkukfksfswzbliuy`.
- Cloud Shows/pairing schema and the follow-up hardening migration are applied.
- Security Advisor reports zero security lints.
- Show media storage is private and the required library/device tables are published to Realtime.
- The production controller and online Cloud Library are on the canonical project.
- Existing desktop relay settings that point at the retired `jtvrr...` project migrate automatically.
- Existing controller pairings from the retired project intentionally require one clean re-pair because anonymous Auth identities do not transfer safely between Supabase projects.
- Production account creation/sign-in has been exercised against the canonical backend and the account/device registry is receiving data.

## 0.6.0 release summary
- Canonical LumaRig Cloud account, Cloud Shows, device registry, revision history, and secure controller pairing.
- Portable local media library plus `.lumarigsong`, `.lumarigshow`, and `.lumarigbackup` workflows.
- Show Creator/Timeline reliability fixes, direct rundown Timeline access, persistent track sizing, record/overdub work, and better editing ergonomics.
- Visualizer, screen-media framing, NDI/video-input recovery, fullscreen/output routing, and second-display handling.
- Shared transport across Timeline, Studio/LumaLive/Ableton, MIDI, Tracks, and ProPresenter.
- Live Show Preflight for blackout, DMX, media, video inputs, displays, Visualizer state, and Show limits.
- Release pipeline now uses committed source versions, cross-platform updater serialization, macOS validation, Windows compile validation, and full browser regression gating.

## Release gate
- Candidate version: `0.6.0`, above the current public `0.5.2` updater release.
- Release metadata is now checked for package/Cargo alignment in CI.
- Keep this PR draft only until the current desktop CI is fully green. Physical second-monitor behavior, real DMX hardware, camera/NDI devices, and multitouch show operation remain real-machine validation items rather than merge blockers for the software branch.

body:
## summary
hardens is_safe_next_path against whatwg backslash open redirect vulnerabilities.

previously is_safe_next_path only checked path.startswith("/") and not path.startswith("//"). under whatwg url parsing in modern browsers, backslashes like /\\evil.com or /\\evil.com/path are normalized into protocol-relative urls (//evil.com), causing post-login redirects to navigate to external attacker-controlled origins.

## changes
- hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/request_utils.py: reject paths starting with backslashes, tabs, whitespace, or containing backslashes anywhere in the target string.
- tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_middleware.py: add unit tests and route integration tests verifying protocol-relative and whatwg backslash payloads are rejected.

## verification

- **Bigger touch targets:** the card actions, the signboard ‹ and ✕, the hotspot menu and the hotspot panel's checkboxes are 44 px under a finger.

author: itzkovichyariv-star
body:
This PR is stacked on #42 (the Eilat vacation) and includes its commit. If #42 is merged first, that commit becomes a no-op here.

## What
Yariv approved this design on 2026-10-02, after six rounds of mock-ups.

**The grid**
- **Look:** modeled on Ariel's printed calendar. A white sheet, each day as a separate rounded square, serif dates, and fixed colors in both light and dark themes.

**The fill shows what kind of day it is**
- **Course days:** each of the three courses is a pale tint with a strong colored edge, and its full name is written on the day:
  - מיומנויות ייעוץ
  - פרקטיקום מש״א
  - פרקטיקום ייעוץ
- **No-teaching days:** Ariel's cream, with the name of the day written on it, e.g. חופשת חנוכה, חופשה באילת, חופשת יום העצמאות.
- **Exam windows:** Ariel's gold, labeled מועד א׳ or מועד ב׳.
- **Semester start/end:** a gold line along the top of the day.
- **Special and make-up days:** marked ⏱ and ↻.
- **Simulation:** marked 🎭 and drawn in its course's color.

**One status word at the bottom of the day**
- **להזיז:** red, with a red ring around the day. A class or guest lecture on a day with no teaching.
- **לתאם:** orange. Something still has to be coordinated.
- **ממתין:** orange. A guest lecture that is not approved yet, shown on the lecture day.
- **מאושר:** green. An approved guest lecture.

**לתאם works ahead of time**
- A guest lecture that is still pending raises לתאם **14 days before** it. Once that date has passed, the item shows on today until it is closed.
- The academic dataset's own swap reminders appear on their own dates.
- The day sheet says what has to be coordinated, with phone and email buttons where available.
- Two buttons close an item: **✓ תואם** and **לא צריך יותר**. Both can be undone. The marks are saved in `data.calendarDone`, through a CAS-guarded mutator, so every user sees the same state.

**Conflicts**
- A class that falls on a no-teaching day (20.11, inside the vacation) is listed in the conflict banner.
- The month header counts what needs attention, e.g. "⚠ N להזיז" and "N לתאם".

**Lecture editor**
- Choosing a date with no teaching shows a red warning right away.
- Saving on such a date asks for confirmation first.

**Legend**
- Cut from 17 swatches to 10 entries, plus one line stating the rule.

## Code
- **`src/lib/calendarCell.ts` (new):** a pure module with all the day rules: fill, label, status words, לתאם items, and class conflicts.
- **`src/components/CalendarPage.tsx`:** the new month cell, header counts, לתאם section in the day sheet, and the new legend. The old stripe/band code is removed. The year poster is unchanged.
- **`src/components/LectureEditor.tsx`:** `blockedReason()`, the inline warning and the confirmation on save.
- **`src/lib/supabase.ts`:** the `calendarDone` type.

## Checks
- **`unit/calendar-cell.spec.ts` (new):** 9 tests, one per approved rule. `npm run test:unit` passes, 204/204.
- **`scripts/calendar-check.mjs`:** the 12 checks that tested the old stripe/band design were rewritten to test the new rules with the same intent (readable at 430px, named, conflicts ringed, plain white paper, legend complete, dark mode). Two checks are new: the warning appears when a blocked date is chosen, and saving asks first, with nothing saved if cancelled. Result: 44/44.
- **`node scripts/deploy-gate.mjs --offline`:** passes.
- **Not run:** the full gate, because its numbered suites write to the live project.

## Not in this PR
- Two-way Google Calendar sync. That is planned as the next phase.

author: tokuhirom
body:
Closes #10954

## Problem

`subset S of Str where * eq "x"; sub f(S :$s) {}; f()` ran `f` silently (Rakudo dies). An unpassed optional parameter bound the subset's *own* type object (`S`), which trivially satisfies `S`, so the predicate never ran. The same held for positional `S $s?`, method params, and multi candidates (`multi g(S $s?)` was selected for `g()`; Rakudo reports `X::Multi::NoMatch`). Consequence for MAIN: `sub MAIN(S :$s)` ran instead of printing the usage.

## Fix

- New `Interpreter::omitted_optional_param_value` (`src/runtime/types/omitted_optional.rs`): an omitted optional binds the parameter's *nominal* type object — a subset's refinee (`Str`, `Int` for `UInt`, walking subset-of-subset chains), as Rakudo does in every language version (a `my S $v` variable still holds `S` before 6.e; unchanged).
- `check_omitted_optional_subset` runs the subset predicate against that value. Wired into the sub binder (positional and named omitted branches), the compiled-method fast path (`call_compiled_method_fast`, whose failure cleanup is now one `unwind_fast_bind!` macro shared with the type-mismatch path), and the multi-dispatch candidate check (`args_matching`; a *defaulted* param keeps its old stand-in, since its default is only evaluated at bind time — `multi xz(CAT $x = * <=> *)`, roast `S12-subset/multi-dispatch.t`).
- Rakudo's explanation ("The parameter is optional and was not passed an argument, so its implicit default value was checked …") is appended (`RuntimeError::with_omitted_optional_note`) to subset and `where` failures of an omitted optional — threaded as an explicit `omitted` flag through the `where` checkers, not by message matching.
- The subset constraint-failure message moved into one helper (`subset_constraint_binding_error`) and now spells the value as `.raku` does (`got Str ("a")`, `got Str (Str)`), matching Rakudo and the `where` failure. `got_type_name` absorbed the native-`array` naming of the now-unused `value_type_display_name`.

## Test

`t/types/enum-subset/omitted-optional-subset-implicit-default.t` (19 tests; also passes under `raku`).

## Verification

```
gate-20261002-150600-fjr5: passed (exit 0)
  verdict: pass  profile full  tree 398c03b6e0b7  commit 05e564d1
  checks      pass  65s
  fmt         pass  15s
  lint        pass  387s
  test        pass  1048s
  roast       pass  known-env: 4  350s
```

(A quick-profile run timed out `roast/S06-signature/named-parameters.t` on the *debug* binary — its 1,000,000-call hot loop; on release it passes in 7.5s, so the full gate was run.)

body:
## Problem
In `login_manual`, pdb raises `BdbQuit` on the line traced *after* `breakpoint()` returns — the `return True`, which sat outside the `try/except` meant to catch it. The intended conversion to `FailedLoginError` never fired, so pressing `q` at the prompt tore down the whole `fbscrape login` batch: one dead account killed the run.

## Fix
Move `return True` inside the `try`, so `BdbQuit` is caught and converted to a clean per-account `FailedLoginError` skip.

## Provenance
Written and used on aengus on 2026-08-31 during the account-pool recovery for the seedlist backfills, but it sat on a branch from before the squash (`fix/qc-scraper-bugs`, `70ba466`) that shares no history with `main`. This PR applies that single commit onto current `main`.

author: kkirchheim
body:
## Summary

`utils.oscr_score` had three problems. It was added in 2d53ad8 together with the SSB benchmark.

**1. Ties and interpolation**
- **Bug:** only the scores of known samples were used as thresholds.
  - Where known and unknown samples share a score, the curve jumped to the new FPR first and then climbed vertically. Constant scores gave about 0 instead of accuracy / 2.
  - Between known thresholds, the curve was interpolated linearly instead of being a step function.
- **Fix:** every unique score, known and unknown, is now a threshold.
  - The curve is an exact step function.
  - Ties between known and unknown samples form a diagonal segment, as in the ROC curve (`sklearn.roc_curve`).
  - The paper's definition counts ties pessimistically: CCR with `<`, FPR with `≤` in terms of the outlier score. That would give 0 for constant scores. A code comment documents this deviation.

| Scores (accuracy 0.5) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| constant | 0.00025 | 0.25 |
| 4 discrete levels | 0.179 | 0.249 |
| 2 known / 2 unknown, no ties (hand-computed) | 0.875 | 0.75 |

**2. Docs**
- The claim "a random detector returns roughly the closed-set accuracy" was wrong: it gives about half of it.
- The docstring now defines CCR(τ) and FPR(τ) as formulas.

**3. Attribution**
- OSCR comes from Dhamija, Günther & Boult, *Reducing Network Agnostophobia*, NeurIPS 2018 (arXiv 1811.04110).
- The docstring cited the SSB paper, which only uses the metric.
- The authors' reference code (`Tools/evaluation_tools.py`) only plots the curve. The area as a single number is what later work reports, for example ARPL's `compute_oscr`, which breaks ties by sort position.

**Docs build:** `docs/conf.py` now places and styles the "Examples" section of functions like that of classes: after the parameters, with the same heading style.

## Test plan
- [x] new `OSCRValuesTest`, all failing before the fix except the random-score test:
  - hand-computed step function, ties, constant scores (exactly acc/2), inverted scores (exactly 0);
  - random scores ≈ acc/2;
  - comparison with a direct computation over all thresholds (continuous scores, 3 and 10 levels).
- [x] `pytest`: 391 passed, 27 skipped
- [x] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .`
- [x] `make clean html` (strict); OSCR "Examples" section checked in the built HTML

author: rafaelburlet
body:
`http_request` told the model only "HTTP request timed out after …ms" when a request ran out of time. For a request that changes something, that reads as "did not happen", and sending it again can do it twice — most receivers cannot tell a repeat from a new request.

**What changes** (`src/tools/builtin/http.ts`)
- `httpTimeoutMessage(timeoutMs, method, wallClock, answeredStatus?)`: for any method but GET and HEAD the message adds that the request may still have reached the server and taken effect, and to check the result there before sending it again. If the response headers had already arrived and only the body stalled, it says the server had already answered `<status>` and that the request reached the server.
- The catch decides "timeout" on **which of our own limits fired** (the abort timer or the wall clock), not on the error's name. An abort after the headers arrived ends the body read with a plain `aborted` error — the transport destroys the socket — so the name check passed it through bare, in exactly the case where the request had certainly landed.

**Not covered**: workflow step timeouts and the agent's own per-tool timeout have their own messages (the latter already says the tool may have run). A request whose body fails on its own before the limit is passed through unchanged.

**Tests** — each mutant tsc-clean, each killed by the named test in `http.test.ts` › *a timed-out request that changes something says it may have landed*:

| mutant | killed by |
|---|---|
| decide by `err.name === 'AbortError'` (the old check) | a POST whose response body stalls after the headers says it reached the server |
| any error after the headers counts as a timeout | a body that fails on its own before the limit is not reported as a timeout |
| an `aborted` message counts as a timeout | the same |
| no warning | the message test, and the three POST timeout tests |
| warning on GET too | the message test; a GET that times out does not |
| abort timer not marked | a POST that is aborted at its timeout; the stall test; the GET test |
| wall clock not marked | a POST that outlives its abort (the wall clock) |
| method not upper-cased | the message test |
| answered status not kept | the stall test |

**Process note:** the first commit (`fc477162`) was pushed after a full-suite run that had one failure: `tests/security/agent-security.test.ts` › *no eval() or new Function()* timed out at 10 s under full load — the commit chain did not stop on it. body:
Allows a founder to replace an existing worker credential without changing its attested identity. Rotation consumes an exact, single-use approval and atomically stores only the new token digest and issuance ID. Only the winning request receives the secret. Prior credentials stop authenticating; issuance-bound replay keys and leases prevent stale claims, reports and defects from crossing rotation. External operations reauthorize the presented token before their effects.

The CLI guide documents all eight scoped fleet commands, ephemeral worker credentials and bounded retries while preserving public commands and proxy setup.

Refs JOV-7393.

## B-682 — « En pause » cards touch each other

**Mechanism.** Every list gets its card spacing from `section = "sec flex flex-col gap-4"`, the cards' direct parent. The « En pause » fold (and « Mis de côté » in « À traiter ») draws its cards inside a `<details>` through a bare `Markup`: no flex column, so no gap — 0 px against 8 px.

**Fix.** `foldedCards` (`ui/variants/layout.ts`) spends the section's own gap (`gap-4`, header to first card and card to card); both folds use it. No new value.

**Family.** The two folds of the app that hold cards: « En pause », « Mis de côté ».

## B-683 — the last card scrolls under the « + »

**Mechanism.** The « + » is 52 px, 16 px above the bar; `#port` ended 32 px above the bar (14 px port padding + 18 px body padding). At full scroll the last card ended 36 px under the button.

**Fix.** The button's size and offset become tokens (`--mq-fab-size`, `--mq-fab-offset`, `theme.css`); the button is drawn from them, and while it is shown (`:root:has(#fab:not([hidden]))`, `base.css`) `#port` gains `--tm-fab-clearance` = size + offset + the catalogue's gap (`index.html`). Hidden button ⇒ no extra space.

**Family.** The « + » exists on the one page `acq` only — Suivis, À traiter, En cours. No other page has a floating action button (Découvrir has none).

§5 (Acquisitions), §6 (Disponibilité des actions — « Résoudre » reachable without hitting the « + »), §12 (Mobile first).

author: brunofurmon
body:
## Problema

No Maestro, quem escolhe um modelo no composer (Pro, Ultra ou um modelo adicional como `gpt-6.1-sol`) recebia a resposta do **ONE Smart** sempre que o turno tinha anexo. Em produção, nos últimos 7 dias, 5.635 turnos chegaram ao pod com um tier diferente do Smart e só 4.808 foram roteados: cerca de 830 (~15%) rodaram no modelo principal contra a escolha do usuário.

Evidência dos dois relatos (MST-221): o pod registra `Applying model tier tier=gpt-6.1-sol` nos turnos com anexo, mas nunca `Model tier routing selected model`. No Hulk, essas chamadas aparecem no alias `maestro-flash`. Nos turnos sem anexo da mesma conversa o roteamento acontece normalmente.

## Causa

`routeModelTierTurn` desistia de qualquer turno com `len(ts.media) > 0`, supondo que o `routeMediaTurn` já tinha trocado o turno para o modelo de visão. Em produção essa troca quase nunca acontece:

- **imagem** vai por `delegateMediaTurn`, uma sub-chamada de visão que vira texto e não troca o modelo;
- **documento** (pdf/docx/xlsx) nunca vai para a visão, por desenho (`messagesContainCurrentTurnMediaTurn`).

Nos dois casos o tier caía e o turno seguia no modelo principal.

## Mudança

- `routeMediaTurn` passa a informar se **esta chamada** leva mídia visual. Uma chamada assim fica onde ele a colocou: no modelo de visão ou, sem modelo de visão configurado, no principal, o único que a config trata como capaz de ver imagem. Sem modelo de visão, a chamada volta ao principal partindo de qualquer modelo ativo: o leve, ou o tier que uma chamada anterior do turno escolheu. O tier só vale nas outras chamadas. A decisão é por chamada, e não pelo modelo ativo, porque `exec.activeCandidates` sobra da chamada anterior.
- Exceção: quando a visão acabou de **recusar** a imagem da chamada (`delegateMediaTurn` agora diz se pulou, delegou ou falhou), o tier assume, como antes. Em prod o `maestro-vision` responde 400 `Provided image is not valid` a screenshots de ferramenta (1.662 sub-chamadas em 7 dias); mandar a mesma imagem para o mesmo modelo só repete a recusa e encerra o turno, enquanto o `maestro-flash` segue com ela (Hulk `pc-cb0f3c777f3c75670885549e`, `succeeded`). Sem tier escolhido, a troca para a visão continua sendo o fallback.
- Quando o tier assume, a janela de contexto da visão (`effectiveContextWindow`) deixa de valer.
- O bloco de roteamento do `CallLLM` (delegação → visão → cron → tier) vira `routeTurnModel`, para os testes exercitarem a mesma ordem do pipeline. A extração não muda a ordem nem os retornos de erro.

## Testes

`pkg/agent/llm_model_tier_test.go`, todos passando pela sequência real (`routeTurnModel`):

| Cenário | Esperado | Antes |
|---|---|---|
| documento anexado | tier escolhido | `maestro-flash` ❌ |
| imagem delegada | tier escolhido | `maestro-flash` ❌ |
| imagem sem delegação (troca para visão) | visão | ✅ |
| visão recusa a imagem na delegação, com tier | tier escolhido, janela de contexto zerada | ✅ (a 3ª versão do fix deixava na visão e o turno terminava em erro; review do @donwellus) |
| visão recusa a imagem na delegação, sem tier | visão (fallback de antes) | ✅ |
| chamada 1 na visão (imagem ainda só como path), chamada 2 com a imagem descrita | tier, janela de contexto zerada | (falhava na 1ª versão do fix) |
| imagem carregada por ferramenta, sem anexo do usuário | visão | o tier tirava da visão ❌ |
| `image_model` igual ao modelo principal, turno de texto | tier escolhido | (falhava na 1ª versão do fix) |
| imagem sem modelo de visão configurado (direto, via bypass do modelo leve, ou vinda do tier de uma chamada anterior) | modelo principal | (a 2ª versão do fix levava ao tier, review do @nickgs1337; a 4ª deixava no tier herdado, review do Devin) |

`go test ./pkg/agent/` completo passa (75 s); `go vet` e golangci-lint v2.10.1 sem achados novos. Numa rodada com `-shuffle=on` caiu `TestEvolutionBridge_TurnEndUsesExplicitAttemptTrail` (`TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: directory not empty`). É flake que já existe: o mesmo grupo de testes falhou 1 em 30 rodadas na `main`.

## Notas

- **Imagem crua no tier**: quando a visão recusa a imagem (ou só parte delas, na delegação parcial, que devolve `delegationDone`), a imagem segue como `data:` para o tier. Num tier sem visão o turno aborta com `does not support image input`. Isso já acontecia na base com imagem de ferramenta; com anexo do usuário a base deixava a chamada na visão, que recusava a mesma imagem de novo. No `maestro-flash` de prod a chamada com a imagem termina com sucesso (Hulk), e o Datadog não tem nenhum `does not support image input` nos últimos 7 dias.
- **Janela de contexto por tier**: `turnContextWindow` não tem valor por tier. Turnos com documento (leituras grandes por ferramenta) agora rodam no tier com o orçamento do modelo principal, igual aos turnos de texto com tier já faziam.

O bump do submódulo e o selo do tier ao vivo vão num PR do curling-products.

body:
## Summary
- introduce versioned `visualPlan` and `visualSpec` schemas while keeping legacy packages valid
- add trusted template, style-profile, and simulation-model registries
- add deterministic anti-hallucination validation for IDs, references, graph axes/series, control ranges, trusted simulation models, grounding, and fallback
- separate render strategies into deterministic, deterministic simulation, Gemini-generated contextual/base art with deterministic overlays, and non-answer-critical Gemini illustration
- require final multimodal audit for generated-image paths and explicit broader grounding policy before search grounding
- add a provider-neutral independent physics-verifier contract suitable for Wolfram or another approved verifier
- document Replit as development-time simulation-template incubation only, not a learner/runtime dependency
- preserve the current Stage-0 18-activity package and existing generation behavior until later visual-generation integration PRs

## Tool-orchestration design
Production roles are intentionally separated:
- Gemini: content/visual planning, optional image-capable aesthetic generation, final multimodal audit
- trusted repository renderer/simulation engine: answer-critical vectors, axes, graphs, labels, geometry, state changes, and interactions
- Wolfram/equivalent verifier: independent symbolic/numerical physics checks
- Replit/equivalent app builder: prototype new simulation primitives before promotion into tested repository code
- Canva/Figma/canvas-style tools: optional design-system exploration, never scientific authority

## Validation
- repository lint: passed
- content validation: passed (16 packages)
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Python: 380 tests passed, 1 skipped
- JS player tests: all passed (loading, rendering, interaction modes, activity deep links, player controls)

author: bossdale
body:
## Summary

**UROLENS-248**: *(Mobile) Backend - View and Manage Notifications*. This is the mobile backend part of story **UROLENS-168** (View and Manage Notifications). The other parts are UROLENS-173 (mobile FE), UROLENS-249 (web FE) and UROLENS-250 (web BE).

The story is the same for every role. Its requirements:
- an unread badge
- a preview of recent notifications
- mark all read
- opening a notification marks it read and goes to what it's about
- a full page showing everything
- an unread-only filter

The backend already had list, mark read and mark all read, but:
- **No unread count.** The apps could only count the 50 notifications they had loaded.
- **No paging or filter.** The list stopped at 50, so older notifications couldn't be reached, and it couldn't be filtered to unread.
- **"Returned for correction" never notified the MedTech.** The app has supported `RESULT_RETURNED` (icon, title, tap to open the sample) for a while, but the backend never sent it.
- **A shared phone got the previous user's pushes.** The push token was never cleared, not on logout and not when someone else signed in on that phone.
- **Pushes went out before the commit,** one at a time with a 5 s timeout each. A request could wait on Expo, and a rolled-back action could still be announced. A failed notification insert also broke the caller's transaction.

## Changes

### Unread badge: `GET /notifications/unread-count`
Returns `{"unreadCount": n}`, counting every unread notification of the caller's. New route; the route count goes from 52 to 53.

### Preview, full page and unread filter: `GET /notifications`
New optional query parameters:
- **`limit`** (1–100): a few for the bell's preview, a page for the full list.
- **`before`** (a notification ID): returns the ones older than it, for loading the next page. The ID breaks ties between notifications created in the same instant, so a page never skips or repeats one. Paging from someone else's notification gives 404 `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND`.
- **`unreadOnly`**: only notifications not yet read.

With no parameters it returns **the same 50-newest plain list as before**, so existing clients are unaffected (including the web's unmerged `feature/notifications` branch).

### Marking read
- Mark one read now answers **404 `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND`** (was the generic `NOT_FOUND`) for a notification that doesn't exist or isn't the caller's.
- Mark all read is unchanged.
- The query logic moved out of the router into `services/user_notifications_service.py`. Every query stays scoped to the caller's own user ID, for every role.

### Returned results notify the MedTech
`ResultReviewService.returnResult` now sends `RESULT_RETURNED`: *"Result for sample SMP-… was returned for correction."*
- **Who gets it:** the specimen's assigned MedTech, or whoever confirmed the result if the specimen has none. (`AnalysisResult.medtechId` is never written anywhere, so it can't be used.)
- **No reason in the message:** pushes show on the lock screen. The app already gets the reason through sync (UROLENS-225).
- **Same transaction** as the status change. If another supervisor action wins the race, nobody is notified.

### Pushes go out after the commit
- `notify` queues the push on the session. A session `after_commit` hook sends everything queued **in one request, in the background**, so no request waits on Expo. A rollback drops the queue, so nothing is announced that didn't happen.
- The notification insert runs in a **savepoint**. A failed insert is logged and rolled back alone, and the caller's action still goes through.
- The push data adds **`notification_id`**, so the app can mark a notification read when its push is tapped.
- A failed send is logged with the message count only, never the token or the text.

### One device, one user's pushes
- `POST /users/push-token` removes the token from anyone else who had it, so a shared phone stops getting the previous user's notifications. It now accepts only an Expo token (`ExponentPushToken[…]` / `ExpoPushToken[…]`, at most 255 characters); anything else is 422.
- **A manual logout clears the user's token.** This is best effort: logout still succeeds if clearing fails. An inactivity sign-out doesn't clear it (a decision for this ticket).

**No migration.** Out of scope per UROLENS-168: deleting a notification, and choosing which events notify.

## Who is affected

| | Impact |
|---|---|
| Mobile (UROLENS-173) | No break. To pick up: `unread-count` for the badge, `limit`/`before`/`unreadOnly` for the preview and full page, mark read on a push tap using `data.notification_id`, and a "mark all read" button. `RESULT_RETURNED` now arrives. |
| Web (UROLENS-249/250) | No break. The same endpoints serve every role (heads-up posted on UROLENS-250). |
| Every role | No break. Default list unchanged; the only new error code is `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND`. |

## Merge notes
- **#83 (UROLENS-245)** also changes `POST /auth/logout` and `changelog.md`, so a conflict is expected there (checked with a dry-run merge). Resolve it so the push token is cleared on a **plain logout only, not on `reason: "INACTIVITY"`**. #83's `tests/integration/test_session_timeout.py` client will also need `standInDb()` from `test_auth_login`, because logout now uses the database session.
- **#77** overlaps in `returnResult` / `api/results.py`. This PR covers its returned-result notification with the fixes from the review comment there.

## Tests
- **`tests/integration/test_notifications_http.py` (22 tests):** through the real routes, with each statement compiled and checked. Covers:
  - the default list stays plain and scoped to the caller
  - the preview (`limit`, `unreadOnly`)
  - paging (`before`, and someone else's cursor gives 404)
  - limit bounds (422)
  - the unread count for every role, and signed-out callers are refused
  - mark read, and someone else's notification is a 404 with nothing committed
  - mark all read is scoped
  - registering a token takes it from others; only Expo tokens are accepted
  - logout clears the token, and logout still works if clearing fails
- **`tests/test_notification_service.py` (+7):** on a real `AsyncSession` with its statements mocked:
  - nothing is sent before the commit
  - one request carries everything queued in a transaction
  - a rollback sends nothing, even after a later commit
  - users without an Expo token get no push
  - a failed insert never raises
  - a failed send is logged without the token or message
  - the returned-result wording
- **`tests/test_result_review_service.py` (+5):** the specimen's MedTech is notified without the reason; the fallback to whoever confirmed it; no MedTech means no notification; a lost race notifies nobody; the route wires in the request's notifier.
- **Updated fixtures:** the logout tests now use a database stand-in instead of silently hitting the "refuse the real database" guard. The supervisor race test overrides the notifier.

**Mutation check:** 35 deliberate breaks of the new logic, each caught by the tests. Among them:
- pushing before the commit
- no rollback handling
- no savepoint
- `notification_id` dropped from the push data
- any of the queries not scoped to the caller
- the unread filter, cursor or limit ignored
- the wrong error code
- the token not taken from others, or cleared from the caller too
- logout not clearing the token
- token validation off
- notifying before the status change, or through the dead `medtechId` column

**Checks:** Python 3.13 with CI's environment: 773 passed. ruff clean; check_naming at its baseline of 9; one Alembic head (0045); OpenAPI valid, 53 routes. D/ANN findings in the touched files went down (36 → 30).

author: diegonvs
body:
## Problem

When a calendar is unpublished in Contentful, its published events still link to it. The Delivery API resolves that link to `calendar: null`, and `parseGraphQLEvent` threw `Event (<id>) doesn't have a calendar`. One such event breaks everything that lists it:

- `algolia-sync-production-crn` has failed on every merge to master since 30/09. `verify-production` and `master-pipeline-success` are skipped; deploys are not affected.
- The event detail page fails to load.
- The user/team/group event indexers fail for any list that includes the event.

It started when the client unpublished the "Spatial Transcriptomics WG" calendar, which 3 past events (2023–2024) still point to. Fixing that content is being handled with the client separately; this PR makes the code tolerate it the next time a calendar is unpublished.

## Fix

**Skip events without a calendar.** This follows the pattern GP2 has used since #3183:
- `parseGraphQLEvent` returns `null` when the event has no calendar.
- Lists drop those events and keep the Contentful `total`.
- `fetchById` returns `null`, so the API answers 404 and `indexEventHandler` removes the event from Algolia.
- `EventDataObject.calendar` stays required.

**Guard the Google Calendar sync.** `fetchByGoogleId` reuses the event list, so a skipped match would read as "no event" and the sync would create a duplicate. It now throws when the list reports a match (`total > 0`) but returns no item. The sync already catches errors per event, so this case keeps today's behaviour: a logged error and no write to Contentful.

**Alert on skipped events.** Each skipped event id is logged and sent to Sentry through an optional `Alerts` dependency, following `ReminderContentfulDataProvider`. It is wired in `app.ts` (API) and `getEventDataProvider` (indexers, Google sync, export script). This is a separate commit, so it can be dropped if we prefer to skip these events silently, as GP2 does.

`export-entity.ts` needs no change. Contentful returns `total: 0` once `skip` passes the end of the collection, so the export loop still ends when events are skipped.

## How to test

Unit tests cover the null parser result, the list filter, `fetchById` returning null, the alerts and the `fetchByGoogleId` guard. The Google Calendar guard can't be exercised end to end without a linked Google calendar.

End to end, in the dedicated environment (`crn-create-environment` label):

1. In the PR's Contentful environment, unpublish a calendar that has published events, and note those events (the calendar's "Incoming links").
2. Open one of those events on the PR frontend: the page shows "Not found" instead of an error.
3. Run the **Sync CRN Algolia** workflow from this branch with `environment-name: Branch`, this PR's number and its Contentful environment id: the sync passes.
   - Optional control: run the same workflow from `master`. It fails with `Event (<id>) doesn't have a calendar`.
4. Reload the events list: those events are gone. They only leave the list after step 3, because the branch index is a copy of Development's and unpublishing a calendar doesn't reindex its events.

After merge, `algolia-sync-production-crn` should pass, `verify-production` and `master-pipeline-success` should run again, and the 3 affected events should no longer be in the index.

author: tochi-mba
body:
## What this does

keyring now reads four more of a person's `keyring` settings from settings-api, and acts on them:

| Setting | What keyring does with it |
| --- | --- |
| `require_reauth_for_credential_changes` | When on, adding, replacing or removing a stored credential (and starting the OAuth consent that will store one) needs the account password again, as `current_password`. A service cannot supply it, so the delegated routes return 403 for that person. The entry *refuses* rather than falling back. While settings-api cannot say whether it is on, a change without the password returns 503. A change with the right password goes ahead, because the right password satisfies the setting either way. Logins never read it. |
| `notify_on_credential_change` | When on, the owner gets an email after a credential is added, replaced or removed, whether by their session, a service, an OAuth callback or an administrator. The email says what kind of change, when and by whom. It never says which credential, never includes any part of one, and has no link. |
| `notify_on_new_session` | When on, every login sends an email with the time and nothing else: no token, no session id. |
| `email_notifications` | The master switch over both notices. Invites and password resets are not covered. |

Someone who has chosen nothing gets exactly what keyring did before: no notices and no second password prompt. **This depends on a settings-api catalogue change:** the three subordinate entries currently default to `true` there, and need to default to `false`. That change is described for the catalogue owner and is not part of this PR.

## Re-authentication cannot be bypassed

- **Service tokens.** The person-facing routes accept only a session, and the delegated routes have no field for a password. Both cases are tested with a service sending its tokens *and* a password.
- **Admin routes.** An administrator deleting *their own* profile through `delete_account_profile` is held to their own setting. Before this, a stolen owner session could remove credentials through that route with no password. The route returns 403 and points to `delete_profile`.
- **Wrong passwords.** A password that is sent is always checked. A wrong one counts toward the account lockout, just like a failed login.
- **Test coverage.** Every route that adds, replaces or removes a credential is tested with the setting on, off and unknowable (settings-api down), with the right password, a wrong one and none. Each test checks that a refused change leaves the vault unchanged.

The decision record is [ADR-0014](docs/adr/0014-reauthentication-per-request.md): the password is checked on each request, not through a "sudo window".

## Also

- settings-client moves from v0.1.0 to v0.4.1. Every `keyring` key is account-scoped, so the resolve names no profile, and a test asserts that.
- `CredentialService.complete_authorization` is split into `redeem_authorization` and `finish_authorization`. This lets the callback read the person's settings before it exchanges the code. If settings-api refuses keyring at the callback, nothing is stored.

## Checks

ruff format, ruff check, mypy --strict and import-linter all pass locally. I ran only the test files that cover the changed code; CI runs the full suite with the 100% branch-coverage gate.

## Cambio
La mínima de losas era máx(0,04·e·fcd/fyd ; 1,8 ‰·e), de la **EHE‑08** (art. 42.3). El **Anejo 19, art. 9.3.1.1 (1), pág. 146** aplica a losas el mínimo de vigas, **ec. (9.1)**, por metro:

As,min = e·fctm,fl / (4,8·fyd), con fctm,fl = máx{(1,6 − h/1000)·fctm; fctm} (ec. 3.23).

**En losas finas sube**: con e = 0,15 m, de 2,76 a **3,02 cm²/m** (fctm,fl = 1,45·fctm).

- Fórmula en `lib/calc/hormigon/comun/cuantias.ts`, compartida por vigas y losas.
- `ResultadoLosa` y `ResultadoDireccionLosa`: `asMinMecanicoCm2PorM` y `asMinGeometricoCm2PorM` → `asMinCm2PorM` (+ `fctmFlMPa`).
- La tarjeta de cada dirección muestra As,min con su cita.

## Test plan
- [x] Test de mínimos reescrito con el cálculo a mano (3,01866 cm²/m); el resto de la planilla no cambia (gobierna la armadura por momento).
- [x] `npm run test`: 1054. `npm run lint` y `tsc --noEmit` pasan.
- [x] Navegador, pestaña limpia: 3,02 cm²/m en las cuatro direcciones, sin «geométrico» ni «NaN», consola sin errores.

## Encontrado, para otras PR
- **Anclaje** en `losa.ts`: `lb = máx(1,4·1,2·Ø², fyk·Ø/14)` es de la EHE‑08 (art. 69).
- Falta el **límite de μ** (como en vigas).
- Falta el **empotramiento parcial** del art. 9.3.1.2 (2): armadura superior para el 25 % del momento del vano (15 % en apoyos extremos).

author: logan-kelsch
body:
## Summary
- add GP-only `bool_mat_ident` for 2D Boolean genes
- assign deterministic first-seen scalar int64 IDs to exact matrix patterns across training samples
- accept generation only for proper partial groupings: `1 < unique IDs < sample count`
- register `inv_bool_mat_ident` as a non-reconstructive NULL inverse
- export the new operation/inverse and document it
- add generation, constraint, dtype/dimension, GP-only, registry, and inverse tests

## Semantics
For source patterns:

```
[A, A, B, C, B]
```

the generated scalar gene is:

```
[0, 0, 1, 2, 1]
```

The operation is rejected when all samples share one pattern or when every sample has a unique pattern.

Pattern identity is exact and includes matrix shape. IDs are assigned in first-seen order.

## Proof category
`partition="null"`: the identity-class scalar is useful forward GP information but cannot reconstruct the source matrix. The inverse is therefore registered with `reconstructive=False`.

author: whysosuresh
body:
## Summary

Every gate job that builds the product's images or starts its stack now pulls Docker Hub images through Google's public mirror (`mirror.gcr.io`), with Docker Hub as the fallback. A Docker Hub outage can no longer fail such a job before a test runs. A static check and a run-time check refuse a job that goes back to pulling from Hub alone.

## Context

#1705: during #1701's `Gate`, `auth.docker.io/token` answered 500. `upgrade-rehearsal / Rehearse compose` then failed in `docker compose build` ("failed to resolve source metadata for docker.io/library/golang:1.25-bookworm") on a change that touched none of it. In the merge queue, that ejects a change that broke nothing.

Every gate job that pulls an image pulls anonymously from Docker Hub alone:
- the compose, all-in-one, Helm (kind) and upgrade-rehearsal lanes;
- the server's image smokes;
- five service or job containers.

Over the 343 `ci.gate.yaml` runs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02, Docker Hub failed one job: #1705's. The rate is low. But one Hub outage of a few minutes would fail every one of these jobs at once.

## Changes

- **`.github/actions/docker-hub-mirror`** merges `registry-mirrors: ["https://mirror.gcr.io"]` into `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, keeping the runner's other keys. It reloads dockerd with SIGHUP (the pid from `/var/run/docker.pid`) and waits, bounded at 30 s, until `docker info` lists the mirror. Otherwise it fails, named, once. It never restarts dockerd: Server Gate's Postgres service container, which its image smoke reaches, would die with it.
- **The seven jobs that pull through dockerd** call it right after the root `npm ci`, before any step that runs `docker` or `kind`: compose-gate, smoke-amd64, smoke-arm64, kind-gate, `rehearse`, `server`, `server-linux-arm64`.
- **The five service and job containers** name `mirror.gcr.io/library/postgres:16` and `mirror.gcr.io/library/ubuntu:24.04`. GitHub pulls them before any step, so no step can give that pull a mirror.
- **`test/install/lib/docker-hub-mirror.mjs`**, the install layer's side:
  - **Gate refusal:** in the gate (`STIGMER_TEST_GATE=1` on GitHub Actions), a pull with no mirror listed is refused, naming the action. The release runs these scripts without the flag, and a developer's machine is not Actions, so neither is refused.
  - **Base images before a build:** BuildKit takes mirrors only when dockerd starts, not on reload (measured below). So before each source build the install layer pulls the build's base images through dockerd. It reads them from the Dockerfiles: `FROM`, `COPY --from` and `RUN --mount … from=`, not the file's own stages. A reference built from an `ARG` is refused. Compose's Dockerfiles come from `docker compose config --format json`, the overlay's own answer.
  - **kind:** its nodes get dockerd's mirrors through containerd's `config_path` and a mounted `docker.io/hosts.toml` (each mirror, then Docker Hub as `server`), the mechanism kind's own registry example uses. With no mirror listed, `kind create cluster` runs exactly as before.
- **`scripts/ci-images.mjs`** judges every workflow the merge queue waits on (`scripts/ci-timeouts.mjs`'s set). It refuses:
  - a service or job container naming a Docker Hub image, or an expression;
  - a step that runs `docker` or `kind` before the job calls the action.
- **`scripts/lane-triggers.test.mjs`:** the still-finds pin gains the new action's body.

## Implementation notes

- **Why Google's mirror, not a copy under `ghcr.io/stigmer/`:** dockerd takes a Docker Hub mirror only as a bare host. Our own copy (#334's shape) could only be reached by rewriting every reference, including those in the previous release's compose file and chart, which the upgrade rehearsals install first.
- **What the mirror serves:** every image the gate pulls, for amd64 and arm64, at Docker Hub's digests (checked on 2026-10-02 for each tag, and for kind v0.24.0's pinned node digest). AWS's public copy lacks `temporalio/auto-setup`.
- **Image names are unchanged:** a daemon or containerd mirror serves `postgres:16` as `postgres:16`, so what users install is what the gate runs. The compose file, chart and Dockerfiles users get are untouched.
- **What reaches BuildKit:** a SIGHUP reload reaches `docker pull`, `docker run` and `compose up`, but not BuildKit. Neither does a `hosts.toml` under `/etc/docker/certs.d` written after start. That is why base images are pulled first rather than dockerd restarted.
- **No retries anywhere:** the action either sees the mirror within its deadline or fails, once.

## Breaking changes

None. Outside the gate, the install scripts behave as before unless the developer's own Docker lists a mirror, in which case kind follows it too.

## Test plan

On Node 22.22.1 (`.nvmrc`):
- `npm run test:scripts`: `# tests 677` / `# pass 673` / `# fail 0` / `# skipped 4`. The 4 skips are the Linux-only apt-cache cases, on macOS.
- New suites: the action's 9 cases (a fake dockerd re-reads `daemon.json` on SIGHUP), the install layer's 12, `ci-images`' 8, and one `install-compose` case.
- `make lint-workflows`: "No findings to report. Good job! (4 ignored, 256 suppressed)".
- `node scripts/test-integrity.mjs --base origin/main`: "1666 test file(s) read, compared with origin/main (04f24b2ae); clean".

Red first for the static check, each restored after:
- a service reference back to `postgres:16`;
- `docker pull alpine` before the action;
- the action moved below kind-gate's `kind version` step.

Each failed, naming the workflow, job and fix; restored, `# pass 8`.

Red first for the run-time check: `buildSourceImages` under `STIGMER_TEST_GATE=1 GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, against a Docker with no mirror, refused with "this job pulls from Docker Hub with no mirror; call ./.github/actions/docker-hub-mirror first".

The outage, reproduced in `docker:28.0.4-dind` (the runners' Docker version), with `registry-1.docker.io`, `auth.docker.io`, `index.docker.io` and `production.cloudflare.docker.com` at `0.0.0.0`:
- **Before the action:** `FROM node:22-slim` plus `COPY --from=golang:1.25-bookworm` failed with "failed to resolve source metadata for docker.io/library/golang:1.25-bookworm", and `docker pull postgres:16` was refused.
- **After the action** ("docker-hub-mirror: dockerd lists https://mirror.gcr.io, then Docker Hub"):
  - `docker pull postgres:16` and `docker run temporalio/auto-setup:1.28.0` passed;
  - a container started before the reload kept its pid;
  - dockerd's pid was unchanged.
  - The build still failed, which is the BuildKit finding above.
- **After `pullBaseImages`** over the Dockerfiles compose reported plus the all-in-one one: it pulled `node:22-slim, debian:bookworm-slim, golang:1.25-bookworm`, and the same BuildKit build passed with Hub down.
- **kind v0.24.0 in the same daemon, with the Hub names also blackholed inside the node:**
  - a cluster created with `kindMirrorArgs` ran `postgres:16` to `Running`, as `docker.io/library/postgres:16`;
  - a cluster created without it stayed in `ImagePullBackOff` ("failed to resolve reference docker.io/library/postgres:16").

This PR edits `.github/actions/`, so its own `Gate` runs every lane. Every Docker job's log should show the action's "dockerd lists" line, and each lane should pass.

## Risks

- **If `mirror.gcr.io` serves a tag late after a re-push:** the gate builds on a slightly older base for a while, as a user's floating tag can.
- **If the mirror is down:** dockerd and containerd fall back to Docker Hub, except for the five service and job containers, which name the mirror directly.
- **Roll back** by reverting this PR. Nothing outside CI and the install scripts reads these files.

Closes #1705

author: thomashendrickx
body:
Part of #85 (A2). Stacked on #88.

## What
- **`fleet.follow({ afterSeq?, max?, waitSeconds? })`** needs `fleet:read`. It is a query, also served as `POST /api/v1/fleet/follow` and as the MCP tool `fleet_follow`. It answers `{ events, lastSeq }`:
  - the events after `afterSeq`, oldest first, up to `max` (1 to 100, default 100);
  - events in the console's live shape (seq, type, time, actor, ship, message, delivery), never their details, as decided;
  - passing `lastSeq` as the next `afterSeq` misses nothing across reconnects. The numbers are the commit-ordered ones the console's live stream uses.
- **Without `afterSeq`** it answers no events and the current `lastSeq`, the place to start from.
- **With `waitSeconds`** (0 to 25) and nothing after the position, it waits on the fleet's event wake-ups and answers as soon as an event commits. It starts watching before it reads a second time, so an event committed in between is answered. A stopping server ends the wait as if its time had passed.
- **Core:** use case `followFleet` in `core/shared`, with a new port `FleetEventWakeups`. The Prisma adapter's existing wake-up hub, which already drives the console's WebSocket, is adapted to that port (`fleetEventWakeupsOf`) and wired in `app.ts`.
- **Docs:** architecture, server, REST and MCP READMEs, decision 0004's list.

## Tests
- Common: input bounds and the output shape.
- Core (`follow-fleet.test.ts`): the start position, events and lastSeq, paging by max, no wait by default, waiting the full time, waking on a commit, refusals for bad max or wait.
- API: a `fleet:read` ship's follow wakes as soon as argo commissions a ship (about 0.5 s of a 20 s wait); refused without `fleet:read`.
- REST and MCP: the start position, then the events after it; the route and tool lists.

## Summary

Make the app look and behave like a desktop application. The spec and the plan are in `docs/superpowers/`.

- **Tokens and theme** (`src/styles/tokens.scss`): all colors, sizes and shadows are CSS custom properties. The theme setting is System, Light or Dark. The main process sets `nativeTheme`, so the menus, the dialogs and the window buttons match. The editor themes come from the same tokens.
- **Window**: hidden title bar (`hiddenInset` with vibrancy on macOS, `titleBarOverlay` on Windows and Linux), default size 1280×800, minimum size 960×600. The saved bounds must be on a connected display. Windows and Linux get a menu button in the title bar.
- **Menu and shortcuts**: the menu changes with the page. It has Undo and Redo, Save, Export, Copy HTML, Send, Beautify, Find, the preview sizes, the sidebar and preview toggles and the theme. A command registry connects the menu items to the page handlers. The file list, the project cards and the Export and More buttons use native context menus.
- **Project page**: one title bar row (breadcrumb, Desktop/Mobile, Send, Export, More, Settings) replaces the toolbar with more than ten buttons. The files sidebar has file icons, the keyboard (arrows, F2, Cmd+Backspace) and a context menu (Rename, Duplicate, Reveal, Move to Trash). The sidebar and the preview can collapse. A new status bar shows the MJML errors (a click goes to the first error), the render time, the engine and the cursor position.
- **Home page**: cards with the folder and the last modified time, a sort (Last opened, Name, Last modified), Finder-style selection with the export actions, a context menu and an empty state.
- **Dialogs**: one dialog style with a header and a footer, a focus trap, focus back to the opener, Enter for the main action from a text field, and only the top dialog handles the keys. The Settings dialog has sections and a new Appearance section. Alerts are toasts above the status bar.
- **Tests**: Vitest for the new pure modules (theme, window bounds, menu template, popup menu, commands, shortcuts, files, projects, layout, modal keys) and reducers (168 tests).
- **Dependency**: `@lezer/highlight` is now a direct dev dependency (it was already installed by `@codemirror/language`).

## Review

A fresh reviewer checked the whole branch: no critical issue. The last commit fixes the important issues: Ctrl+W on Windows and Linux, the project time, the keys of stacked dialogs, Enter on tabs and radios, and the menu on Windows and Linux.

Known small issues, not fixed in this PR:

- Enter in the error dialog opens GitHub.
- With "Also move the folder to the trash" checked, Enter removes the project and moves the folder to the trash.
- The project context menu acts on one card, not on the whole selection.
- At 960 px on Windows with auto-save off, the right side of the title bar can overflow.
- Rename accepts an empty name or a name with `/`.

author: enjay27
body:
## Bug (seen on the first tracked runs)
- The NAS's MinIO endpoint was wrong, so the `train_stdout.log` upload timed out. The sender stops at the first failure, so the run's closing status, and every later run, never went out: the run stayed RUNNING (clock icon in the UI).
- A run cancelled with Ctrl+C also stayed RUNNING, because `train.py` only caught a failing command.

## Changes
- `tracker.sync`: a failed **artifact** is logged and retried at the next start; it no longer stops the run's other events or the runs after it. After 3 tries it is given up (`RunQueue.fail_event`) so one broken file cannot slow every start. Any other failure still stops the queue in place (existing guarantee, tested).
- `stage_tracking.finish_training` closes the run **before** the artifacts go up. `training_status`: Ctrl+C -> `KILLED`, a failing command -> `FAILED`. `train.py` handles `KeyboardInterrupt`.
- Artifacts: `train.yaml`, the preprocess manifest and `trainer_state.json` always; the noisy `train_stdout.log` only for a FAILED/KILLED run (traceback). The LoRA's trainable/all parameter counts are read from the log into tags (`tracking.model_size_tags`).
- Tests first (they failed before the change): 6 in `test_tracker.py`, 5 in `test_stage_tracking.py`, 2 in `test_tracking.py`, 1 in `test_run_queue.py`.

## Verified
- `ruff check .` clean; `python -m pytest`: 571 passed; the four stage scripts import cleanly.
- Close-then-upload order against a real MLflow 3.16.1 server: run status `KILLED` and the artifact present afterwards.

## Not verified
- `NOT VERIFIED: model part` — the Ctrl+C path in `train.py` never ran (no GPU in the session). Checklist in `.memory/active-issues/unverified-on-gpu.md`.

body:
## Anlass
P-25-Lauf A2 (02.10.2026): Nach „sicher“ übersprang NINA im Sicherungscontainer alles hinter *NINA-PM Wait until Safe or Night End* (`Items[SKIPPED]: 1` = *Unpark Scope*), der Zielcontainer startete mit geparkter Montierung. Ursache in NINA 3.2: `SequentialStrategy` prüft die Schleifenbedingungen nach **jeder** Anweisung und markiert den Rest als übersprungen.

Entscheidung Sven: **kein Plugin-Code** dafür (#202 geschlossen), sondern über die Sequenzvorlage – nach dem Muster seiner Starfront-Sequenz (Wiederherstellung am Anfang des sicheren Containers, Home statt Park).

## Neue Vorlage (nur Doku)
```
NINA-PM Nacht                  [NINA-PM Night Loop]
├─ Ziel                        [Loop While Safe + NINA-PM Night Loop]  Trigger wie bisher
│    1. Wiederherstellen: Unpark Scope | Home-Variante: Set Tracking Sidereal (+ rig-abhängig Strom, Open Cover, Wartezeit)
│    2. Blöcke                 [NINA-PM Night Loop]
│         └─ NINA-PM Instructions
└─ Sicherung                   [Loop While Unsafe + NINA-PM Night Loop]
     Stop Guiding → Park Scope | Find Home + Set Tracking Stopped (+ Close Cover, Strom aus)
     → NINA-PM Wait until Safe or Night End   ← letzte Anweisung
Ende: Stop Guiding → Park Scope | Find Home + Set Tracking Stopped → Warm Camera
```
- „Blöcke“ verhindert, dass die Wiederherstellung vor jedem Block läuft (NINA-PM führt einen Block je Aufruf aus).
- *Unpark Scope* ohne geparkte Montierung ist in NINA wirkungslos („Mount is already unparked“), nach Home schaltet NINAs Slew die Nachführung selbst ein (`AscomTelescope.SlewToCoordinates`: `TrackingEnabled = true`).

`execution.md` §1 (Tabelle, Inspector-Prüfpunkte, Spec-Ergänzung) und §4.6 (Mechanismus, unsicher bis Nachtende), `sample-sequences.md` (Bau-Anleitung), `plugin-test-protocol.md` P-25, Briefs AP-16c und AP-16h, FK 14.x und TK (jeweils innerhalb bestehender Zeilen – Zeilenzahl unverändert, `concept/INDEX.md` stimmt weiter).

Die eingecheckten Beispielsequenzen `Samples/one-night-safety.json` und `one-night.json` folgen noch der alten Vorlage → in NINA nach `sample-sequences.md` neu bauen und exportieren (Variante nach Wahl).

body:
## Summary

Backport of `8a1b2af` from `main` (shipped in 5.1.x) to the `5.0.0-rc` line, so users on Angular 12–15 get the same sorting behaviour without upgrading.

`sortOnMultipleKeys` in `projects/core/src/lib/utilities/utilities.ts` now:

- compares string pairs with `localeCompare(…, undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' })` — natural alphanumeric order (`Item 2` before `Item 10`), case-insensitive, and å/ä/ö ordered by the end user's locale rules instead of UTF-16 code units;
- treats `undefined` like `null` (sorted last);
- `continue`s to the next sort key when values are equal, instead of returning `0` (fixes multi-key tiebreaking broken since rc.20's "handle null and equal values").

Behaviour is identical to `main`; the only textual difference is prettier line wrapping per this branch's config. No public API changes.

### Before / after (ascending, single key)

| Input | rc.20 | this PR (`sv-SE` runtime locale) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Örebro, Ängelholm, Åre, Alingsås, Zürich` | `Alingsås, Zürich, Ängelholm, Åre, Örebro` | `Alingsås, Zürich, Åre, Ängelholm, Örebro` |
| `Item 10, Item 2, Item 1, Item 20` | `Item 1, Item 10, Item 2, Item 20` | `Item 1, Item 2, Item 10, Item 20` |
| `banana, Apple, cherry` | `Apple, banana, cherry` | `Apple, banana, cherry` |

Note: no locale is passed, so collation follows the browser's default locale (same as `main`). In an `en` browser, Å/Ä/Ö are treated as accented A/O and interleave with them.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (ng-packagr) succeeds.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` pass on the changed file.
- An assertion script importing the real `sortOnMultipleKeys` passes under both `en-US` and `sv-SE` runtime locales (natural numeric order, case-insensitivity, null/undefined last, multi-key tiebreak with mixed asc/desc, numbers still numeric, Å/Ä/Ö after Z under Swedish collation).
- No spec file added: the `core` project on this branch has no test target (`main` moved to vitest later), so `main`'s `utilities.spec.ts` changes could not run here.

author: tippingcows
body:
## What was happening

Source code pasted into a web assistant an org has approved raises `source_code_leak` (`high`, and `block` at the default block severity). The existing escape hatch, per-tool suppression, is keyed by a tool id taken from the User-Agent or a `tool` field. A coding assistant has one (`claude-code:source_code_leak`). A prompt typed into claude.ai has neither, so the rule could not be aimed at it. The only handle left was `unknown`, which covers every untagged capture, including the ones going to tools nobody approved.

One operator had dismissed more than twenty such findings by hand.

## What changed

A suppression key that **contains a dot** is a host, matched against where the prompt is going: that host and its subdomains, on whole labels, the same rule the sanctioned list uses.

- `claude.ai:source_code_leak` allows source code to `claude.ai` (and `www.claude.ai`, etc.) and **nowhere else**: not `claude.ai.evil.example`, not `chatgpt.com`.
- The secrets and PII in the same paste are still caught; only the named category is dropped.
- It reads the same two settings as the tool rules (`GATEWAY_TOOL_SUPPRESS` and the tenant's `tool_suppress`). **Nothing changes for a tenant that does not set one.** No new column, no migration, no new default.
- The protection simulator already treated `claude.ai` as the tool id for the browser plane, so it would have honoured this setting while real captures did not. They now agree.
- The Settings field label and example, the README and `docs/overview.md` now say hosts work.

`policy` needs the same destination-to-host helpers the shadow-AI detector got in #269, so they move to `app/hosts.py` rather than one module importing another's private names. `shadow_ai.py` imports them under its existing names. Pure move, no behaviour change.

## Why opt-in rather than "anything sanctioned may carry code"

Approving a tool is not the same as approving proprietary code going to it (an org may sanction ChatGPT for general use and still not want source pasted in). Making that automatic would silently drop alerts for every tenant. This way each org states it, per host, in a setting it already has.

## After it deploys

Set Settings → "Per-tool or per-site suppressions" to `claude.ai:source_code_leak` (append with `;` to anything already there). Whether a given capture is covered depends on it reporting a destination; captures with none are not matched by a host key.

## Verification

- 6 new tests: 5 unit (host and subdomains, look-alikes, dotless keys stay tool ids, deployment setting, filter composition) and one end to end through the ingest API with a per-tenant setting (allowed to claude.ai, still flagged to chatgpt.com, secret in the same paste still flagged). All fail on `main`.
- Recall, evasion, false-positive and code-discrimination benchmarks are byte-identical to `main`.
- Backend suite: 2579 passed, 11 skipped.
