## What changes

Before: the webview pixel gate (`pnpm test:vscode:csp`) ran on stable VS Code only. No run checked that a lit 3D mesh draws in its material's colour, so a material that lost its colour passed every check.

After: the gate drives a box with an orange `StandardMaterial3D` beside a twin with the box hidden. At least 2000 pixels must differ, and their mean blue over mean red must be at most 0.5 (the albedo's own ratio is 0.25, a grey or white material is near 1). CI also runs the gate on the `engines.vscode` floor, VS Code 1.85.0.

How:
- `TEXTSCENE_VSCODE_VERSION` picks the build, through the same `vscodeTestVersion` the extension's suites use. The `min` integration leg now runs the gate.
- VS Code 1.85 (Electron 25) refuses Playwright's `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` attach call. When that happens, `driveScene` attaches through `cdpRelay.mjs`, a local relay that answers the call and passes the rest through. This adds `ws` as a root dev dependency.
- The driver picked a cached build with a string sort, so it ran 1.85 instead of 1.140 when both were cached. It now picks the requested version.
- `sceneText.mjs` gains `hideSceneNode`, and `pixels.mjs` gains `meanColourUnderMask`.

## How you checked it

- `pnpm test:vscode:csp` on Linux and Xvfb, all eight runs pass:
  - VS Code 1.140.0: 23,258 box pixels on a 565x430 canvas, blue over red 0.30.
  - VS Code 1.85.0 (`TEXTSCENE_VSCODE_VERSION=min`, through the relay): 16,776 box pixels on 384x365, blue over red 0.30.
- With the albedo forced to white in `standardmaterial3d/decode.ts`, only the box check fails (blue over red 1.10).
- With `MeshInstance3D` drawing nothing, the box check fails with 0 pixels.
- `pnpm type-check:all`, `pnpm type-check:tests`, `pnpm test:unit` (27,426 tests), `npx eslint scripts/vscode`, `pnpm format:check`.

body:
## Summary

Fix retained diff cards in offline Try mode and keep individual file review anchored within the native page.

`AppModel.placeChangeCards()` locates a completed turn by its starting transcript message ID. Seeded sessions used unrelated turn IDs, so patches were captured but never displayed. Derive both `Session.completedTurnID` and `SessionState.turnID` from the latest user message (or the first retained message for assistant-only samples). Preserve the welcome fixture's existing completion ID by assigning it to its user message.

`NativeDiffView` now uses vertical scrolling with wrapped code instead of a two-axis canvas. Content starts directly under the fixed file header; line numbers and change markers remain beside each source line. The shared inline Changes title applies both when opening a file directly and when navigating from Show all.

During verification, changing to the first accessibility text size stalled rendering with sustained ~99% CPU. A process sample showed repeated underlying transcript lazy-layout work. Keying the transcript `LazyVStack` by `dynamicTypeSize` refreshes its measurements when the font category changes. The same physical route now stays responsive through maximum accessibility size and landscape.

The retained-card regression covers seven files, placement after the transcript and reopening for both completed samples. It failed on the merged base and passes with the fixture fix.

The blank Composer project and checkout selectors now have 16 pt of adjacent padding instead of 32 pt. Outer leading alignment and vertical touch padding stay the same.

The selected-session header replaces its top material fade with a native `.glassEffect(.regular, in: Rectangle())` surface on iOS 26+. It covers the Sessions button, title, PR menu and actions through the top safe area and does not intercept touches. The blank Composer and older-platform material fallback retain their existing presentation.

The [failed TestFlight run](https://github.com/hideoutgames/zremote/actions/runs/37053588916) stopped during unsigned Swift Release compilation, before signing/export/upload. `Binding(get:…, set: model.setBackgroundFullHeight)` generated a Bool main-actor reabstraction thunk that crashed Swift 6.3.3 IRGen (`SmallVector::grow_pod`). A minimal device-target reproduction produced the identical generated symbol and stack on local Xcode 26.6. Using `set: { model.setBackgroundFullHeight($0) }` compiles with the same Swift 6 / `-O` / device flags. Signing and distribution configuration are unchanged.

### Validation

- Glass header and archive workaround: affected-source Swift syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed. Full unsigned Xcode 26.6 Release device build and recorded simulator verification are in progress.

- Selector spacing (`b649080`): affected-source Swift syntax parsing, whitespace check, pinned Xcode 27 RC iOS build with stable inputs, and recorded offline iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 portrait/native-large checks passed. Both pickers open independently, and longer project/checkout labels remain inline with existing ellipses.

- Fixture fix: 28 targeted tests passed (`DemoRetainedChangesTests`, `CoreBehaviorTests`, `UnifiedDiffParserTests`), pinned Xcode 27 RC iOS build and recorded iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 feature checks passed.
- Viewer and text-size fix: affected-source Swift syntax parsing, `git diff --check`, and pinned Xcode 27 RC iOS build passed. The shared resource runner reported exit 0 and `inputsStable=True` for the source now committed as `2465864`.
- Recorded iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 checks passed: top alignment, wrapping and gutters, direct-card and Show all/Back navigation, native Copy, the previously failing accessibility-size checkpoint, maximum accessibility size, and landscape vertical scrolling without horizontal/diagonal drift. Ordinary light/dark readability also passed in the preceding viewer run.
- All three CI checks passed on `2465864`.
- Simulator restored to blank Try with native large text, portrait/System Light, empty draft and dismissed keyboard.

### Qualifications

Changing text size and restoring it shifted the underlying transcript viewport approximately 60 px. Content remained intact; Jump to latest restored the original live-edge viewport. Exact automatic reader-position preservation and active selection across a text-size transition are not established.

The short seeded single-hunk patches do not establish long-file or multiple-hunk UI behavior. iPad, Android, live authentication/backend and additional platforms remain untested for this viewer change.

author: miguel-heygen
body:
## What

Layer rows in the timeline now show their own layer instead of a flat bar. A text layer's row draws its own words as text, in its own weight and colour and its font as Studio has it; a visual layer's row shows a picture of that layer alone. Closes desktop's text-clip report (text clips such as Subtitle and Cta tiled their rendered text as repeated thumbnails). On a project where most layers span the whole film, every one of those rows used to be a plain pale bar.

## Why it happened

Three things stacked:

1. `useRenderClipContent` only gave a layer row a picture when it was shorter than 92% of the film and its id did not contain backdrop, background, overlay, scrim or mask. A full-length layer failed the first test and fell back to the flat bar.
2. Even with a picture, a full-length row's thumbnail captured the whole frame, so every such row showed the same image.
3. Layer rows found by id or class had no selector, so a thumbnail could not ask for one layer anyway (composition hosts still got one from `data-composition-id`). `timelineElementHelpers.ts` checked "is this an HTML element" with `instanceof` against the preview window. The preview's nodes carry the editor window's prototypes (documented in core `runtime/domRealm.ts`), so the check was false for those rows on every load I ran; core's notes say it happens on some loads. The same check also stopped video and audio rows from reading their source length.

## Fix

- A layer that is only text (a text tag whose children are all text leaves, the rule the canvas text editor already uses: `isTextBearingTag` / `isEditableTextLeaf` in `domEditingDom.ts`) gets its words and computed font family, weight and colour when the row is built (`readTimelineText`, called from `applyMediaMetadataFromElement`, which both row builders go through). A layer that paints a background image or gradient is not a text layer and keeps its picture. A text row renders its words on one clipped line (`TextClipContent`), with no capture, on the layer's own background colour when it has an opaque one, otherwise on a theme strip chosen for contrast (light behind dark text, dark behind light text). The timeline's change check compares text by value, and a canvas text edit, which skips the preview reload, re-reads the edited layer's row (`refreshTimelineRowText`). `isEditableTextLeaf` moves from `domEditingLayers.ts` to `domEditingDom.ts` beside `isTextBearingTag`, so the timeline can use it without an import cycle.
- The film-length rule and the id pattern are gone, so a full-length HTML layer gets a picture like any other. Media, audio and hidden-thumbnail rows are unchanged.
- The thumbnail capture fades out the row's siblings at each level above it, so the picture shows that layer alone. One helper (`getElementScreenshotClip` in studio-server) now serves both the Vite and the CLI capture paths; the copy inside `vite.browser.ts` is deleted. Each faded sibling gets an inline `opacity: 0 !important`; the page keeps its own list of what it faded and the exact previous inline opacity, so no marker is added to the markup and each sibling's inline opacity is put back exactly. The CLI, which reuses one loaded page for later captures, restores them after every screenshot (`clearElementScreenshotIsolation`); without that, the next capture on the page came back blank.
- The thumbnail cache version goes from v4 to v5, so rows that already had a selector stop serving their old whole-frame crop. The cache key now hashes the selector instead of replacing punctuation, so `#a\.b` and `#a_b` no longer share one cached picture, and long selectors are no longer cut at 80 characters.
- Core exports its existing realm-independent element checks as `@hyperframes/core/runtime/dom-realm`, and the timeline helpers use them.

## Tests

- `useRenderClipContent.test.ts`: a full-length row with an id gets a picture.
- `useRenderClipContent.test.ts`: a row with text renders `TextClipContent`. Fails without the branch.
- `timelineElementHelpers.test.ts`: `readTimelineText` reads an `h1` with a `span` as one line with its font, weight and colour, and returns nothing for a container holding a non-text child, an empty div, or a non-text tag. The container case fails without the text-only rule.
- `screenshotClip.test.ts`: every sibling on the element's ancestor path is faded out, and the element, its subtree and its ancestors are left alone. A sibling with its own `opacity: 1 !important` is still hidden and gets that exact value back on clear, as does one whose opacity is `var(--alpha, 0|1)`. After a clear, isolating a different element hides only its own siblings.
- `thumbnail.test.ts`: `#a\.b` and `#a_b` are captured separately; the old key served the second from the first's cache.
- `studioServer.test.ts`: a selector capture clears its isolation after the screenshot. It fails without the clear. The describe block now shuts its server down after each test, because the thumbnail browser lease is module-wide and leaked one test's fake browser into the next.
- `timelineElementHelpers.test.ts`: a row whose node comes from another realm keeps its `#id` selector, and a foreign `<video>` still yields its source length. Both fail on the old check.

## Cost

Measured cold, on a 60 s fixture film with 24 rows, scrolling the whole timeline:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rows with a picture | 12 of 24 | 24 of 24 |
| Captures | 14 | 26 |
| Median capture | 10.8 s | 11.0 s |
| Last thumbnail lands | 134 s | 201 s |

About one capture per row, so the first open of a long film takes longer to fill in. A second open hits the thumbnail cache. (That run predates text rows; those cards are now drawn as text and need no capture.)

Rows on screen first, cold, no scrolling, six rows in view, two runs each:

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| The 24-row film (labelled flat-colour cards) | 3 of 6 visible rows get a picture; the last lands at 34 to 36 s | All 6 visible rows draw at once as text; nothing to wait for |
| The same film with gradient cards (every row captured) | 3 of 6 visible rows get a picture; the last lands at 33 to 47 s | All 6 get a picture; the last lands at 56 s |

On the gradient film every capture this PR makes goes to a visible row (6 rows plus the composition card), where main spends 3 of its 6 on rows off screen. The last of the six lands later only because Studio's capture path renders one page at a time, about 5.5 s each; batching captures is the follow-up.

The CLI path was checked separately on the built CLI (`hyperframes preview` from source always serves through Vite): Title, then Waves, then the whole frame requested at once on one page. Before the clear, Waves and the whole frame came back blank; with it, all three are right.

## Limitation

Text rows show the words present when the timeline is built or the text is edited in Studio; words a script swaps in during playback are not tracked. A font that only the composition loads falls back to Studio's fonts in the row.

A layer is captured without its siblings, so a layer whose look depends on what is behind it (`mix-blend-mode`, `backdrop-filter`) is shown against its parent's background rather than the sibling it blends with.

## Before

A text-heavy fixture: Backdrop and Shape are visual layers; Title, Subtitle and Cta are text. On main the full-length rows are flat bars, Subtitle is a blurred, tiled picture of its words, and Cta tiles a picture of the whole frame.

![Backdrop, Shape and Title as flat bars, Subtitle a blurred tiled raster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4044bab7-fc57-4d0a-87e4-dfd717809b6e)

![Subtitle blurred and tiled, Cta tiling whole-frame pictures](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/521f7c1a-b500-447e-9edc-8846160712bd)

## After

Backdrop and Shape show their own pictures; Title, Subtitle and Cta show their own words as text, in their own colour and font (the font as Studio has it), Cta on its own red.

![Backdrop and Shape pictures, Tit

author: mithrandir21
body:
Closes #321.

Every game page showed the red "Fuzzy match" warning, even for exact matches like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and No Man's Sky, and some pages showed the wrong game's metadata (God of War from 2009 instead of 2018, Stray from 2017, Portal resolving to "Mac Portal").

## Root causes
1. **The Steam id never reached the game page.** ITAD's `/games/info/v2` returns the Steam `appid`, but `ItadGamePrices.toGameDetails` hard-coded `steamAppID = null`. The game page therefore never joined IGDB by Steam id and always fell back to a title lookup, and every title lookup set the warning.
2. **IGDB can list several Steam entries for one game.** The IGDB mapper took the first, so Portal (IGDB id 71) resolved to Steam app 52003 "Mac Portal" instead of 400.
3. **Exact-name lookups were unordered.** IGDB has four games named exactly "God of War" (2001, 2005, a 2009 port, 2018); `limit 1` without a sort returned the 2009 port.

## Fix
- The ITAD Steam id now flows into `GameDetails`, so the game page uses the exact Steam-id join (verified live: all seven test titles resolve correctly by Steam id, including God of War → the 2018 game).
- The IGDB mapper prefers the Steam entry named like the game (`external_games.name` is now requested).
- Exact-name lookups sort by `total_rating_count desc`. This is only reached when a deal has no Steam id.
- The warning (`isUncertainMatch`, renamed from `resolvedByTitle`) is now shown only when a title lookup matched a differently named game, ignoring case, punctuation and ™/®/©.

## Tests
- `isSameTitle`: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, No Man's Sky, The Last of Us™ Part I, Ghost of Tsushima DIRECTOR'S CUT ↔ "Ghost of Tsushima: Director's Cut", Stray (same); Portal ↔ Mac Portal and Portal ↔ Portal 2 (different).
- Game page: a Steam-id join beats the title lookup and is certain (God of War 2018 vs 2005); an exact title match with no Steam id is certain; a differing title match is flagged.
- IGDB: Portal's Steam entries pick 400 over "Mac Portal"; the exact-name query prefers the most-rated game.
- ITAD: game details carry the info `appid`.
- `:feature:game`, `:remote:igdb` and `:remote:itad` pass on Android host and the iOS simulator.

## Notes
- Game details are cached for 2 hours, so pages cached before this fix keep the old warning until the cache expires.
- On the iOS simulator (Release, merged with #326), Clair Obscur, God of War and Stray now show the correct game with no warning.
- Heads-up: this and #326 both add a fixture just above `THREE_CANDIDATES_BODY` in `IgdbSourceImplTest.kt`, so whichever merges second needs a trivial keep-both conflict resolution.

author: marius-patrik
body:
Planned PR **9** of Phase 2 (issue #129). Stacked on #136.

## Goal

Quests follow the same parent-and-subclass pattern as rules, and there are twenty of them.

## What changed

| What | Change |
|---|---|
| `model/game/quest.py` | rewritten. `Quest` carries `name`, `description`, `reward`, `when`, and implements `parameters()`, `progress()`, `observe_move()`, `observe_result()`, `validate() -> bool` and `reset()`. **`condition_fn` is gone** |
| `model/game/quests.py` | the twenty built-ins, in two families |
| `model/game/events.py` | `MoveEvent` and `ResultEvent` — what the game tells a rule or a quest. Every flag defaults, so a caller that knows less than the full picture describes what it knows rather than a wrong answer |
| `model/game/field.py` | `Field`, the declaration one form renderer turns into widgets (registered as `notes/object_model.md` §9). `Quest.parameters()` returns `List[Field]` |
| `model/misc/quest_manager.py` | rewritten. Holds the quests **in play for the current game** only; `observe_move` / `observe_result` route each event to the quests waiting for it; `total_reward()` derives experience from the completed quests |

## The twenty, and their `when`

`after_move` — twelve: `FirstBlood`, `CaptureN`, `CaptureOfType`, `MovePieceNTimes`,
`ReachedSquare`, `VisitNSquares`, `SurvivePlies`, `SurviveWithoutCapture`, `CastleN`,
`PromoteN`, `EnPassantN`, `MakeCheckN`.

`at_game_end` — eight: `NeverInCheck`, `KingOnlyGame`, `GameResult`, `WonBy`,
`GameAtLeast`, `MaterialAhead`, `Pacifist`, `CompositeQuest`.

## A deviation from the manual, stated rather than absorbed

`SCRATCHPAD.md` §6 PR 9 lists `NeverInCheck` and `KingOnlyGame` under `after_move`. **Both
are `at_game_end` here.** Neither can be judged after a single move: nothing before the last
move can establish that check was never suffered, or that nothing else will ever move. A
quest judged `after_move` would complete on the opening move and mean nothing — which is
precisely the "completes on the intended event and **not before**" clause the same
acceptance criterion demands. The plan defect is a mis-grouping in the `when` column; the
quest list itself is delivered in full.

## No chess in the engine

Nothing here names a chess piece. Anything game-specific arrives as a parameter:
`CaptureOfType(piece_type=...)`, `KingOnlyGame(royal_kind=...)`, and
`NeverInCheck`/`MakeCheckN` reading a boolean flag off the event rather than looking for a
king. The same quest classes serve a game that has never been heard of.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `Quest.validate()` takes no arguments — asserted directly against the signature, for
      the parent and all twenty built-ins, because a signature is exactly what this
      requirement fixes
- [x] a quest built from each `when` completes on the intended event and **not before** —
      16 tests, one per quest, each of which feeds the quest an event that must *not*
      complete it before feeding it one that must
- [x] a quest completes once and stays completed
- [x] progress renders current and target — `progress() -> Tuple[int, int]`, so a card
      renders `3/5`
- [x] `condition_fn` is gone
- [x] quests in play and quests completed are held separately; XP is derived —
      `QuestManager` holds in-play quests, `User.add_quest` remains the holder of completed
      ones, and `total_reward()` sums the completed rewards, so `User` gains no field

## Verification

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
144 passed, 1 skipped in 1.65s

$ .venv/bin/python -m black --check .
All done! 67 files would be left unchanged.

$ .venv/bin/python -m properdocs build --strict
(zero warnings, zero errors)
```

`tests/test_quest.py` and `tests/test_quest_manager.py` were replaced by one rewritten
`tests/test_quest.py`. **The old tests asserted the old API** — they passed a
`condition_fn` and a context to `validate(context)` — so they were not weakened, they were
replaced by tests of the API the requirements specify. The manager tests were folded in
rather than dropped: registration, routing, completion-once, reset and reward derivation
are all still covered.

One thing the strict build caught, worth recording: `**kwargs` had no PEP 484 annotation,
which `griffe` reports as a warning and `--strict` turns into a failure. Annotated.

## Stack

- base: `feature/board-generalisation` (#136)
- merge order: #128 → #132 → #133 → #135 → #136 → **this** → …

---

Closes #147 (planned PR 9)

author: pacocotera
body:
The workbench's short #G/#E hashes cannot reconstruct a genome. This standalone proof adds a versioned five-layer tree and reversible G inherited/T complete-snapshot strings, using either an exact shared foundation or an embedded one. Ordered allele copies, actual parent/donor provenance and every supported literal T field survive decoding without rerunning the creature generator.

The compact contact G/S example is 724 binary bytes / 975 text characters, compared with 2,229-byte genome JSON; its exact catalogue is supplied separately. Embedded foundations and whole snapshots remain large. Explicit versions, numeric preservation, canonical bytes, integrity checks and parser/data bounds reject malformed, mismatched or unsupported records rather than silently losing fields.

Validation: coder and independent technical reviewer passed seven focused gates on Node 24.19.0; all nine retained strings decoded/re-encoded exactly, four T snapshots matched original packets/trees, and actual cross provenance matched. Complete contact G/S bytes plus numeric/map/Unicode goldens are pinned for Node 22 CI. Existing CI installs the pinned cbor2@2.3.0 dependency before host checks. Evidence: prototype/generator-workbench/evidence/genome-tree-codec/README.md; contract: prototype/generator-workbench/codec-contract.md.

Stacked on PR82 (codex/module-scene-workbench). No UI/API/native/device/provider/QR integration, execution/rights claim, sandbox activation or save reset. Owner's new pet/colour reference direction is recorded as design intent; it is not implemented art approval.

Exact-source [CI37054714645 passed](https://github.com/PacoCotera/critter-lab/actions/runs/37054714645) for `3439ad62d98189e786abbabd01a72198b5723d61`, including the complete protocol golden on Node 22 and the existing framework build.

author: andrewchen5678
body:
## Summary

- Arm `AutoFrameBufferUpdate` with interval 0 in every Apple session: `ard` on the physical displays, `ard` with `virtual_display = true`, and `ard-high-performance`. Apple's viewer arms a running session with 0 in both of its modes and sends all-ones only while paused; the one-second interval was remotex's own, from the High Performance input-freeze fix.
- That pacing slowed official Standard mode. On a physical display the Mac answers an incremental request late, so a scrolling window on a physical MacBook Pro drew 2–9 updates a second with the Mac silent for a second at a time, where the same scroll on a virtual display drew 18–30. With interval 0 it is smooth.
- Log once a second, at `debug`, where the read loop's time went between updates: between updates, reading the rectangles, and the video sink.
- Release 0.0.324.

## Risk

Unpaced pushes are the condition the input freeze was measured under, on a virtual display. A High Performance Mac's sender skips a viewer on the media stream, so its pushes carry no pixels once the stream is up; Standard's unofficial virtual display is the mode most exposed. `docs/apple-vnc-889.md` records the one-second interval as what to return to, for the affected mode alone, if the freeze comes back.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --lib`
- [x] macwork (physical Mac), official Standard, interval 0 everywhere: smooth by eye
- [x] macvm, official Standard: 27–28 Mpx/s at interval 0 against 13–14 at one second
- [ ] macwork with this branch's final build, in each of the three modes

body:
## Summary

- **Per-course reminder schedule:** course settings get an "Automatic reminders" option (Off by default, Weekly, Every 2 weeks, Monthly).
- **Daily job:** `GET /api/cron/training-reminders` runs at 14:00 UTC (about 10am Eastern). It emails every enrolled person who hasn't completed the course once a full interval has passed since their last reminder, or since their invite if they've never had one.
- **Manual push:** the roster gets "Send reminder now" (everyone unfinished, after a confirm) and a per-person "Remind" button. Each person shows when they were last reminded. Backed by `POST /api/admin/training/courses/[id]/remind` (admin only).
- **The email:** one personal email per person with their first name, progress ("2 of 6 lessons") and a "Continue your training" button straight to `/training/<course>`, plus both sign-in options (Google or email code).

## Notes for reviewers

- **Sending:** new `sendEmailBatch` in `lib/email.ts` uses Resend's batch API (100 per call, "permissive" validation so one bad address fails alone). Messages are single-recipient, so addresses aren't exposed and the office inbox isn't copied, unlike the BCC invite.
- **Who is skipped:** completed and removed people, people without an email, and anyone on an unpublished course (scheduled or manual).
- **Clock:** `training_enrollments.last_reminded_at` / `reminder_count` are stamped only for successful sends, so a failed send is retried on the next run. `isReminderDue` allows half a day of slack so a daily job running a little early doesn't skip a day.
- **Senders:** manual reminders come from the admin's name with replies to them; scheduled ones come from "STSA Church" with replies to `EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`.
- **Migration** `drizzle/0011_bizarre_wallop.sql` only adds three columns (default `'off'`, so no course starts sending). Already applied to the dev Neon database.
- **Heads-up on rollout:** switching an existing course to Weekly will email anyone invited more than a week ago on the next daily run. The job needs `CRON_SECRET` in Vercel (already used by the calendar sync).
- No unsubscribe link: an admin stops reminders by turning them off for the course or removing the person. Rationale in `docs/adr/0026-training-reminder-emails.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test` (184 passing), including `isReminderDue` boundaries and `lib/trainingReminders.test.ts`: unfinished/removed/completed filtering, due vs now modes, single-person push, clock restart, failed sends not stamped, unpublished refusal, cron route rejects calls without the secret
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` and `next lint` clean
- [x] Both new routes return 401 to unauthenticated calls on the dev server
- [ ] Click-through of the course setting and roster buttons as a signed-in admin (session expired during this session), testing on a course whose only enrollee is yourself since dev uses live Resend

author: sh41
body:
Fixes #4326. Part of #4206.

The expander now expands structs, `super` outside functions, and captures of named functions as each supported Elixir release from 1.11 to 1.20 does. Struct fields and enforced keys are read from each module's compiled struct metadata. Captures dispatch as calls do, and from 1.17 each capture argument takes a step of the hygiene counter. Each is compared with the Elixir compiler through probes and its trace events, which now include `struct_expansion`. Nothing in the plugin uses the expander yet, and no user-visible behaviour changes.

## Commits

1. `feat(expander): expand structs from each module's struct metadata`: the `Structs` input and its decoder, the `%` clause, and `ExpansionObserver.structExpanded`.
2. `feat(expander): expand super and the captures that dispatch`: `super`, `&super(…)` and `&super/N` outside a function, and captures through `elixir_dispatch`'s `import_function`, `require_function` and `remote_function`.
3. `feat(expander): give each capture argument a hygiene counter from 1.17`: `escape/3`'s counter, name, context and metadata for each distinct `&N`.
4. `test(expander): compare structs and captures with the compiler's trace`: the probe oracle keeps `struct_expansion` events, and `StructProbeTest` and the new probe cases compare them.

## What is ported

- `elixir_map:expand_struct/5` and its helpers: `validate_struct/2`, `delete_struct_key/3`, `assert_and_trace_struct_assocs/4`, `assert_struct_info_if_not_function/4`, the struct loads, and `struct_undef/2` with `in_context/2`. Builds, updates, matches, and variable or pinned struct names in a match.
- `super(…)`, `&super(…)` and `&super/N`: the match and guard assertion, then `resolve_super/3`'s module and function scope checks.
- `elixir_dispatch:import_function/4`, `require_function/5` and `remote_function/5` for captures, and `expand_fn_capture/4`'s remote and local outcomes, including `undefined_local_capture` for `&foo/1` in a module body.
- `elixir_fn:escape/3`'s `&N` clause per release: no counter below 1.17.0-rc.1; then a counter per distinct `&N` on a variable named `capture`; then its position in `capture` metadata from 1.19.0-rc.1; then `_&` in `elixir_fn`'s context from 1.20.0-rc.5. `escape/3` also keeps a variable's context when it rebuilds a call.
- Below 1.17.0-rc.1, `expand_fn_capture/4` traces a remote capture twice. That is an expectation on the test side, not data in the expander.

## The `Structs` input

`Structs.of(module)` gives `Absent` (no `__struct__/1`), `Unreadable`, or `Present(fields, enforced)`, where `enforced` is `Known(keys)` or `Unknown`. `Expander.expand` takes it as a required parameter after `exports`, and `Run` holds it. `ModuleStruct.from` decodes the `:struct` term of a module's `Dbgi` chunk by its shape, never by release:

- up to 1.13, `{default_struct, enforced_keys}`;
- from 1.14, a list of `%{field, default, required}`;
- on 1.18.x and 1.19.0-rc.0, the same list without `required`, so the enforced keys are `Unknown`.

`V1.struct` exposes the term. Tests read it from each leg's beams (`legStructs`). There is no production `Structs` yet.

The module being defined is never read from `Structs`: in its own body Elixir expands it before any `defstruct` in it runs, and from 1.14.1 answers `inaccessible_struct`. Before 1.14.1 the expander stops there (below).

## Version entries

Each is an `ElixirLanguageFeature` entry that cites its commit, with an `ElixirLanguageFeatureTest` row:

- `STRUCT_KEYS_MUST_BE_ATOMS`, v1.17.0-rc.0 (`elixir-lang/elixir@514355f3d`). A non-atom struct key is `invalid_key_for_struct` on every path, before the struct is read. Before it, a build raises the struct function's `KeyError`, and an update or a match is `unknown_key_for_struct`.
- `STRUCT_KEYS_IN_FUNCTIONS_LEFT_TO_TYPES`, v1.20.0-rc.2 (`elixir-lang/elixir@a0ef7f0c3`). Inside a function, a struct update or match reads no struct.
- `CAPTURE_ARGUMENT_COUNTER`, v1.17.0-rc.1 (`elixir-lang/elixir@53c93b91d`). Each distinct `&N` takes a hygiene counter, which its variable, `capture`, carries.
- `CAPTURE_ARGUMENT_POSITION_META`, v1.19.0-rc.1 (`elixir-lang/elixir@59a1ad913`). The variable records its position as `capture` metadata after its counter.
- `CAPTURE_ARGUMENT_IN_ELIXIR_FN_CONTEXT`, v1.20.0-rc.5 (`elixir-lang/elixir@aae39c87d`). The variable is `_&`, in `elixir_fn`'s context.
- `STRUCT_OF_MODULE_BEING_DEFINED_NEVER_LOADED`, v1.14.1 (`elixir-lang/elixir@b78b48058`, a backport of `elixir-lang/elixir@904072081`). In its own body, the module being defined has no struct until it defines `__struct__`, so `%__MODULE__{}` is `inaccessible_struct`. Before it, a loaded module of the same name answers.

`REMOTE_CAPTURE_REPORTED_AT_CALL` (`elixir-lang/elixir@6c068176d`, v1.14.0-rc.1) now also says that the arity forms build their call with the name's metadata, so their dispatch, errors and macro boundary are at the name.

## The heads

`STRUCT` (`{'%',_,[_,_]}`), `SUPER` (`{super,_,V1} when is_list(V1)`), `CAPTURE_SUPER` and `CAPTURE_SUPER_ARITY` were declared before and returned `Unported`. They now expand. `PortParityTest` checks each against every leg's expander manifest.

## `Unported` points turned into answers

- `%` structs.
- `super`, `&super(…)` and `&super/N` outside a function.
- In the capture code (#4303):
  - `&f/a` with a name that could be a variable;
  - an imported or local capture that isn't a special form;
  - a remote capture whose module part is an atom.

The tests that pinned them as `Unported` now pin their answers. `ExpanderTest.testAStructIsUnported` is deleted, since `StructExpanderTest.testAnUndefinedStruct` covers the same case.

## `Unported` points left

Each is a stop, never a wrong answer:

- **Needs the module's definitions:**
  - `super` and `&super` inside a function;
  - a local capture inside a function;
  - the struct of the module being defined, inside a function: a build on every release, and an update or a match below 1.20.0-rc.2.
- **Needs quoted-import dispatch:** a capture whose call carries quoted-import metadata. Only macro output carries it.
- **Needs evaluation the expander doesn't do:**
  - a struct whose metadata can't be read, for example a hand-written `__struct__/1`;
  - a build that omits a field, on releases whose metadata doesn't record enforced keys (1.18.x and 1.19.0-rc.0);
  - a second `__struct__` key;
  - a capture whose module's exports can't be read.
- **Depends on what is loaded on the compiling node,** which the expander can't know:
  - up to 1.12, a capture of a macro of an unrequired module, which Elixir answers by whether that module is already loaded;
  - before 1.14.1, the struct of the module being defined at module level, which Elixir answers from a loaded module of the same name if there is one.

## Never produced

`struct_name_mismatch` and `invalid_struct_return_value` need a hand-written `__struct__/1`. Such a module reads as `Unreadable`, so the expander stops before either.

## Where the port differs from Elixir

- **A capture's module part.** When a capture becomes an `fn`, Elixir's `fn` calls the expanded module part. The expander puts that atom in the `fn` when the module part's value is an atom, so `&alias!(Integer).to_string(&1, 2)` expands `alias!` once. A module part whose value isn't an atom is expanded again in the `fn`, as no expanded tree is kept. That matches Elixir only where expanding it again gives the same, as for a variable written in the source. A variable a macro makes, such as `&var!(m).f(&1, 2)`, or an imported or inlined call, can differ. No case is run for it.
- **A quoted `&f/a` from 1.14.0-rc.1.** By reading, Elixir checks the quoted import on the name's metadata, where `elixir_quote` doesn't put it, so it misses the import. The expander does the same. No source capture reaches this until quoted-import dispatch is ported.

## Treatments that differ from the issue's plan

- **A second `__struct__` key is `Unported`.** Below 1.19 Elixir

author: script-kid-io
body:
## What changed

A component that checks in can no longer grant itself access to a secret.

### Before

`RegisterComponent` read `plugin:secrets`, split it, and wrote one `can_resolve` tuple per name for the caller's own principal (`service_secret_binding.go`). The only gate was the `plugin_principal:` prefix, which proves the caller holds a plugin SVID and nothing about which secrets it may read. The safety argument in the comment was a manifest reviewed in GitOps. ADR-0097 deletes the manifest.

### After

`bindDeclaredSecrets` asks FGA `Check(system_tenant:_system, platform_enabled, component:plugin/<name>)` before it writes anything. The startup seeder (`reconciler.SeedComponentCatalogGate`) writes that tuple only for an embedded catalog entry whose image passed release-signature verification (`verifyCatalogImages`). So the binding happens only for a component the operator ships. For every other component the declared list is advisory, the daemon logs that and writes nothing, and the component reaches a secret only through a tenant admin's grant (dashboard#174). No authorizer, or a check error, writes nothing: an undecidable gate is a closed gate.

The raw embedded table was not the gate on purpose: membership in the table says the operator listed it, the tuple says the image also verified.

### The catalog had no plugin

Measured: 9 tools, 3 agents, 3 connectors, 0 plugins. So with the gate alone, no plugin check-in would bind, including the first-party GitHub plugin that `exit-test-tool-dispatch.yml` deploys and whose revocation suite (`tests/e2e/plugin_secret_revocation_test.go`) reads the binding the plugin wrote for itself. That plugin gains a catalog manifest, `manifests/github-plugin.yaml`, `kind: plugin`, pinned to the same digest the workflow deploys (`sha256:12a5cb2a…`). The image carries two sigstore bundles on its referrers fallback tag, so the seeder's verification has something to verify. The workflow now says the two digests move together.

### Residual reach, filed as gibson#576

The gate keys on the name the check-in registers under, because nothing links a `plugin_principal:<uuid>` to the catalog entry it was deployed for. A plugin principal is minted only by a tenant admin, so the remaining reach is an admin-minted identity registering under a catalog plugin's name inside its own tenant, on that tenant's own secrets. Platform scope stays unreachable. #576 records the principal-to-catalog link that closes it.

### Acceptance

| Criterion | Where |
|---|---|
| A check-in from a component not in the signed catalog writes zero tuples, whatever it declares, proven by a test that fails before the change | `TestBindDeclaredSecrets_OutsideCatalogWritesNothing` (wrote two tuples before) |
| A catalog component still binds | `TestBindDeclaredSecrets_PluginGrantsCanResolve` against an `offering("plugin", "github")` recorder, and the GitHub plugin manifest |
| Resolving an ungranted secret fails with an error naming the secret and the missing grant | `authorizeCredentialResolve`: `no can_resolve grant on secret "<name>" for this caller; a tenant admin grants it`, PERMISSION_DENIED, never an empty value |
| A required ungranted secret fails the component at boot | already true in the SDK: `plugin.Serve` step 10 resolves every `scope: startup, required: true` secret and returns `required startup secret %q is unavailable` before any method serves |
| The audit row distinguishes no grant from no secret | `decision_reason` is `fga_no_can_resolve` when the grant is missing and `not_found` only after the grant check passed and the store has no row. Authorization is answered first, so a caller with no grant never learns whether the secret exists. |
| `non-plugin-secret-isolation` still holds | `TestBindDeclaredSecrets_NonPluginSkipped` unchanged: a tool or agent principal writes nothing |

### Checks run

`go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages, `go test` on `internal/platform/component`, `internal/platform/componentcatalog`, `internal/infra/reconciler`, and the catalog, verification and seed tests in `internal/server/daemon`.

Closes #554

Docs-PR: not-applicable: ADR-0097 already states the invariant; the code comment and the manifest carry the mechanism

body:
Fixes #436

## Class

`routine`, as the issue sets it: a refactor with every knob range and every picker group unchanged, plus the five labels the issue spells out word for word. The diff stays out of the `reviewed` areas.

## What changed

- **Knob ranges come from the catalog** (decision 1). The new `packages/app/src/patchKnobRange.ts` holds `knobRangeOf(row)`, which turns a catalog row into a knob's `min`, `max`, `curve: 'log'` when the scale is not `linear`, and `logFloor` from the row's `floor`. It also holds `voiceKnobRange(path)`, the catalog row at a voice path. Every knob over a voice target in `patchKnobTables.ts` spreads `voiceKnobRange(...)` and states only its label, step and readout. These are cutoff, resonance, vowel, env amount, both LFOs' rate and amount, the pitch-env amount, the operators' level, feedback and width, and the envelope rows' Decay and D Crv.
  - **Seam for shared entries.** `OP_KNOBS` and the envelope rows serve every operator or envelope slot, so they take operator A's row: the target table builds each operator's rows from one row. A test holds every knob whose own path is a target to that path's row, so this choice can't drift.
  - **Non-target paths on shared entries.** The pitch envelope's Decay and the filter and pitch envelopes' D Crv are not targets, but they share the entry, so they now read the same catalog range. Their values are unchanged and pinned.
- **Every range is pinned** (decision 2). `patchKnobRange.test.ts` pins all 145 `allPatchKnobs()` ranges to their values from before the change: path, min, max, curve and logFloor. A one-off change fails it. The voice half of `automationTargetParity.test.ts` is deleted and the strip half stays.
- **Picker groups come from the catalog** (decision 3).
  - Each `VOICE_AUTOMATION_ROWS` row is now a `VoiceAutomationRow` carrying `path` and `section` (`filter`, `operator` with its `op`, `lfo` or `pitch`). `voiceSectionOf(code)` reads the section from the target table's code layout (`VT_OP_BASE`, `VT_OP_STRIDE`, `VT_LFO_AMOUNT`, `VT_PITCH_ENV_AMOUNT`), with no string tests.
  - The catalog's own `OPERATOR_PATH` regex in `lookOf` is gone too.
  - In the app, `VOICE_GROUPS` is a map from section to label with no `claims`, plus `voiceGroupLabel(section, opNames)`. `OPERATOR_PATH` is gone.
  - `pickerGroups` groups rows by section in catalog order, and `laneTitle` reads the row's section. Neither re-parses the id.
- **Labels** (decision 4): `Dcy Crv`, `Fdbk`, `LFO 1 Amt`, `LFO 2 Amt` and `Pitch Env` in the catalog looks.
- **Hand-spelled ids** (decision 5): `songAutomationModel.test.ts` builds its Tape and EQ ids with `formatTargetId` and tests the voice kind with `targetKind`. `automationTargetParity.test.ts` builds the send ids with `formatTargetId`.
- **Stale comment** (decision 6): the `voiceTargetTables.ts` header now says there is one look per path in the catalog. This is a comment-only change, and `build-worklets --check` reports every bundle current.
- **Engine index**: exports the `VoiceAutomationRow` and `VoiceSection` types.

## How to check it

- `npx vitest run packages/engine/src/automation packages/app/src/patchKnob packages/app/src/knobDefaults packages/app/src/songAutomation packages/app/src/automationTargetParity packages/app/src/stepModLane packages/app/src/knobAutomation`: 25 files, 276 tests, all passing. This includes the new pin, the section tests, and a picker test pinning every group's options for a part with no inserts. The existing tests cover four operator groups, a part with inserts and a part at `FM_LANES_MAX`.
- `node scripts/build-worklets.mjs --check`: all current.
- `npm run typecheck && npm run lint`: clean.
- In headless Chrome, on the worktree's dev server with a song imported whose Grid part has step lanes on `ops.0.env.decayCurve`, `ops.0.feedback`, `lfo.amount` and `pitchEnvAmount`:
  - The step-lane headers read `Op A Dcy Crv`, `Op A Fdbk`, `LFO 1 Amt` and `Pitch Env`, all uncut. `Op A Dcy Crv` fills the header's 66 px exactly. The old `Op A Decay Crv` measured 78 px against 66.
  - I set each of the 30 voice labels into the header in turn and measured it. **None is cut.**
  - The Song tab's lane picker, opened on all four parts, shows Mixer, the insert groups, `Voice · Filter`, `Voice · Op A` to `Op D`, `Voice · LFO` and `Voice · Pitch`, in that order with the new labels. A lane's kind line reads `Voice · Filter` and `Voice · Op A`.

## Outside owned folders

None. The new `packages/app/src/patchKnobRange.ts` and its test are the helper decision 1 places beside `patchKnobTables.ts`.

## Decision record

`docs/log/2026-10-02-knob-ranges-from-the-catalog.md` (new). It supersedes the parity-test arrangement for voice rows from `2026-10-01-song-automation-lanes` decisions 5 and 6. Earlier records are untouched.

author: szommark
body:
No migration — the game runs entirely in the browser and saves nothing.

## What
A new **Games** tab (Játékok) on the Vocabulary page with a word grid game. Pick a wordlist, a size (3×3 / 4×4 / 5×5) and whether hints are on. N² + N words are drawn at random from the list: the grid plus one row of decoys.

**With hints** — each cell shows a Hungarian meaning; drag the English words (plus decoys) onto them. After the last cell: green = right, red = wrong. Greens lock; fix the reds and press Check until all green.

**Without hints**
1. All words are shown mixed in an (N+1)×N grid for a few seconds (11 / 15 / 20 s, skippable).
2. They're shuffled into a deck; draw one at a time into a cell or onto "Not in the grid" (max N cards).
3. After the last card: green exact · blue right row · purple right column · yellow in the grid elsewhere · red not in the grid.
4. Decoys drop out (red ones stay crossed out in their cell until replaced); wrongly discarded words come back yellow. Rearrange → Check → repeat until solved. The finished grid shows each word's Hungarian meaning.

Cards move by drag and drop, or by tapping a card and then its place (touch). Dropping on an occupied cell swaps.

## Files
- `src/lib/vocabGrid.ts` — pure rules: puzzle, moves, feedback, checks
- `src/components/Vocabulary/GridGame.tsx` — the board
- `src/components/Vocabulary/GamesTab.tsx` — setup
- `src/pages/VocabularyPage.tsx`, `src/lib/i18n.tsx` — tab + HU/EN/DE strings

## Verification
- A scripted test of the rules (esbuild bundle) covering both modes: decoy dropping, tray return, all five colours, swaps, green locking and solving.
- Both modes played in the dev server through a temporary harness with a mocked wordlist (removed before commit). Checked: real HTML5 drag-and-drop events, tap-to-place, the discard limit, Check enablement, and the 5×5 grid at 375 px with no horizontal overflow.
- `npm run lint` and `vite build` pass.

## Notes
- Hint mode only uses words that have a Hungarian meaning, one word per meaning, so each cell's hint is unambiguous.
- Hints are always Hungarian (the only translation wordlists store), regardless of the UI language.

body:
## What

Phase 2 of plan 02 (one audit protocol for ingests). **Stacked on #499** (base is its branch): merge #499 first, and GitHub retargets this PR to `main`. The diff below is phase 2 only.

## Changes

- **Market** (`MarketIngestor._slice`): the hand-rolled start/finish bracket is replaced by `ingest_log.audited`. A normal slice returns `Outcome(rows, "ok", note)`, an unpublished B3 file returns `Outcome(0, "skipped", ...)`, and a raised failure is still collected (not re-raised) so one bad session does not abandon the rest. `run()` still fails the process at the end if any slice failed.
- **ANBIMA** (`AnbimaIngestor.daily_update`): one `audited` call around fetch, parse and upsert. The `_log_start` and `_log_finish` pass-throughs are deleted. A failed fetch or an empty parse still ends in an `error` row and raises.
- **`Outcome`**: an `ok` row may now carry a note. The market ingest records dropped tickers and revisions on the ok row, which #499's version refused. Found while migrating; the first PR's "an ok Outcome cannot carry a message" rule was too strict.
- Audit rows keep the same columns, statuses and period keys.

## Not migrated: ETF market

`ingest_etf_market` is a synchronous call from `run_daily`. Folding it into the async `audited` would change `run_daily` and the event loop for no gain, and it already writes through `ingest_log.start` and `finish`. Left as it is.

## Tests

Market and ANBIMA's existing tests pass unchanged, except ANBIMA's six log-column tests, which called the deleted `_log_start` and `_log_finish` directly. They now go through `daily_update` and check the same things (real columns, NOT NULL fields, `started_at` not clobbered, `error_msg`, conflict key) plus one run id on both rows. One #499 test was rewritten to assert the note is allowed. Full offline suite: 2606 passed (`tests/test_research_agent_eval.py` skipped: it needs an optional `agents` package that is not installed here, and fails the same way on main).

## Next

Phase 3: B3 (12 `run_id` blocks and the `_log_*` pass-throughs). CVM last.

body:
## Summary
- Adds tests for the `package`, `launch`, `compile-check`, and help commands in the dispatcher CLI module (`internal/dispatcher`), along with the attestation-based release lookup. No production code changes.
- Launch tests go through a `launchDeps` value where every dependency that could reach a real Editor is faked. The fake kill calls `t.Fatal` unless a test overrides it, the Editor path resolves to a no-op executable, and every wait and IPC probe is stubbed. A regression in the branch under test therefore cannot start, focus, or stop a real Unity process. The one test that exercises the real Unix kill starts its own child process and kills only that one.
- Release lookup and attestation tests serve pages and bundles from `httptest`. They assert the exact request URLs, including `per_page=100&page=N`, and that bundle, tag, and malformed-bundle failures fail closed.
- Each failure test asserts a message, path, or error identity that only the targeted branch produces. Key branches were checked by temporarily disabling them and confirming that the test fails.

## Untestable remainder
- compile_check.go:runCompileCheck: everything after the Editor resolves. It runs the offline compile through the Editor-bundled Roslyn compiler, so it needs a real Unity Editor install. Option parsing and every resolution failure before that point are covered.
- attestation_release.go:fetchAttestationSubjectManifest: the code after `attestation.VerifySubjects` succeeds, plus the embedded trusted-root load error. The first needs a real Sigstore bundle signed by the release workflow. The second cannot fail, because the trusted root is embedded at build time. Bundle, tag, and verification failures are covered and fail closed.
- launch_process_kill.go:killProcessById: the `os.FindProcess` error branch. `os.FindProcess` never fails on Unix.

Concurrent state restores could keep refilling the CLAP configuration mailbox while the audio callback drained it. The drain now processes only the queue prefix present at its start (at most 128 commands); later arrivals wait for the next callback while accepted restore readback remains immediate.

Closes #1415.

The audit in `docs/audits/clap-boundary-1415.md` includes every wrapper lock/borrow, plugin registry and session/map ownership, the three-cursor reuse proof and reset cancellation exception, and the allocation-check reach map with explicit gaps. No additional in-scope defect was verified. Three exported-factory regressions cover concurrent restore arrival, a stalled configuration consumer filling/reclaiming the complete 2,048-cell input pool, and fault/reset cancellation with untimed flush retention. No persisted state or shader changes.

- Allocation-guarded vendor tests: 24 boundary + 1 auxiliary passed.

This change moves work out of the main loop. We only need to increment the step counter and check for cancellation in loops (back edges) and calls. We increment the counter by a constant scaled by the number of instructions between such checks, as estimated by the benchmarks here.

Clients may need to adjust their SetMaxSteps parameter to taste. (Let us know if you think our scale factor is way off.)

Also, add bazel.star, a set of pure-Starlark benchmarks (path manipulation, config/DAG/template evaluation) intended to be somewhat representative of Bazel workloads.

Of the benchmarks that showed any change, we got:

  bench_calling            -5.76%

body:
## Summary

An audit of the merged PR #729 (the row-scoped dead-segment law, the APX×AVX-512 EVEX fold pins, the both-sides encdiff gate parity) found two soft spots in the gate's evidence chain: the *disassembler* that decides every `BEATS`/`ok` verdict was unpinned (whatever objdump the runner image happened to ship), and the per-row exit contract was blind to aggregate drift — a row slipping `BEATS -> ok-best` kept the gate green forever. Both are closed here, and the families with the thinnest evidence grow into CI-reproducible oracle records.

**In one line:** pin the 2.47 `as`+`objdump` oracle pair and a checked-in verdict histogram into the encdiff corpus gate, make the fold-law opt-in read comment-stripped source, and record the APX×AVX-512 EGPR and `ebp` flip-law rows against them.

### What changes

**The oracle is now a pair, and the aggregate is a contract**
- `encdiff.py` gains `--objdump` (the disassembler decides `decodes_same`, hence `BEATS`/`ok` — it is as much an oracle as `as`) and `--expect-histogram`, which fails unless the run's per-verdict counts match the checked-in baseline. Counts only, compared through the nonzero projection, so `BEATS` staying `BEATS` through better bytes needs no baseline churn, while drift, new rows, deleted rows and classes appearing from zero all fail.
- `ci.yml` + `ci_local.sh` run the gate against the pair and the baseline; `check_ci_gate_parity.py` enforces both pins on both sides; `test_ci_gate_parity.py` mutation-checks each, with token-based owner dispatch — the checker that owns a pin is derived from the differential program, and the *non-owning* checker must accept the mutation, proving the dispatch is load-bearing.
- `ensure_gas_247.sh` builds `as` and `objdump` from the same 2.47 tree and treats an as-only cache as an interrupted provision (both binaries, or rebuild).

**Corpus, pins, and the comment-stripped opt-in (audit D3)**
- `index-fold-64.insn`: `+7` APX×AVX-512 EGPR rows (fold rows land `BEATS` over GAS's 11-byte SIB+disp32 forms with round-trip verification, turning one-time manual probes into a CI oracle record) and `+4` rows for the `ebp` half of the `{rbp, ebp}` flip set, which the law claimed but pinned in neither mode.
- `expected-verdicts.txt`: the aggregate baseline with every class explicit including zeros — **205 rows: 174 BEATS, 21 ok, 10 ORACLE-INVALID** (consistent with the pre-existing 194-row record: 166→174 and 18→21).
- `mod.rs`: Rust byte-pins for the four ebp flip rows in `index_fold_tests`; `avx.rs`/`core.rs` comments corrected to state the EGPR evidence is oracle-recorded, not merely probed.
- `_ROW_SEG_FOLD` now matches the comment-stripped source, exactly like `_canon_insn`: a trailing comment quoting a flip-shaped operand no longer opts its row into the dead-segment strip — previously a dropped-prefix regression on a non-flip row could have been laundered into a pass.
- `engineering/FOLLOWUP-2026-10-02-pr729-audit-adjudicated.md` records the audit adjudication end to end.

author: yonatankarp
body:
The sidebar drew each mini's picture with `AsyncImage`, which only loads again when the file's address changes. Try Again on a picture waiting to be checked draws a new `source.png` under the same name, so the mini's page showed the new picture while its row in the sidebar kept the old one.

The row now uses `Thumbnail`, as the mini's page does, which loads again when the mini's time changes. For a mini without a print file that time is its picture's (`Gallery.madeAt`), and the gallery reloads when the job ends, so the new picture reaches the row. `Thumbnail` gains a `fill` option so the row still fills its square as before; nothing else looks different, so no docs or screenshots change.

Fixes #338

## Release note

**The sidebar keeps up with Try Again:** after drawing a picture to check again, its row on the left shows the new picture, not the old one.

## How I checked

- New `GalleryTests.testAPictureDrawnAgainChangesTheMinisTime`: a mini with only its picture to check, drawn again under the same name, must get a later time and compare as changed, which is what the row now reloads by. Failing first: with `Gallery.madeAt` planted to ignore `source.png`, it failed with "the sidebar would keep the old picture" and "a reload wouldn't pass the new time on"; restored, it passes.
- `cd app && swift test`: 552 tests, 0 failures.
- There's no test target for the app's views, so the row's switch to `Thumbnail` itself has no test.

## Not verified

- Not tried by hand in the app (Try Again on a picture to check, then looking at the sidebar). The row's look (filled 44 pt square, rounded corners) wasn't compared by eye either; it uses the same fill and size as before.

* Implemented **Suspend and Resume functionality** for managing user account access.
* Added support for transitioning user accounts between **Active** and **Suspended** states.
* Updated the backend to handle account status changes with proper validation.
* Integrated account status checks with the **authentication and authorization flow**.
* Prevented suspended users from accessing protected application features.
* Added **Suspend** action for administrators to temporarily restrict user access.
* Added **Resume** action to restore suspended users back to an active state.
* Updated the admin user-management interface to display the user's current account status.
* Added dynamic action buttons based on the user's current status.
* Added confirmation handling to prevent accidental account suspension or restoration.
* Added appropriate success and error feedback for status-change operations.

* Implemented suspension as a **temporary access restriction** instead of permanently deleting the account.
* Improved overall **user lifecycle and access management** for the admin portal.
* Established a reusable account-status management flow that can be extended for additional user states.

author: kendrahartnett
body:
## Summary

This PR moves **The Dietrich Files** from a mostly static media experience to a data-driven multimedia archive.

The Gallery, Music, and Film sections now use structured catalog data and reusable rendering logic, making it easier to add and manage media without rewriting the UI for each new item.

## What Changed

### Art Gallery
- Moved artwork content into a structured media catalog
- Gallery now renders artwork dynamically
- Preserved the existing responsive gallery layout
- Preserved lightbox viewing and keyboard accessibility
- Added support for scaling the gallery to 40+ artwork records
- Added lazy-loading support for gallery images

### Music
- Added catalog-driven music tracks
- Added an interactive track list
- Added selected-track state
- Connected track selection to the audio player
- Added and tested two real audio tracks
- Verified switching between tracks, playback, pause, seeking, and progress behavior

### Film
- Added catalog-driven film records
- Added interactive film selection
- Connected selected films to the video player
- Added and tested two real MP4 films
- Verified switching between films and playback behavior
- Preserved native browser video controls

### Media Architecture
Introduced a clearer separation between media metadata, media assets, and rendering logic.

Current pattern:

`catalog → renderer → UI`

This establishes the foundation for eventually moving toward:

`database / object storage → renderer → UI`

without needing to rebuild the existing Gallery, Music, and Film interfaces.

### Large Media / Git LFS
- Added Git LFS handling for large audio and video assets
- WAV files are tracked through Git LFS
- MP4 files are tracked through Git LFS
- Verified that large media files are not being committed directly as normal Git objects

## Testing

Verified:

- Gallery renders real artwork
- Gallery lightbox works
- Both music tracks load and play
- Switching between music tracks works correctly
- Both films load and play
- Switching Film 1 → Film 2 → Film 1 works correctly
- Media state and titles update correctly
- Navigation remains functional
- No obvious missing-file or console errors
- Existing visual design and responsive behavior are preserved

## Architecture Decision

The application remains frontend-only for this milestone.

No database, backend, framework migration, authentication system, or external media storage was introduced.

This was intentional: the goal of this phase was to validate the data-driven media architecture with real content before adding additional infrastructure.

## Next Steps

The next phase will evaluate moving large media files out of Git LFS and into external object storage.

Planned progression:

`Git LFS → object storage → verify external media playback → database-backed metadata → future media-management/admin tools`

This PR serves as the working multimedia checkpoint before beginning that migration.

author: mcencini
body:
## What changed

The last eleven shipped sequences are written as functions of the system and the protocol, in the shape of #138, #139 and #140. No shipped sequence is a `SequenceApp` subclass after this PR.

| Module | Function | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `gre3D_sequence` | `gre3d` | one sequence |
| `se3D_sequence` | `se3d` | one sequence |
| `bssfp3D_sequence` | `bssfp3d` | each phase cycle's catalyst, then its train |
| `gre_multiecho3D_sequence` | `gre_multiecho3d` | one sequence |
| `epi2D_sequence` | `epi2d` | the calibration when undersampled or multiband, the reference, then the scan |
| `epi3D_sequence` | `epi3d` | the calibration when undersampled, the reference, then the scan |
| `se_epi_propeller2D_sequence` | `se_epi_propeller2d` | one sequence |
| `fse3D_sequence` | `fse3d` | one sequence |
| `mprage3D_sequence` | `mprage3d` | one sequence |
| `mprage_stack_of_spirals3D_sequence` | `mprage_stack_of_spirals3d` | one sequence |
| `mprage_stack_of_stars3D_sequence` | `mprage_stack_of_stars3d` | one sequence |

- **Functions.** Each function takes `system=None` first and the protocol as keyword-only parameters, which are the class's `init_sequence` parameters in the same order, with the same annotations and defaults. `system` is held under the module's `MAX_GRAD` and `MAX_SLEW`, which are module constants with the other settings. `main` is the function.
- **Chains.** `bssfp3d`, `epi2d` and `epi3d` return the list the class wrote: the prescans in play order, then the main sequence. Calling the module therefore returns the list where the class's `main` returned the main sequence alone. The gallery pages and the explanation figures take the main sequence as the last element.
- **File names of a chain.** `sequences.write` writes a later file whose name an earlier file of the chain has taken as `<stem>_<Name>_<position>.seq`, the position counted from 0. A chain of distinct names is written to the same files with the same bytes as before. `bssfp3d` needs the rule: with more than one phase cycle, its catalysts and its trains each record one `Name`, and each would otherwise be written over the one before. `cli.run` writes through `sequences.write`.
- **`fse3D_sequence.design_trains`** takes the prescribed refocusing angle and whether the trains are individually parameterised, in place of the application it read them from.
- **Tests.**
  - `tests/legacy/` keeps the class form of each of the eleven, unedited. `tests/test_sequence_parity.py` holds each function to byte parity with it at the defaults, at the protocols below, and for systems above and below the module limits. It compares every file of a chain.
  - The parity file gains 36 non-default protocols: five for the fast spin echo, four for the Cartesian MPRAGE and three for each of the others. The first protocol of each sequence changes every parameter the design admits together. The others reach what the defaults leave out, among them phase cycles, blade angle schemes, slice passes, multiband, segmented and packeted slices, nonselective and spatial-spectral excitation, shells and CAIPI lattices, partial Fourier, wave encoding, shuffled view ordering, a periphery with its own echo train length and TR, and optimised refocusing trains.
  - The protocols that design the refocusing trains with torchsim skip where it is not installed.
  - The tests of the eleven read the definitions, labels, blocks, waveforms and RF events of what the function returns, and the sampling helpers, in place of class attributes, and keep every invariant they held. `tests/sampling_regression.json` drops the entries that read class attributes and keeps the label digests.
  - `tests/zoo.py` gains `chain()`, and the shared docstring, example and sampling tests accept a list of sequences.
  - The tests of what an application resolves and times run over the class form of every shipped sequence, from `tests/legacy/`, since none is shipped as a class.
- **Docs.** The catalogue and the sequence-application page state that the shipped sequences are functions. The page's `SequenceApp` subclassing example subclasses an application defined on the page. The fast-spin-echo gallery scripts read the echo spacing, the shots, the refocusing schedules and each shot's TR from the sequence.

## Why

A shipped sequence is a function `sequence(system, **protocol)` that returns what is written. pulserver's sequence plugins bind these functions to the scanner protocol.

## Validation

- On the same tree built on #140's commit before it was squashed:
  - `bash scripts/format_and_lint.sh --check`: 348 files already formatted, all checks passed.
  - Full `pytest -q`, with torchsim installed: 6349 passed, 43 skipped. The skips are the ones `main` has; none is a test parametrised over no sequence.
  - `bash scripts/build_docs.sh`: build succeeded under `-W`, with no warnings. The 14 gallery scripts that design one of the eleven sequences, or take the scan of a chain, were also run directly; each exits 0.
- Outside the suite, 880 random protocols and systems for the eleven sequences:
  - Each parameter was drawn from its default and the values the parity protocols give it, under five systems: the defaults, limits above and below the module's, dead times, and 1.5 T.
  - 586 built byte-identically from the original class and the function, and 294 were refused by both with the same exception and message. None differed.
  - The refusals are design refusals, for example an echo spacing, TE or TR shorter than the train or the readout achieves, wave cycles that do not fit the flat top, or a slice count that is not a multiple of the multiband factor.

## Documentation impact

- The eleven reference pages are generated from the new docstrings, with the `system` entry first and, for a chain, a Returns entry that describes the list.
- `docs/sequences.md` and `docs/explanations/design/sequence-application.md`, as above. The sequence-application page states the file names of a chain whose names repeat.
- The gallery pages of `bssfp3d`, `epi2d`, `epi3d` and the fast spin echo, and `gallery/06-checks/01_constraint_checks.py`, take the main sequence from the list or read the timing from the sequence.

author: kburym
body:
## What
Fixes #394. `load_dotenv` in `utils_env.star` no longer runs `cat` through a shell, and parses the file properly. The red tests are the first commit, the fix the second.

## The bug
It ran `cat '<project_root>/.env'`, so a project path containing a single quote broke the command (and `|| true` hid the failure, so nothing loaded). Values were `strip('"').strip("'")`, so `export FOO=bar` became a key named `export FOO`, and a value with an embedded quote was truncated.

## Changes
- The file is read with `read_file` and parsed in Starlark. Nothing goes through a shell, and Tilt now re-evaluates the Tiltfile when the `.env` changes (the `cat` call did not register the file).
- Lines may be `NAME=value` or `export NAME=value`. Comments, blank lines and anything that is not an assignment to a valid name are ignored. One layer of matching quotes is removed; single quotes are literal; inside double quotes a backslash escapes a quote, a backslash or a `$`, and `\n`, `\r`, `\t` are expanded. A missing file does nothing.
- I kept the function and its API instead of deleting it: it has no callers in this repo (verified), but it is an exported `Utils` function that an external overlay could call.

## How it was tested
Three tests run the real function through Tilt against real files: plain, exported, double-quoted, single-quoted, embedded-quote, empty and `a=b=c` values plus comments and a non-assignment line; a project path containing a single quote; and a missing `.env`. Red first, for the right reason (`TDK_T_EXPORTED: expected [baz] but got [<unset>]`), then green. `biome check .` and `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; full CLI suite 604 passed. Every Tiltfile loads `utils_env.star` through `utils.star`, which the new tests also load.

## Not covered
- Inline comments on unquoted values (`FOO=bar # note`) are not stripped, as before.
- Variable expansion inside values (`A=$B`) is not done.
- It does not undo the `$$` that generated env files use for Docker Compose; it reads the project `.env`, not those files.
- I did not run a full `tdk up` for this change.
- It is still not called from anywhere in this repo; wiring it to the project `.env` is a separate decision.

author: rdimascio
body:
Classic Era had no data for NPCs, spawns, quest titles or quest givers, so Claude answered those from memory. This adds them from community data, labeled as such everywhere.

**Why cMaNGOS:** QuestieDB has no license. VMaNGOS takes its world data from `brotalnia/database`, which also has none. cMaNGOS `classic-db` ships its own GPL-3.0 LICENSE. The plan and its review are in `docs/plans/vmangos-era-data.md`.

## What it does

- `claude-wow data sync --flavor classic_era --source community` fetches `Full_DB/ClassicDB_1_12_1_z<rev>.sql.gz`. It checks the file against the git sha and size from the GitHub listing, caps the download at 64 MB and the unpacked dump at 256 MB, and reads the mysqldump INSERT rows (no SQLite, no new dependency).
- The data goes to its own store, `data/classic_era/community/`, with its own pointer, lock, swap and converter `shape`. A client re-sync never removes it.
- `wow_npc` is new: name, title, the quests the NPC gives and ends, every map it stands on, and a sample of spawns spread over those maps. Event and dungeon spawns are marked.
- `wow_quest` gets the title, the givers and enders (objects with their spawns), and a search by title.
- Every row is `trust: community-db`, and the prompt says to call it community data. There are no levels or other numbers.
- Orders still refuse `{npc:ID}` and `{quest:ID}`, so no community name reaches the stream overlay.
- If the client data changes after a community sync, `wowdata` leaves out the coordinates and names the command to fix that.

## Real data (z2815, 2026-10-02)

- 9,902 NPCs, 4,245 quests (3,532 in the Era client) and 237 quest objects.
- 482 rows dropped: 481 developer or unused names and 1 empty name. About 10 MB on disk, 3 s.
- 55 of 17,593 shared item IDs (0.31%) have a different name in Era, mostly renamed developer tributes. That is why everything is labeled.
- Spot checks: Undertaker Mordo is in Tirisfal Glades at 30.22, 71.65. "Wanted: Hogger" comes from the two Wanted Posters and ends at Marshal Dughan. Young Black Bear is found in Wetlands. Drunken Bruiser has 46 spawns.

## Tests

- `npm test`: 957 tests, 955 pass, 2 skipped. `test:bun`: 955 pass. `test:e2e`: 54 pass.
- 22 guards mutation-checked: each test fails with its guard removed.
- The fixture `tests/fixtures/cmangos/classicdb.sql` is hand-written; no real rows are copied.
- Three fresh-eyes rounds on fable and gpt-6-astra: the plan, the code, and the fixes.

Not done: the community store keeps its own small pointer and swap code instead of sharing datasync's, because the pointer format differs. NPC names in the phrase index are a follow-up.

author: hoxton314
body:
## What changed
- **Squash N commits…** in the multi-select context menu, plus a palette action `squash_selected`. It opens `graph/SquashDialog.svelte`:
  - The combined message (each commit's message, oldest first) is editable.
  - An autostash option is on by default.
  - The dialog says how many newer commits will be rebased on top.
- **Backend** `git/squash.rs`:
  - `plan_squash` validates the selection and returns a plan.
  - `squash` runs the plan through the existing interactive-rebase backend: the oldest selected commit is picked, the rest are squashed into it with the message, and newer commits are picked on top. Squashing from the root uses `--root`.
- **Refused, with a clear message:**
  - fewer than two commits
  - a selection that isn't contiguous
  - commits not on HEAD's first-parent line
  - a merge commit between the selection and HEAD (the rebase would flatten it)
- **Already pushed:** the dialog names the remote-tracking branches that contain the commits and warns that a force push will be needed.
  - The check walks each remote branch only back to the squash base, with a shared budget of 20k commits. If the budget runs out, the dialog says the check is incomplete.
- **Plan recomputed on submit:** `squash_commits` builds the plan again, so a moved HEAD can't apply a stale todo. It also refuses while another operation is in progress.
- **Paused squash:** if the rebase stops part-way (e.g. a newer commit conflicts), the dialog closes and points to the operation banner.

## Verification
- Ran `npm run check`, `npm run build`, vitest (54), `cargo test` (129), and clippy `-D warnings` on 1.94 and 1.99.
- New Rust tests in `squash::tests`:
  - Squashing a run in the middle (selection order doesn't matter) keeps the later commits and all files.
  - Squashing from the root works.
  - Pushed detection: a remote ref behind the run is not counted, and the check is skipped when not requested.
  - Every refusal case.
- Sabotage check: removing the contiguity check makes the tests fail.
- New e2e step: select the two e2e commits, choose *Squash 2 commits…* from the context menu, set the message and submit. It then checks that history is one commit and that autostash restored the modified files.
- The code review found no correctness bugs. Its two low findings (cost of the pushed check, and a stale submit button after a paused squash) are fixed in the second commit.

## Not verified
- No manual desktop run: synthetic input isn't allowed. The e2e step only runs in CI.

Closes #58

author: ksyasuda
body:
## Summary

On Windows, SubMiner plays YouTube through a resolved direct googlevideo stream URL, so mpv's `path` is the stream rather than the YouTube page. The subtitle generation runtime only recognized local files and YouTube page URLs, so the manual Whisper modal reported "Open a local video or audio file, or a YouTube video" during active playback. The still-playing check (used before loading generated subtitles) and the cancel-on-switch check had the same blind spot.

The YouTube playback runtime, which resolves the stream, now records `{ streamUrl, sourceUrl }` and exposes `getYoutubeSourceUrlForStream`. Subtitle generation maps the mpv path through it before its YouTube identity checks. macOS/Linux are unaffected: mpv's `path` stays the watch URL there.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / internal
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Other

## How was this tested?

- New tests in `youtube-playback-runtime.test.ts` (stream maps to source; other paths return null) and `subtitle-generation-runtime.test.ts` (generation on a resolved stream loads subtitles and is not cancelled by re-reporting the same stream; switching to another stream cancels). All fail on the old code.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test:src`, `bun run test:scripts`, `bun run format:check:src`, `bun run changelog:lint`, `bun run changelog:pr-check`.
- Needs a manual Windows pass: start and cancel Whisper generation during YouTube playback.

## Checklist

- [x] Reconciled current-outcome changelog fragment(s), or this PR is labeled `skip-changelog` (see [`changes/README.md`](../changes/README.md))
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR if behavior, defaults, flags, shortcuts, ports, or APIs changed
- [x] Relevant checks pass locally (typecheck, tests, build)

body:
